title: Multipartite Mixed-Species Entanglement Over A Quantum Network
authors: D. Main, P. Drmota, E. M. Ainley, A. Agrawal, D. Webb, S. Saner, O. Bǎzǎvan, B. C. Nichol, R. Srinivas, D. P. Nadlinger, G. Araneda, And D. M. Lucas
abstract:
Author(s): D. Main, P. Drmota, E. M. Ainley, A. Agrawal, D. Webb, S. Saner, O. Bǎzǎvan, B. C. Nichol, R. Srinivas, D. P. Nadlinger, G. Araneda, and D. M. Lucas

We generate multipartite entangled states of two, three, and four matter qubits, where the entanglement is distributed over macroscopic distances via a photonic network link. Trapped-ion [MATH] qubits are entangled directly via an optical fibre link, and the entanglement is subsequ…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160801] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally generate multipartite entangled states of two, three, and four matter qubits distributed over macroscopic distances through a photonic fibre network link.
motivation: Distributing genuine multipartite entanglement between remote matter qubits is a prerequisite for scalable quantum networks, yet prior demonstrations have been limited to few qubits or short distances.
method: Trapped-ion qubits of mixed species are entangled directly via an optical fibre link, with the photonic-mediated entanglement subsequently extended to additional qubits to build up two-, three-, and four-partite states.
result: Multipartite entangled states across two, three, and four matter qubits are generated with entanglement distributed over macroscopic distances via the photonic network link.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a viable route toward modular, networked quantum computing and multi-node entanglement distribution using mixed-species trapped-ion nodes.

title: Tripartite Haar Random State Has No Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Zhi Li, Takato Mori, And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi Li, Takato Mori, and Beni Yoshida

Researchers demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from tripartite Haar random states by local operations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041013] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that tripartite Haar random states contain no bipartite EPR entanglement distillable by local operations.
motivation: Understanding entanglement structure in random multipartite states is central to entanglement theory and has implications for quantum information processing.
method: The authors analyze tripartite Haar random quantum states and study bipartite entanglement distillation under local operations and classical communication.
result: They demonstrate that bipartite Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen entanglement cannot be distilled from such tripartite Haar random states.
conclusion: This establishes a sharp limitation on bipartite entanglement extraction from generic tripartite random states, clarifying multipartite entanglement structure.

title: Information Thermodynamics Of Agents: The Work Capacity Of Channels With Memory
authors: Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, And Hans J. Briegel
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas J. Fiderer, Paul C. Barth, Isaac D. Smith, and Hans J. Briegel

An information-theoretic model of agents, i.e., complex self-organizing systems, shows that agents must forget parts of their past actions in order to operate at thermodynamic efficiency.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041004] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an information-theoretic model of agents as complex self-organizing systems and shows that thermodynamic efficiency requires forgetting parts of past actions.
motivation: Understanding how adaptive agents process information under thermodynamic constraints is central to connecting information theory with non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze work capacity of channels with memory within an information-theoretic agent model, deriving conditions relating memory retention, past actions, and thermodynamic efficiency.
result: They find that agents operating at thermodynamic efficiency must discard some information about their past actions, imposing a trade-off between memory and work extraction.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic rationale for forgetting in agents and links information processing architectures to fundamental efficiency limits.

title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation With Quantum Feedback
authors: Ryotaro Honma And Tan van Vu
abstract:
Author(s): Ryotaro Honma and Tan Van Vu

Fluctuations are intrinsic to microscopic systems and impose fundamental limits on nonequilibrium precision, as captured by the thermodynamic uncertainty relation (TUR), which links current fluctuations to entropy production. While feedback control is expected to further suppress fluctuations, its r…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160406] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation for quantum systems under feedback control, quantifying how measurement-based feedback can suppress current fluctuations relative to entropy production.
motivation: Classical TURs bound the precision of nonequilibrium currents by entropy production, and feedback control is expected to relax or tighten these bounds, but a fully quantum formulation accounting for measurement backaction and information gain was missing.
method: Using a quantum stochastic/measurement framework, they model a continuously monitored open quantum system with feedback, quantify entropy production and information acquired by the controller, and derive a modified trade-off between current fluctuations and dissipation.
result: They obtain a generalized TUR in which the fluctuation bound is modified by the information extracted through measurement, showing that quantum feedback can enhance precision beyond the feedback-free bound within limits set by thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The work extends thermodynamic uncertainty relations to the quantum feedback regime, clarifying how measurement information and quantum coherence enter fluctuation-dissipation trade-offs and providing bounds relevant to precision control of microscopic quantum devices.

title: Robust Superradiance And Spontaneous Spin Ordering In Disordered Waveguide Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Xin H. H. Zhang, Daniel Malz, and Peter Rabl

Spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins protects the hallmark burst of superradiance against strong spatial and spectral disorder in photonic waveguides.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033034] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that spontaneous self-organization of atomic spins can protect superradiant emission against strong spatial and spectral disorder in waveguide quantum electrodynamics.
motivation: Superradiance is a hallmark collective quantum optical effect, but it is typically fragile in the presence of inhomogeneous broadening and positional disorder. The authors seek a mechanism that preserves collective emission in realistic disordered waveguide QED settings.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a waveguide QED model of atomic spins with spatial and spectral disorder, focusing on spontaneous spin ordering and its impact on collective superradiant dynamics.
result: They find that spontaneous spin ordering emerges and enables a robust superradiant burst that survives strong disorder, countering the usual degradation of collective emission.
conclusion: Disorder-induced self-organization can stabilize collective quantum optical phenomena, with implications for scalable waveguide QED and hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Far-from-Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Non-Abelian Thermal States
authors: Franklin L. S. Rodrigues And Eric Lutz
abstract:
Author(s): Franklin L. S. Rodrigues and Eric Lutz

Noncommutativity of observables is a defining feature of quantum physics. It plays a fundamental role in the formulation of the uncertainty principle for complementary variables and strongly affects the thermodynamic behavior of systems with noncommuting, that is, non-Abelian, conserved quantities. …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160401] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a far-from-equilibrium thermodynamic framework for quantum states with noncommuting (non-Abelian) conserved charges, showing how noncommutativity modifies work, entropy, and fluctuation-type relations.
motivation: Noncommutativity of observables is a defining quantum feature, yet standard thermodynamic treatments of thermal states with multiple conserved quantities (e.g., charge, spin, particle number) implicitly assume these charges commute; the authors aim to characterize how non-Abelian conserved quantities alter thermodynamic behavior away from equilibrium.
method: The authors generalize quantum thermodynamic formalism — thermal (Gibbs-like) states with non-Abelian charges, entropy and free-energy-like quantities, and work/heat definitions — to the far-from-equilibrium regime, deriving generalized second-law-type bounds and fluctuation relations that account for the noncommuting structure of the conserved observables.
result: They obtain modified thermodynamic inequalities and work bounds in which noncommutativity of the conserved charges produces additional quantum contributions, explicitly distinguishing non-Abelian from Abelian thermal-state thermodynamics and identifying regimes where the departures become significant.
conclusion: Non-Abelian conserved quantities fundamentally reshape far-from-equilibrium thermodynamics, requiring generalized laws and providing a framework for describing quantum systems with noncommuting charges, with implications for quantum engines and information-theoretic treatments of work and entropy.

title: Reliable Global Entanglement Distribution Based On Probabilistic Photon Sources
authors: Pei-Xi Liu, Yu-Ping Lin, Zong-Quan Zhou, Chuan-Feng Li, And Guang-Can Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Pei-Xi Liu, Yu-Ping Lin, Zong-Quan Zhou, Chuan-Feng Li, and Guang-Can Guo

Probabilistic photon sources (PPSs) are the most mature quantum light sources and offer a practical route toward a quantum-repeater-based quantum internet. However, the intrinsic noise from multiphoton emission has hindered the construction of global-scale quantum repeaters with multiple elementary …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042429] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a scheme for reliable global-scale entanglement distribution using probabilistic photon sources, mitigating multiphoton-emission noise in multi-segment quantum repeaters.
motivation: Probabilistic photon sources are the most mature quantum light sources and offer a practical route to a repeater-based quantum internet, but their intrinsic multiphoton emission noise has so far prevented the construction of global-scale repeaters with many elementary links.
method: The authors analyze the impact of multiphoton-emission noise on repeater chains built from probabilistic sources and develop a protocol/architecture designed to suppress or tolerate this noise across multiple elementary links.
result: The proposed approach is shown to enable reliable entanglement distribution over global distances, extending repeater operation beyond what naive scaling with noisy probabilistic sources would allow.
conclusion: Probabilistic photon sources can support practical, large-scale quantum repeater networks, providing a realistic path toward a global quantum internet.

title: Thermoelectric Information Engine Driven By An Autonomous Maxwell Demon Across Quantum-to-classical Transitions
authors: M. Bernal-Santibañez, José Mondaca, And Felipe Barra
abstract:
Author(s): M. Bernal-Santibañez, José Mondaca, and Felipe Barra

We study a three-terminal thermoelectric engine, focusing on the role of quantum coherence and information flow. A double dot connects two reservoirs at different chemical potentials, while a third dot monitors their occupation via Coulomb interaction and can be interpreted as an autonomous Maxwell …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044121] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes a three-terminal thermoelectric information engine in which an autonomous Maxwell demon monitors a double quantum dot and regulates transport, with emphasis on quantum coherence and information flow across the quantum-to-classical transition.
motivation: Autonomous Maxwell demons provide a concrete setting to connect information flow, thermodynamic performance, and quantum coherence in nanoscale engines. The authors aim to clarify how genuine quantum effects modify the demon's operation and engine efficiency.
method: A double dot coupled to two reservoirs at different chemical potentials is monitored by a third quantum dot via Coulomb interaction, realizing an autonomous Maxwell demon. The thermoelectric engine is characterized using information-theoretic quantities and coherence measures, comparing quantum and classical regimes.
result: The engine's performance is linked to information flow between the demon and the double dot, and quantum coherence is shown to influence transport and thermodynamic efficiency. The analysis identifies regimes across the quantum-to-classical transition where information-assisted operation is enhanced or suppressed.
conclusion: The work provides an information-thermodynamic characterization of an autonomous Maxwell demon and demonstrates how quantum coherence affects thermoelectric energy conversion. It strengthens the connection between information flow, quantum thermodynamics, and nanoscale engine performance.

title: Unified Geometric Formalism For Dissipation And Its Fluctuations In Finite-time Microscopic Heat Engines
authors: Gentaro Watanabe, Guo-Hua Xu, And Yuki Minami
abstract:
Author(s): Gentaro Watanabe, Guo-Hua Xu, and Yuki Minami

Microscopic heat engines operate in regimes where thermodynamic quantities fluctuate strongly, making stochastic effects an essential aspect of their performance. However, existing geometric formulations of finite-time thermodynamics primarily characterize average dissipation and do not systematical…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043037] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a unified geometric formalism describing both average dissipation and its fluctuations in finite-time microscopic heat engines.
motivation: Microscopic heat engines exhibit strong thermodynamic fluctuations, but existing geometric finite-time thermodynamic frameworks mainly characterize average dissipation and lack a systematic treatment of fluctuations.
method: The authors construct a geometric framework for finite-time microscopic heat engines that incorporates stochastic thermodynamic effects and captures dissipation fluctuations alongside average dissipation.
result: The formalism provides a unified geometric description of dissipation and its fluctuations, extending finite-time thermodynamic geometry beyond average-performance measures.
conclusion: This work offers a systematic geometric approach for analyzing fluctuating dissipation in microscopic heat engines, relevant to finite-time thermodynamics at the quantum scale.

title: Finite-Size Quantum Key Distribution Rates From Rényi Entropies Using Conic Optimization
authors: Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, And Mateus Araújo
abstract:
Author(s): Mariana Navarro, Andrés González Lorente, Pablo V. Parellada, Carlos Pascual-García, and Mateus Araújo

A conic optimization method addressing a critical challenge in key rate estimation for quantum key distribution is presented, providing tighter security bounds and fast numerical convergence.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033051] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a conic optimization method for computing finite-size quantum key distribution rates using Rényi entropies, yielding tighter security bounds and faster numerical convergence.
motivation: Finite-size effects are critical for practical QKD security, but existing key-rate estimation methods can be loose or computationally demanding.
method: The authors formulate key-rate estimation as a conic optimization problem based on Rényi entropy bounds, enabling efficient numerical evaluation of finite-size security parameters.
result: The approach provides tighter finite-size QKD security bounds and demonstrates fast numerical convergence compared with existing techniques.
conclusion: Conic optimization with Rényi entropies offers a practical and rigorous tool for finite-size QKD security analysis, improving both accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Semidefinite Block-Matrix Relaxations For Computing Quantum Correlations
authors: Nicola D’alessandro, Carles Roch I Carceller, And Armin Tavakoli
abstract:
Author(s): Nicola D’Alessandro, Carles Roch i Carceller, and Armin Tavakoli

Researchers provide a computational method for bounding the correlations arising in a multitude of quantum information problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031050] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a hierarchy of semidefinite block-matrix relaxations that yields computable bounds on quantum correlations arising in diverse quantum information problems.
motivation: Computing the set of quantum correlations—relevant to Bell nonlocality, self-testing, and device-independent protocols—is a notoriously hard, generally undecidable problem, so practical converging outer approximations are needed.
method: They formulate a general semidefinite-programming relaxation framework based on block-matrix (moment/Positivstellensatz-style) structures that can be instantiated for many correlation-computation tasks and tightened order by order.
result: The relaxations provide rigorous upper bounds on quantum correlation sets for a variety of scenarios, offering a unified and efficient computational tool demonstrated on concrete examples.
conclusion: The method gives a versatile numerical toolkit for bounding quantum correlations, with direct applications to entanglement/Bell scenarios and device-independent analysis.

title: Bayesian Phase Stabilization At The Shot-Noise Limit For Scalable Quantum Networks
authors: Guang-Cheng Liu, Chao-Hui Xue, Fa-Xi Chen, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yi Yang, Li-Bo Li, Bin Wang, Bo-Wen Yang, Hai-Feng Jiang, Yong Wan, Ye Wang, Jiu-Peng Chen, Qiang Zhang, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Guang-Cheng Liu, Chao-Hui Xue, Fa-Xi Chen, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yi Yang, Li-Bo Li, Bin Wang, Bo-Wen Yang, Hai-Feng Jiang, Yong Wan, Ye Wang, Jiu-Peng Chen, Qiang Zhang, and Jian-Wei Pan

High-precision optical phase stabilization in quantum networks is fundamentally constrained by the strict photon-flux and duty-cycle limits required to avoid disturbing fragile quantum states. This challenge becomes especially critical when coordinating multiple independent light sources for multist…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160802] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates Bayesian phase stabilization at the shot-noise limit for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: High-precision optical phase stabilization in quantum networks is limited by strict photon-flux and duty-cycle constraints, especially when coordinating multiple independent light sources in multinode settings.
method: The authors develop a Bayesian phase-stabilization approach designed to operate under weak-light conditions imposed by fragile quantum states.
result: The scheme achieves phase stabilization at the shot-noise limit, supporting scalable operation across multiple independent light sources.
conclusion: This work provides an enabling technique for practical scalable quantum networks by overcoming phase-stabilization constraints in multinode quantum communication architectures.

title: Relationship Between Vanishing Pairwise Entanglement And Global Separability: Entanglement Structure And Measures In $w$ Subspace
authors: Reza Hamzehofi
abstract:
Author(s): Reza Hamzehofi

The [MATH] subspace is defined as the subspace of the [MATH]-qubit Hilbert space spanned by states containing at most one excitation. In this work, a separability criterion is established for pure and mixed states supported in this subspace: if all reduced two-qubit subsystems are separable, then the enti…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042425] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a separability criterion in the w subspace of multiqubit Hilbert space, showing that global separability follows from separability of all reduced two-qubit subsystems, and analyzes the entanglement structure and measures in this subspace.
motivation: It addresses the fundamental question of when vanishing pairwise entanglement implies global separability, focusing on the restricted but physically relevant w subspace.
method: The authors define the w subspace spanned by states with at most one excitation and derive a separability criterion for both pure and mixed states supported in this subspace, supported by entanglement measure analysis.
result: A state in the w subspace is fully separable if and only if all its reduced two-qubit subsystems are separable, yielding a practical criterion and characterization of entanglement structure.
conclusion: The work provides a useful separability test and entanglement-measure framework for states in the w subspace, clarifying the relationship between pairwise and global entanglement in this setting.

title: Non-Abelian Quantum Signal Processing: A Composite Pulse For Fast Analytic Control Of Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
authors: Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Shraddha Singh, Baptiste Royer, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers extend quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytical control of hybrid oscillator-qubit quantum processors.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041018] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends quantum signal processing to noncommuting control variables, enabling analytic composite-pulse control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qubit architectures require fast, high-fidelity control, but standard quantum signal processing assumes commuting control variables and is insufficient for such platforms.
method: The authors generalize quantum signal processing to non-Abelian control variables and construct composite pulses for analytic control of hybrid oscillator-qubit processors.
result: The approach yields analytical control protocols that can be applied to hybrid oscillator-qubit systems, enabling fast composite-pulse sequences without purely numerical optimization.
conclusion: This work provides a practical theoretical framework for controlling hybrid quantum processors and expands the scope of quantum signal processing to noncommuting control settings.

title: Entanglement Certification Using Noncontextuality Inequalities
authors: Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, Jonah Spodek, David Schmid, Carter Reid, Liam J. Morrison, Thomas Jennewein, Kevin J. Resch, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers demonstrate a gauge-independent entanglement certification method based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without requiring prior measurement device characterization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031057] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a gauge-independent entanglement certification scheme based on noncontextuality inequalities that detects entangled states without prior characterization of measurement devices.
motivation: Standard entanglement witnesses and tomographic certification require trusting or characterizing measurement devices, which is impractical and assumption-laden; noncontextuality inequalities offer a route to certify entanglement under weaker, more physical assumptions.
method: The authors derive noncontextuality inequalities whose violation is a gauge-independent witness of entanglement, then implement them experimentally using photonic measurement devices to certify entangled states without device tomography.
result: The experiment observes violations of the noncontextuality inequalities for entangled states, certifying entanglement while remaining robust to unknown measurement gauge choices and device imperfections.
conclusion: Noncontextuality inequalities provide a practical, assumption-light alternative to device-dependent witnesses and full device-independent self-testing for entanglement certification, bridging nonclassicality certification and entanglement theory.

title: Geometric Optimization Over Quantum State Spaces: Tight Uncertainty Relations And Resource Certification
authors: Ma-Cheng Yang And Cong-Feng Qiao
abstract:
Author(s): Ma-Cheng Yang and Cong-Feng Qiao

Determining the fundamental limits of nonlinear functionals of quantum measurement statistics is a crucial yet generally intractable nonconvex optimization problem. We introduce a generic support-function-based outer-approximation framework for solving concave-minimization (or convex-maximization) p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160201] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a support-function-based outer-approximation framework that turns intractable nonconvex optimizations over quantum measurement statistics into tractable convex programs, yielding tight uncertainty relations and improved resource certification.
motivation: Fundamental limits on nonlinear functionals of measurement statistics (e.g., entropic uncertainty, entanglement witnesses, steering and nonlocality bounds) are typically nonconvex and computationally hard, so practical, generic and tight bounding techniques are needed.
method: They formulate concave minimization (convex maximization) over quantum state spaces via an outer approximation built from support functions of the state set, iteratively refining the relaxation to converge to tight bounds on the target nonlinear functional.
result: The framework reproduces and tightens known uncertainty relations and provides certified bounds for resource-detection tasks such as entanglement and steering witnesses, outperforming existing semidefinite or ad hoc approaches in several examples.
conclusion: Geometric optimization via support functions offers a generic, computationally feasible route to tight, certifiable bounds in quantum information, with applications to uncertainty quantification and resource certification.

title: Traceable Quantum Secret Sharing
authors: Mengyan Qiao, Jian Long, Yu Li, And Zhu Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Mengyan Qiao, Jian Long, Yu Li, and Zhu Cao

Quantum secret sharing protects distributed quantum information against unauthorized reconstruction, yet existing schemes provide no intrinsic accountability when shares are leaked or forged. This missing capability is particularly relevant in realistic distributed settings, where compromised partic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042430] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes traceable quantum secret sharing, adding accountability to detect and attribute leaked or forged shares in distributed quantum secret-sharing schemes.
motivation: Existing quantum secret-sharing schemes protect distributed quantum information but lack intrinsic accountability when shares are leaked or forged, which is important in realistic settings with compromised participants.
method: The authors design a quantum secret-sharing protocol with traceability, likely by embedding verifiable/traceable credentials or share-authentication mechanisms into the sharing and reconstruction process.
result: The proposed scheme enables tracing of leaked or forged shares while preserving the secret-sharing functionality, though the abstract does not provide detailed performance metrics.
conclusion: Traceable quantum secret sharing addresses a practical accountability gap in multi-party quantum communication and may be useful for secure distributed quantum information applications.

title: Stochastic Multipath Routing For High-throughput Entanglement Distribution In Quantum Repeater Networks
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit Mishra and Kang Hao Cheong

The authors show that balancing shorter and longer routes through stochastic path selection can improve entanglement distribution in quantum repeater networks. An intermediate routing bias yields higher throughput than consistently favoring either short or long paths across a broad range of network conditions.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L040601] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: A stochastic multipath routing strategy that balances short and long paths improves entanglement distribution throughput in quantum repeater networks.
motivation: Entanglement routing in quantum repeater networks must trade off the higher success probability of short paths against the greater resource efficiency and load-balancing benefits of longer, less-congested routes; static policies favoring one extreme may be suboptimal.
method: The authors introduce a stochastic path-selection scheme with a tunable routing bias and evaluate its entanglement distribution throughput against deterministic short- and long-path-favoring policies across a range of network conditions.
result: An intermediate bias yields higher throughput than consistently preferring either short or long paths, with the benefit holding across a broad range of network parameters.
conclusion: Stochastic, bias-tunable multipath routing offers a simple yet effective mechanism for enhancing throughput in quantum repeater networks, suggesting routing policy diversity is valuable for network design.

title: Overcoming Intrinsic Material Limitations Through Cavity Feedback
authors: M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, And J. P. Davis
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ebrahimi, Y. Huang, V. A. S. V. Bittencourt, A. Rashedi, A. Metelmann, and J. P. Davis

Active dissipation control via a feedback loop overcomes intrinsic magnetic losses, achieving strong coupling among photons, magnons, and phonons in cavity magnomechanics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031068] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses cavity feedback to actively control dissipation and overcome intrinsic magnetic losses, enabling strong photon-magnon-phonon coupling in a cavity magnomechanical system.
motivation: Intrinsic material losses in magnomechanical platforms limit the achievable coupling strength and coherent hybrid dynamics. The authors aim to circumvent these material limitations without requiring better materials.
method: They implement an active feedback loop that modifies the effective dissipation of the cavity-magnomechanical system, and analyze the resulting coupled photon-magnon-phonon dynamics.
result: Feedback control suppresses the detrimental magnetic losses sufficiently to reach the strong-coupling regime among photons, magnons, and phonons.
conclusion: Active dissipation control via cavity feedback is a viable route to enhance hybrid quantum interactions in platforms with unavoidable material losses.

title: Efficient Entanglement Purification Circuit Design For Dual-Species Atom Arrays
authors: Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Bikun Li, Daniel Dilley, Alvin Gonzales, Thomas A. Hahn, Ryan White, Rotem Arnon, Hannes Bernien, Zain Saleem, and Liang Jiang

A dual-species atomic array reduces technical overhead (no local addressing needed and nondestructive midcircuit measurements) and enables efficient entanglement purification for applications in quantum networking and distributed computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033044] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper designs efficient entanglement purification circuits tailored to dual-species neutral-atom arrays, exploiting species-selective operations and mid-circuit measurements to reduce resource overhead for networking and distributed quantum computation.
motivation: Entanglement purification is essential for distributing high-fidelity entanglement over noisy channels, but standard circuits demand extensive local addressing and destructive measurements that are costly on atomic-array hardware. Dual-species arrays offer species-selective control and nondestructive mid-circuit readout, motivating purification schemes built around these native capabilities.
method: The authors construct purification circuits in which one species acts as the communication qubit and the other as the ancilla/memory, using collective (addressing-free) gates and nondestructive mid-circuit measurement with feed-forward. They analyze circuit-level performance, comparing resource cost and fidelity gain against conventional single-species purification protocols.
result: The proposed dual-species circuits achieve efficient entanglement purification with substantially reduced technical overhead — no individual addressing and repeat-until-success measurement reuse — yielding favorable fidelity-versus-resource tradeoffs relative to standard approaches.
conclusion: Dual-species atomic arrays provide a practical, hardware-efficient route to entanglement purification, making them attractive for repeater-style quantum networking and distributed quantum computing architectures.

title: Self-Configuring Quantum Networks With Superposition Of Trajectories
authors: Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, And Wolfgang Dür
abstract:
Author(s): Albie Chan, Zheng Shi, Jorge Miguel-Ramiro, Luca Dellantonio, Christine A. Muschik, and Wolfgang Dür

A self-configuring quantum network protocol integrates superposed quantum paths with variational optimization techniques to mitigate decoherence and establish high-fidelity connections without requiring prior noise knowledge.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033038] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a self-configuring quantum network protocol that combines superpositions of quantum trajectories with variational optimization to establish high-fidelity entanglement connections without prior knowledge of the channel noise.
motivation: Realistic quantum networks suffer from unknown and fluctuating noise, so protocols that must be pre-optimized for a known error model are impractical; a scheme that adapts itself to the actual noise is therefore desirable.
method: The protocol places the propagating quantum signal in a superposition of trajectories and variationally optimizes the resulting interference/control parameters on the fly, using measurement feedback to learn and counteract decoherence.
result: The variational, self-configuring approach yields high-fidelity connections across noisy channels without requiring prior noise characterization, outperforming non-adaptive strategies.
conclusion: Superposition of trajectories plus variational optimization provides a practical route toward adaptive, noise-robust quantum network links, relevant for repeater and entanglement-distribution architectures.

title: Systematic Construction Of Time-Dependent Hamiltonians For Microwave-Driven Josephson Circuits
authors: Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, And Robert J. Schoelkopf
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Lu, Tianpu Zhao, André Vallières, Kevin C. Smith, Daniel Weiss, Xinyuan You, Yaxing Zhang, Suhas Ganjam, Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Shantanu Mundhada, Ziwen Huang, Ian Mondragon-Shem, Steven M. Girvin, Jens Koch, and Robert J. Schoelkopf

A versatile framework bridges layout-level microwave simulations with quantum dynamics, enabling realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033039] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a systematic framework for constructing time-dependent Hamiltonians for microwave-driven Josephson circuits by linking layout-level microwave simulations to quantum dynamics.
motivation: Realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits requires going beyond simplified lumped-element descriptions to capture layout-dependent microwave effects.
method: The authors bridge electromagnetic layout simulations with quantum circuit dynamics to derive time-dependent Hamiltonians for Josephson circuits under microwave driving.
result: The framework enables more realistic modeling of driven superconducting circuits and provides a systematic construction applicable to circuit QED architectures.
conclusion: This approach improves the fidelity of quantum dynamics modeling for superconducting hardware and is useful for designing and analyzing driven Josephson-circuit experiments.

title: Superextensive Charging Power In The Absence Of Global Operations
authors: Anupam Sarkar, Sheryl Mathew, And Sibasish Ghosh
abstract:
Author(s): Anupam Sarkar, Sheryl Mathew, and Sibasish Ghosh

Quantum batteries provide a setting to investigate whether quantum effects can enhance the rate of energy storage beyond classical limits. While superextensive charging power has been reported in a few models, the fundamental physical requirements for achieving such scaling remain unclear. Here we i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160403] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies physical conditions under which quantum batteries can exhibit superextensive charging power without requiring global operations.
motivation: Superextensive charging power has been observed in some quantum battery models, but the fundamental requirements for achieving such scaling remained unclear.
method: The authors analyze quantum battery charging protocols and derive conditions for superextensive power scaling while restricting to local or non-global operations.
result: They show that superextensive charging power can arise even in the absence of global operations, clarifying the role of quantum effects and operational constraints.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for understanding and designing quantum batteries with enhanced charging performance under realistic operational restrictions.

title: Breakdown Of The Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced By Auxiliary Circuit Modes
authors: Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, And Alexandre Blais
abstract:
Author(s): Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Cristóbal Lledó, and Alexandre Blais

Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041012] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that degrade Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.
motivation: Kerr-cat qubits are promising for biased-noise-protected superconducting quantum information, but their coherence under strong driving can be limited by unintended coupling to auxiliary circuit modes.
method: The authors analyze the driven Kerr-cat qubit together with auxiliary circuit modes and identify multiphoton resonance conditions that affect the qubit tunneling time.
result: Auxiliary modes are shown to induce multiphoton resonances that break down the Kerr-cat qubit tunneling time and coherence under strong driving.
conclusion: Designs and operating regimes for Kerr-cat qubits must account for and mitigate auxiliary-mode-induced resonances to preserve coherence.

title: Fast Gates For Bit-Flip Protected Superconducting Qubits
authors: C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): C. A. Siegele, A. A. Sokolova, L. N. Kapoor, F. Hassani, and J. M. Fink

An architecture design for real-time tunable bit-flip protection yields a hardware-efficient, noise-biased platform amenable to error correction and scalability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043008] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hardware-efficient architecture for real-time tunable bit-flip protection in superconducting qubits, enabling fast gates on a noise-biased platform suitable for error correction and scaling.
motivation: Superconducting qubit platforms need improved noise bias and hardware-efficient protection against bit-flip errors while maintaining fast gate operation for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors design an architecture for real-time tunable bit-flip protection and analyze its compatibility with fast gate operations in superconducting qubits.
result: The design yields a noise-biased superconducting qubit platform that is hardware-efficient and amenable to error correction and scalability.
conclusion: This work advances practical superconducting qubit hardware by combining bit-flip protection with fast gates, supporting future scalable error-corrected quantum processors.

title: Predicting Magic From Very Few Measurements
authors: J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, And R. A. Macêdo
abstract:
Author(s): J. M. Varela, L. L. Keller, A. de Oliveira Junior, D. A. Moreira, R. Chaves, and R. A. Macêdo

A near-optimal method quantifies nonstabilizerness—the resource that enables universal quantum computation—from a small number of Pauli measurements, extending its estimation to system sizes beyond the reach of standard techniques.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043009] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A near-optimal method quantifies nonstabilizerness (magic) from few Pauli measurements, enabling estimation for system sizes beyond standard techniques.
motivation: Magic is the resource enabling universal quantum computation, but its estimation typically requires many measurements, limiting scalability.
method: The authors propose a method using a small number of Pauli measurements, likely based on randomized measurements or classical shadows, to estimate magic monotones.
result: The method achieves near-optimal sample complexity and extends magic estimation to system sizes beyond the reach of standard techniques.
conclusion: This provides an efficient way to quantify magic, advancing resource-theoretic characterization for near-term quantum devices.

title: Ising On The Donut: Regimes Of Topological Quantum Error Correction From Statistical Mechanics
authors: Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, And Dominic J. Williamson
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas H. English, Sam Roberts, Stephen D. Bartlett, Andrew C. Doherty, and Dominic J. Williamson

An exact mapping to the 2D Ising model produces closed-form logical failure rates for the toric code, offering an analytic tool kit for benchmarking topological codes beyond current computational limits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043004] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes an exact mapping between toric-code logical failure rates and the 2D Ising model, yielding closed-form analytic expressions for topological quantum error correction.
motivation: Benchmarking topological quantum error-correcting codes at large code distances is computationally expensive, motivating analytic tools that can predict logical failure rates beyond current simulation limits.
method: The authors use an exact statistical-mechanical mapping between the toric code and the 2D Ising model to derive closed-form logical failure rates and analyze distinct error-correction regimes.
result: They obtain analytic expressions for logical failure rates and identify regimes of topological quantum error correction, providing a toolkit for benchmarking topological codes.
conclusion: The Ising-model mapping offers practical closed-form benchmarks for toric-code performance and clarifies connections between topological quantum error correction and statistical mechanics.

title: Fundamental Limitations On The Reliabilities Of Power And Work In Quantum Batteries
authors: Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, And Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Brij Mohan, Tanmoy Pandit, Maciej Lewenstein, and Manabendra Nath Bera

A fundamental quantum uncertainty relation reveals an unavoidable trade-off between the reliabilities of the charging power and the work deposited during the charging and discharging of quantum batteries, establishing essential design limits for future quantum energy storage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033057] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a fundamental quantum uncertainty relation showing an unavoidable trade-off between the reliability of charging power and the reliability of the work deposited in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising for future energy storage, but fluctuations in power and work limit their practical utility; understanding fundamental bounds on these fluctuations is therefore essential for device design.
method: The authors formulate uncertainty relations for the charging and discharging dynamics of quantum batteries, quantifying the variances (unreliabilities) of power and work and deriving trade-off bounds from the underlying quantum dynamics.
result: They establish that the reliabilities of power and work cannot both be made arbitrarily high, obtaining an unavoidable trade-off that sets design limits for quantum energy storage protocols.
conclusion: The derived uncertainty relations provide fundamental performance bounds and design guidelines for quantum batteries, linking quantum fluctuation constraints to practical energy-storage applications.

title: Circuit-Based Characterization Of Finite-Temperature Quantum Phases And Self-Correcting Quantum Memory
authors: Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, And Shengqi Sang
abstract:
Author(s): Ruochen Ma, Vedika Khemani, and Shengqi Sang

A circuit-based framework characterizing thermal quantum phases via a correlation-decay condition is presented, establishing self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033052] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: A circuit-based framework characterizes finite-temperature quantum phases through a correlation-decay condition and identifies self-correction as a universal property of finite-temperature quantum memories.
motivation: The work aims to clarify how thermal quantum phases can be characterized and whether finite-temperature quantum memories can be self-correcting.
method: The authors develop a circuit-based characterization of thermal quantum phases using a correlation-decay condition.
result: They establish a connection between finite-temperature quantum phase structure and self-correcting quantum memory, showing self-correction as a universal property in this setting.
conclusion: The paper provides a unifying framework linking finite-temperature phase classification with the stability of self-correcting quantum memories.

title: Dissipation-engineered Dual-charger Quantum Batteries
authors: Yi-Jia Yang, Yu-Qiang Liu, Zheng Liu, Zhi-Hao Ma, Ming-Xing Luo, And Chang-Shui Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-jia Yang, Yu-qiang Liu, Zheng Liu, Zhi-Hao Ma, Ming-Xing Luo, and Chang-shui Yu

Suppressing coherent energy backflow while maintaining extractable energy in a stable nonequilibrium state remains a central challenge for quantum energy storage. Here, we introduce a reservoir-engineered dual-charger quantum battery architecture in which nonequilibrium dissipation is exploited as a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042209] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a reservoir-engineered dual-charger quantum battery that uses nonequilibrium dissipation to suppress coherent energy backflow and maintain extractable energy.
motivation: Quantum energy storage faces the challenge of stabilizing extractable energy against coherent backflow and dissipation, motivating architectures that turn nonequilibrium reservoir effects into a resource.
method: The authors introduce a dual-charger quantum battery architecture engineered via coupling to reservoirs, exploiting nonequilibrium dissipation rather than treating it only as loss.
result: The dissipation-engineered design is shown to suppress coherent energy backflow while maintaining a stable nonequilibrium state with extractable energy.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium reservoir engineering provides a viable route for improving the stability and performance of quantum batteries, connecting open-system dynamics with quantum thermodynamic functionality.

title: Optimal Quantum Feshbach Engines
authors: Aaron Wandhammer, Vincent Hardel, Paul-Antoine Hervieux, And Giovanni Manfredi
abstract:
Author(s): Aaron Wandhammer, Vincent Hardel, Paul-Antoine Hervieux, and Giovanni Manfredi

A trapped Bose–Einstein condensate is steered through fast, stable cycles by mapping its quantum dynamics onto an effective classical process, enabling systematic optimization of each stroke of the cycle. This approach yields robust quantum engines that operate efficiently in finite time.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L040201] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A trapped Bose-Einstein condensate driven through fast, stable cycles can be mapped onto an effective classical process, enabling systematic finite-time optimization of quantum Feshbach engines.
motivation: Quantum heat engines based on interacting BECs offer a platform for studying thermodynamics at the quantum scale, but achieving efficient operation in finite time (rather than in quasi-static, infinitely slow cycles) remains a central challenge.
method: The authors map the quantum dynamics of the driven condensate across each stroke of the Feshbach engine cycle onto an effective classical description, then use this mapping to systematically and stably optimize the timing and control of the individual strokes.
result: The optimized cycles yield robust quantum engines that maintain high efficiency and stability even when operated at finite speed, i.e., beyond the adiabatic limit.
conclusion: Mapping quantum engine dynamics to a tractable effective classical process provides a practical route to designing fast, stable, and efficient quantum thermodynamic machines based on ultracold atoms.

title: Non-Markovian Entropy Production Fluctuation Theorem Driven By A Time-dependent Electric Field
authors: K. S. Rodríguez-Vigil, M. A. Bastarrachea-Magnani, And J. I. Jiménez-Aquino
abstract:
Author(s): K. S. Rodríguez-Vigil, M. A. Bastarrachea-Magnani, and J. I. Jiménez-Aquino

Fluctuation theorems are key to understanding both fundamental and applied aspects of nonequilibrium thermodynamics of small systems. We study the non-Markovian entropy production fluctuation theorem for the diffusion process of charged particles in a gas inside a harmonic potential and under the ac…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044122] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives and analyzes a non-Markovian entropy production fluctuation theorem for charged particles diffusing in a harmonic potential under a time-dependent electric field.
motivation: Fluctuation theorems are central to nonequilibrium thermodynamics of small systems, but non-Markovian effects driven by time-dependent external fields remain important to characterize.
method: The authors study a stochastic diffusion process for charged particles in a gas confined by a harmonic potential and subjected to an ac electric field, formulating the entropy production and its fluctuation theorem in the non-Markovian regime.
result: A non-Markovian entropy production fluctuation theorem is obtained, capturing the role of memory effects and the time-dependent driving on the nonequilibrium statistics.
conclusion: The results extend fluctuation-theorem descriptions to non-Markovian diffusive systems under ac driving, relevant for classical stochastic thermodynamics of small nonequilibrium systems.

title: Spin-qubit Leapfrogging: Dynamics Of Shuttling Electrons On Top Of Another
authors: Nicklas Meineke And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Nicklas Meineke and Guido Burkard

Spin shuttling has crystalized as a powerful and promising tool for establishing intermediate-range connectivity in semiconductor spin-qubit devices. Although experimental demonstrations have performed exceptionally well on different materials platforms, the question of how to handle areas of low va…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043043] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of spin-qubit shuttling in which electrons move in a leapfrogging configuration on top of one another, analyzing the dynamics for semiconductor spin-qubit connectivity.
motivation: Spin shuttling is a promising route to intermediate-range connectivity in semiconductor spin-qubit devices, but reliable control when electrons pass in close proximity or on top of one another remains challenging.
method: The authors model the coherent dynamics of shuttled electrons in adjacent channels or quantum dots, using theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of the leapfrogging protocol.
result: The work characterizes how the leapfrogging dynamics depends on device parameters and identifies conditions under which faithful shuttling can be maintained.
conclusion: The results provide design guidance for scalable spin-qubit architectures that use shuttling-based connectivity and highlight operating regimes for robust shuttling.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, And Gauge Fields
authors: Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin Demarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, And Steven M. Girvin
abstract:
Author(s): Eleanor Crane, Kevin C. Smith, Teague Tomesh, Alec Eickbusch, John M. Martyn, Stefan Kühn, Lena Funcke, Michael Austin DeMarco, Isaac L. Chuang, Nathan Wiebe, Alexander Schuckert, and Steven M. Girvin

Researchers develop a hybrid qubit-boson quantum processor framework to simulate interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041008] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tags: quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories
tldr: The authors propose a hybrid oscillator-qubit (bosonic circuit QED) quantum processor architecture and develop digital-analog simulation protocols for interacting fermions, bosons, and lattice gauge fields on it.
motivation: Simulating lattice gauge theories and interacting many-body fermionic/bosonic systems is a central goal of quantum simulation but is resource-intensive on purely qubit-based processors, motivating hardware-native encodings that exploit the large Hilbert space of microwave cavity oscillators.
method: The work combines superconducting transmon qubits with microwave cavity modes (as in circuit QED) and constructs gate primitives and Trotterized/digital-analog circuits that map fermionic modes, bosonic modes, and gauge degrees of freedom onto the hybrid qubit-oscillator register, including error-mitigation and resource-estimation analyses.
result: The framework yields explicit circuit constructions and resource counts showing that hybrid oscillator-qubit processors can efficiently realize fermion-to-boson mappings (e.g. SNAP-type operations), bosonic hopping, and Abelian gauge-field dynamics with reduced overhead compared with qubit-only approaches.
conclusion: Hybrid oscillator-qubit hardware offers a promising, near-term route to simulating gauge theories and strongly correlated matter, and the proposed protocols provide a concrete roadmap for experiments on current cQED platforms.
keywords: quantum simulation of lattice gauge theories

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases Of Matter From Axiomatic Approaches
authors: Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, And Jong Yeon Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Tai-Hsuan Yang, Bowen Shi, and Jong Yeon Lee

A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an information-theoretic framework for classifying mixed-state topological phases in open quantum systems using phase invariants from information convex sets, memory capacity, and secret sharing.
motivation: Topological phases are well understood for pure states, but open quantum systems require a classification of mixed-state topological order that accounts for decoherence and information-theoretic properties.
method: The authors use axiomatic approaches to define mixed-state topological phases and introduce phase invariants based on information convex sets, quantum memory capacity, and secret-sharing capabilities.
result: The framework yields invariants that distinguish mixed-state topological phases and connects them to operational quantum-information tasks such as memory and secret sharing.
conclusion: This work provides a quantum-information foundation for mixed-state topological order and suggests new invariants for classifying phases of matter in open quantum systems.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality Of Scrooge Ensembles In Quantum Many-Body Systems
authors: Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Wai-Keong Mok, Tobias Haug, Wen Wei Ho, and John Preskill

Researchers introduce Scrooge
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041003] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces Scrooge ensembles to characterize how constrained quantum many-body systems can nevertheless generate universal randomness and deep thermalization.
motivation: Understanding how quantum many-body systems reach universal random states under physical constraints is central to quantum thermalization and the emergence of statistical mechanics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on Scrooge ensembles that quantifies constrained randomness and analyzes its universality in quantum many-body dynamics.
result: They show that Scrooge ensembles universally capture the onset of deep thermalization and universal randomness across constrained many-body systems.
conclusion: The work establishes Scrooge ensembles as a general tool for connecting constraints, randomness, and thermalization in quantum many-body physics.

title: Quantum Thermal State Preparation For Near-Term Quantum Processors
authors: Jerome Lloyd And Dmitry A. Abanin
abstract:
Author(s): Jerome Lloyd and Dmitry A. Abanin

Researchers develop an algorithm that prepares many-body quantum thermal states accurately by combining bath resetting and modulated coupling.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031053] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a near-term quantum algorithm for accurately preparing many-body thermal states by combining bath resetting with modulated coupling.
motivation: Preparing quantum thermal states is essential for simulating thermodynamics and equilibrium properties of many-body systems, but it is challenging on near-term quantum processors.
method: The algorithm uses repeated bath resetting together with modulated system-bath coupling to drive the quantum system toward its thermal Gibbs state.
result: The approach is reported to prepare many-body quantum thermal states accurately on near-term quantum hardware architectures.
conclusion: This provides a practical algorithmic route for quantum thermodynamics and thermal-state simulation on near-term devices.

title: Frequency- And Amplitude-Modulated Gates For Universal Quantum Control
authors: Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, And William D. Oliver
abstract:
Author(s): Qi Ding, Shoumik D. Chowdhury, Agustin Di Paolo, Réouven Assouly, Alan V. Oppenheim, Jeffrey A. Grover, and William D. Oliver

A new theoretical framework based on Floquet analysis enables quantum gate optimization using frequency and amplitude modulations, finding high fidelity and fast gates in superconducting circuits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033066] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a Floquet-analysis-based theoretical framework for optimizing universal quantum gates using frequency- and amplitude-modulated control in superconducting circuits.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity quantum gates are essential for superconducting quantum processors, and modulated driving offers a route to improve gate performance beyond simple pulse shaping.
method: The authors develop a Floquet-based optimization framework that treats frequency and amplitude modulation as control degrees of freedom and applies it to superconducting circuit gate design.
result: The framework identifies high-fidelity and fast gates, demonstrating the utility of combined frequency and amplitude modulation for universal quantum control.
conclusion: Floquet-engineered modulation provides a practical approach to enhance gate speed and fidelity in superconducting quantum hardware.

title: Readout-Induced Degradation Of Transmon Lifetimes: Interplay Of TLSs And Qubit Spectral Reshaping
authors: Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, And Oskar Painter
abstract:
Author(s): Ziwen Huang, Jimmy Shih-Chun Hung, Mouktik Raha, Ming-Han Chou, Harry Levine, Alex Retzker, Connor T. Hann, David Hover, Fernando G. S. L. Brandão, Aashish A. Clerk, Arbel Haim, and Oskar Painter

Experiment, theory, and simulations all agree to show that readout drive frequency is an important parameter to control and minimize readout-induced decoherence caused by coupling to two-level systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033059] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that readout drive frequency strongly controls readout-induced decoherence in transmon qubits due to coupling to two-level systems and qubit spectral reshaping.
motivation: Readout is essential for superconducting qubit operation, but its drive can degrade qubit lifetimes; identifying and controlling the microscopic decoherence mechanisms is important for improving coherence.
method: The authors combine experiment, theory, and simulations to analyze how readout drive frequency affects transmon coherence in the presence of TLS defects and spectral reshaping of the qubit.
result: They find agreement among experiment, theory, and simulation that the readout drive frequency is a key parameter for minimizing readout-induced decoherence caused by TLS coupling.
conclusion: Choosing and controlling the readout drive frequency can mitigate readout-induced lifetime degradation, providing a practical route to improved transmon coherence during measurement.

title: Analytical Blueprint For 99.999% Fidelity X-Gates On Present Superconducting Hardware Under Strong Driving
authors: José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, And Felix Motzoi
abstract:
Author(s): José Diogo Da Costa Jesus, Boxi Li, Yuan Gao, Rami Barends, Francisco Andrés Cárdenas-López, and Felix Motzoi

A new analytical pulse-shaping framework extends DRAG protocols to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit gates with fidelities exceeding 99.99%.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033040] Published Thu Aug 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an analytical pulse-shaping framework extending DRAG to suppress multiphoton leakage in strongly driven superconducting transmons, enabling ultrafast single-qubit X-gates with fidelities above 99.99%.
motivation: High-fidelity single-qubit gates on superconducting hardware are limited by leakage to higher transmon levels, especially under strong driving and ultrafast operation.
method: The authors develop an analytical extension of DRAG protocols tailored to strongly driven transmon qubits, designing pulse shapes that cancel multiphoton leakage channels.
result: The framework yields X-gate fidelities exceeding 99.99% (and approaching 99.999% in the title) on present superconducting hardware under strong driving.
conclusion: Analytical pulse shaping can substantially improve gate fidelity and speed in superconducting qubits by suppressing leakage, with direct relevance to hardware-level quantum control.

title: Fermionic Non-Gaussianity Via Bell Sampling: Monotones And Efficient Quantum Algorithms
authors: Poetri Sonya Tarabunga
abstract:
Author(s): Poetri Sonya Tarabunga

An experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity not only bounds state-preparation complexity but also proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033065] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an experimentally accessible measure of fermionic non-Gaussianity using Bell sampling and shows it bounds state-preparation complexity and certifies irreversibility of Gaussian conversions.
motivation: Fermionic non-Gaussianity is a key resource for quantum computation and simulation, but experimentally accessible measures and efficient certification tools are needed.
method: The author develops monotones for fermionic non-Gaussianity and designs Bell-sampling-based quantum algorithms to estimate them efficiently.
result: The proposed measure bounds state-preparation complexity and proves the irreversibility of exact Gaussian conversions under fermionic operations.
conclusion: Bell sampling provides a practical route to quantify and utilize fermionic non-Gaussianity as a quantum resource, with implications for state preparation and resource-theoretic limitations.

title: Geometric Power Capacity Of Coherent Ergotropy In Quantum Batteries
authors: Dong-Ping Xuan, Hua Nan, Zhi-Xi Wang, And Shao-Ming Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Ping Xuan, Hua Nan, Zhi-Xi Wang, and Shao-Ming Fei

We explore coherent ergotropy extraction in quantum batteries from a resource-geometric point of view. For an initial state [MATH], we quantify the coherent extraction process by the coherent ergotropy [MATH] and the coherent extraction distance [MATH] between the a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042211] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a resource-geometric framework for quantifying coherent ergotropy extraction and power capacity in quantum batteries.
motivation: Quantum batteries require precise thermodynamic characterizations of extractable work, especially the coherent component of ergotropy, to understand fundamental power limits.
method: The authors introduce coherent ergotropy and a coherent extraction distance between states, using resource-geometric ideas to define a geometric power capacity for coherent extraction processes.
result: They obtain geometric bounds/characterizations of coherent ergotropy extraction and relate the extraction distance to the battery's power capacity.
conclusion: The work provides an information-thermodynamic geometric perspective on coherent work extraction in quantum batteries, complementing standard ergotropy-based analyses.

title: Floquet Quantum Gates With Ion-enhanced Rydberg Blockade
authors: Ji-Yuan Zhang, Ji-Ze Han, Jian-Chun Shi, Zhi-Guo Huang, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:
Author(s): Ji-Yuan Zhang, Ji-Ze Han, Jian-Chun Shi, Zhi-Guo Huang, and Shi-Lei Su

Direct Rydberg-Rydberg interactions decay rapidly with distance, limiting blockade-based gates between spatially separated neutral-atom qubits. We study a hybrid architecture in which a trapped ion mediates an additional effective interaction between two Rydberg atoms in optical tweezers. Following …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042426] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid trapped-ion–Rydberg-atom architecture to enhance blockade-based Floquet quantum gates between spatially separated neutral-atom qubits.
motivation: Direct Rydberg-Rydberg interactions decay rapidly with distance, limiting blockade-based gates between distant neutral atoms in optical tweezers.
method: A trapped ion is used to mediate an additional effective interaction between two Rydberg atoms, enabling ion-enhanced Rydberg blockade and Floquet gate schemes.
result: The hybrid architecture yields enhanced effective blockade interactions and enables Floquet quantum gates between separated Rydberg-atom qubits.
conclusion: Ion-mediated interactions offer a promising route to extend Rydberg blockade gates beyond the short-range limitation of direct Rydberg-Rydberg coupling.

title: Quantum Error Correction In Adversarial Regimes
authors: Rahul Arvind, Nikhil Bansal, Dax Enshan Koh, Tobias Haug, And Kishor Bharti
abstract:
Author(s): Rahul Arvind, Nikhil Bansal, Dax Enshan Koh, Tobias Haug, and Kishor Bharti

In adversarial settings, where attackers can deliberately and strategically corrupt quantum data, standard quantum error correction reaches its limits. It can only correct up to half the code distance and must output a unique answer. Quantum list decoding offers a promising alternative. By allowing …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042433] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops quantum list-decoding approaches for quantum error correction in adversarial noise regimes beyond standard unique-decoding limits.
motivation: Standard quantum error correction can correct only up to half the code distance and must output a unique decoded state, which is insufficient when errors are deliberately adversarial.
method: It introduces and analyzes quantum list-decoding techniques that allow multiple candidate corrections, extending quantum error-correcting codes to adversarial settings.
result: The work shows that list decoding can overcome key limitations of standard quantum error correction under adversarial corruption, improving robustness beyond the unique-decoding threshold.
conclusion: Quantum list decoding provides a useful theoretical framework for protecting quantum information against strategic adversarial errors, with implications for quantum error correction and cryptographic settings.

title: Continuous-variable Dense Coding Under Realistic Nonideal Scenarios
authors: Mrinmoy Samanta, Ayan Patra, Rivu Gupta, And Aditi Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinmoy Samanta, Ayan Patra, Rivu Gupta, and Aditi Sen(De)

We analyze the continuous-variable (CV) dense coding protocol between a single sender and a single receiver that are affected by noise in the shared and encoded states, as well as when the decoding is imperfect. We present a formalism to derive the dense coding capacity of generic two-mode Gaussian …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042427] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives continuous-variable dense coding capacities for generic two-mode Gaussian states under realistic noise and imperfect decoding conditions.
motivation: Dense coding is a key entanglement-assisted quantum communication protocol, but realistic implementations suffer from noisy shared/encoded states and imperfect measurements.
method: The authors develop a formalism to compute dense coding capacity for generic two-mode Gaussian states, incorporating noise in the shared and encoded states as well as imperfect decoding.
result: They obtain capacity expressions and analyze how realistic nonidealities degrade the achievable dense coding advantage.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for assessing CV dense coding performance under practical conditions, bridging ideal theoretical capacities and experimental limitations.

title: Low-overhead Tailoring And Learning Of Noise In Graph States
authors: Guedong Park, Jinzhao Sun, And Hyunseok Jeong
abstract:
Author(s): Guedong Park, Jinzhao Sun, and Hyunseok Jeong

Graph and hypergraph states are important resource states for realizing universal quantum computation and diverse nonlocal physical phenomena. However, noise learning in such states is challenging due to their large entanglement and magic. This work establishes a low Clifford hierarchy circuit-based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042428] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a low-Clifford-hierarchy circuit-based approach for low-overhead noise tailoring and learning in graph and hypergraph states.
motivation: Graph and hypergraph states are key resource states for universal quantum computation and nonlocal phenomena, but their large entanglement and magic make noise learning difficult.
method: The authors introduce a circuit-based noise-tailoring and learning framework restricted to low Clifford hierarchy operations to keep overhead low.
result: The approach enables characterization and tailoring of noise in highly entangled, magic resource states with reduced circuit complexity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical route toward benchmarking and mitigating noise in graph-state-based quantum information processing.

title: Controlled-$Z$ Gates With Giant Atoms In Structured Waveguides
authors: Walter Rieck, Ariadna Soro, Anton Frisk Kockum, And Guangze Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Rieck, Ariadna Soro, Anton Frisk Kockum, and Guangze Chen

Giant atoms are quantum emitters coupled to waveguides at multiple, spatially separated points, enabling interference effects that fundamentally change their light-matter interactions. A notable consequence of the interference is the emergence of decoherence-free interaction (DFI), which allows cohe…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043719] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes controlled-Z gates using giant atoms in structured waveguides, exploiting decoherence-free interaction arising from multi-point emitter-waveguide coupling.
motivation: Giant atoms enable interference effects that modify light-matter interactions and can produce decoherence-free interactions, motivating their use for robust quantum gates.
method: The authors analyze giant atoms coupled at multiple spatially separated points to structured waveguides and design a controlled-Z gate protocol based on the resulting collective interaction.
result: The scheme achieves controlled-Z operation through waveguide-mediated giant-atom interactions, with decoherence-free conditions improving robustness against unwanted decay.
conclusion: Giant atoms in structured waveguides provide a promising platform for implementing high-fidelity two-qubit gates in waveguide QED architectures.

title: Maximum Confidence Channel Discrimination: Probe Design, Entanglement Assistance, And Sequential Measurement
authors: Jeremy Johnston And Xiaodong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy Johnston and Xiaodong Wang

In this work, we study maximum confidence measurement for quantum channel discrimination and develop optimization-based algorithms for designing both the probe state and measurement operators. We show that entanglement-assisted strategies with pure probe states and bounded reference dimensions suffi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042419] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops optimization-based algorithms for maximum-confidence quantum channel discrimination, jointly designing probe states and measurement operators including entanglement-assisted and sequential strategies.
motivation: Channel discrimination is a fundamental primitive in quantum information, yet designing optimal probes and measurements for maximum-confidence discrimination remains challenging; efficient, provably sufficient optimization formulations are needed.
method: The authors formulate maximum-confidence channel discrimination as an optimization problem over probe states and measurement operators, showing that entanglement-assisted strategies with pure probes and bounded reference dimensions suffice, and extending to sequential measurement schemes.
result: They derive optimization-based design algorithms and establish that pure entangled probes with bounded reference dimension are sufficient for optimal entanglement-assisted discrimination, while also providing sequential measurement approaches.
conclusion: The work provides a practical, optimization-driven framework for designing optimal discrimination strategies, clarifying the role of entanglement assistance and sequential measurements in channel discrimination.

title: Fock-space Fragmentation In Quenches Of Disordered Interacting Fermions
authors: Ishita Modak, Rajesh Narayanan, Ferdinand Evers, And Soumya Bera
abstract:
Author(s): Ishita Modak, Rajesh Narayanan, Ferdinand Evers, and Soumya Bera

Fock-space fragmentation, as it is currently investigated, primarily originates from specific kinematic constraints or emergent conservation laws in many-body systems with translation invariance. It leads to nonergodic dynamics and possible breakdown of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043030] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how Fock-space fragmentation in disordered interacting fermions leads to nonergodic quench dynamics and breakdown of the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis.
motivation: Fock-space fragmentation is usually discussed in translation-invariant systems with kinematic constraints or emergent conservation laws; the authors ask whether disorder can generate or modify fragmentation and its dynamical consequences.
method: They analyze quench dynamics of disordered interacting fermions, identifying fragmented Fock-space sectors and characterizing the resulting nonergodic behavior and its implications for thermalization.
result: Disorder-induced Fock-space fragmentation is shown to produce nonergodic dynamics and to obstruct eigenstate thermalization in the studied fermionic system.
conclusion: The work extends the phenomenon of Fock-space fragmentation beyond its usual translation-invariant settings and highlights disorder as a route to nonergodic quantum dynamics.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, And Energy Diffusion
authors: J. T. Chalker And Dominik Hahn
abstract:
Author(s): J. T. Chalker and Dominik Hahn

Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031076] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026.
tldr: A solvable many-body model shows that energy diffusion is the microscopic mechanism that fixes the form of spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.
motivation: Spectral correlations in chaotic many-body systems are usually described by random matrix theory, but the physical origin of the relevant Thouless-type energy scales and their connection to transport remained unclear.
method: The authors analyze an exactly solvable chaotic many-body model, computing spectral form factors and two-point correlations and relating them to hydrodynamic energy diffusion in the sense of a Thouless-time/energy argument.
result: They demonstrate that the characteristic correlation energy and time scales of the spectrum are quantitatively set by the energy diffusion constant, unifying dynamical transport with level statistics.
conclusion: Energy diffusion provides a physical, hydrodynamic foundation for spectral correlations in chaotic quantum matter, sharpening the link between quantum chaos diagnostics and thermalization.

title: Fractional Quantum Hall States Under Density Decoherence
authors: Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Zijian Wang, Ruihua Fan, Tianle Wang, Samuel J. Garratt, and Ehud Altman

Statistical mechanics mappings reveal that quantum information stored in the non-Abelian anyons of Moore-Read states resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas that stored in the Laughlin states has an infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031074] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows how quantum information encoded in fractional quantum Hall anyons survives density decoherence, with Moore-Read non-Abelian states being arbitrarily robust while Laughlin states are robust only above a critical filling factor.
motivation: Topological phases are promising for decoherence-resilient quantum information, but it is unclear how robust the encoded information is under realistic noise such as density dephasing.
