method: The authors use statistical-mechanics mappings to analyze fractional quantum Hall states under density decoherence and assess the resilience of the quantum information stored in their anyonic excitations.
result: Information in Moore-Read non-Abelian anyons resists arbitrary density dephasing, whereas Laughlin-state information has infinite robustness only above a critical filling factor.
conclusion: The robustness of topological quantum information under decoherence depends qualitatively on the fractional quantum Hall state and its filling factor, with implications for topological quantum memory.

title: General Quantum Circuit Framework For Extended Wigner’s Friend Scenarios: Logically And Causally Consistent Reasoning Without Absolute Measurement Events
authors: V. Vilasini And Mischa P. Woods
abstract:
Author(s): V. Vilasini and Mischa P. Woods

Researchers develop a quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner’s friend scenarios, resolving logical paradoxes by tracking Heisenberg cuts.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031062] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general quantum circuit framework for extended Wigner's friend scenarios that tracks Heisenberg cuts to enable logically and causally consistent reasoning without absolute measurement events.
motivation: Extended Wigner's friend scenarios raise apparent logical paradoxes about measurement, observers, and causal consistency in quantum theory, challenging standard assumptions about objective events.
method: The authors formulate extended Wigner's friend scenarios as quantum circuits with observers and measurements, representing different Heisenberg cuts and analyzing consistency conditions across them.
result: The framework resolves the paradoxes by avoiding absolute measurement events and providing a coherent logical and causal account of the different observer perspectives.
conclusion: This work clarifies foundational issues in quantum measurement and causal reasoning, offering a general circuit-based tool relevant to quantum information foundations.

title: Refinements Of The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis Under Local Rotational Invariance Via Free Probability
authors: Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Author(s): Elisa Vallini, Laura Foini, and Silvia Pappalardi

Using the mathematical language of free probability theory, researchers reveal how local rotational invariance structures matrix-element correlations, including their first subleading corrections.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043007] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses free probability theory to refine the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis by showing how local rotational invariance constrains matrix-element correlations, including first subleading corrections.
motivation: The eigenstate thermalization hypothesis is central to understanding thermalization and quantum chaos, but its detailed structure and corrections require sharper mathematical characterization, especially in the presence of symmetries.
method: The authors employ free probability theory to analyze matrix-element correlations under local rotational invariance and derive their leading and first subleading structure.
result: They reveal how local rotational invariance organizes matrix-element correlations and determine the first subleading corrections to the standard ETH form.
conclusion: These refinements provide a more precise formulation of ETH in rotationally invariant settings and clarify how symmetry and free-probabilistic structures constrain quantum chaotic matrix elements.

title: Hole Spin Resilient To Dipole-Induced Thermal Effects
authors: V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. de Franceschi, B. Martinez, And B. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): V. Champain, G. Boschetto, H. Niebojewski, B. Bertrand, L. Mauro, C. Haab, M. Bassi, V. Schmitt, X. Jehl, S. Zihlmann, R. Maurand, Y.-M. Niquet, C. B. Winkelmann, S. De Franceschi, B. Martinez, and B. Brun

A silicon hole spin unveils an electric origin of thermal frequency shifts and exhibits a magnetic-field sweet-spot immune to those, guiding the design of thermally robust semiconductor qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043005] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: A silicon hole spin qubit shows an electric-origin thermal frequency shift that can be suppressed at a magnetic-field sweet spot, enabling thermally robust semiconductor qubit design.
motivation: Semiconductor spin qubits suffer from thermal fluctuations that shift transition frequencies and degrade coherence, so understanding and mitigating thermal effects is important for scalable quantum hardware.
method: The authors characterize a silicon hole spin qubit and analyze the temperature dependence of its resonance frequency, identifying a dipole-induced electric mechanism and a magnetic-field operating point insensitive to thermal shifts.
result: They observe thermal frequency shifts of electric origin and demonstrate a magnetic-field sweet spot where the qubit frequency is immune to these fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings provide design guidance for thermally resilient hole-spin qubits and highlight sweet-spot operation as a route to robust semiconductor quantum processors.

title: Free Cumulants In Full Eigenstate Thermalization From Boundary Scrambling
authors: Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch, Gabriel O. Alves, Michael A. Rampp, and Pieter W. Claeys

The introduction of boundary scrambling as a solvable many-body quantum model yields an analytically tractable study of higher-order out-of-time-order correlation function dynamics and new insights into free probability and the emergence of random-matrix behavior.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043003] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a solvable boundary-scrambling model to analytically study higher-order out-of-time-order correlators and connect free cumulants to full eigenstate thermalization and random-matrix behavior.
motivation: Understanding the emergence of eigenstate thermalization and random-matrix statistics from scrambling dynamics is a central problem in many-body quantum chaos, especially beyond leading-order out-of-time-order correlators.
method: The authors use a boundary-scrambling many-body quantum model and free-probability techniques, specifically free cumulants, to compute higher-order out-of-time-order correlation functions analytically.
result: They obtain tractable dynamics for higher-order out-of-time-order correlators and show how free cumulants control the emergence of full eigenstate thermalization and random-matrix behavior in the model.
conclusion: The work provides an analytically solvable framework linking boundary scrambling, free probability, and eigenstate thermalization, offering new insight into higher-order quantum chaos indicators.

title: Quantum Simulation With Rydberg Ions In A Penning Trap
authors: Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, And Igor Lesanovsky
abstract:
Author(s): Wilson S. Martins, Markus Hennrich, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, and Igor Lesanovsky

Theoretical work tames the complicated dynamics of Rydberg ions in the high magnetic field of a Penning trap, showing large dipole-dipole interactions, which will enable quantum simulations in new regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033064] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical analysis shows that Rydberg ions in a Penning trap can exhibit strong dipole-dipole interactions and enable quantum simulation in new regimes.
motivation: Rydberg ions combine long-range interactions with trapped-ion control, but their behavior in the strong magnetic field of a Penning trap is complex and needs theoretical understanding.
method: The authors theoretically model the dynamics of Rydberg ions in a Penning trap, accounting for the high magnetic field and characterizing the resulting dipole-dipole interactions.
result: They find that large dipole-dipole interactions emerge, making the system suitable for quantum simulation in regimes not readily accessible with other platforms.
conclusion: Rydberg ions in Penning traps are a promising hybrid platform for quantum simulation, though the work is primarily a theoretical platform study rather than a core quantum-information or thermodynamics result.

title: In Situ Benchmarking Of Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits: Clifford Circuits
authors: Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Michael J. Gullans
abstract:
Author(s): Xiao Xiao, Dominik Hangleiter, Dolev Bluvstein, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Michael J. Gullans

Using only existing error syndrome data and no additional calibration circuits, it is possible to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033055] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an in situ benchmarking method for fault-tolerant quantum circuits using existing error syndrome data and Clifford circuits.
motivation: Verifying encoded quantum computations and benchmarking quantum hardware typically requires extra calibration circuits, which can be costly and disruptive.
method: The authors use only existing error syndrome data, without additional calibration circuits, to efficiently benchmark quantum hardware and verify encoded computations based on Clifford circuits.
result: The approach enables efficient in situ benchmarking and verification of fault-tolerant quantum circuits using syndrome data alone.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for assessing fault-tolerant quantum hardware and encoded computations without extra calibration overhead.

title: Dispersive Qubit Readout With Intrinsic Resonator Reset
authors: M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. Divincenzo, R. Barends, And P. A. Bushev
abstract:
Author(s): M. Jerger, F. Motzoi, Y. Gao, C. Dickel, L. Buchmann, F. A. Cárdenas-López, A. Bengtsson, G. Tancredi, C. W. Warren, J. Bylander, D. DiVincenzo, R. Barends, and P. A. Bushev

Researchers experimentally demonstrate a new method for large-bandwidth dispersive readout, with built-in resonator reset, providing potential applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033042] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates a large-bandwidth dispersive qubit readout scheme with intrinsic resonator reset for superconducting qubit architectures.
motivation: Fast, high-fidelity qubit readout with minimal resonator recovery time is important for superconducting quantum computing and quantum error correction.
method: The authors implement and characterize a dispersive readout protocol that incorporates built-in resonator reset, enabling large-bandwidth measurement while reducing the need for separate reset operations.
result: The experiment shows that the intrinsic-reset readout approach can achieve fast dispersive measurement with practical reset behavior, indicating suitability for repeated or syndrome-based measurements.
conclusion: This readout technique is a useful hardware-level advance for superconducting qubit control and may benefit quantum error correction protocols.

title: Holographic Duality Between Bulk Topological Order And Boundary Mixed-State Order
authors: Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, And Yizhi You
abstract:
Author(s): Tsung-Cheng Lu, Yu-Jie Liu, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, and Yizhi You

Mapping open quantum systems to higher-dimensional topological order provides a new framework for characterizing strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033041] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a holographic duality mapping bulk topological order to boundary mixed-state order, offering a framework for strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium quantum phases.
motivation: Open quantum systems require new theoretical tools to characterize mixed-state phases and symmetry-breaking patterns beyond equilibrium paradigms.
method: The authors develop a holographic bulk-boundary correspondence linking higher-dimensional topological order to boundary mixed-state order in open quantum systems.
result: The duality establishes a mapping between bulk topological order and boundary mixed-state order, enabling the characterization of strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and nonequilibrium phases.
conclusion: This holographic framework provides a new lens for classifying and understanding mixed-state quantum phases and their topological signatures.

title: Bistable Squeezing In A Multimode Circuit-quantum-acoustodynamics System
authors: Can Hong, Ke-Wen Xiao, And Wen-Yuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Can Hong, Ke-Wen Xiao, and Wen-Yuan Wang

Recent experiments in circuit quantum acoustodynamics (cQAD) have demonstrated on-chip multimode phononic interactions and single-mode phonon squeezing [von Lüpke et al.,
tldr: A theoretical study proposing bistable squeezing and squeezing redistribution in a multimode circuit quantum acoustodynamics platform.
motivation: Recent circuit quantum acoustodynamics experiments have demonstrated multimode phononic interactions and single-mode phonon squeezing, but bistable squeezing and the redistribution of squeezing among multiple mechanical modes remain less explored.
method: The authors likely model a superconducting-circuit-based acoustodynamic system with multiple mechanical modes and nonlinear phonon interactions, then analyze quadrature squeezing, stability, and mode-to-mode redistribution via effective Hamiltonians or master-equation methods.
result: The paper predicts regimes of bistable phonon squeezing and shows how squeezing can be redistributed across mechanical modes by tuning system parameters.
conclusion: Multimode circuit quantum acoustodynamics is a promising platform for generating and controlling nonclassical phonon states, with potential relevance for hybrid quantum information processing and phononic quantum technologies.

title: Phase-preserving Steady-state Operations Beyond Lindblad Master Equations
authors: Man Yin Cheung, Mona Berciu, And Kyle Monkman
abstract:
Author(s): Man Yin Cheung, Mona Berciu, and Kyle Monkman

We consider a class of nonunitary operations that is naturally implemented via a combination of projective measurement and unitary operators. We implement these operations without using measurements by coupling the system to an infinite set of ancilla states and time-evolving with a single time-inde…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042420] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a way to implement phase-preserving nonunitary steady-state operations without measurements by coupling the system to an infinite ancilla set and evolving under a time-independent Hamiltonian.
motivation: Nonunitary operations are usually implemented via projective measurements plus unitaries, but such measurement-based implementations may be undesirable or difficult, motivating alternative Hamiltonian-only constructions beyond standard Lindblad master equations.
method: The authors consider a class of phase-preserving nonunitary operations and replace the measurement step by coupling the system to an infinite set of ancilla states, followed by time evolution under a single time-independent Hamiltonian.
result: They show that this ancilla-coupling approach can realize the desired steady-state operations without measurements and goes beyond the usual Lindblad master equation framework.
conclusion: The work provides a Hamiltonian-based route to phase-preserving nonunitary quantum operations, expanding the set of physically implementable steady-state transformations.

title: Phase Transitions In Computation Time Of Brownian Circuits
authors: Kota Okajima And Koji Hukushima
abstract:
Author(s): Kota Okajima and Koji Hukushima

Brownian circuits perform computations using stochastic transitions driven by thermal fluctuations. While the energetic costs of such fluctuation-driven computation have been extensively studied within stochastic thermodynamics, much less is known about its computational complexity, in particular, h…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043059] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies Brownian circuits, which compute via thermally driven stochastic transitions, and identifies phase transitions in their computation time, linking stochastic thermodynamics to computational complexity.
motivation: Energetic costs of fluctuation-driven computation are well studied in stochastic thermodynamics, but the computational-complexity and time-complexity aspects of Brownian circuits remain less understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic dynamics of Brownian circuits, likely using tools from stochastic thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, to characterize computation time and its transitions.
result: They find phase transitions in the computation time of Brownian circuits, revealing sharp changes in computational behavior as system parameters vary.
conclusion: The work connects thermal-fluctuation-driven computation with complexity phase transitions, suggesting that stochastic thermodynamic descriptions can capture computation-time constraints and transitions in Brownian circuits.

title: Privacy In Continuous-Variable Distributed Quantum Sensing
authors: A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, And Ulrik L. Andersen
abstract:
Author(s): A. de Oliveira Junior, Anton L. Andersen, Benjamin Lundgren Larsen, Sean William Moore, Damian Markham, Masahiro Takeoka, Jonatan Bohr Brask, and Ulrik L. Andersen

The feasibility of privately estimating continuous-variable quantum parameters in network scenarios is investigated through achievable protocols and no-go results.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033036] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies whether continuous-variable quantum parameters can be estimated privately in distributed network scenarios, establishing achievable protocols and no-go results.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced precision across networked parties, but the privacy of the underlying parameter estimation in such multi-party settings is not well understood.
method: The authors formulate private continuous-variable parameter estimation in a network scenario and analyze it via achievable protocols and information-theoretic no-go arguments.
result: They identify conditions under which private distributed estimation is feasible and prove limitations showing when privacy cannot be guaranteed.
conclusion: Privacy imposes fundamental constraints on distributed continuous-variable quantum sensing, with achievable protocols delineating what is possible in networked estimation tasks.

title: Quantum Battery Optimized By Parametric Amplification
authors: Fang-Mei Yang, Jun-Hong An, And Fu-Quan Dou
abstract:
Author(s): Fang-Mei Yang, Jun-Hong An, and Fu-Quan Dou

The parametric amplification enabled by two-photon driving constitutes a versatile platform for advanced quantum technologies. We present an optimized scheme for implementing quantum batteries (QBs) based on a superconducting circuit system, where a two-photon-driven LC resonator serves as the charg…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042616] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an optimized quantum battery scheme based on parametric amplification in a two-photon-driven superconducting LC resonator.
motivation: Quantum batteries require efficient charging mechanisms, and parametric amplification provides a controllable platform for enhancing energy transfer at the quantum scale.
method: The authors design a superconducting circuit in which a two-photon-driven LC resonator acts as the charger for a quantum battery, and they optimize the charging protocol.
result: The optimized scheme is expected to improve quantum battery charging performance within a superconducting-circuit platform.
conclusion: Parametric amplification via two-photon driving offers a promising route for implementing and optimizing quantum batteries.

title: Quantum Trajectories For Time-binned Data And Their Closeness To Fully Conditioned Quantum Trajectories
authors: Nattaphong Wonglakhon, Areeya Chantasri, And Howard M. Wiseman
abstract:
Author(s): Nattaphong Wonglakhon, Areeya Chantasri, and Howard M. Wiseman

Quantum trajectories are dynamical equations for quantum states conditioned on the results of a time-continuous measurement, such as a continuous-in-time current [MATH]. Recently, there has been renewed interest in finite-interval dynamical maps for quantum trajectories, where the m…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042415] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops quantum trajectory equations for time-binned measurement data and assesses how closely they approximate fully conditioned quantum trajectories.
motivation: Continuous quantum measurements are often recorded in finite time bins, so finite-interval dynamical maps are needed to describe the conditioned quantum state accurately.
method: The authors formulate quantum trajectories conditioned on time-binned data and compare them with fully conditioned trajectories obtained from continuous measurement records.
result: They characterize the conditions under which time-binned quantum trajectories remain close to fully conditioned ones, quantifying the accuracy of finite-interval maps.
conclusion: Time-binned trajectory formulations can provide a useful and controlled approximation to fully conditioned quantum dynamics in continuously monitored open quantum systems.

title: Imaginarity-assisted Minimum Error Discrimination
authors: Zhihua Guo, Yadi Qiao, Huaixin Cao, And Tsung-Lin Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Zhihua Guo, Yadi Qiao, Huaixin Cao, and Tsung-Lin Lee

Minimum error discrimination is a general approach for quantum-state discrimination. This work establishes a connection between quantum imaginarity and minimum error discrimination, investigating the conditions under which auxiliary quantum states can enhance the maximum average success probability …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042418] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper connects quantum imaginarity to minimum-error state discrimination and identifies when auxiliary quantum states can improve the maximum average success probability.
motivation: Minimum-error discrimination is a central task in quantum information, and understanding which quantum resources can enhance discrimination performance is operationally important.
method: The authors establish a connection between quantum imaginarity and minimum-error discrimination, then analyze conditions under which auxiliary quantum states enhance the maximum average success probability.
result: They show that imaginarity-related properties determine whether auxiliary states provide an advantage in minimum-error discrimination.
conclusion: Imaginarity acts as an operational resource for minimum-error discrimination, yielding criteria for assisted discrimination advantages.

title: Charge Transport Capacity As A Probe Of Resonances In Models Of Many-body Localization
authors: Jessica K. Jiang, Federica M. Surace, And Olexei I. Motrunich
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica K. Jiang, Federica M. Surace, and Olexei I. Motrunich

Many-body localization (MBL) breaks the standard paradigm of quantum thermalization and has evaded a complete understanding due to mysterious finite-size effects in numerics. Here, by introducing and calculating the charge transport capacity in MBL systems, the authors connect these finite-sized effects to increasingly probable larger many-body resonances with increasing system sizes, occurring even at very strong disorder. A perturbative model explains the physics of these resonances and reconciles these resonances with the possibility of asymptotically stable MBL.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194203] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces charge transport capacity as a probe of many-body resonances that explain finite-size effects in models of many-body localization.
motivation: Many-body localization challenges standard quantum thermalization, but its numerical study is plagued by mysterious finite-size effects and the possibility of asymptotically stable MBL remains debated.
method: The authors define and calculate the charge transport capacity in MBL systems and support the numerical findings with a perturbative model describing many-body resonances.
result: They connect finite-size effects to increasingly probable larger many-body resonances at strong disorder and show how these resonances can be reconciled with asymptotically stable MBL.
conclusion: Charge transport capacity provides a useful diagnostic for resonances in MBL systems and helps clarify the finite-size physics underlying the MBL debate.

title: Mixed-State Phases From Local Reversibility
authors: Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, And Timothy H. Hsieh
abstract:
Author(s): Shengqi Sang, Leonardo A. Lessa, Roger S. K. Mong, Tarun Grover, Chong Wang, and Timothy H. Hsieh

Researchers establish a framework using local reversibility to correctly classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041014] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a local-reversibility framework to classify phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems.
motivation: Standard classifications of quantum phases are challenged by decoherence and noise, so a framework is needed to characterize mixed-state phases in open quantum systems.
method: The authors use local reversibility, likely via equivalence under local reversible quantum channels or finite-depth local operations, to define and distinguish mixed-state phases.
result: The framework correctly classifies phases of matter in open and noisy quantum systems, providing a robust mixed-state phase classification.
conclusion: Local reversibility offers a principled way to understand and classify quantum phases beyond pure-state and closed-system settings.

title: Emergence Of Classical Stochasticity
authors: Xuan Du Trinh, Ismaël Septembre, And Hai-Chau Nguyen
abstract:
Author(s): Xuan Du Trinh, Ismaël Septembre, and Hai-Chau Nguyen

We examine the emergence of classical stochasticity for a quantum system governed by a Pauli-type master equation. It is well known that while such equations describe the evolution of probabilities, they do not automatically justify reasoning based on the assumption that the system exists in a defin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042207] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes when a quantum system governed by a Pauli-type master equation admits a genuinely classical stochastic description.
motivation: Pauli-type master equations describe probability evolution, but this alone does not justify treating the system as being in a definite classical state; the authors examine the emergence of classical stochasticity.
method: The authors study a quantum system under a Pauli-type master equation and analyze the conditions under which its probabilistic dynamics can be interpreted as a classical stochastic process.
result: The analysis identifies conditions and limitations for the emergence of classical stochastic behavior from the quantum master-equation description.
conclusion: Classical stochastic reasoning is not automatically justified by Pauli-type dynamics and requires specific conditions for a definite-state interpretation.

title: Variational Formulation Of Stochastic Thermodynamics: Spatially Extended Systems
authors: Héctor Vaquero Del Pino, François Gay-Balmaz, Hiroaki Yoshimura, And Lock Yue Chew
abstract:
Author(s): Héctor Vaquero del Pino, François Gay-Balmaz, Hiroaki Yoshimura, and Lock Yue Chew

Stochastic field theories are often constructed phenomenologically, without a systematic assessment of thermodynamic consistency or local detailed balance. This may hinder a physical description of irreversibility at the field-theoretic level beyond the standard statistical formulation of stochastic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044125] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a variational, Lagrangian formulation of stochastic thermodynamics for spatially extended (field-theoretic) systems, providing a systematic way to enforce thermodynamic consistency and local detailed balance rather than constructing stochastic field theories phenomenologically.
motivation: Stochastic field theories are typically built on phenomenological grounds, so thermodynamic consistency and local detailed balance are not guaranteed, which obscures a physically sound description of irreversibility at the field level.
method: Using a variational/Lagrangian framework (in the spirit of stochastic geometric mechanics), the authors derive stochastic field equations together with their thermodynamic structure, including fluctuation-dissipation relations and entropy production for continuum systems.
result: The formulation yields thermodynamically consistent stochastic field dynamics with explicit local detailed balance conditions, giving a systematic route to identifying irreversibility and entropy production in spatially extended stochastic systems.
conclusion: Variational principles can serve as a rigorous foundation for stochastic thermodynamics of continuum systems, extending standard stochastic thermodynamics beyond finite-dimensional settings.

title: Collective Strong Coupling Of Thermal Atoms To Integrated Microring Resonators
authors: Xiaoyu Cheng, Benyamin Shnirman, Alexandra Köpf, Guangcanlan Yang, Hong X. Tang, Hadiseh Alaeian, Tilman Pfau, And Robert Löw
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoyu Cheng, Benyamin Shnirman, Alexandra Köpf, Guangcanlan Yang, Hong X. Tang, Hadiseh Alaeian, Tilman Pfau, and Robert Löw

Strong coupling between atomic ensembles and high-quality optical cavities enables collective and nonlinear phenomena that are central to cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED). Many experiments have been performed on this topic, with most of them focusing on cold atoms. Here, we experimentally demon…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043063] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates collective strong coupling between thermal atomic ensembles and integrated microring resonators.
motivation: Strong coupling between atomic ensembles and high-quality optical cavities is central to cavity QED, but most experiments use cold atoms; extending this to thermal atoms and chip-integrated cavities could enable more practical hybrid quantum platforms.
method: The authors couple thermal atoms to an integrated high-Q microring resonator and characterize the system through optical transmission/spectroscopy to observe collective strong coupling.
result: Collective strong coupling is achieved with thermal atoms and an integrated microring resonator, demonstrating cavity-QED behavior without the need for cold-atom apparatus.
conclusion: Integrated microring resonators are shown to be a viable platform for collective strong coupling with thermal atomic ensembles, with potential for scalable hybrid quantum systems and on-chip cavity QED.

title: Exact Nonequilibrium Steady States Of Boundary-driven Circuit With Xyz Gates
authors: Xin Zhang, Tomaž Prosen, And Vladislav Popkov
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Zhang, Tomaž Prosen, and Vladislav Popkov

We obtain the exact many-body density operator of a boundary-driven XXZ quantum circuit via a spatially inhomogeneous matrix product ansatz. The ansatz has formally infinite bond dimension and generalizes authors’ previous construction [Popkov and Prosen,
tldr: The paper constructs exact nonequilibrium steady states for a boundary-driven XXZ quantum circuit using a spatially inhomogeneous matrix product ansatz with formally infinite bond dimension.
motivation: Boundary-driven quantum circuits provide controlled models of open quantum many-body systems, but exact nonequilibrium steady states are rare and technically challenging to obtain.
method: The authors generalize a previous matrix product ansatz construction to the boundary-driven XXZ circuit with XYZ gates, allowing a spatially inhomogeneous ansatz of formally infinite bond dimension.
result: They obtain the exact many-body density operator of the nonequilibrium steady state for this boundary-driven circuit.
conclusion: The work extends exact solvability of boundary-driven open quantum circuits and provides a rare analytical handle on their nonequilibrium steady states.

title: Information-Theoretic Principle Of Emergent 1-Form Symmetries
authors: Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Jie Liu, Wen-Tao Xu, Frank Pollmann, and Michael Knap

Viewing emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction(QEC) makes them detectable with QEC decoders, providing efficient protocols for revealing emergent symmetry structure and probing phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043006] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an information-theoretic framework that uses quantum error correction decoders to detect emergent 1-form symmetries and probe phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Emergent 1-form symmetries are important for understanding topological order and phase structure, but detecting them efficiently in quantum many-body systems remains challenging.
method: The authors interpret emergent 1-form symmetries through the lens of quantum error correction, enabling detection via QEC decoders and efficient protocols.
result: This approach reveals emergent symmetry structure and provides efficient protocols for probing phase transitions in quantum many-body systems.
conclusion: Connecting emergent 1-form symmetries to QEC yields practical detection tools and deepens the information-theoretic understanding of many-body phases.

title: Complexity Of Quantum Trajectories
authors: Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, And Rosario Fazio
abstract:
Author(s): Luca Lumia, Emanuele Tirrito, Mario Collura, Fabian H. L. Essler, and Rosario Fazio

An unsupervised, data-driven framework based on the intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe for detecting integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems beyond the transient regime, while new results on autonomous chaos are discussed.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033049] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces an unsupervised, data-driven intrinsic-dimension framework to detect integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems via quantum trajectories beyond the transient regime.
motivation: Probing integrability and ergodicity breaking in open quantum systems is challenging because transient dynamics and environmental effects can obscure signatures of quantum chaos and thermalization.
method: The authors analyze quantum trajectories of open quantum systems and use the intrinsic dimension as a data-driven unsupervised measure to characterize their complexity, applying it to detect integrability and ergodicity breaking and to study autonomous chaos.
result: The intrinsic dimension of quantum trajectories provides a robust probe of integrability and ergodicity breaking beyond transients, and reveals new features of autonomous chaos in the considered open-system dynamics.
conclusion: The framework offers a practical, data-driven tool for characterizing complexity and chaotic behavior in open quantum systems, with potential use in distinguishing integrable, ergodic, and non-ergodic regimes.

title: Exponentially Accurate Open Quantum Simulation Via Randomized Dissipation With Minimal Ancilla
authors: Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, And Naoki Yamamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Jumpei Kato, Kaito Wada, Kosuke Ito, and Naoki Yamamoto

Exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems is made viable for early fault-tolerant devices via a random compilation method requiring a minimal number of ancilla qubits.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033046] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a randomized dissipation method for exponentially accurate simulation of open quantum systems on early fault-tolerant devices using minimal ancilla qubits.
motivation: Simulating open quantum systems accurately is resource-intensive, especially on near-term fault-tolerant hardware where ancilla qubits are limited.
method: The authors use a random compilation approach to implement dissipative dynamics, reducing ancilla requirements while maintaining exponential accuracy.
result: The method enables exponentially accurate open quantum system simulation with a minimal number of ancilla qubits, making it viable for early fault-tolerant devices.
conclusion: This work provides a resource-efficient route to simulating open quantum dynamics, broadening the applicability of early fault-tolerant quantum processors.

title: Microwave Spectroscopy Of Few-Carrier States In Bilayer Graphene Quantum Dots
authors: Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, And Klaus Ensslin
abstract:
Author(s): Max J. Ruckriegel, Christoph Adam, Rebecca Bolt, Chuyao Tong, David Kealhofer, Artem O. Denisov, Mohsen Bahrami Panah, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Thomas Ihn, and Klaus Ensslin

Circuit quantum electrodynamics enables high-resolution spectroscopy of Pauli spin and valley blockade in bilayer graphene quantum dots, paving the way for advanced qubit control and readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033037] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: Microwave cavity spectroscopy resolves Pauli spin and valley blockade in few-carrier bilayer graphene quantum dots, establishing graphene dots as a viable circuit-QED qubit platform.
motivation: Bilayer graphene quantum dots host spin and valley degrees of freedom that could serve as qubits, but their few-carrier regime and the resulting blockade physics have not been characterized with the high resolution needed for qubit control and readout.
method: The authors embed bilayer graphene quantum dots in a microwave resonator and perform circuit-QED dispersive spectroscopy on devices occupied by only a few charge carriers, extracting the excitation spectra associated with spin and valley blockade.
result: High-resolution microwave spectroscopy reveals resolved Pauli spin and valley blockade features in the few-carrier regime, quantifying the level structure and providing the parameters needed for coherent manipulation and readout.
conclusion: Circuit QED spectroscopy demonstrates that bilayer graphene quantum dots are a promising hybrid platform for spin- and valley-based qubits coupled to superconducting resonators, motivating future coherent control experiments.

title: Long-time Exponential Decompositions Of non-Markovian Gaussian Baths
authors: Zhen Huang, Zhiyan Ding, Ke Wang, Jason Kaye, Xiantao Li, And Lin Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen Huang, Zhiyan Ding, Ke Wang, Jason Kaye, Xiantao Li, and Lin Lin

Gaussian baths are widely used to model non-Markovian environments, yet the cost of accurate simulation at long times remains poorly understood, especially when spectral densities exhibit nonanalytic behavior as in a range of realistic models. We rigorously bound the complexity of representing bath …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043053] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes rigorous complexity bounds for exponentially decomposing non-Markovian Gaussian baths to enable accurate long-time simulation.
motivation: Gaussian baths are widely used to model non-Markovian environments, but the cost of accurately simulating them at long times is poorly understood, especially for spectral densities with nonanalytic behavior.
method: The authors derive rigorous bounds on the complexity of representing bath correlation functions via exponential decompositions and analyze long-time simulation accuracy for non-Markovian Gaussian baths.
result: They provide complexity bounds showing how the representation cost scales, including for realistic spectral densities with nonanalytic features, and clarify the requirements for accurate long-time simulation.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding and practical simulation of non-Markovian open quantum systems by giving rigorous guarantees for exponential bath decompositions.

title: Universality And Weak-ergodicity Breaking In Quantum Quenches
authors: Guido Giachetti, Andrea Solfanelli, And Nicolò Defenu
abstract:
Author(s): Guido Giachetti, Andrea Solfanelli, and Nicolò Defenu

Understanding equilibration and universality after sudden quantum quenches remains a central challenge in isolated many-body systems. Persistent oscillations and anomalous scaling reported in lattice models appear to challenge the standard picture based on integrability and quantum-to-classical corr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043026] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a universality-based framework for equilibration after sudden quantum quenches in isolated many-body systems, explaining persistent oscillations and anomalous scaling through weak ergodicity breaking.
motivation: Standard pictures of post-quench equilibration based on integrability and quantum-to-classical correspondence fail to account for persistent oscillations and anomalous scaling observed in lattice models, motivating a more general universality-based description.
method: The authors analyze quench dynamics in isolated many-body systems, presumably within a field-theoretic / renormalization-group framework, classifying deviations from thermal equilibration in terms of weak ergodicity breaking and universality classes.
result: They identify universal behavior governing post-quench relaxation and show that weak ergodicity breaking, rather than integrability alone, can produce the reported persistent oscillations and anomalous dynamical scaling.
conclusion: Universality and weak ergodicity breaking provide a unified lens for understanding non-thermalizing quench dynamics, refining the standard integrability-based picture of equilibration.

title: Stability, Degeneracy, And Scalability Of A 600-Site Cavity Array Microscope
authors: Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, And Jonathan Simon
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Soper, Danial Shadmany, Adam L. Shaw, Lukas Palm, David I. Schuster, and Jonathan Simon

A scalable cavity array microscope architecture is presented, featuring over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, providing opportunities for quantum networking and sensing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041009] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a scalable cavity array microscope with over 600 independent optical cavities for parallelized light-matter interactions, aimed at quantum networking and sensing applications.
motivation: Large-scale, individually addressable cavity arrays are needed to scale up light-matter interfaces for quantum information platforms, but maintaining stability and uniformity across many cavities is challenging.
method: The authors design and characterize a cavity array microscope architecture containing more than 600 independent optical cavities, assessing its stability, degeneracy, and scalability for parallel operation.
result: The platform demonstrates stable operation and scalable architecture across the cavity array, enabling parallelized light-matter interactions and providing a foundation for quantum networking and sensing applications.
conclusion: This cavity array microscope offers a practical route toward large-scale hybrid quantum optical platforms, with potential impact on networked quantum technologies and sensing.

title: Theory Of Out-of-Time-Ordered Transport
authors: Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, And Luca V. Delacrétaz
abstract:
Author(s): Ruchira Mishra, Jiaozi Wang, Silvia Pappalardi, and Luca V. Delacrétaz

Researchers establish an effective field theory capturing late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041010] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops an effective field theory for late-time out-of-time-order correlators to uncover hidden transport parameters.
motivation: Out-of-time-order correlators are key diagnostics of quantum chaos and scrambling, but their late-time behavior and connection to transport are not fully captured by existing frameworks.
method: The authors construct an effective field theory describing late-time out-of-time-order correlator dynamics in many-body systems and relate its parameters to transport properties.
result: They show that late-time OTOC behavior encodes transport parameters that may be hidden from conventional probes.
conclusion: This provides a systematic framework linking quantum chaos diagnostics to transport in complex quantum systems.

title: Experimentally Accessible Measurement Of Irreversibility In Stochastic Systems By Categorizing Single-Molecule Displacements
authors: Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, And Stefano Bo
abstract:
Author(s): Alvaro Lanza, Inés Martínez-Martín, Rafael Tapia-Rojo, and Stefano Bo

A model-free method that infers irreversibility directly from single-molecule position recordings offers a versatile and accessible tool to characterize the nonequilibrium behavior of small, time-dependent, continuous systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031052] Published Wed Aug 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a model-free method to infer irreversibility in stochastic systems directly from single-molecule position recordings.
motivation: Characterizing nonequilibrium behavior in small, time-dependent continuous systems often requires model assumptions that are difficult to justify experimentally.
method: The authors categorize single-molecule displacements to estimate irreversibility without relying on a specific underlying dynamical model.
result: The approach provides an experimentally accessible way to detect and quantify nonequilibrium behavior from recorded trajectories.
conclusion: This offers a versatile tool for studying irreversibility in stochastic systems, with relevance to stochastic thermodynamics and single-molecule experiments.

title: Universal Sample Complexity Bounds In Quantum Learning Theory Via Fisher Information Matrix
authors: Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, And Liang Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Hyukgun Kwon, Seok Hyung Lie, and Liang Jiang

A framework shows that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033063] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes universal sample-complexity bounds for general quantum learning tasks using the inverse Fisher information matrix as the governing quantity.
motivation: Quantum learning theory lacks general, platform-independent bounds on how many samples are needed for estimation and learning tasks. The authors aim to provide a unified information-theoretic framework for such bounds.
method: They formulate quantum learning in terms of parameter estimation and derive sample-complexity bounds from the quantum Fisher information matrix, connecting the inverse Fisher information to the required number of samples.
result: The main result shows that the sample complexity of general quantum learning is governed by the inverse Fisher information matrix, yielding universal bounds that apply across different quantum learning settings.
conclusion: Fisher-information-based analysis provides a general and unifying route to sample-complexity bounds in quantum learning theory, with implications for quantum estimation and learning protocols.

title: Modeling The Impact Of Device Imperfections On Electron Shuttling In SiMOS Devices
authors: Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, And Andrew J. Fisher
abstract:
Author(s): Jack J. Turner, Christian W. Binder, Guido Burkard, and Andrew J. Fisher

Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS devices are presented, identifying operating regimes resilient to common device imperfections and charge defects.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033054] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: Three-dimensional simulations of electron shuttling in realistic SiMOS (silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor) devices identify operating regimes that are robust against common device imperfections and charge defects.
motivation: Electron shuttling is a key enabling technique for scaling silicon spin-qubit processors, but realistic SiMOS devices contain disorder, interface roughness, and charge traps that can degrade coherent transport of electrons between quantum dots.
method: The authors perform three-dimensional electrostatic and transport simulations of a SiMOS shuttling channel, incorporating device imperfections such as gate misalignment, oxide thickness variation, and charged defect sites, and map out the resulting potential landscapes and shuttling fidelity.
result: The simulations reveal specific parameter regimes (gate voltage sequences and device geometries) in which electron shuttling remains resilient to the modeled imperfections and charge defects, while other regimes show failure modes such as trapping or loss.
conclusion: The work provides practical design guidance for SiMOS-based shuttling architectures, indicating which operating regimes should be targeted to achieve robust, fault-tolerant electron transport in scaled silicon spin-qubit devices.

title: Magnetic Domains Stabilized By Symmetry-Protected Zero Modes
authors: Pavel Kos, Dominik S. Wild, And Kristian Knakkergaard Nielsen
abstract:
Author(s): Pavel Kos, Dominik S. Wild, and Kristian Knakkergaard Nielsen

Understanding mechanisms for the breakdown of thermalization in closed quantum systems is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. We demonstrate strong nonergodic behavior in the XX model on coupled chains, where domain-wall initial states retain an inhomogeneous magnetization profile for ar…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160402] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors show that domain-wall initial states in the XX model on coupled chains exhibit strong nonergodic behavior, with magnetization domains stabilized by symmetry-protected zero modes.
motivation: Understanding mechanisms by which closed quantum systems fail to thermalize is a central problem in quantum many-body physics, and identifying robust nonergodic behavior is key to this goal.
method: They analyze the XX model on coupled chains starting from domain-wall initial states, using symmetry-protected zero modes to explain the persistent inhomogeneous magnetization profile.
result: Domain-wall initial states retain an inhomogeneous magnetization profile for long times, demonstrating strong nonergodic behavior tied to the presence of symmetry-protected zero modes.
conclusion: Symmetry-protected zero modes provide a mechanism for stabilizing magnetic domains, offering a route to nonergodic dynamics in constrained quantum many-body systems.

title: Source Temporal Imperfections In Measurement-device-independent Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Zhi-Jian Hu, Guan-Jie Fan-Yuan, Wei-Xin Xie, Shuang Wang, Wei Chen, Zhen-Qiang Yin, Fang-Xiang Wang, De-Yong He, Guang-Can Guo, And Zheng-Fu Han
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Jian Hu, Guan-Jie Fan-Yuan, Wei-Xin Xie, Shuang Wang, Wei Chen, Zhen-Qiang Yin, Fang-Xiang Wang, De-Yong He, Guang-Can Guo, and Zheng-Fu Han

In high-speed quantum key distribution systems, the repetition rate is a critical factor limiting system efficiency. In the implementation of the measurement-device-independent quantum key distribution protocol based on two-photon interference, inherent temporal imperfections can significantly impac…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042435] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how inherent temporal imperfections in high-speed pulsing sources (e.g., timing jitter, pulse-width mismatch, and frequency drift) degrade two-photon interference and hence the secret-key rate of measurement-device-independent QKD.
motivation: At high repetition rates, the repetition rate limits system efficiency, but source temporal imperfections that break indistinguishability of the two photons at the Bell-state measurement are typically ignored or only crudely modeled, so their quantitative impact on MDI-QKD performance and security is unclear.
method: The authors build a model of source temporal imperfections — timing jitter, pulse broadening, and spectral/temporal mismatch between the two legitimate senders — and propagate these into the Hong-Ou-Mandel visibility of the two-photon interference, then into the MDI-QKD gain and quantum bit-error-rate parameters used in finite-key/decoy-state rate estimation.
result: They quantify the dependence of interference visibility (and consequently the achievable key rate and secure distance) on the magnitude of the temporal imperfections and identify the tolerances required at high repetition rates.
conclusion: Source temporal imperfections impose stringent requirements on high-speed MDI-QKD implementations; the derived error model provides practical design guidelines and can be incorporated into security analyses of realistic systems.

title: From Coupled ${\mathbb{Z}}_{3}$ Rabi Models To The ${\mathbb{Z}}_{3}$ Potts Model
authors: Anatoliy I. Lotkov, Valerii K. Kozin, Denis V. Kurlov, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Anatoliy I. Lotkov, Valerii K. Kozin, Denis V. Kurlov, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

We study a [MATH]-symmetric Rabi model that describes a three-level system coupled to two bosonic modes. We derive a mapping of the two-mode [MATH] Rabi model onto a qubit-boson ring. This mapping allows us to formulate a realistic implementation of the [MATH] Rab…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043046] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies a Z3-symmetric Rabi model with a three-level system coupled to two bosonic modes and maps it to a qubit-boson ring and the Z3 Potts model.
motivation: The work aims to connect coupled light-matter Rabi models to paradigmatic spin models and enable realistic implementations of Z3-symmetric quantum simulator architectures.
method: The authors derive an exact mapping between the two-mode Z3 Rabi model and a qubit-boson ring, then relate this construction to the Z3 Potts model.
result: This mapping provides a route to implement and analyze Z3 Potts-model physics using coupled three-level/bosonic-mode systems, with possible experimental realizations in hybrid quantum platforms.
conclusion: The results establish a bridge between Z3 Rabi physics and Potts-model statistical mechanics, useful for quantum simulation in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Birthmarks: Ergodicity Breaking Beyond Scarring
authors: Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, And Joonas Keski-Rahkonen
abstract:
Author(s): Anton M. Graf, Saul Atwood, Mingxuan Xiao, Roland Ketzmerick, Eric J. Heller, and Joonas Keski-Rahkonen

Researchers develop a theoretical framework showing that quantum systems permanently retain a memory of their initial state and early dynamics, in defiance of classical expectations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031063] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a theoretical framework for quantum systems that permanently retain memory of their initial state and early dynamics, revealing ergodicity breaking beyond conventional quantum scarring.
motivation: Classical ergodicity predicts that chaotic systems lose memory of initial conditions, while quantum scarring provides known exceptions; the authors ask whether quantum memory effects are more general.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for quantum ergodicity breaking and initial-state memory, likely analyzing wavefunction or spectral signatures beyond standard scarring diagnostics.
result: They show that quantum systems can exhibit persistent 'birthmarks' of their initial state and early dynamics, defying classical ergodic expectations.
conclusion: The work broadens the phenomenon of ergodicity breaking in quantum systems and suggests that initial-state memory is a more general feature than previously recognized.

title: Improved Error Correction With Leakage Reduction Units Built Into Qubit Measurement In A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, And Leonardo Dicarlo
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejie Xin, Sean L. M. van der Meer, Marc Serra-Peralta, Tim H. F. Vroomans, Matvey Finkel, Hendrik M. Veen, Marc W. Beekman, and Leonardo DiCarlo

Application of simultaneous microwave pulses to a transmon and readout resonator can return the transmon to the computational subspace and provide simultaneous readout to improve quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033062] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates a superconducting-qubit measurement scheme that uses simultaneous microwave pulses on a transmon and its readout resonator to reduce leakage and improve quantum error correction.
motivation: Leakage out of the computational subspace degrades error correction in superconducting processors, so integrating leakage reduction with qubit readout could improve hardware-level QEC performance.
method: Simultaneous microwave pulses are applied to the transmon and readout resonator to return the transmon to the computational subspace while performing readout on a superconducting quantum processor.
result: The approach provides simultaneous leakage reduction and readout, leading to improved error correction performance in the superconducting processor.
conclusion: Built-in leakage reduction during measurement is a promising technique for enhancing QEC in transmon-based quantum processors.

title: Logical Accreditation: A Framework For Efficient Certification Of Fault-Tolerant Computations
authors: James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, And Elham Kashefi
abstract:
Author(s): James Mills, Adithya Sireesh, Dominik Leichtle, Joschka Roffe, and Elham Kashefi

Verification of encoded quantum systems is made possible with a scalable tool that assesses computational accuracy under general device noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033053] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces 'logical accreditation', a scalable framework for certifying the accuracy of fault-tolerant encoded quantum computations under general device noise.
motivation: Verifying that encoded, fault-tolerant quantum computations produce correct results is essential yet challenging, since full state verification is intractable at scale and hardware noise is hard to characterize.
method: The authors develop a certification protocol that assesses computational accuracy of logical qubits by leveraging the structure of fault-tolerant encodings, enabling efficient accreditation of computations under general noise models.
result: The framework provides a scalable tool that certifies the correctness of fault-tolerant computations without requiring full tomography, with guarantees holding under broad device noise.
conclusion: Logical accreditation offers a practical and efficient route to trusting encoded quantum computations, bridging fault-tolerance and verification.

title: Moments Of Quantum Channel Ensembles
authors: Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, And M. Cerezo
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Duschenes, Diego García-Martín, Zoë Holmes, and M. Cerezo

A general framework for the study of statistical moments of quantum channel ensembles is introduced, providing new insights into noisy quantum circuits and variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033050] Published Wed Sep 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a general framework for characterizing statistical moments of ensembles of quantum channels, extending design-based (frame-potential) tools from state ensembles to noisy channel ensembles.
motivation: Randomized benchmarking, classical shadows, and variational quantum algorithms all rely on averaging over ensembles of noisy channels, yet the theory of moments and designs for states is far more developed than the analogous theory for channels.
method: The authors define moments of quantum channel ensembles and derive algebraic/combinatorial tools (frame potentials, twirling identities) to compute and bound them, then apply these to analyze average-case behaviour of noisy circuit and variational-algorithm ensembles.
result: They obtain new bounds and formulas quantifying how noise channels' moments govern the behaviour of noisy circuits, providing improved tools for analyzing variational quantum algorithm trainability and noise-induced phenomena.
conclusion: Channel-ensemble moments form a versatile framework linking quantum channel theory to practical analysis of noisy quantum circuits, extending design-based machinery beyond the state picture.

title: Disambiguating Pauli Noise In Quantum Computers
authors: Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, And Alireza Seif
abstract:
Author(s): Edward H. Chen, Senrui Chen, Laurin E. Fischer, Andrew Eddins, Luke C. G. Govia, Brad Mitchell, Andre He, Youngseok Kim, Liang Jiang, and Alireza Seif

The unavoidable “gauge” ambiguity in learning a quantum computer’s noise does not hinder error mitigation, and this remaining degree of freedom can even be optimized to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033045] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that gauge ambiguity in learning Pauli noise on quantum computers does not prevent error mitigation and can be optimized to improve mitigation efficiency.
motivation: Learning a quantum computer's noise is complicated by unavoidable gauge freedoms, and it was unclear whether these ambiguities limit practical error mitigation.
method: The authors analyze Pauli noise learning under gauge transformations and study how different gauge choices affect the performance of error-mitigation protocols.
result: They find that the gauge degree of freedom is not an obstacle to mitigation and can be tuned to make mitigation dramatically more efficient.
conclusion: Gauge ambiguity in Pauli noise characterization can be exploited rather than eliminated, enabling more effective error mitigation on quantum computers.

title: Learning Volterra Memory Kernels For non-Markovian Qubit Dynamics
authors: Jimmie Adriazola And Katarzyna Roszak
abstract:
Author(s): Jimmie Adriazola and Katarzyna Roszak

We develop a data-driven framework for identifying non-Markovian equations of motion for open quantum systems, demonstrated here for qubit-environment dynamics. Starting from the Nakajima–Zwanzig formalism, we vectorize the reduced density matrix into a four-dimensional state vector and cast the dyn…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042615] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a data-driven method to learn Volterra memory kernels for non-Markovian qubit dynamics using the Nakajima-Zwanzig formalism.
motivation: Non-Markovian open quantum system dynamics are difficult to model because memory effects require solving complicated integro-differential equations; data-driven identification can simplify this task.
method: The authors vectorize the reduced density matrix into a four-dimensional state vector and cast the dynamics as a Volterra equation, then learn the memory kernel from simulated or experimental trajectory data.
result: The framework successfully recovers non-Markovian equations of motion for qubit-environment systems, demonstrating that learned kernels can reproduce memory-dependent dynamics.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical route to identifying non-Markovian models of open quantum systems without full microscopic knowledge of the environment.

title: Driven Square Lattice Of Quantum Dots In A Magnetic Field Coupled To A Cylindrical Far Infrared Photon Cavity
authors: Vidar Gudmundsson, Vram Mughnetsyan, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Jeng-Da Chai, Nzar Rauf Abdullah, Chi-Shung Tang, Wen-Hsuan Kuan, Valeriu Moldoveanu, And Andrei Manolescu
abstract:
Author(s): Vidar Gudmundsson, Vram Mughnetsyan, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Jeng-Da Chai, Nzar Rauf Abdullah, Chi-Shung Tang, Wen-Hsuan Kuan, Valeriu Moldoveanu, and Andrei Manolescu

We present a comprehensive computational study of driven quantum dot arrays in a square lattice configuration subject to an external magnetic field and coupled to a cylindrical far-infrared photon cavity. The driving is introduced through a harmonic modulation of the full electron-photon interaction…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245302] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: A computational study of driven square-lattice quantum dot arrays in a magnetic field coupled to a cylindrical far-infrared photon cavity.
motivation: The work aims to understand driven electron-photon dynamics in cavity-coupled quantum dot lattices under magnetic confinement.
method: The authors model a square quantum dot array coupled to a cylindrical far-infrared cavity and introduce driving via harmonic modulation of the full electron-photon interaction, using computational simulation.
result: The study provides a detailed computational characterization of how the cavity coupling, magnetic field, and driving influence the electronic and photonic properties of the quantum dot lattice.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled quantum dot arrays are relevant as hybrid light-matter platforms, particularly for far-infrared quantum control and engineered photon-mediated interactions.

title: High-fidelity Molecular Quantum Logic Gates Resilient To Interaction Fluctuation
authors: Yan Lu And Xiao-Feng Shi
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Lu and Xiao-Feng Shi

Although polar molecules are promising candidates for quantum computing, entangling gates built with them suffer from fluctuations in the dipole-dipole interaction (DDI). A high-fidelity molecular gate protocol is introduced that uses an exotic spin echo to suppress population in DDI-active states, alongside a theoretical framework revealing that DDI couples to only half of the motional modes during the gate.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042004] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a high-fidelity entangling-gate protocol for polar-molecule quantum computing that uses an exotic spin echo to suppress sensitivity to dipole-dipole interaction fluctuations.
motivation: Polar molecules are attractive qubit candidates, but entangling gates based on dipole-dipole interactions suffer from interaction fluctuations that degrade fidelity.
method: The authors introduce a molecular gate scheme employing an exotic spin echo to avoid population in DDI-active states, and develop a theoretical framework showing that DDI couples to only half of the motional modes during the gate.
result: The protocol is designed to be resilient to DDI fluctuations and is argued to enable high-fidelity molecular quantum logic gates, with the theoretical analysis identifying which motional modes participate in the interaction.
conclusion: This work advances polar-molecule quantum computing by providing a fluctuation-resilient gate protocol and a clearer understanding of motional-mode coupling in DDI-based gates.

title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance Quantization And Gate-Tunable Induced Superconducting Gap In Germanium
authors: Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, And Silvano de Franceschi
abstract:
Author(s): Elyjah Kiyooka, Chotivut Tangchingchai, Gonzalo Troncoso Fernandez-Bada, Boris Brun-Barriere, Simon Zihlmann, Romain Maurand, Francois Lefloch, Vivien Schmitt, Jean-Michel Hartmann, Manuel Houzet, and Silvano De Franceschi

Experiments in Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts demonstrate a gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gap and near-ideal superconducting conductance quantization in excellent agreement with theory.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033043] Published Tue Sep 01, 2026.
tldr: Germanium/SiGe quantum point contacts show gate-tunable proximity-induced superconducting gaps and near-ideal Andreev conductance quantization matching theory.
motivation: Semiconductor-superconductor hybrids are a leading platform for Majorana and Andreev-based qubits, and Ge hole gases offer strong spin-orbit coupling plus CMOS compatibility, but proximity effects in Ge-based constrictions remain poorly characterized.
method: Fabrication of Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts with superconducting electrodes (proximity-induced gap) and low-temperature transport measurements of differential conductance versus gate voltage and bias, compared with theoretical models of Andreev reflection.
result: A gate-tunable induced superconducting gap is demonstrated together with conductance quantization approaching the ideal Andreev limit, in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The results establish Ge/SiGe quantum point contacts as a viable, gate-controllable hybrid platform for superconducting-semiconductor quantum devices, including Andreev and topological qubit architectures.

title: Chiral Transfer And Entanglement Generation Of Even-parity Bell States With Engineered Two-photon Loss
authors: Lin Xiao, Jian Li, Mu Zhou, Bin Wei, Qing-Xu Li, And Jia-Ji Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Lin Xiao, Jian Li, Mu Zhou, Bin Wei, Qing-Xu Li, and Jia-Ji Zhu

We investigate chiral transfer and dissipative generation of even-parity Bell states in a two-qubit system with coherent two-photon driving and engineered two-photon loss. We find that adiabatic encirclement of a second-order exceptional point induces direction-dependent transfer between the Bell st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042417] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies chiral, direction-dependent transfer between even-parity Bell states and their dissipative generation in a two-qubit system driven coherently with two photons and subject to engineered two-photon loss, exploiting adiabatic encirclement of a second-order exceptional point.
motivation: Dissipative state engineering and non-Hermitian exceptional-point physics offer routes to deterministic, robust preparation and control of entangled states, motivating a study of how engineered loss can steer Bell-state dynamics.
method: A two-qubit model with coherent two-photon driving and engineered two-photon loss is analyzed, using adiabatic encircling of a second-order exceptional point to realize chiral transfer and dissipative generation of even-parity Bell states.
result: Adiabatic encirclement of the exceptional point yields direction-dependent (chiral) transfer between Bell states, and the engineered two-photon loss enables dissipative generation of even-parity Bell states.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian exceptional-point dynamics combined with tailored dissipation provides a controllable mechanism for chiral Bell-state manipulation and entanglement generation, though the work is largely platform-agnostic and theoretical.

title: Frequency Up-conversion Of Infrared Signals Via Molecular Cavity Optomechanical Systems With Gain
authors: Shu-Xian Quan, Fen Zou, And Yong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Shu-Xian Quan, Fen Zou, and Yong Li

Molecular cavity optomechanical systems have recently emerged as a promising platform for enhancing infrared detection sensitivity, owing to their ability to up-convert low-frequency infrared (IR) photons to visible frequency range. Generally, under red-detuned pumping in such systems, the maximum c…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043725] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes frequency up-conversion of infrared photons to the visible band in molecular cavity optomechanical systems operating with gain, deriving the achievable conversion efficiency and noise performance.
motivation: Molecular cavity optomechanics offers a compact route to boost infrared detection sensitivity by converting low-frequency IR photons into the visible regime where low-noise detectors exist, motivating a quantitative theory of the up-conversion process.
method: A cavity optomechanical model of the molecular system under red-detuned pumping is developed, including gain, and the maximum conversion efficiency together with added-noise contributions is derived analytically (possibly with numerical evaluation).
result: The authors obtain expressions for the maximum up-conversion efficiency and identify the conditions under which gain in the molecular cavity enhances conversion while characterizing the associated noise floor.
conclusion: Molecular cavity optomechanical systems with gain are shown to be viable platforms for sensitive infrared-to-visible up-conversion, with the derived bounds guiding future transducer design.

title: Full Eigenstate Thermalization In Integrable Spin Systems
authors: Tanay Pathak
abstract:
Author(s): Tanay Pathak

The Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) is a standard tool to understand the thermalization properties of an isolated quantum system. Its generalization to higher-order correlations of matrix elements of local operators, dubbed the full ETH, relates the ETH free cumulants to the corresponding…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044124] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the full Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis by relating ETH free cumulants to higher-order correlations of local operator matrix elements, and shows how this structure persists in integrable spin systems.
motivation: Standard ETH constrains diagonal and two-point matrix elements of local observables, but thermalization of higher-order correlation functions requires a generalization known as full ETH, whose free-probability structure is still poorly understood, particularly in integrable models where ETH is expected to fail or hold only in modified form.
method: The author develops a free-probability formulation of full ETH, expressing connected higher-order correlations of local operator matrix elements in terms of ETH free cumulants, and tests the resulting predictions analytically/numerically in integrable spin chains.
result: The analysis shows that full ETH-type cumulant relations can be formulated consistently and captures how higher-order matrix-element correlations behave in integrable spin systems, delineating where standard ETH-like structure survives.
conclusion: Full ETH provides a sharper characterization of thermalization in isolated quantum systems, and integrable spin systems offer a useful testing ground for its higher-order cumulant structure.

title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Phase-Space Bosonic Dynamics Via Automatic Differentiation
authors: Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, And Cristiano Ciuti
abstract:
Author(s): Jacopo Tosca, Francesco Carnazza, Luca Giacomelli, and Cristiano Ciuti

Researchers introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method combining analytical techniques with automatic differentiation to reveal the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031077] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method with automatic differentiation to simulate critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.
motivation: Large open quantum bosonic lattices are challenging to simulate, motivating scalable methods that go beyond exact diagonalization or simple mean-field approaches.
method: It combines an analytical multi-Gaussian phase-space representation with variational optimization powered by automatic differentiation to approximate open-system dynamics.
result: The approach captures critical dynamics in large open bosonic lattices and demonstrates scalability compared with conventional methods.
conclusion: This provides a practical computational framework for studying non-equilibrium and critical phenomena in open quantum bosonic many-body systems.

title: Ultra-Slow Orbital And Spin Dynamics In An Electrically Tunable Quantum Dot Molecule
authors: Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, And Jonathan Finley
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Thalacker, Michelle Lienhart, Markus Stöcker, Nadeem Akhlaq, Irina Ivanova, Nikolai Bart, Arne Ludwig, Johannes Schall, Stephan Reitzenstein, Dirk Reuter, Steffen Wilksen, Christopher Gies, Krzysztof Gawarecki, Paweł Machnikowski, Kai Müller, and Jonathan Finley

A new study demonstrates the optical charging of spins in a quantum dot molecule, while keeping the tunability of its parameter, which can become an important building block for multidimensional photonic cluster state generation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033056] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates optical charging of resident spins in an electrically tunable quantum dot molecule, preserving gate tunability, as a building block for multidimensional photonic cluster-state generation.
motivation: Spin-charged quantum dot molecules are attractive solid-state interfaces between stationary spins and flying photons, but charging the spin state optically while retaining electrical control over the level structure is difficult.
method: Optical spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements on an electrically gated quantum dot molecule, resolving ultra-slow orbital and spin dynamics of the charged complex under applied electric field.
result: Optical charging of spins is achieved while the molecular level alignment remains electrically tunable, and the observed orbital/spin dynamics are anomalously slow, indicating long-lived spin and charge configurations.
conclusion: The device provides a tunable spin-photon platform that could serve as a resource for generating multidimensional photonic cluster states, relevant to measurement-based quantum computing and spin-photon interfaces.

title: Heisenberg Scaling In Optical Magnetometry With Measurement-induced Correlations As A Quantum Resource
authors: Georg Engelhardt, Ming Li, Xingchang Wang, Junyan Luo, And J. F. Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Georg Engelhardt, Ming Li, Xingchang Wang, JunYan Luo, and J. F. Chen

Theoretical proposals to reach the Heisenberg scaling of the measurement precision typically require carefully engineered interactions or initial entanglement. In studying optical magnetometry, we show that the continuous collective measurement process itself can generate the necessary many-body qua…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043722] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Continuous collective measurement in optical magnetometry can itself generate many-body quantum correlations that enable Heisenberg-limited sensitivity without engineered interactions or initial entanglement.
motivation: Heisenberg scaling in quantum metrology typically requires carefully engineered interactions or initial entangled states, which are demanding to realize experimentally.
method: The authors theoretically study optical magnetometry under continuous collective measurement and analyze how measurement-induced correlations act as a quantum resource for parameter estimation.
result: They show that the measurement process can generate the necessary many-body quantum correlations, allowing Heisenberg scaling of measurement precision in optical magnetometry.
