conclusion: Measurement-induced correlations provide a practical quantum resource for enhanced magnetometry, potentially relaxing the need for complex state preparation or interaction engineering.

title: Level Statistics Of The Disordered Haldane-Shastry Model With $1/{r}^{α}$ Interaction
authors: Vengatesan Ganapathy, Pranay Patil, And Ajit C. Balram
abstract:
Author(s): Vengatesan Ganapathy, Pranay Patil, and Ajit C. Balram

Understanding how the interaction range and various types of disorder affect the level statistics of many-body quantum systems, leading to the emergence of many-body localization (MBL), is a challenging open frontier. We study the level statistics of a variant of the spin-[MATH] Haldane-Shastry model…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245118] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Numerically studies level statistics of a disordered spin-1/2 Haldane-Shastry model with long-range 1/r^α interactions to map out the emergence of many-body localization as a function of interaction range and disorder type.
motivation: How interaction range and disorder type control the crossover to many-body localization remains an open question, and exactly solvable-ish long-range models like Haldane-Shastry offer a controlled setting to probe it.
method: Computes spectral level-spacing statistics (e.g., gap-ratio distributions) of the disordered Haldane-Shastry Hamiltonian with tunable 1/r^α couplings for various disorder strengths and ranges, likely via exact diagonalization.
result: Identifies regimes of Poisson versus Wigner-Dyson-like level statistics, delineating where MBL-like behavior emerges as the interaction range α and disorder strength are varied.
conclusion: The level statistics reveal how interaction range and disorder type govern localization in long-range spin models, clarifying the boundary between thermalizing and localized phases.

title: $\mathrm{Λ}$-Enhanced Gray-Molasses Loading And Eit Cooling Of Neutral Atoms In Nanophotonic Traps
authors: Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, And Riccardo Pennetta
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Pache, Antoine Glicenstein, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, Arno Rauschenbeutel, and Riccardo Pennetta

Λ-enhanced gray molasses and electromagnetically induced transparency cooling enable efficient loading and longer storage times, improving the practicality of nanophotonic interfaces for neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043010] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Λ-enhanced gray molasses and EIT cooling are combined to improve loading efficiency and storage times of neutral atoms in nanophotonic traps, enhancing the practicality of atom-photon interfaces.
motivation: Nanophotonic interfaces with trapped neutral atoms are promising for quantum networking and light-matter quantum processing, but poor loading efficiency and short trap lifetimes limit their usefulness.
method: The authors implement Λ-enhanced gray molasses for efficient loading of cold atoms into nanophotonic traps and apply electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) cooling to reduce atomic motion and extend storage times.
result: The combined cooling and loading scheme yields improved loading into the nanophotonic trap and longer storage/lifetime of the trapped atoms compared with standard techniques.
conclusion: The approach makes nanophotonic atom traps more practical for quantum interface applications by improving loading and coherence-relevant storage times.

title: Multiband Dispersion And Warped Vortices Of Strongly Interacting Photons
authors: Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, And Ofer Firstenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Bankim Chandra Das, Dmytro Kiselov, Lee Drori, Ariel Nakav, Alexander Poddubny, and Ofer Firstenberg

A new study develops an analytical framework to understand and control nonlinear multiphoton processes in strongly interacting Rydberg media.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043002] Published Fri Oct 02, 2026.
tldr: An analytical framework describes nonlinear multiphoton propagation in strongly interacting Rydberg media, revealing multiband dispersion and warped vortex structures.
motivation: Strongly interacting Rydberg media offer a platform for controlling photon-photon interactions, but multiphoton nonlinear processes are complex and require theoretical understanding.
method: The authors develop an analytical treatment of strongly interacting photons in Rydberg media to derive multiband dispersion relations and vortex solutions.
result: The study identifies multiband dispersion and warped vortex structures for strongly interacting photons.
conclusion: This provides a theoretical tool for understanding and controlling nonlinear multiphoton dynamics in Rydberg quantum optical media.

title: Fluctuation-response Design Rules For Nonequilibrium Flows
authors: Ying-Jen Yang And Ken A. Dill
abstract:
Author(s): Ying-Jen Yang and Ken A. Dill

Biomolecular machines operate as stochastic flows on networks. Here, we develop a principled approach to network design where local transition rates are systematically tuned to achieve global dynamical objectives. Based on the fluctuation-response duality in caliber force theory, our formalism unifi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043039] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops fluctuation-response-based design rules for tuning local transition rates in stochastic nonequilibrium networks to achieve global dynamical objectives.
motivation: Biomolecular machines can be modeled as stochastic flows on networks, but principled methods for designing local rates to realize desired global behavior are lacking.
method: Using fluctuation-response duality in caliber force theory, the authors derive a formalism that maps changes in local transition rates to changes in global nonequilibrium flow observables.
result: They obtain systematic design rules for network optimization, unifying response relations and enabling targeted tuning of stochastic network dynamics.
conclusion: This provides a general framework for designing nonequilibrium stochastic networks, with implications for biomolecular machine modeling and control.

title: Monitored Quantum Transport Through A Disordered One-dimensional Conductor
authors: J. Sánchez Fernán, J. Tworzydło, And C. W. J. Beenakker
abstract:
Author(s): J. Sánchez Fernán, J. Tworzydło, and C. W. J. Beenakker

We formulate a quantum master equation for the many-particle density matrix of electrons propagating through a single-mode conductor, combining elastic scattering by disorder with time-resolved projective measurements that monitor the outcome of scattering events. For noninteracting electrons the ch…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225129] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper formulates a quantum master equation for monitored electron transport through a disordered single-mode conductor, combining disorder scattering with projective measurements of scattering events.
motivation: It aims to understand how time-resolved projective monitoring modifies many-particle quantum transport in a disordered conductor.
method: A quantum master equation for the many-particle density matrix is developed, incorporating elastic scattering by disorder and projective measurements that record scattering outcomes.
result: The framework describes how monitoring affects electron propagation and transport statistics in the single-mode disordered conductor for noninteracting electrons.
conclusion: The work links measurement backaction and open-system dynamics to mesoscopic quantum transport, showing that projective monitoring can alter transport behavior in disordered conductors.

title: Quantum State Designs From Minimally Random Quantum Circuits
authors: Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathon Riddell, Katja Klobas, and Bruno Bertini

For quantum circuits that generate complex dynamics, a single, one-site operation is sufficient to produce randomness, showcasing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033047] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that minimally random quantum circuits, requiring only a single one-site operation, can generate quantum state designs, revealing a trade-off between dynamical chaos and randomness.
motivation: Understanding how much randomness is needed in quantum circuits to produce complex dynamics and state designs is important for efficient generation of pseudo-random quantum states.
method: The authors analyze quantum circuits with minimal randomness, specifically a single one-site operation, and study their ability to produce quantum state designs and chaotic dynamics.
result: They find that a single one-site operation suffices to generate randomness, demonstrating a trade-off between dynamical chaos and the amount of randomness required.
conclusion: This work clarifies minimal resource requirements for quantum state designs and connects randomness generation to chaotic dynamics in quantum circuits.

title: Lévy-Khintchine Structure Enables Fast-Forwardable Lindbladian Simulation
authors: Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, And Chenghua Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, and Chenghua Liu

Simulation of open quantum systems is an area of active research in quantum algorithms. In this Letter, we revisit the connection between Markovian open-system dynamics and averages of Hamiltonian real-time evolutions, which we refer to as Hamiltonian twirling channels. By applying the Lévy-Khintchi…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160405] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors exploit the Lévy-Khintchine representation of Markovian open-system dynamics to construct fast-forwardable quantum algorithms for simulating Lindbladians.
motivation: Simulating Markovian open quantum dynamics is a central task for quantum algorithms, but generic Lindbladian simulation is costly; the paper seeks structure that enables efficient (fast-forwardable) simulation.
method: They reinterpret Markovian dynamics as Hamiltonian twirling channels (averages of Hamiltonian real-time evolutions) and apply the Lévy-Khintchine decomposition to expose a fast-forwardable structure, then build a quantum simulation algorithm on it.
result: The Lévy-Khintchine structure yields a fast-forwardable Lindbladian simulation scheme with improved complexity over generic approaches.
conclusion: Identifying Lévy-Khintchine structure provides a route to efficient simulation of open quantum systems, connecting Markovian dynamics to Hamiltonian twirling.

title: Dynamical Signatures Of A Connectivity-breaking Global Bifurcation In A Driven-dissipative Kerr Dimer
authors: Zhan-Cheng Zhu, Sheng-Chen Liu, And Liang-You Peng
abstract:
Author(s): Zhan-Cheng Zhu, Sheng-Chen Liu, and Liang-You Peng

Driven-dissipative nonlinear systems can exhibit global phase-space structures that are not captured by local fixed-point analysis alone. Here we study two coupled Kerr cavities and investigate how a global bifurcation that changes the connectivity of strange attractors is reflected in quantum dynam…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043724] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how a connectivity-breaking global bifurcation in a driven-dissipative Kerr dimer is reflected in quantum dynamical signatures.
motivation: Driven-dissipative nonlinear systems can exhibit global phase-space structures missed by local fixed-point analysis, and how such structures manifest in quantum dynamics remains unclear.
method: The authors analyze two coupled Kerr cavities using phase-space and attractor/bifurcation analysis together with quantum dynamical simulations.
result: They identify a global bifurcation that changes the connectivity of strange attractors and find corresponding signatures in the quantum dynamics.
conclusion: The work shows that global bifurcations can leave detectable imprints in quantum observables, providing a route to probe phase-space topology in driven-dissipative nonlinear systems.

title: Chirped-pulse Adiabatic Population Transfer In A Dissipative Three-level Ladder: Bath-dependent Transfer Via The Multiple Davydov ${\mathrm{D}}_{2}$ Ansatz
authors: Pradhyun Naresh, Yiying Yan, Frank Grossmann, And Yang Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Pradhyun Naresh, Yiying Yan, Frank Grossmann, and Yang Zhao

Rapid adiabatic passage, which enables complete population transfer via a frequency-chirped laser pulse, is valued for its robustness to pulse-area fluctuations in quantum-dot control. Previous work by Werther and Grossmann [M. Werther and F. Grossmann,
tldr: The paper theoretically studies chirped-pulse adiabatic population transfer in a dissipative three-level ladder using the multiple Davydov D2 ansatz and finds bath-dependent transfer behavior.
motivation: Rapid adiabatic passage is attractive for robust quantum-dot control because it is insensitive to pulse-area fluctuations, but realistic environments introduce dissipation that can alter transfer fidelity.
method: The authors model a three-level ladder driven by a frequency-chirped pulse and coupled to a bath, solving the dissipative dynamics with the multiple Davydov D2 ansatz.
result: The analysis shows that population transfer depends on bath parameters, indicating that environmental coupling can significantly modify adiabatic passage performance.
conclusion: The work provides insight into robust quantum control in open systems and highlights the need to account for bath effects when designing chirped-pulse protocols.

title: Interaction-Assisted Topological Pumping In Few- And Many-Atom Rydberg Arrays
authors: Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, And Bryce Gadway
abstract:
Author(s): Chenxi Huang, Tao Chen, Qian Liang, Matthew A. Krebs, Ethan Springhorn, Ruiyu Li, Mingsheng Tian, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Jacob P. Covey, and Bryce Gadway

Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays are found to be able to bind particles into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031075] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: Strong dipolar interactions in Rydberg atom arrays bind atoms into correlated pairs and clusters that undergo efficient topological pumping along a synthetic dimension.
motivation: Topological pumping is typically studied for single particles or non-interacting bands; how strong, long-range dipolar interactions modify and possibly assist pumping in few- and many-body settings is largely unexplored.
method: Experiments and theory in Rydberg atom arrays where dipolar interactions create correlated pairs and clusters, which are then driven through a synthetic dimension to realize topological transport.
result: Interaction-bound pairs and clusters are shown to be pumped efficiently, with interaction-assisted transport emerging in both few-atom and many-atom regimes.
conclusion: Interactions can be a resource rather than a nuisance for topological pumping, suggesting Rydberg arrays as a platform for studying correlated topological transport and interaction-enabled quantum simulation.

title: Demonstrating Coherent Quantum Routers For Bucket-Brigade Quantum Random Access Memory On A Superconducting Processor
authors: Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, And Guo-Ping Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng Zhang, Yun-Jie Wang, Peng Wang, Ren-Ze Zhao, Xiao-Yan Yang, Ze-An Zhao, Tian-Le Wang, Hai-Feng Zhang, Zhi-Fei Li, Yuan Wu, Hao-Ran Tao, Liang-Liang Guo, Lei Du, Chi Zhang, Zhi-Long Jia, Wei-Cheng Kong, Zhuo-Zhi Zhang, Xiang-Xiang Song, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Peng Duan, and Guo-Ping Guo

Researchers demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor to realize resilient routing for quantum memories.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031051] Published Tue Aug 25, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally demonstrate coherent quantum routers on a superconducting processor that implement bucket-brigade routing for quantum random access memory (QRAM).
motivation: Bucket-brigade QRAM promises exponential speedups but requires routers that coherently route flying qubits to memory cells without disturbing stored quantum data, a demanding requirement that has not been realized experimentally.
method: A superconducting processor is used to implement router circuits — coherently controlled two-level systems acting as routing nodes — and their operation is characterized through quantum process/state tomography and routing fidelity benchmarks within a bucket-brigade QRAM architecture.
result: Coherent routing of quantum information between memory cells is achieved with high fidelity, demonstrating that the router primitive for bucket-brigade QRAM is realizable on a superconducting platform.
conclusion: The work provides an experimental building block toward scalable QRAM, indicating that coherent quantum routing is feasible with current superconducting technology despite remaining challenges of depth and error accumulation.

title: First-Principles Calculations Of Internal Conversion Processes In Spin Defects
authors: Stefano Paolo Villani, Yu Jin, And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Stefano Paolo Villani, Yu Jin, and Giulia Galli

Optically active spin defects are foundational for quantum technologies, yet common approximations underestimate their internal conversion (IC) rates by orders of magnitude. We propose a broad, predictive framework to compute IC rates that incorporates multiconfigurational effects via many-body wave…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 163603] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a first-principles multiconfigurational framework for computing internal conversion rates in optically active spin defects, correcting order-of-magnitude errors from standard approximations.
motivation: Optically active spin defects underpin many quantum technology platforms, but conventional computational approaches severely underestimate internal conversion rates, undermining predictive design of defect-based qubits and spin-photon interfaces.
method: They construct a broad ab initio framework that incorporates multiconfigurational effects through many-body wavefunctions to compute internal conversion rates for spin defects, benchmarked against known systems.
result: The proposed approach reproduces internal conversion rates that agree far better with experiment than standard single-reference methods, which can be off by orders of magnitude.
conclusion: Accurate treatment of multiconfigurational effects is essential for predicting non-radiative decay in spin defects, providing a practical tool for screening colour-centre candidates in quantum applications.

title: Efficient Mapping Of Multiconstraint Satisfaction Problems To Rydberg Platforms
authors: Robert Gloeckner, Shahram Panahiyan, Frederik Koch, Dieter Jaksch, And Joseph Doetsch
abstract:
Author(s): Robert Gloeckner, Shahram Panahiyan, Frederik Koch, Dieter Jaksch, and Joseph Doetsch

We present a hardware-native gadget framework for solving constraint-satisfaction problems on Rydberg quantum computing architectures. Our approach introduces a compact [MATH] gadget that enforces exactly-one constraints, ubiquitous in combinatorial optimization, directly through geometr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043054] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a hardware-native 'gadget' framework that compiles exactly-one constraint satisfaction problems directly onto Rydberg atom arrays using geometric placement of atoms.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems such as graph coloring and exact-cover require exactly-one constraints, which are costly to embed on near-term neutral-atom hardware; a compact, geometry-driven encoding reduces resource overhead.
method: A compact gadget enforcing exactly-one constraints is designed and mapped onto Rydberg blockade geometries, then benchmarked against conventional encodings on multiconstraint satisfaction instances.
result: The gadget framework yields more compact embeddings with fewer atoms and simplified connectivity relative to standard encodings, improving feasibility of solving multiconstraint problems on Rydberg platforms.
conclusion: Hardware-native gadget compilation offers a practical route to embedding combinatorial optimization problems on Rydberg quantum computers, though the work is primarily an applied mapping/compilation study rather than a platform characterization or information-theoretic advance.

title: Quantum Contact Processes On A Topological Lattice
authors: Julius Bohm, Richard Schmidt, Michael Fleischhauer, And Daniel Brady
abstract:
Author(s): Julius Bohm, Richard Schmidt, Michael Fleischhauer, and Daniel Brady

Contact processes play an important role in classical nonequilibrium dynamics, describing the spreading of diseases, the dynamics of earthquakes and forest fires, and the distribution of information through the internet. Here we show that their quantum counterpart, where the spreading occurs through…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194303] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces and analyzes a quantum contact process on a topological lattice to study nonequilibrium spreading dynamics and phase behavior.
motivation: Classical contact processes describe spreading phenomena such as epidemics and information propagation, but their quantum counterparts remain less understood, especially on nontrivial lattice geometries.
method: The authors formulate a quantum contact process, likely as an open quantum many-body system with coherent and dissipative spreading dynamics, and analyze its behavior on a topological lattice.
result: The study identifies how quantum effects and topological lattice structure modify the nonequilibrium spreading dynamics and phase transitions of the contact process.
conclusion: Quantum contact processes on topological lattices provide a platform for exploring nonequilibrium phase transitions and spreading dynamics beyond classical contact-process models.

title: Probing Critical Phases In Quasiperiodic Systems Via Subsystem Information Capacity
authors: Huaijin Dong And Long Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Huaijin Dong and Long Zhang

We systematically investigate the entanglement and information dynamics of quasiperiodic systems across their extended, critical, and localized phases, aiming to identify dynamical signatures that can reveal the multifractal spatial structure of critical states and distinguish critical phases from t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204202] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies entanglement and information dynamics in quasiperiodic systems to identify signatures of multifractal critical states and distinguish critical from extended/localized phases.
motivation: Quasiperiodic systems host extended, critical, and localized phases whose critical states have multifractal structure, and the authors aim to find dynamical information-based probes of these phases.
method: They systematically analyze entanglement and information dynamics, likely using subsystem information capacity and related quantities, across the phase diagram of quasiperiodic models.
result: The authors identify dynamical signatures that reveal multifractal spatial structure and help distinguish critical phases from extended and localized ones.
conclusion: Subsystem information capacity and entanglement dynamics can serve as practical probes of criticality and multifractality in quasiperiodic systems.

title: Mixed Eigenstates In Spin-boson Systems With One-photon And Two-photon Interactions
authors: David Villaseñor And Marko Robnik
abstract:
Author(s): David Villaseñor and Marko Robnik

Spin-boson systems have attracted increasing attention as accessible experimental platforms and for their potential applications in designing quantum technologies. One characteristic of these systems is the transition from regular to completely chaotic behavior when certain control parameters are va…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044206] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies mixed eigenstates and the regular-to-chaotic transition in spin-boson systems with one-photon and two-photon interactions.
motivation: Spin-boson models are experimentally relevant platforms, and understanding their chaotic regimes and eigenstate mixing is important for controlling quantum behavior.
method: The authors analyze mixed eigenstates in spin-boson systems incorporating both one-photon and two-photon interactions, examining how control parameters drive the transition from regular to chaotic dynamics.
result: They characterize eigenstate mixing and identify signatures of the transition to chaos in these spin-boson models.
conclusion: The work clarifies how one- and two-photon interactions affect mixed eigenstate structure and chaotic behavior in spin-boson systems.

title: Distributed Quantum Simulation
authors: Tianfeng Feng, Jue Xu, Wenjun Yu, Zekun Ye, Penghui Yao, And Qi Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Tianfeng Feng, Jue Xu, Wenjun Yu, Zekun Ye, Penghui Yao, and Qi Zhao

Quantum simulation is a promising pathway toward practical quantum advantage by simulating large-scale quantum systems. In this Letter, we propose communication-efficient distributed quantum simulation protocols by exploring three quantum simulation algorithms, including the product formula, the tru…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160601] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes communication-efficient distributed protocols for quantum simulation by adapting product-formula and related simulation algorithms to a distributed setting.
motivation: Large-scale quantum simulation is a leading route to practical quantum advantage, but realizing it on a single device is challenging, motivating distributed quantum computation across multiple processors.
method: The authors design distributed versions of quantum simulation algorithms, including product-formula/Trotter-type methods, and analyze their communication cost and efficiency.
result: They obtain communication-efficient distributed quantum simulation protocols, demonstrating that simulation tasks can be distributed with reduced communication overhead.
conclusion: Distributed quantum simulation offers a viable path toward scalable quantum advantage, with algorithmic choices strongly affecting communication requirements.

title: Quantum Sensing In The Presence Of Pulse Errors And Qubit Leakage
authors: David M. Lancaster, Muhammad Ali Shahbaz, Hamed Goli Yousefabad, Sanway Chatterjee, Eegan Ram, And Jonathan D. Weinstein
abstract:
Author(s): David M. Lancaster, Muhammad Ali Shahbaz, Hamed Goli Yousefabad, Sanway Chatterjee, Eegan Ram, and Jonathan D. Weinstein

Using both simulation and experiment, we investigate the robustness of dynamical decoupling sequences to pulse errors: rotation errors and detuning errors. Whereas prior work examined the effect of errors on coherence times, here we show that quantum sensing can be affected by pulse errors in dramat…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043034] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: Simulation and experiment show that pulse errors (rotation and detuning errors) can dramatically degrade quantum sensing with dynamical decoupling sequences, beyond their known effect on coherence times.
motivation: Prior work on dynamical decoupling mostly characterized how pulse errors shorten coherence times; the authors ask whether these same errors corrupt the sensing signal itself, which matters for practical metrology with imperfect control.
method: They combine numerical simulation with experiments (apparently on a spin/atomic ensemble platform) to compare several dynamical decoupling sequences under deliberately introduced rotation-angle and detuning errors, quantifying the resulting sensing performance.
result: Pulse errors are found to affect quantum sensing more severely than coherence-time measurements would suggest, with qubit leakage and accumulated rotation/detuning errors producing large sensing biases and signal loss.
conclusion: Sensing protocols must be designed and benchmarked against realistic control errors rather than coherence times alone; error-robust decoupling sequences are needed for reliable quantum metrology.

title: Energy-Efficient Control Of Interacting Microscopic Systems: When Longer Paths Save Energy
authors: Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, And Clemens Bechinger
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Monter, Lars T. Stutzer, Sarah A. M. Loos, and Clemens Bechinger

Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions offers a route to control multiparticle systems efficiently, enabling substantial reductions in the energetic cost of microscopic transport.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031079] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that in a system of hydrodynamically interacting colloidal particles, taking geometrically longer transport paths can reduce the total energetic cost of moving the particles.
motivation: Controlling and transporting microscopic objects efficiently is energetically costly; the authors ask whether exploiting hydrodynamic coupling between particles can lower the work required for microscopic transport.
method: Experiments on interacting microscopic particles in a viscous fluid, combined with a theoretical/optimal-control analysis of trajectories that minimize dissipated energy under hydrodynamic interactions.
result: Counterintuitively, paths that are longer in geometric length can require less total energy, because hydrodynamic interactions let particles 'draft' on one another and reduce viscous dissipation.
conclusion: Harnessing hydrodynamic interactions provides a practical route to energy-efficient control of multiparticle microscopic systems, with implications for optimal microscopic transport and the thermodynamics of driven soft-matter systems.

title: Quantum-corrected Floquet Dynamics: Bridging Fully Quantum And Semiclassical Regimes
authors: E. K. Twyeffort And A. D. Armour
abstract:
Author(s): E. K. Twyeffort and A. D. Armour

Semiclassical descriptions of a few-level system coupled to an electromagnetic field mode reduce the field to a time-dependent driving term. Although such methods are widely used, the underlying quantum character of the field generates corrections to the dynamics that can become significant. Here, w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043726] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares fully quantum and semiclassical Floquet descriptions of a few-level system coupled to an electromagnetic field mode and quantifies corrections arising from the quantum nature of the drive.
motivation: Semiclassical Floquet treatments replace a quantized field mode with a time-dependent drive, but this approximation can miss quantum corrections that become important in certain regimes.
method: The authors analyze a few-level system coupled to an electromagnetic field mode, contrasting a fully quantum treatment with the semiclassical driven-system description to identify and characterize quantum corrections.
result: They show how the quantum character of the field generates corrections to the semiclassical Floquet dynamics and clarify when these corrections become significant.
conclusion: The work bridges fully quantum and semiclassical regimes, providing a framework for assessing the validity of semiclassical Floquet descriptions in driven quantum systems.

title: Complexity Drives The Symmetry Breaking Of Temperature Fluctuations
authors: D. Rosales Herrera, M. Y. Gallegos Ruiz, A. Fernández Téllez, J. R. Alvarado García, And J. E. Ramírez
abstract:
Author(s): D. Rosales Herrera, M. Y. Gallegos Ruiz, A. Fernández Téllez, J. R. Alvarado García, and J. E. Ramírez

Frequently, nonextensive systems are described through [MATH]-exponential functions, where the [MATH] parameter determines how far a system is from equilibrium. In this work, we study systems constrained to [MATH] to describe systems near thermal equilibrium, and derive the probability density function a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044117] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies temperature fluctuations in nonextensive systems near thermal equilibrium using q-exponential distributions and relates complexity to symmetry breaking.
motivation: Nonextensive statistical mechanics often uses q-exponentials to characterize systems away from equilibrium, but the near-equilibrium limit and the nature of temperature fluctuations require clarification.
method: The authors constrain the nonextensivity parameter toward the equilibrium limit q -> 1 and derive a probability density function for temperature fluctuations, analyzing its symmetry-breaking behavior.
result: They find that complexity, quantified through the nonextensive framework, drives symmetry breaking in the temperature fluctuation distribution near equilibrium.
conclusion: The work provides a statistical-mechanical characterization of near-equilibrium nonextensive systems and highlights how complexity can induce symmetry breaking in thermal fluctuations.

title: Asymptotically Solvable Quantum Circuits
authors: Samuel H. Pickering And Bruno Bertini
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel H. Pickering and Bruno Bertini

A new family of quantum circuits gives rise to correlations that are chaotic at short scales yet exactly solvable at long scales.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a new family of quantum circuits whose short-scale correlations are chaotic but whose long-scale behavior is exactly solvable.
motivation: It aims to bridge chaotic quantum dynamics and exact solvability, providing tractable models for understanding long-scale correlation structure in quantum many-body systems.
method: The authors construct and analyze a family of quantum circuits designed to be asymptotically solvable, deriving exact results for long-distance or long-time correlation behavior.
result: The circuits exhibit chaotic correlations at short scales while remaining exactly solvable at long scales, yielding analytic control over asymptotic dynamics.
conclusion: This provides a useful model class for studying chaotic quantum circuits and long-scale universal behavior, though it is not directly focused on the researcher's priority areas.

title: Electrically Tunable Orbital Coupling And Quantum Light Emission From O-Band Quantum Dot Molecules
authors: P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, And J. J. Finley
abstract:
Author(s): P. S. Avdienko, L. Hanschke, Q. Buchinger, N. Akhlaq, I. Lubianskii, E. Weber, H. Riedl, M. Kamp, T. Huber-Loyola, S. Höfling, A. T. Pfenning, K. Müller, and J. J. Finley

Telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules exhibit electrically tunable orbital coupling, opening a route toward 2D photonic cluster states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033070] Published Wed Sep 30, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates electrically tunable orbital coupling and quantum light emission from telecom O-band InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules, pointing toward 2D photonic cluster states.
motivation: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources and scalable photonic cluster states are important for quantum communication and photonic quantum information processing, motivating tunable solid-state emitters.
method: The authors fabricate and characterize InAs/InGaAs quantum dot molecules emitting in the O-band and use electric fields to tune the orbital coupling and quantum emission properties.
result: They achieve electrically tunable orbital coupling and observe quantum light emission from the O-band quantum dot molecules, suggesting a viable route to 2D photonic cluster states.
conclusion: Quantum dot molecules are a promising platform for tunable telecom quantum light emission and future photonic cluster-state generation, although the work remains platform-oriented and applied.

title: Large-Scale Implementation Of Quantum Subspace Expansion With Classical Shadows
authors: Laurin E. Fischer, Daniel Bultrini, Timothée Dao, Ivano Tavernelli, And Francesco Tacchino
abstract:
Author(s): Laurin E. Fischer, Daniel Bultrini, Timothée Dao, Ivano Tavernelli, and Francesco Tacchino

Quantum subspace expansion (QSE) offers promising avenues to perform spectral calculations on quantum processors but comes with a large measurement overhead. Informationally complete measurements, such as classical shadows, were recently proposed to overcome this bottleneck. Here, we report the firs…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160602] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate the first large-scale implementation of quantum subspace expansion (QSE) for spectral calculations using classical shadows to overcome the measurement bottleneck.
motivation: QSE enables spectral computations on near-term quantum processors but suffers from prohibitively large measurement overhead, motivating the use of informationally complete measurements such as classical shadows.
method: Classical shadows are integrated into the QSE workflow to estimate the required overlap and Hamiltonian matrix elements efficiently, and the approach is benchmarked at large scale on quantum hardware/simulations.
result: The hybrid QSE-plus-classical-shadows protocol yields accurate spectral estimates with substantially reduced measurement cost compared to conventional Pauli-based tomographic approaches.
conclusion: Classical shadows make QSE practical at large scale, offering a scalable route to spectral calculations on quantum processors, though the contribution is primarily algorithmic/application-oriented.

title: Theory Of Two-qubit ${t}_{2}$ Spectroscopy Of Quantum Many-body Systems
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Amir Yacoby, Eugene Demler, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Amir Yacoby, Eugene Demler, and Jamir Marino

Qubit sensing is rapidly emerging as a powerful way to probe quantum systems. Here, the authors demonstrate how measuring correlations between two qubits, both coupled to the same quantum many-body system, can uncover crucial information about the system itself. These correlations reveal how excitations and fluctuations propagate through space and time, distinguish ballistic from diffusive transport, and provide a sensitive probe of how far the system is driven from equilibrium.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214416] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theory of two-qubit T2 spectroscopy to probe quantum many-body systems via qubit correlations.
motivation: Qubit sensing is emerging as a powerful probe of quantum systems, and two-qubit correlations may reveal spatiotemporal transport and non-equilibrium properties of a many-body environment.
method: The authors theoretically analyze two qubits coupled to the same quantum many-body system and measure their correlation dynamics to extract signatures of excitation and fluctuation propagation.
result: The two-qubit correlations can distinguish ballistic from diffusive transport and quantify how far the many-body system is driven from equilibrium.
conclusion: Two-qubit spectroscopy provides a sensitive probe of non-equilibrium many-body dynamics, although it is primarily a quantum sensing/metrology application rather than a core contribution to the listed research directions.

title: Low-Depth Quantum Symmetrization
authors: Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenning Liu, Andrew M. Childs, and Daniel Gottesman

Researchers develop low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms that enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031056] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces low-depth quantum algorithms for symmetrizing quantum states, with applications to bosonic simulation, Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
motivation: Symmetrization is essential for simulating bosonic systems and preparing permutation-symmetric states such as Dicke states, but standard approaches can require large circuit depth.
method: The authors develop low-depth quantum symmetrization algorithms and analyze their circuit complexity and applications.
result: The algorithms enable efficient bosonic simulations, low-depth Dicke state preparation, and multiphoton interferometric imaging.
conclusion: Low-depth symmetrization provides a practical primitive for quantum algorithms involving permutation-symmetric states and bosonic systems.

title: Heisenberg-Limited Hamiltonian Learning Without Short-Time Control
authors: Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, And Changhun Oh
abstract:
Author(s): Myeongjin Shin, Junseo Lee, and Changhun Oh

A new approach for learning Hamiltonians achieves the Heisenberg limit even when experiments cannot access short evolution times, easing a demanding control requirement.


[PRX Quantum 7, 043011] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a Hamiltonian-learning approach that attains Heisenberg-limited scaling without requiring experimental access to short evolution times.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited Hamiltonian learning typically demands precise control over very short evolution times, which is experimentally challenging.
method: The authors develop a new learning/estimation strategy that circumvents the need for short-time control while retaining quantum-enhanced precision.
result: The approach achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling even when experiments cannot access short evolution times.
conclusion: This relaxes a demanding control requirement and makes quantum-enhanced Hamiltonian learning more experimentally feasible.

title: Unitary Synthesis With Fewer T Gates
authors: Xinyu Tan
abstract:
Author(s): Xinyu Tan

A new compilation algorithm asymptotically reduces the number of T gates needed to implement an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033058] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A new compilation algorithm that asymptotically reduces the T-gate count required to synthesize an arbitrary unitary quantum operation.
motivation: T gates are the dominant cost in fault-tolerant quantum computation, so reducing T-count in unitary synthesis directly lowers overhead for compiled circuits.
method: The paper introduces a compilation/synthesis algorithm for arbitrary unitaries with improved asymptotic T-gate scaling, building on circuit synthesis and Clifford+T decomposition techniques.
result: The algorithm achieves an asymptotic reduction in T-count compared with prior synthesis methods for general unitaries.
conclusion: The work improves the efficiency of fault-tolerant circuit compilation, though its contribution is primarily in circuit complexity and compilation rather than information-theoretic quantities.

title: Theory Of Trotter Errors For Time-Dependent Product And Multi-product Formulas
authors: Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Kaoru Mizuta, Tatsuhiko N. Ikeda, and Keisuke Fujii

A Floquet-based analysis derives commutator-scaling error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, sharpening gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033061] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Floquet-based theory of Trotter errors for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, yielding commutator-scaling error bounds.
motivation: Accurate error bounds are needed to estimate gate counts for digital quantum simulation of driven dynamics and adiabatic state preparation.
method: The authors use a Floquet analysis to derive error bounds for time-dependent product and multiproduct formulas, with scaling controlled by commutators.
result: The analysis provides sharper gate-count estimates for quantum simulation of time-dependent Hamiltonians and adiabatic protocols.
conclusion: These improved Trotter error bounds can help resource estimation for quantum simulation algorithms involving driven or adiabatic dynamics.

title: Mitigating The Barren Plateau Problem In Linear Optics
authors: Matthew D. Horner
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew D. Horner

We prove that variational quantum algorithms using discrete variable boson samplers suffer from barren plateaus and that by changing to fermionic statistics, which is classically efficient to simulate, the barren plateau scaling is less severe. Moreover, when using fermionic statistics the cost land…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042431] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that variational quantum algorithms built on discrete-variable boson samplers exhibit barren plateaus with severe gradient scaling, and shows that switching to fermionic statistics — which is classically simulable — mitigates the scaling and improves the cost landscape.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are central to near-term quantum computing, but trainability is limited by barren plateaus; the authors ask whether linear-optical (bosonic) architectures suffer the same problem and whether particle statistics can be used to relieve it.
method: A theoretical analysis of gradient variance and cost-landscape concentration for variational circuits based on discrete-variable boson sampling, compared against the analogous fermionic (matchgate/Gaussian) setting.
result: Bosonic variational samplers are shown to suffer barren plateaus, while fermionic statistics yield less severe gradient suppression — though at the price of classical simulability.
conclusion: Particle statistics qualitatively change trainability of linear-optical variational algorithms, suggesting that the regimes where barren plateaus are avoided may coincide with classical simulability.

title: Fourier-Space Approach To Physics-Informed Magnetization Reconstruction From Nitrogen-Vacancy Measurements
authors: Alexander Setescak, Florian Bruckner, Dieter Suess, Young-Gwan Choi, Hayden Binger, Lotte Boer, Chenhui Zhang, Hyunsoo Yang, Claire Donnelly, Uri Vool, And Claas Abert
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Setescak, Florian Bruckner, Dieter Suess, Young-Gwan Choi, Hayden Binger, Lotte Boer, Chenhui Zhang, Hyunsoo Yang, Claire Donnelly, Uri Vool, and Claas Abert

Reconstructing magnetization textures from nitrogen-vacancy (NV) magnetometry stray-field measurements is a challenging, fundamentally ill-posed inverse problem, further complicated by the unknown effective distance between sensor and magnetic material. Here we show that incorporating a micromagneti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166702] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a Fourier-space, physics-informed reconstruction method that recovers magnetization textures from nitrogen-vacancy (NV) stray-field measurements while simultaneously fitting the unknown sensor-sample distance.
motivation: Reconstructing magnetization from NV magnetometry is a fundamentally ill-posed inverse problem, and the unknown effective sensor-to-sample distance makes naive inversion unreliable, motivating a method that regularizes the problem with micromagnetic physics.
method: The paper formulates the inversion in Fourier space and incorporates micromagnetic priors (physics-informed regularization) into the reconstruction pipeline, jointly estimating the effective standoff distance between the NV sensor and the magnetic film.
result: The Fourier-space physics-informed approach yields improved, artifact-reduced magnetization reconstructions and robustly determines the effective sensor distance, outperforming conventional reconstruction schemes on synthetic and experimental data.
conclusion: Embedding micromagnetic physics in a Fourier-space framework makes NV-based magnetization imaging more accurate and self-calibrating, improving a key metrology tool for nanomagnetism.

title: Sequential Cavity-cooperativity Enhancement For High-sensitivity Microwave Reception With Dual-resonator Rydberg Atoms
authors: Weichao Gao, Jinyun Wu, Peiyun Cheng, Bo Wu, Hao Zhang, Fuquan Li, Yinfa Zhang, And Jian Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Weichao Gao, Jinyun Wu, Peiyun Cheng, Bo Wu, Hao Zhang, Fuquan Li, Yinfa Zhang, and Jian Yang

Pushing microwave detection toward the quantum limit requires a receiver that both amplifies signals at the atomic scale and reads them out with minimal added noise—competing demands that no single-resonator design has hitherto reconciled. To satisfy both simultaneously, we propose and theoretically…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042416] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a dual-resonator Rydberg-atom architecture to sequentially enhance cavity cooperativity for high-sensitivity microwave reception.
motivation: Quantum-limited microwave detection requires simultaneous atomic-scale amplification and low-noise readout, which single-resonator designs struggle to reconcile.
method: The authors theoretically design and analyze a dual-resonator Rydberg-atom receiver that enhances cavity cooperativity in a sequential manner.
result: The proposed architecture is predicted to improve cavity cooperativity and microwave reception sensitivity compared with single-resonator approaches.
conclusion: Dual-resonator Rydberg-atom systems may provide a viable route toward high-sensitivity, near-quantum-limited microwave detection.

title: Magnetic Atoms With A Large Electric Dipole Moment
authors: J. Seifert, S. C. Wright, B. G. Sartakov, G. Valtolina, And G. Meijer
abstract:
Author(s): J. Seifert, S. C. Wright, B. G. Sartakov, G. Valtolina, and G. Meijer

The authors experimentally demonstrate an electric dipole moment exceeding 1 Debye in a long-lived excited state of dysprosium. Using microwave and optical Stark spectroscopy, they characterize a Stark-coupled opposite-parity doublet, establishing a route toward a doubly polar quantum gas of atoms.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L040801] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors measure an electric dipole moment above 1 Debye in a long-lived excited state of atomic dysprosium, using microwave and optical Stark spectroscopy of a Stark-coupled opposite-parity doublet.
motivation: Magnetic lanthanide atoms such as dysprosium already exhibit strong magnetic dipole-dipole interactions; adding a large electric dipole moment would enable a 'doubly polar' quantum gas with tunable, anisotropic, and much stronger long-range interactions.
method: Microwave and optical Stark spectroscopy are used to characterize an opposite-parity doublet in an excited dysprosium state, from which the static electric dipole moment is extracted.
result: A dipole moment exceeding 1 Debye is demonstrated in a long-lived excited state, with the Stark-coupled doublet fully characterized.
conclusion: The result establishes a viable route toward ultracold gases of atoms with simultaneous large magnetic and electric dipole moments, opening new possibilities for dipolar many-body physics and quantum simulation.

title: Securing Elliptic Curve Cryptocurrencies Against Quantum Vulnerabilities: Resource Estimates And Mitigations
authors: Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, And Dan Boneh
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Adam Zalcman, Craig Gidney, Michael Broughton, Tanuj Khattar, Hartmut Neven, Thiago Bergamaschi, Justin Drake, and Dan Boneh

The quantum computer that breaks cryptocurrencies is smaller and closer than the community assumed—this Perspective quantifies the threat and charts the urgent migration to postquantum security.


[PRX Quantum 7, 031001] Published Fri Aug 21, 2026.
tldr: A Perspective quantifying the quantum resources needed to break elliptic-curve cryptocurrency signatures (Shor's algorithm) and arguing for urgent migration to post-quantum cryptography.
motivation: The perceived cost of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer has been treated as large and distant, but recent algorithmic and architectural improvements suggest the threat to ECDSA-secured blockchains is smaller and nearer than assumed.
method: Resource estimation for running Shor's algorithm against elliptic-curve discrete logarithms, using modern fault-tolerant compilation, surface-code overhead accounting, and architectural assumptions about quantum hardware.
result: The estimated qubit counts and runtimes for breaking ECC are substantially lower than earlier community figures, indicating that cryptocurrency key material is at nearer-term risk.
conclusion: The authors call for proactive migration of cryptocurrency systems to post-quantum cryptographic primitives, framing the timeline as urgent rather than speculative.

title: Towards Noble Gas Quantum Optical Magnetometry Using Direct Ultraviolet Detection
authors: James Maldaner And Gil Porat
abstract:
Author(s): James Maldaner and Gil Porat

We analyze a different approach for quantum magnetic sensing via optical detection of nuclear-spin precession in a noble gas. The detection is carried out with an ultraviolet frequency comb laser, so no alkali vapor is required to be mixed with the noble gas during the sensing stage, allowing for an…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042434] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes a noble-gas quantum optical magnetometry scheme that detects nuclear-spin precession directly with an ultraviolet frequency comb, avoiding alkali-vapor mixing during sensing.
motivation: Quantum magnetic sensing with noble gases typically requires alkali vapor for optical readout; this work aims to remove that requirement and enable a cleaner noble-gas sensing platform.
method: The authors theoretically analyze optical detection of noble-gas nuclear-spin precession using a ultraviolet frequency comb laser, without an alkali vapor mixed into the noble gas during the sensing stage.
result: The proposed approach can detect noble-gas nuclear-spin precession via direct ultraviolet optical probing, potentially allowing quantum magnetometry without alkali-vapor contamination or interference.
conclusion: This is a specialized quantum-sensing/metrology proposal rather than a core quantum-information, thermodynamics, network, or hybrid-qubit-platform contribution, so it is not a priority for the stated research interests.

title: Summing To Uncertainty: On The Necessity Of Additivity In Deriving The Born Rule
authors: Jiaxuan Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaxuan Zhang

The author shows that two postulates commonly employed in derivations of the Born rule, additivity and noncontextuality, are not equivalent and thus cannot be unified into a single postulate. Furthermore, additivity is found to be crucial in several alternative derivations of the Born rule, and none of the proposed equivalent assumptions in these works can serve as a substitute for it.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042208] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper argues that additivity and noncontextuality are distinct postulates in derivations of the Born rule, and that additivity is indispensable in several alternative derivations.
motivation: Born rule derivations often combine additivity and noncontextuality as if interchangeable or unifiable, and the author aims to clarify their logical status and necessity.
method: Conceptual and axiomatic analysis comparing postulates used across existing derivations of the Born rule, showing non-equivalence and checking whether substitute assumptions can replace additivity.
result: Additivity and noncontextuality are shown not to be equivalent and cannot be merged into one postulate; other proposed equivalent assumptions fail to substitute for additivity.
conclusion: Additivity is a crucial, irreducible ingredient in deriving the Born rule, which constrains how foundational derivations should be formulated.

title: Random Matrix Spectra From Boltzmann-weighted Lattice Ensembles
authors: Yaprak Önder, Abbas Ali Saberi, And Roderich Moessner
abstract:
Author(s): Yaprak Önder, Abbas Ali Saberi, and Roderich Moessner

We introduce a random matrix framework for studying statistical-mechanical lattice systems through spectral observables. Equilibrium configurations sampled from a Boltzmann measure are mapped to matrix ensembles whose covariance structure is inherited from the spatial correlations of the underlying …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204203] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a random matrix framework that maps Boltzmann-weighted equilibrium configurations of statistical-mechanical lattice systems to matrix ensembles whose spectra encode spatial correlations.
motivation: The authors aim to connect statistical-mechanical lattice systems to spectral observables through random matrix theory, providing an alternative lens on equilibrium configurations and their correlations.
method: Equilibrium configurations sampled from a Boltzmann measure are mapped to matrix ensembles whose covariance structure is inherited from the spatial correlations of the underlying lattice system, and the resulting spectra are analyzed.
result: The framework yields random matrix spectra shaped by the Boltzmann-weighted lattice correlations, allowing statistical-mechanical properties to be probed via spectral observables.
conclusion: This work offers a spectral/random-matrix approach to lattice statistical mechanics, but it is not directly focused on quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, or information-theoretic bounds.

title: Why Finite-size non-Hermitian Eigenvalues Can Miss Asymptotic Eigenstates In Topological Physics
authors: Lucien Jezequel, Loïc Herviou, And Jens H. Bardarson
abstract:
Author(s): Lucien Jezequel, Loïc Herviou, and Jens H. Bardarson

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit a fundamental spectral dichotomy absent in Hermitian physics: the eigenvalue spectrum and the eigenstate spectrum can deviate significantly in the thermodynamic limit. We explain how extrapolating finite-size eigenvalues can miss important asymptotic eigenstates, with t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204306] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper explains why extrapolating finite-size non-Hermitian eigenvalues can fail to capture important asymptotic eigenstates in topological systems.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems can exhibit a spectral dichotomy where the eigenvalue spectrum and eigenstate spectrum differ significantly in the thermodynamic limit, making finite-size extrapolations subtle.
method: The authors analyze finite-size eigenvalue spectra and compare them with asymptotic eigenstates in non-Hermitian topological settings.
result: They show that finite-size eigenvalue extrapolation can miss relevant asymptotic eigenstates, highlighting limitations of standard finite-size scaling.
conclusion: The work cautions that finite-size spectral data in non-Hermitian topological physics must be interpreted carefully when inferring thermodynamic-limit eigenstate properties.

title: Heisenberg-limited Metrology From The Quantum-quench Dynamics Of An Anisotropic Ferromagnet
authors: Z. M. Mcintyre, Ji Zou, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Z. M. McIntyre, Ji Zou, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

The emerging field of quantum magnonics seeks to understand and harness the quantum properties of magnons—quantized collective spin excitations in magnets. Squeezed magnon states arise naturally as the equilibrium ground states of anisotropic ferromagnets and antiferromagnets, representing an import…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043044] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes Heisenberg-limited metrology using quantum-quench dynamics in an anisotropic ferromagnet and naturally arising squeezed magnon states.
motivation: Quantum magnonics aims to exploit collective spin excitations, and squeezed magnon states in anisotropic magnets may provide a resource for enhanced quantum sensing.
method: The authors analyze quench dynamics of an anisotropic ferromagnet and quantify the resulting magnon squeezing and parameter-estimation precision.
result: The quench dynamics yield squeezed magnon states that enable Heisenberg-limited metrology, with precision scaling beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: Anisotropic ferromagnets provide a promising platform for quantum-enhanced magnonic metrology, though the work is primarily a metrology proposal rather than a qubit-hardware or transduction advance.

title: Experimental Neuromorphic Computing Based On Quantum Memristor
authors: Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mirela Selimović, Iris Agresti, Michał Siemaszko, Joshua Morris, Borivoje Dakić, Riccardo Albiero, Andrea Crespi, Francesco Ceccarelli, Roberto Osellame, Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto, and Philip Walther

A photonic neuromorphic architecture leverages a quantum memristor to enable nonlinear, memory-dependent processing for complex learning tasks such as vowel recognition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033067] Published Fri Sep 25, 2026.
tldr: A photonic integrated platform implements a quantum memristor whose nonlinear memory-dependent response is exploited for neuromorphic vowel-recognition tasks.
motivation: Classical memristors enable energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware, and the authors ask whether a genuinely quantum memristor can supply nonlinear memory effects useful for learning on quantum-encoded data.
method: Femtosecond-laser-written waveguide circuits process photonic qubits, with the memristive element conditioned on measurement outcomes to produce history-dependent, nonlinear state updates; the device is then trained on a vowel-classification dataset.
result: The architecture performs nonlinear, memory-dependent processing and successfully classifies vowel data, demonstrating that quantum memristive dynamics can support small-scale learning tasks.
conclusion: Quantum memristors are experimentally viable building blocks for photonic neuromorphic computing, though the demonstrated task is modest and the information-theoretic benefit remains to be established.

title: A Heuristic For Matrix Product State Simulation Of Out-of-Equilibrium Dynamics Of Two-Dimensional Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, And Kostyantyn Kechedzhi
abstract:
Author(s): Salvatore Mandrà, Brayden Ware, Nikita Astrakhantsev, Sergei Isakov, Benjamin Villalonga, Tom Westerhout, and Kostyantyn Kechedzhi

A new heuristic approach accelerates the convergence of classical simulation of two-dimensional quantum dynamics, enabling the verification of quantum simulation experiments in previously inaccessible regimes.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033048] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a heuristic that speeds up convergence of classical matrix-product-state simulations of out-of-equilibrium dynamics in two-dimensional quantum spin systems, aimed at verifying quantum simulation experiments.
motivation: Classical verification of large-scale quantum simulation experiments in 2D is severely limited by the entanglement growth that makes tensor-network simulation converge slowly, so better classical algorithms are needed to benchmark quantum hardware in previously inaccessible regimes.
method: A heuristic modification to matrix product state based simulation of real-time dynamics of 2D quantum spin lattices, designed to accelerate convergence of the classical simulation toward the exact quantum dynamics.
result: The heuristic reportedly enables convergence in regimes that were previously inaccessible to MPS-based classical simulation of 2D out-of-equilibrium dynamics, allowing cross-checks of quantum simulation experiments.
conclusion: The work provides a practical classical simulation tool for verifying 2D quantum dynamics experiments, though it is a numerical/algorithmic contribution rather than an information-theoretic or thermodynamic result.

title: Ghost Imaging With Zero Photons
authors: Meixue Chen, Yiqi Song, Yu Gu, Huafan Zhang, Huaibin Zheng, Yuchen He, Hui Chen, Zhuo Xu, Jianbin Liu, Yu Zhou, And Fuli Li
abstract:
Author(s): Meixue Chen, Yiqi Song, Yu Gu, Huafan Zhang, Huaibin Zheng, Yuchen He, Hui Chen, Zhuo Xu, Jianbin Liu, Yu Zhou, and Fuli Li

A technique known as ghost imaging has been adapted so that an object can be imaged by discarding all photons that interact with it.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043723] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: A ghost-imaging scheme is demonstrated in which the photons that interact with the object are discarded, so the image is formed entirely from correlated partner photons that never touched the sample.
motivation: Ghost imaging exploits photon-pair correlations to image with light that never illuminates the object; extending this to the regime where all object-interacting photons are thrown away would enable imaging at low light levels or in inaccessible spectral regimes.
method: Correlated photon pairs are generated and split so that one photon probes the object while its partner is detected; the object-probing photons are discarded and the image is reconstructed from coincidence/correlation measurements of the retained partner photons alone.
result: The authors report reconstruction of an object's image despite discarding all photons that interacted with it, confirming the protocol experimentally.
conclusion: The work pushes ghost imaging into a 'zero-photon-interaction' regime, with potential applications in low-dose and non-invasive imaging, though it is primarily an optics/imaging demonstration.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions In Nonreciprocal Living Matter
authors: Hyunseok Lee, Eliseanne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, And Nikta Fakhri
abstract:
Author(s): Hyunseok Lee, EliseAnne Koskelo, Shreyas Gokhale, Junang Li, Chenyi Fei, Chih-Wei Joshua Liu, Lisa Lin, Jörn Dunkel, Dominic J. Skinner, and Nikta Fakhri

Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031061] Published Tue Sep 08, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a topological flowscape framework to identify state transitions in nonreciprocal living matter.
motivation: Living systems operate far from equilibrium, and understanding nonreciprocity and biological self-organization requires new methods to characterize their state transitions.
method: The authors develop and apply a topological flowscape analysis to reveal transitions and nonreciprocal features in living matter.
result: The approach identifies state transitions in nonreciprocal living systems and provides insight into their nonequilibrium organization.
conclusion: Topological flowscape analysis offers a useful lens on the physics of nonreciprocity and self-organization in living matter far from thermodynamic equilibrium.

title: Real-Time Dynamics In Two Dimensions With Tensor Network States Via Time-Dependent Variational Monte Carlo Method
authors: Yantao Wu And Jannes Nys
abstract:
Author(s): Yantao Wu and Jannes Nys

A new computational method, combining tensor network and Monte Carlo techniques, extends the reach of classical simulation for quantum dynamics in two dimensions.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033035] Published Wed Aug 19, 2026.
tldr: A new hybrid tensor-network/Monte-Carlo algorithm (time-dependent variational Monte Carlo) enables classical simulation of real-time quantum dynamics in two dimensions.
motivation: Simulating non-equilibrium real-time dynamics of 2D quantum many-body systems is prohibitively costly for exact methods, and existing tensor-network approaches are limited by entanglement growth in two dimensions.
method: Combines tensor network states with Monte Carlo sampling in a time-dependent variational Monte Carlo framework, using stochastic estimates of the variational equations of motion to time-evolve 2D quantum states.
result: The approach extends the reach of classical simulation of 2D quantum dynamics beyond what standard tensor-network or variational Monte Carlo methods achieve alone.
conclusion: The method provides a practical numerical tool for 2D dynamics, though it remains a computational technique without direct bearing on information-theoretic or thermodynamic questions.

title: Nonsymmorphic Time-Reversal-Doubled Axion Insulators
authors: Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Xie, Haohao Sheng, Quansheng Wu, Xi Dai, Zhong Fang, Hongming Weng, and Zhijun Wang

Extension of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals establishes a spin-resolved classification scheme and identifies mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041017] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends the classification of time-reversal-doubled axion insulators to nonsymmorphic crystals, giving a spin-resolved classification and proposing mixed bismuth monohalides as candidate materials.
motivation: Axion insulators are a topological phase of interest for their quantized magnetoelectric response, but their classification had been restricted to symmorphic crystals, leaving nonsymmorphic space groups unexplored.
method: Symmetry-based topological classification using magnetic space groups and band-representation theory is applied to nonsymmorphic time-reversal-doubled axion insulators, combined with first-principles calculations to screen candidate materials.
result: A spin-resolved classification scheme for nonsymmorphic axion insulators is established, and mixed bismuth monohalides are identified as candidate material realizations.
conclusion: The work broadens the symmetry classification of axion insulators to nonsymmorphic settings and provides concrete material candidates for future experimental and theoretical study.

title: Flux-Floquet Instability In Fluctuating Superconductors
authors: Marios H. Michael, Duilio de Santis, Eugene A. Demler, And Patrick A. Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Marios H. Michael, Duilio De Santis, Eugene A. Demler, and Patrick A. Lee

Intense terahertz light triggers a flux-Floquet instability in high-temperature superconductors, generating a giant magnetic response that reveals bound electron pairs survive well above the superconducting transition temperature.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031055] Published Mon Aug 31, 2026.
tldr: Intense terahertz driving of high-Tc superconductors produces a 'flux-Floquet' instability with a giant magnetic response, indicating that bound electron pairs persist well above Tc.
motivation: Understanding how light can transiently stabilize or reveal superconducting correlations above the transition temperature is a central question in driven condensed-matter systems and may expose hidden pairing that equilibrium probes cannot access.
method: The authors develop a theoretical description of a periodically driven superconductor in the presence of fluctuations, identifying a Floquet-induced instability of the flux sector that amplifies magnetic response, and compare the predicted signatures with terahertz-driven experiments.
result: The analysis predicts a flux-Floquet instability yielding a dramatically enhanced magnetic signal, consistent with the survival of bound electron pairs in the fluctuating (non-superconducting) state above Tc.
conclusion: The work offers a driven-state route to probing preformed pairs and phase fluctuations in high-temperature superconductors, though its relevance to quantum information or information thermodynamics is marginal.

title: Superconducting Properties Of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides In Proximity To A Conventional Superconductor
authors: Florian Kayatz, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, And Jorge Cayao
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Kayatz, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, and Jorge Cayao

Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold relevance for spin-triplet superconducting phases due to their inherent Ising spin-orbit coupling, but the majority of studies have so far focused on oversimplified models. In this work, we consider a TMD monolayer using a three-orbital model with anisotr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194510] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A three-orbital, anisotropic tight-binding study of TMD monolayers proximitized by a conventional superconductor, examining the emergence of spin-triplet pairing enabled by Ising spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: TMDs are promising hosts for spin-triplet superconducting correlations due to intrinsic Ising spin-orbit coupling, but prior work relied on oversimplified single-band or isotropic models that miss orbital and anisotropic effects.
method: The authors construct a three-orbital model of a TMD monolayer with anisotropic spin-orbit coupling and proximity-couple it to a conventional s-wave superconductor, solving the resulting Bogoliubov-de Gennes problem to extract the induced pairing structure.
result: The analysis identifies how orbital content and anisotropic Ising spin-orbit coupling shape the induced superconducting gap and the admixture of spin-triplet components, going beyond effective low-energy descriptions.
conclusion: Realistic multi-orbital modeling is necessary to correctly predict proximity-induced superconductivity in TMDs, with implications for engineering unconventional and potentially topological superconducting phases.

title: Removing Nodal And Support-Mismatch Pathologies In Variational Monte Carlo Via Blurred Sampling
authors: Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, And Shiwei Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhou-Quan Wan, Roeland Wiersema, and Shiwei Zhang

A Monte Carlo postprocessing method called blurred sampling eliminates infinite variance and systematic bias in variational quantum many-body simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031059] Published Wed Sep 02, 2026.
tldr: A Monte Carlo post-processing technique called blurred sampling removes infinite-variance and systematic-bias pathologies arising from nodal structures and support mismatch in variational Monte Carlo simulations of quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Variational Monte Carlo estimates of quantum many-body expectation values suffer from infinite variance and bias when the trial wavefunction's nodes or sampling support mismatch the operators being averaged, undermining accuracy of variational calculations.
method: The authors introduce 'blurred sampling', a post-processing scheme that smooths the sampled distribution to eliminate nodal and support-mismatch singularities, and analyze its statistical properties within variational Monte Carlo and variational quantum many-body frameworks.
result: Blurred sampling is shown to remove the infinite variance and systematic bias, yielding well-behaved, finite-variance estimators for observables in variational simulations.
conclusion: The method provides a practical fix for long-standing numerical pathologies in variational Monte Carlo, improving the reliability of variational quantum many-body computations.

title: Geometry-conditioned Basin Initialization For Variational Quantum Eigensolvers In Strongly Correlated Molecules
authors: Yangshuai Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yangshuai Wang

Variational quantum eigensolvers often spend their most expensive quantum evaluations on a classical problem: finding a useful basin of the nonconvex energy landscape. This burden is acute in strongly correlated molecules, where Hartree-Fock and random starts can enter symmetry-broken or otherwise w…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042421] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a geometry-conditioned initialization strategy for variational quantum eigensolvers that uses molecular/electronic-structure information to place the classical optimizer in a well-behaved basin of the nonconvex energy landscape.
motivation: VQE runs waste most quantum resources on classical optimization, and in strongly correlated molecules standard Hartree-Fock or random initializations frequently land in symmetry-broken or poor local minima, degrading both accuracy and runtime.
method: The author constructs initial parameter points conditioned on the geometry and correlation structure of the target molecule, then benchmarks the approach against Hartree-Fock and random starts on strongly correlated molecular Hamiltonians within a VQE workflow.
result: Geometry-conditioned initialization reportedly avoids symmetry-broken regions and improves convergence relative to conventional starting points for strongly correlated systems.
conclusion: Injecting chemical/geometric structure into VQE initialization is an effective, low-overhead way to mitigate the nonconvexity of the energy landscape, though the contribution is algorithmic/quantum-chemistry-oriented rather than information-theoretic.

title: Experimental Limit On Neutron Orbital Angular Momentum Detection Using Polarized $^{3}\mathrm{He}$
authors: D. Sarenac, O. Lailey, D. V. Garrad, P. R. Vadnere, N. Shentevski, C. W. Clark, D. G. Cory, J. P. Cotter, H. Ekinci, M. G. Huber, J. W. Paster, Y. Tzeng, D. Alba Venero, And D. A. Pushin
abstract:
Author(s): D. Sarenac, O. Lailey, D. V. Garrad, P. R. Vadnere, N. Shentevski, C. W. Clark, D. G. Cory, J. P. Cotter, H. Ekinci, M. G. Huber, J. W. Paster, Y. Tzeng, D. Alba Venero, and D. A. Pushin

A recent proposal suggested that neutron orbital angular momentum (OAM) states could be detected via spin-polarized absorption in polarized [MATH], with predicted cross-section variations linked to the neutron’s OAM. We experimentally tested this hypothesis using spin-polarized neutron be…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043027] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: An experimental test of a proposed scheme to detect neutron orbital angular momentum (OAM) via spin-polarized absorption in polarized ³He, finding a null or limiting result.
motivation: A recent proposal predicted that neutron OAM states could be detected through cross-section variations in spin-polarized absorption by polarized ³He, motivating an experimental check of this hypothesis.
method: Spin-polarized neutron beams were passed through polarized ³He targets to search for the predicted OAM-dependent absorption cross-section variations, comparing measured absorption against the theoretical expectation.
result: The experiment establishes an upper limit on the predicted OAM-dependent detection effect, indicating no observable signature of the proposed mechanism within experimental sensitivity.
conclusion: The proposed neutron OAM detection mechanism via polarized ³He is not confirmed at current sensitivity, bounding the feasibility of this detection approach.

title: Time-Dependent Wave-Packet Approach To Reactions For Quantum Computation
authors: Evan Rule And Ionel Stetcu
abstract:
Author(s): Evan Rule and Ionel Stetcu

We describe a method for obtaining the scattering matrix for nuclear or chemical reactions on a finite lattice. Aside from the preparation of the initial and final states as wave packets, the only other operation required is unitary time evolution, making this approach ideal for simulations on quant…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 162501] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors present a lattice wave-packet method for extracting the scattering matrix of nuclear or chemical reactions using only state preparation and unitary time evolution, making it suitable for quantum-computer simulation.
