motivation: Scattering and reaction cross sections are hard to compute classically for strongly interacting many-body systems, motivating algorithms that map naturally onto quantum hardware.
method: Initial and final asymptotic states are prepared as wave packets on a finite lattice; the S-matrix elements are then extracted from overlaps after unitary time evolution under the interacting Hamiltonian.
result: The protocol requires only wave-packet preparation and time evolution, avoiding explicit adiabatic switching or complex-time methods, and is argued to be well suited to near-term quantum simulation.
conclusion: The approach offers a hardware-friendly route to reaction scattering for nuclear and chemical physics, but is a quantum-simulation algorithm rather than a contribution to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Protocols For A Many-Body Phase Microscope: From Coherences And $d$-Wave Superconductivity To Green’s Functions
authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, And Fabian Grusdt
abstract:
Author(s): Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, and Fabian Grusdt

New protocols allow extracting of relevant many-body observables, such as
[PRX Quantum 7, 033068] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes quantum-gas-microscope measurement protocols that extract many-body observables such as d-wave superconducting order parameters, coherences, and Green's functions from cold-atom quantum simulators.
motivation: Quantum gas microscopes provide site-resolved access to strongly correlated fermionic systems, but connecting raw density/spin snapshots to physically meaningful many-body quantities like pairing order parameters and Green's functions requires dedicated measurement protocols.
method: The authors design and analyze experimental protocols, based on local addressing, coherent manipulation, and time-of-flight or interference techniques in state-of-the-art quantum gas microscopes, for reconstructing coherences, d-wave pairing correlations, and single-particle Green's functions.
result: The protocols are shown to enable extraction of relevant many-body observables, including superconducting order parameters, from realistic microscope data, bridging cold-atom experiments with condensed-matter observables.
conclusion: The work establishes practical measurement schemes that extend the capabilities of quantum gas microscopes toward characterizing correlated and paired quantum phases, though it lies outside the four targeted research directions.

title: Digital Dissipative State Preparation For Frustration-Free Gapless Quantum Systems
authors: Johannes Feldmeier, Yu-Jie Liu, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Soonwon Choi
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Feldmeier, Yu-Jie Liu, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Soonwon Choi

Preparing algebraically correlated ground states of quantum many-body systems is an important, yet challenging task for quantum simulation. We introduce a protocol that employs local projective measurements and unitary feedback for frustration-free gapless systems. Our approach prepares a priori unk…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 160404] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces a digital dissipative protocol using local projective measurements and unitary feedback to prepare algebraically correlated ground states of frustration-free gapless quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Preparing correlated ground states of gapless quantum many-body systems is a challenging task for quantum simulation, especially when the target states are not easily generated by conventional unitary circuits.
method: The authors propose a protocol that combines local projective measurements with unitary feedback to engineer dissipative dynamics for frustration-free gapless systems.
result: The protocol is shown to prepare algebraically correlated ground states in the gapless regime, addressing a setting that is difficult for existing state-preparation methods.
conclusion: This work offers a measurement-and-feedback approach to dissipative state preparation for gapless many-body systems, with potential relevance to quantum simulation.

title: Photons In Media: A Second-quantization Scheme Based On The Optical Dirac Equation
authors: Lili Yang, Longlong Feng, And Pengming Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Lili Yang, Longlong Feng, and Pengming Zhang

We develop a second-quantization framework for source-free photons based on an optical Dirac-like formulation of Maxwell theory. The analysis applies to the restricted class of spin-degenerate media considered here. The electromagnetic field is recast as a four-component spinorlike wave function con…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042210] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a second-quantization scheme for source-free photons in spin-degenerate media using an optical Dirac-like formulation of Maxwell theory.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a consistent quantum framework for photons propagating in media by leveraging an optical Dirac equation analogy.
method: Maxwell's equations in the restricted class of spin-degenerate media are recast as a four-component spinor-like wave equation, which is then second-quantized.
result: A second-quantized description of photons in such media is obtained within the optical Dirac formalism.
conclusion: The framework may offer a useful foundation for quantum optics in media, but it does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Nonlinear Subharmonic Response And Spectral Shifts In Bichromatically Driven Atomic Magnetic Resonance
authors: Xu-Xing Geng, Ao-Dong Xie, Cheng Sheng, Kai Jin, Jian-Feng Xiao, Wang-Wang Tang, Yan Yan, Guo-Qing Yang, Hui Huang, Guang-Ming Huang, Hong-Ping Liu, And Gao-Xiang Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xu-xing Geng, Ao-dong Xie, Cheng Sheng, Kai Jin, Jian-feng Xiao, Wang-wang Tang, Yan Yan, Guo-qing Yang, Hui Huang, Guang-ming Huang, Hong-Ping Liu, and Gao-xiang Li

Subharmonic resonances can provide spectral observables beyond the main atomic magnetic-resonance spectrum, but their physical origin and use under bichromatic driving remain unclear. We study cesium-vapor magnetic resonance driven by two rf fields. The first field serves as a calibrated local refer…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042811] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies nonlinear subharmonic resonances and spectral shifts in bichromatically driven cesium-vapor magnetic resonance.
motivation: Subharmonic resonances may provide spectral observables beyond the main atomic magnetic-resonance spectrum, but their origin and behavior under bichromatic driving are not well understood.
method: Cesium-vapor magnetic resonance is driven by two radio-frequency fields, with the first acting as a calibrated local reference, to characterize the nonlinear subharmonic response and spectral shifts.
result: The authors identify and analyze subharmonic resonance features and spectral shifts arising from the bichromatic driving.
conclusion: The work clarifies the physical origin and potential use of subharmonic resonances in bichromatically driven atomic magnetic resonance.

title: Nodal Line Semimetals With Nonquantized Berry Phase
authors: Zhi-Xia Li, Liangliang Huang, Min-Xue Yang, Feng Tang, D. Y. Xing, And Wei Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Xia Li, Liangliang Huang, Min-Xue Yang, Feng Tang, D. Y. Xing, and Wei Chen

Nodal line semimetals (NLSMs) are topological materials characterized by one-dimensional band crossings in momentum space, which typically carry a Berry phase quantized to integer multiples of [MATH]. Here, we extend the conventional paradigm to a class of NLSMs in which the Berry phase can take arbitr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225128] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors extend the paradigm of nodal-line semimetals to a class where the Berry phase around the nodal line is no longer quantized to integer multiples of pi but can take arbitrary values.
motivation: Conventional nodal-line semimetals are characterized by one-dimensional band crossings carrying a Berry phase quantized to integer multiples of pi, and the authors ask whether this quantization is fundamental or can be relaxed in a broader class of materials.
method: The work uses tight-binding/lattice model constructions combined with symmetry and topological-band-theory analysis to identify and characterize nodal-line semimetals whose Berry phase departs from the quantized values.
result: The paper demonstrates that a class of nodal-line semimetals exists in which the Berry phase can take arbitrary (nonquantized) values, and it identifies the symmetry and band-structure conditions under which this occurs.
conclusion: The quantized Berry phase of nodal-line semimetals is not universal; nonquantized Berry phases define a broader family of topological semimetals with potentially distinct surface and transport signatures.

title: Experimental Realization Of A Dusty Plasma Rocking Ratchet With Current Reversal
authors: Shun-Xin Zhang, Shuo Wang, Ting-Yu Yao, Yong-Liang Zhang, Bao-Quan Ai, And Ya-Feng He
abstract:
Author(s): Shun-xin Zhang, Shuo Wang, Ting-yu Yao, Yong-liang Zhang, Bao-quan Ai, and Ya-feng He

A single dust particle confined in an asymmetric ratchet potential is periodically driven by two oppositely directed laser beams, forming an underdamped dusty plasma rocking ratchet. We experimentally investigate the transport dynamics of the particle under varying driving amplitudes and frequencies…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045205] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: An experimental study of a single dust particle in an asymmetric ratchet potential driven by two oppositely directed laser beams, demonstrating a rocking ratchet with current reversal in a dusty plasma.
motivation: Ratchets convert unbiased fluctuations or periodic driving into directed transport, and the authors aim to realize and characterize such rectification in a classical, underdamped dusty-plasma setting where the direction of transport can be externally controlled.
method: A single dust particle is confined in an asymmetric potential and periodically driven by two counter-propagating laser beams, forming an underdamped rocking ratchet; transport dynamics are measured as a function of driving amplitude and frequency.
result: The particle exhibits directed net motion whose direction reverses as the driving parameters (amplitude/frequency) are varied, revealing the parameter regimes for normal and current-reversal ratchet behavior.
conclusion: The experiment demonstrates controllable current reversal in a dusty-plasma rocking ratchet, providing a classical platform for studying ratchet transport and offering tunable control over particle directionality.

title: Observable Scaling Hierarchies In Multiphoton Dissipative Quantum Sensing
authors: Shahram Panahiyan
abstract:
Author(s): Shahram Panahiyan

We investigate how quantum correlations in squeezed driving fields determine scaling laws in dissipative multiphoton quantum sensing. Independently squeezed fields yield factorized scaling, with separate absorption and emission contributions and nonlinear thresholds that suppress exponential scaling…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043035] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how correlations in squeezed driving fields set scaling laws for dissipative multiphoton quantum sensing.
motivation: Quantum sensing with squeezed and dissipative multiphoton dynamics may offer enhanced scaling, but the role of drive correlations in determining those scaling laws is unclear.
method: The author theoretically studies dissipative multiphoton quantum sensing under independently squeezed driving fields and derives observable scaling hierarchies from absorption and emission contributions.
result: Independently squeezed fields produce factorized scaling, with separate absorption and emission terms and nonlinear thresholds that suppress exponential scaling.
conclusion: Quantum correlations in squeezed drives qualitatively control sensing scaling, and threshold effects can limit exponential enhancement in dissipative multiphoton sensing.

title: Vanishing Phase Stiffness And Fluctuation-Dominated Superconductivity In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$
authors: Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, And B. J. Ramshaw
abstract:
Author(s): Sahas Kamat, Jared Dans, Shanta Saha, Daniel F. Agterberg, Johnpierre Paglione, and B. J. Ramshaw

Ultrasound measurements in uranium ditelluride (
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041006] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: Ultrasound measurements on UTe2 reveal superconducting phase fluctuations persisting up to twice Tc, indicating a vanishing phase stiffness and fluctuation-dominated superconductivity with large kinetic inductance.
motivation: UTe2 is an unusual heavy-fermion superconductor whose order parameter symmetry and pairing mechanism remain debated; the authors ask whether its superconductivity is weakened by phase fluctuations rather than by a small pairing amplitude.
method: The authors perform high-precision ultrasound (elastic modulus) measurements as a function of temperature on single-crystal UTe2 and extract the superfluid stiffness and fluctuation regime from the elastic response near and above Tc.
result: Superconducting precursor fluctuations are observed up to roughly 2Tc, implying an anomalously small superfluid phase stiffness in an otherwise clean material, which translates into a very large kinetic inductance.
conclusion: UTe2 lies in a fluctuation-dominated superconducting regime, with implications for its pairing state and possible use as a high-kinetic-inductance material.

title: Theory Of Quantum-Enhanced Interferometry With General Markovian Light Sources
authors: Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, And Rahul Trivedi
abstract:
Author(s): Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Daniel Malz, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, and Rahul Trivedi

A new framework for designing and evaluating quantum light sources clarifies where realistic devices can provide a quantum advantage in interferometry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033069] Published Tue Sep 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a theoretical framework for quantum-enhanced interferometry using general Markovian light sources and identifies conditions for realistic quantum advantage.
motivation: Quantum light sources are often idealized, so a general framework is needed to assess when realistic, Markovian sources can outperform classical interferometry.
method: The authors formulate a theory of interferometry with general Markovian light sources, enabling systematic design and evaluation of quantum-enhanced measurement protocols.
result: The framework clarifies parameter regimes where realistic quantum light sources provide an advantage and where they do not.
conclusion: This work offers guidance for designing practical quantum light sources and interferometric schemes with realistic noise and Markovian dynamics.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm For Nonlinear Fluid Dynamics With Bounded Quantum Advantage
authors: David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, And Stephen Rolston
abstract:
Author(s): David Jennings, Kamil Korzekwa, Matteo Lostaglio, Richard Ashworth, Emanuele Marsili, and Stephen Rolston

A detailed resource analysis identifies the fundamental bottlenecks and achievable speedups for nonlinear fluid simulations on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033060] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents an end-to-end fault-tolerant quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics and analyzes the resources required to achieve a bounded quantum advantage.
motivation: Nonlinear fluid simulations are computationally demanding, and quantum algorithms may offer speedups, but practical advantages require careful resource accounting under fault-tolerant quantum computing constraints.
method: The authors perform a detailed resource analysis of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for nonlinear fluid dynamics, identifying bottlenecks and achievable speedups on a fault-tolerant quantum computer.
result: The analysis identifies fundamental resource bottlenecks and characterizes the conditions under which bounded quantum advantage can be achieved for nonlinear fluid simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a resource-aware assessment of quantum advantage for nonlinear fluid dynamics, clarifying where fault-tolerant quantum computation may or may not provide practical benefits.

title: Mass-imbalanced Two-dimensional Bose-Fermi Mixtures With Boson-fermion Pairing
authors: Cristiano L. K. Chiarappa, Pietro Bovini, And Pierbiagio Pieri
abstract:
Author(s): Cristiano L. K. Chiarappa, Pietro Bovini, and Pierbiagio Pieri

We analyze a two-dimensional Bose-Fermi mixture at zero temperature in the presence of a tunable Bose-Fermi attraction. We adopt a diagrammatic [MATH]-matrix approach and study the behavior of several thermodynamic quantities for the two species as functions of density, mass ratio, and coupling strengt…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043307] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A T-matrix diagrammatic study of zero-temperature two-dimensional Bose-Fermi mixtures with tunable Bose-Fermi attraction, computing thermodynamic quantities versus density, mass ratio, and coupling.
motivation: Mass-imbalanced Bose-Fermi mixtures with pairing are relevant to ultracold-atom many-body physics, where the interplay of statistics, mass imbalance, and dimensionality is poorly understood in 2D.
method: The authors use a diagrammatic T-matrix (ladder) approximation to treat Bose-Fermi pairing at zero temperature and evaluate thermodynamic observables of both species as functions of density, mass ratio, and coupling strength.
result: Thermodynamic quantities for the bosonic and fermionic components are obtained across a range of densities, mass ratios, and interaction strengths, revealing how pairing and mass imbalance modify the mixture's equation of state and related properties.
conclusion: The results characterize the many-body behavior of 2D Bose-Fermi mixtures with boson-fermion pairing, providing reference predictions for ultracold-atom experiments.

title: Wilson-Loop-Ideal Bands And General Idealization
authors: Awwab A. Azam, Biao Lian, Shinsei Ryu, And Jiabin Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Awwab A. Azam, Biao Lian, Shinsei Ryu, and Jiabin Yu

Quantum geometry is universally bounded from below by Wilson-loop windings. In this Letter, we define an isolated set of bands to be Wilson-loop ideal, if their quantum metric saturates the Wilson-loop lower bound. The definition naturally incorporates the known Chern-ideal and Euler-ideal bands, an…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166601] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The Letter introduces the notion of 'Wilson-loop ideal' bands, an isolated set of bands whose quantum metric saturates the universal lower bound set by Wilson-loop windings, generalizing Chern-ideal and Euler-ideal bands.
motivation: Quantum geometry in band theory is bounded below by Wilson-loop windings, but a unifying framework capturing when this bound is saturated across different topological classes was lacking.
method: The authors define Wilson-loop idealization via saturation of the quantum-metric lower bound and analyze its consequences for band dispersion and topological character, subsuming known Chern-ideal and Euler-ideal constructions.
result: A general criterion for ideal quantum geometry is established, showing that Chern-ideal and Euler-ideal bands are special cases of the broader Wilson-loop-ideal class.
conclusion: Wilson-loop idealization provides a unified geometric characterization of flat-band-like systems, with implications for correlated band-structure physics rather than for quantum information processing.

title: Probability Distribution Analysis Of The Cascaded Variational Quantum Eigensolver
authors: Yi-Hua Lai, John P. T. Stenger, Gloria Bazargan, Igor V. Schweigert, And Daniel Gunlycke
abstract:
Author(s): Yi-Hua Lai, John P. T. Stenger, Gloria Bazargan, Igor V. Schweigert, and Daniel Gunlycke

The cascaded variational quantum eigensolver (CVQE) circumvents the need for iterative communication between the quantum and classical processing units that is necessary in the conventional VQE algorithm. While CVQE offers complete freedom to choose the guiding state as input, not all guiding states…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042436] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes probability distributions in the cascaded variational quantum eigensolver (CVQE) to understand how the choice of guiding state affects performance.
motivation: CVQE avoids iterative quantum-classical communication in conventional VQE, but its success depends on the guiding state, and not all guiding states are suitable.
method: The authors study the probability distribution arising in CVQE and relate it to the guiding state, likely using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They identify conditions or metrics on guiding states that determine the effectiveness of CVQE.
conclusion: The analysis provides guidance for selecting guiding states in CVQE, improving its practical applicability for quantum eigenvalue problems.

title: Thermal Ionization Of Impurity-bound Quasiholes In The Fractional Quantum Hall Effect
authors: Ke Huang, Sankar Das Sarma, And Xiao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Ke Huang, Sankar Das Sarma, and Xiao Li

We study the interplay between a Coulomb impurity and quasiholes in a fractional quantum Hall (FQH) state at finite temperatures. While a repulsive impurity can pin a quasihole and stabilize the FQH state, an attractive impurity cannot bind quasiholes. We demonstrate that at finite temperatures, a q…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194204] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies finite-temperature thermal ionization of impurity-bound quasiholes in fractional quantum Hall states.
motivation: Coulomb impurities can pin quasiholes and affect fractional quantum Hall stability, but the finite-temperature interplay between impurities and quasiholes is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze quasihole binding to repulsive and attractive Coulomb impurities in fractional quantum Hall systems at finite temperature.
result: Repulsive impurities can pin quasiholes and stabilize the FQH state, while attractive impurities cannot bind quasiholes; thermal ionization of bound quasiholes is characterized.
conclusion: The work clarifies how temperature and impurity sign affect quasihole binding and fractional quantum Hall state stability.

title: State Matrix Representations For The Unified Treatment Of non-Hermitian Photonic Multilayer Systems
authors: Anna A. Varvari, Nicholas S. Nye, Dimitrios I. Karatzidis, And Nikolaos V. Kantartzis
abstract:
Author(s): Anna A. Varvari, Nicholas S. Nye, Dimitrios I. Karatzidis, and Nikolaos V. Kantartzis

This work addresses a frequently overlooked aspect of one-dimensional non-Hermitian multilayered systems: the distinction between modal and operational non-Hermitian responses. While the scattering matrix is commonly used to identify special operational regimes in non-Hermitian systems, the full-sta…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204307] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops state-matrix formalisms to unify the treatment of modal versus operational non-Hermitian responses in one-dimensional photonic multilayer stacks.
motivation: Scattering matrices are widely used to identify exceptional-point and other non-Hermitian regimes in multilayers, but this can conflate modal properties of the structure with operationally observable responses; a full state-matrix description is argued to be needed to disentangle them.
method: Transfer/state-matrix representations are formulated for general one-dimensional non-Hermitian layered media and compared against scattering-matrix descriptions to isolate modal from operational behavior.
result: The state-matrix framework yields a unified account of non-Hermitian multilayer response, clarifying which features are intrinsic to the modes and which emerge only in scattering/operational quantities.
conclusion: The approach provides a cleaner conceptual and computational toolkit for designing and interpreting non-Hermitian photonic multilayer devices.

title: Sensitivity To Perturbations In The Three-dimensional Anderson Model
authors: Piotr Tokarczyk, Lev Vidmar, Anatoli Polkovnikov, And Patrycja Łydżba
abstract:
Author(s): Piotr Tokarczyk, Lev Vidmar, Anatoli Polkovnikov, and Patrycja Łydżba

We investigate the fidelity susceptibility, which quantifies the sensitivity of single-particle eigenstates to perturbations, in the three-dimensional Anderson model. As a function of disorder strength [MATH], it exhibits two distinct peaks. The first peak signals a crossover at weak disorder strength …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214203] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies fidelity susceptibility of single-particle eigenstates in the three-dimensional Anderson model and identifies two disorder-related peaks signaling distinct crossovers.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize how sensitive eigenstates are to perturbations in a disordered lattice and to connect this sensitivity to localization physics.
method: They compute the fidelity susceptibility for single-particle eigenstates of the 3D Anderson model as a function of disorder strength.
result: The fidelity susceptibility exhibits two distinct peaks; the first is associated with a weak-disorder crossover, while the second is likely tied to the Anderson localization transition.
conclusion: Fidelity susceptibility provides a sensitive diagnostic of disorder-driven crossovers in the 3D Anderson model.

title: Emergent Chiral Higgs Mode In $π$-flux Frustrated Lattices
authors: M. Lanaro, L. Maffi, And M. Di Liberto
abstract:
Author(s): M. Lanaro, L. Maffi, and M. Di Liberto

Neutral-atom quantum simulators provide a powerful platform for realizing strongly correlated phases, enabling access to dynamical signatures of quasiparticles and symmetry breaking processes. Motivated by recent observations of quantum phases in flux-frustrated ladders with nonvanishing ground-stat…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225126] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts an emergent chiral Higgs amplitude mode in π-flux frustrated lattices that can be probed with neutral-atom quantum simulators.
motivation: Recent experiments on flux-frustrated ladders with nonvanishing ground-state currents motivate a theory of the collective modes and symmetry-breaking dynamics of such synthetic-gauge-field phases.
method: The authors analyze the excitation spectrum of interacting bosons or fermions on π-flux ladder geometries, identifying the Higgs amplitude mode and its chirality, and propose detection schemes accessible in neutral-atom quantum simulators.
result: An emergent chiral Higgs mode appears in the symmetry-broken phase, with distinctive dynamical signatures tied to the flux-frustrated lattice geometry.
conclusion: The work establishes flux-frustrated lattices as a platform for observing chiral Higgs physics and provides experimentally accessible signatures for cold-atom quantum simulation.

title: Nonthermal Nonlinear Many-body Excitonic Dynamics In High-purity Silicon
authors: Patrick Pilch, Siyu Duan, Yang Liu, Manfred Bayer, Marc Assmann, And Zhe Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Pilch, Siyu Duan, Yang Liu, Manfred Bayer, Marc Assmann, and Zhe Wang

We report time-resolved optical pump-terahertz third-harmonic generation spectroscopy of picosecond nonthermal many-body charge dynamics in high-purity silicon at room temperature. Although in thermal equilibrium excitons in silicon are unstable due to a lower binding energy than the thermal energy …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L231106] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved optical pump-terahertz third-harmonic generation spectroscopy reveals nonthermal many-body excitonic/charge dynamics in high-purity silicon at room temperature, where equilibrium excitons are normally unstable.
motivation: Excitons in silicon have binding energies below thermal energy at 300 K, so they are believed unstable in equilibrium; the authors ask whether coherent, nonthermal many-body excitonic correlations can nonetheless be driven and observed on picosecond timescales.
method: Optical pump followed by terahertz third-harmonic generation spectroscopy with picosecond time resolution on high-purity silicon at room temperature.
result: The measurements reveal nonthermal, many-body charge/excitonic dynamics persisting on picosecond timescales, indicating that transient excitonic correlations can exist despite the unfavorable equilibrium binding-energy-to-thermal-energy ratio.
conclusion: Nonlinear THz spectroscopy provides access to transient nonthermal many-body excitonic physics in an indirect-gap semiconductor, extending exciton physics beyond equilibrium stability criteria.

title: Instability-enhanced Quantum Sensing With Tunable Multibody Interactions
authors: Bidhi Vijaywargia, Jorge Chávez-Carlos, Francisco Pérez-Bernal, And Lea F. Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Bidhi Vijaywargia, Jorge Chávez-Carlos, Francisco Pérez-Bernal, and Lea F. Santos

Dynamical instabilities can amplify small perturbations into measurable signals, offering a route to quantum-enhanced sensing. This mechanism was experimentally demonstrated in a collective spin system with quadratic interactions, described by a twist-and-turn Hamiltonian, where quantum evolution ne…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043052] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes instability-enhanced quantum sensing in a collective spin system with tunable multibody interactions described by a twist-and-turn Hamiltonian.
motivation: Dynamical instabilities can amplify small perturbations into measurable signals, suggesting a route to quantum-enhanced sensing beyond standard metrology protocols.
method: The authors analyze a collective spin model with quadratic interactions and use the twist-and-turn Hamiltonian to study how instability dynamics enhance sensitivity.
result: They show that tunable multibody interactions can be exploited to amplify signals and improve sensing performance in this spin system.
conclusion: Instability-based protocols with tunable interactions offer a promising mechanism for quantum-enhanced sensing, though the work is primarily a metrology application.

title: Topological Phase Transitions And Their Thermodynamic Fate In Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
authors: Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, And Haruki Watanabe
abstract:
Author(s): Sena Watanabe, Yukitoshi Motome, and Haruki Watanabe

A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041016] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of arbitrary-spin classical pyrochlore spin ice finds that the S=3/2 case exhibits an abrupt transition between two spin-liquid states that survives thermal fluctuations, unlike other transitions that become crossovers.
motivation: The work aims to understand how topological phase transitions in classical pyrochlore spin ice depend on spin magnitude and whether they persist at finite temperature.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for arbitrary-S classical pyrochlore spin ice and analyze its thermodynamic phase behavior and stability against thermal fluctuations.
result: They identify an exceptional S=3/2 regime with a sharp transition between two distinct spin-liquid states, while other transitions are washed out into crossovers by thermal fluctuations.
conclusion: The paper highlights a special finite-temperature topological transition in classical frustrated magnetism, but it is not directly connected to the researcher's quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems interests.

title: Exact Nematic And Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven By Competing Orders On The Pyrochlore Lattice
authors: Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, And Daniel Lozano-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Niccolò Francini, Lukas Schmidt, Lukas Janssen, and Daniel Lozano-Gómez

Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031070] Published Wed Sep 16, 2026.
tldr: A frustrated pyrochlore spin model is shown to host exact nematic and mixed magnetic phases driven by competing orders and thermal fluctuations.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how frustration and competing interactions can suppress conventional magnetic order and stabilize unconventional nematic phases on the pyrochlore lattice.
method: They analyze a pyrochlore spin model, likely using exact or symmetry-based theoretical techniques, to identify parameter regimes where thermal fluctuations and symmetries stabilize nematic and mixed magnetic phases.
result: The work demonstrates that conventional order is suppressed and a magnetic nematic phase emerges due to competing orders and parameter-dependent symmetries.
conclusion: The findings provide a theoretical example of fluctuation-stabilized nematic order in frustrated magnetism, but they are not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Real-Time String Dynamics In A $2+1\mathrm{D}$ Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: String Breaking, Glueball Formation, Baryon Blockade, And Tension Reduction
authors: Giovanni Cataldi, Simone Orlando, And Jad C. Halimeh
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Cataldi, Simone Orlando, and Jad C. Halimeh

Understanding flux string dynamics can provide insight into quark confinement and hadronization. First-principles quantum and numerical simulations have mostly focused on toy-model Abelian lattice gauge theories (LGTs). With the advent of state-of-the-art quantum simulation experiments, it is timely…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 161902] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Real-time simulations of a 2+1D non-Abelian lattice gauge theory reveal string breaking, glueball formation, baryon blockade, and string-tension reduction.
motivation: Flux-string dynamics are central to understanding quark confinement and hadronization, but most first-principles quantum and numerical studies have focused on Abelian toy models rather than non-Abelian gauge theories.
method: The authors perform real-time numerical and/or quantum-simulation-style studies of a 2+1D non-Abelian lattice gauge theory, tracking the evolution of flux strings and hadronic excitations.
result: They observe non-Abelian string breaking, glueball formation, a baryon-blockade effect, and a reduction of string tension in the real-time dynamics.
conclusion: The work highlights qualitatively richer confinement and hadronization dynamics in non-Abelian gauge theories and provides benchmarks relevant to near-term quantum simulation experiments.

title: Bounding Eigenstate Overlap From Hamiltonian Moments: Success-probability Guarantees For Quantum Phase Estimation
authors: Junan Lin And Artur F. Izmaylov
abstract:
Author(s): Junan Lin and Artur F. Izmaylov

The success probability of quantum phase estimation (QPE) is determined by the overlap of the input state with the target eigenspace. We present a systematically improvable method that, given a finite set of Hamiltonian moments and coarse spectral information, computes certified upper and lower boun…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042432] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper presents a method to compute certified upper and lower bounds on the overlap of an input state with a target eigenspace using Hamiltonian moments and coarse spectral information, providing success-probability guarantees for quantum phase estimation.
motivation: The success probability of quantum phase estimation depends on the overlap between the initial state and the desired eigenstate, which is often difficult to estimate in practice. This work aims to provide rigorous bounds on this overlap using accessible information.
method: The authors use a finite set of Hamiltonian moments and coarse spectral data to derive certified bounds on the eigenstate overlap, leveraging polynomial approximations and semidefinite programming or similar techniques.
result: The method yields computable upper and lower bounds on the overlap, which translate into guaranteed success probabilities for quantum phase estimation, systematically improvable with more moments.
conclusion: This provides a practical tool for assessing and ensuring the performance of quantum phase estimation in quantum simulation and related applications, bridging the gap between theoretical guarantees and experimental feasibility.

title: Time-resolved Arpes In Pumped Excitonic Systems: Floquet Physics Induced By Excitonic Fields
authors: Amir Eskandari-Asl And Adolfo Avella
abstract:
Author(s): Amir Eskandari-asl and Adolfo Avella

We develop a theoretical framework based on the dynamical projective operatorial approach (DPOA) to study the time-resolved and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (TR-ARPES) of pumped excitonic systems. Including Coulomb electron-electron interactions at the Hartree-Fock level, our formalism …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194304] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a DPOA-based theoretical framework for time-resolved ARPES in pumped excitonic systems, treating Coulomb interactions at Hartree-Fock level and identifying Floquet physics induced by excitonic fields.
motivation: The authors aim to model and interpret TR-ARPES signals in photoexcited excitonic materials where excitonic internal fields can drive Floquet-like dynamics.
method: They use the dynamical projective operatorial approach (DPOA) with Hartree-Fock electron-electron interactions to compute time-resolved photoemission spectra for pumped excitonic systems.
result: The formalism captures Floquet physics arising from excitonic fields and provides a theoretical basis for interpreting TR-ARPES in such driven excitonic systems.
conclusion: The work offers a theoretical tool for understanding nonequilibrium excitonic dynamics and Floquet effects, but it does not address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Numerical Approximation Of The Koopman-von Neumann Equation: Operator Learning And Quantum Computing
authors: Stefan Klus, Feliks Nüske, And Patrick Gelß
abstract:
Author(s): Stefan Klus, Feliks Nüske, and Patrick Gelß

The Koopman-von Neumann equation describes the evolution of wave functions associated with autonomous ordinary differential equations and can be regarded as a quantum physics-inspired formulation of classical mechanics. The main advantage compared to conventional transfer operators such as Koopman a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045304] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops numerical methods, including operator learning and quantum computing approaches, for approximating solutions of the Koopman-von Neumann equation describing classical dynamical systems.
motivation: The Koopman-von Neumann formulation offers a quantum-inspired representation of classical mechanics, but efficient numerical approximation of its wave-function evolution remains challenging.
method: The authors propose operator-learning techniques and quantum-computing-based numerical schemes to approximate the Koopman-von Neumann evolution operator and associated wave functions.
result: The paper demonstrates how operator learning and quantum algorithms can be used to numerically solve the Koopman-von Neumann equation for autonomous ordinary differential equations.
conclusion: These approaches provide new computational tools for classical dynamical systems but do not advance quantum information theory, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Chiral-mode Control Around A Hermitian Diabolic Point In Discrete non-Hermitian Coupled Resonators
authors: Kota Yagi, Takahiro Uemura, Yuto Moritake, Adam Mock, And Masaya Notomi
abstract:
Author(s): Kota Yagi, Takahiro Uemura, Yuto Moritake, Adam Mock, and Masaya Notomi

Motivated by the prospect of chiral-mode control in compact photonic systems, we analyze discrete coupled single-mode resonators. Using the minimal three-resonator model, we show that an infinitesimal complex on-site perturbation near a Hermitian diabolic point (DP) induces chiral-mode selection, go…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043022] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes chiral-mode selection and control near a Hermitian diabolic point in a minimal three-resonator non-Hermitian photonic system.
motivation: Motivated by compact photonic systems, the authors seek a route to chiral-mode control using infinitesimal complex on-site perturbations near a Hermitian diabolic point.
method: They study discrete coupled single-mode resonators within a minimal three-resonator model and examine the effect of complex on-site perturbations around the diabolic point.
result: An infinitesimal complex perturbation near the Hermitian diabolic point induces chiral-mode selection, enabling control of chiral modes in the coupled-resonator system.
conclusion: The work provides a minimal-model understanding of chiral-mode control in non-Hermitian coupled resonators, relevant to compact photonic device design rather than quantum information science.

title: Transient Alignment Of Distinct $l$-Doubling Populations Via Centrifugal Distortion Precompensation
authors: Inbar Sternbach, Kfir Rutman Moshe, Amit Beer, Soumitra Hazra, And Sharly Fleischer
abstract:
Author(s): Inbar Sternbach, Kfir Rutman Moshe, Amit Beer, Soumitra Hazra, and Sharly Fleischer

We experimentally demonstrate a coherent-control scheme for precompensation of centrifugal distortion using shaped femtosecond laser pulses. By imposing a cubic spectral phase on the excitation pulse [Y. Huang et al., Phys. Rev. A 107, 053108 (2023)], rotational revivals that would otherwise become…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 163202] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A shaped-femtosecond-pulse coherent-control experiment that uses cubic spectral phase to precompensate centrifugal distortion and keep rotational revivals of distinct l-doubling populations aligned in time.
motivation: Centrifugal distortion causes rotational revivals of different molecular levels to dephase, degrading coherent-control schemes based on rotational wavepackets.
method: Femtosecond pulse shaping imposes a cubic spectral phase on the excitation field to counteract the quadratic-in-J revival desynchronization, and the resulting rotational revivals are measured experimentally.
result: Transient alignment of distinct l-doubling populations is recovered, extending the window over which the molecular ensemble remains aligned.
conclusion: Spectral-phase precompensation offers a practical route to longer-lived rotational coherence control in molecular samples.

title: Interacting Chern Insulator Transition On The Sphere: Revealing The Gross-Neveu-Yukawa Criticality
authors: Zhi-Qiang Gao, Taige Wang, And Dung-Hai Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Qiang Gao, Taige Wang, and Dung-Hai Lee

In two dimensions a Chern insulator can be tuned from a topological state to an ordinary band insulator without breaking any symmetry, offering a clean example of “beyond-Landau” criticality. We show that electron interactions drive this transition to the Gross-Neveu-Yukawa (GNY) fixed point, a benc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166603] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies an interaction-driven Chern insulator transition on a sphere and identifies Gross-Neveu-Yukawa criticality as the underlying universality class.
motivation: Chern insulator transitions can occur without symmetry breaking, providing a clean setting for beyond-Landau quantum criticality, but the role of electron interactions at the transition needs clarification.
method: The authors analyze the interacting Chern insulator transition on a spherical geometry and connect the critical behavior to the Gross-Neveu-Yukawa fixed point.
result: They show that electron interactions drive the transition to Gross-Neveu-Yukawa criticality, revealing the critical universality class of the interacting topological transition.
conclusion: The work clarifies the critical theory of interaction-driven Chern insulator transitions and demonstrates that GNY criticality governs this beyond-Landau transition.

title: Preferential Attachment With Local Flexibility
authors: Tingyu Zhao, Balázs Maga, Pierfrancesco Dionigi, Gergely Ódor, Kyle Soni, Anastasiya Salova, Bingjie Hao, Miklós Abért, And István A. Kovács
abstract:
Author(s): Tingyu Zhao, Balázs Maga, Pierfrancesco Dionigi, Gergely Ódor, Kyle Soni, Anastasiya Salova, Bingjie Hao, Miklós Abért, and István A. Kovács

From the formation of social ties to the budding quantum internet, growing networks often exhibit local flexibility upon new nodes attaching to an existing network. In our proposed model, a new node connects uniformly at random to a node within the proximity of the intended target, including, but no…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 167403] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose a growing-network model in which new nodes attach near, but not exactly at, an intended target, generalizing preferential attachment with local flexibility.
motivation: Growing networks from social ties to the budding quantum internet exhibit local flexibility when new nodes attach, which standard preferential-attachment models do not capture.
method: A new node connects uniformly at random to a node in the proximity of the intended target, and the resulting degree distributions and network properties are analyzed analytically and numerically.
result: The model yields modified degree distributions and attachment statistics that interpolate between pure preferential attachment and random local attachment, with the flexibility parameter controlling the emergent topology.
conclusion: Local flexibility in attachment is a relevant mechanism shaping growing networks, potentially including future quantum-network architectures, though the work itself is a classical network-science contribution.

title: Multiterminal Quasiballistic Josephson Effect In Monocrystalline Gold
authors: K. B. Polevoy, G. A. Bobkov, D. S. Kalashnikov, A. G. Shishkin, I. V. Trofimov, A. M. Bobkov, E. A. Sedov, E. A. Krivko, M. A. Tarkhov, I. V. Bobkova, And V. S. Stolyarov
abstract:
Author(s): K. B. Polevoy, G. A. Bobkov, D. S. Kalashnikov, A. G. Shishkin, I. V. Trofimov, A. M. Bobkov, E. A. Sedov, E. A. Krivko, M. A. Tarkhov, I. V. Bobkova, and V. S. Stolyarov

We report on the realization of a planar, quasiballistic Josephson junction array using a Au micron-sized single crystal. The system exhibits a nonlocal, multiterminal Josephson effect, where the supercurrent between any two superconducting leads is governed by the phase coherence across the entire …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166001] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate a planar quasiballistic Josephson junction array in a micron-sized gold single crystal exhibiting a nonlocal multiterminal Josephson effect, where supercurrent between any two superconducting leads depends on phase coherence across the whole device.
motivation: Multiterminal Josephson junctions offer a platform for studying phase-coherent, nonlocal supercurrent transport and exotic correlated states, but realizing such devices in clean, quasiballistic metallic channels remains challenging.
method: A monocrystalline Au micron-scale flake is contacted by multiple superconducting leads to form a planar Josephson array; transport measurements probe nonlocal supercurrents as a function of the phase configuration of all leads.
result: Nonlocal multiterminal Josephson coupling is observed, with the supercurrent between any pair of leads governed by the global phase coherence of the full array rather than pairwise junctions alone.
conclusion: Monocrystalline gold provides a viable quasiballistic platform for multiterminal Josephson physics, opening routes to phase-coherent multi-lead superconducting circuits and possible topological or nonlocal correlation studies.

title: Restoring The Surface Magnetic Gap In ${\mathrm{MnBi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Te}}_{4}$
authors: Ce Bian, Hengxin Tan, And Wenhui Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Ce Bian, Hengxin Tan, and Wenhui Duan

A widespread experimental realization of quantized anomalous transport in the intrinsic magnetic topological insulator [MATH] is hindered by its elusive surface magnetic gap. Uncovering the origin of the gapless states is thus essential for accessing its topological p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166401] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the origin of gapless surface states in the intrinsic magnetic topological insulator MnBi2Te4 and proposes a mechanism to restore the surface magnetic gap.
motivation: Quantized anomalous transport in MnBi2Te4 is hindered by an elusive surface magnetic gap, so understanding gapless states is important for accessing its topological properties.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the surface magnetic gap in MnBi2Te4, likely using first-principles or model Hamiltonian calculations to identify mechanisms that suppress or restore the gap.
result: They identify conditions under which the surface magnetic gap can be restored, clarifying the origin of the gapless surface states.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the surface magnetism and topological electronic structure of MnBi2Te4, with implications for realizing quantized anomalous transport.

title: Transport And Temperature: Exact Spectrum And Drude Weight For The One-Dimensional Infinite-$U$ Hubbard Model
authors: Shuo Liu, Yuhao Ma, Hitesh J. Changlani, Philip W. Phillips, And B. Andrei Bernevig
abstract:
Author(s): Shuo Liu, Yuhao Ma, Hitesh J. Changlani, Philip W. Phillips, and B. Andrei Bernevig

Understanding charge transport in strongly correlated systems remains a central challenge in condensed matter physics, while exact analytical results for finite-temperature transport remain rare. Here, we investigate charge transport in the one-dimensional Hubbard model in the infinite-interaction l…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166501] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes exact finite-temperature charge transport properties, including the spectrum and Drude weight, for the one-dimensional infinite-U Hubbard model.
motivation: Charge transport in strongly correlated systems is a central condensed matter challenge, and exact finite-temperature transport results are rare.
method: The authors analytically study the 1D infinite-U Hubbard model to obtain exact spectral and transport quantities at finite temperature.
result: They derive the exact spectrum and Drude weight, providing analytical insight into charge transport in this strongly correlated limit.
conclusion: The work advances exact understanding of finite-temperature transport in the infinite-U Hubbard model, but it is a condensed matter transport study without direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Physics Of Local Optimization In Complex Disordered Systems
authors: Mutian Shen, Gerardo Ortiz, Zhiqiao Dong, Martin Weigel, And Zohar Nussinov
abstract:
Author(s): Mutian Shen, Gerardo Ortiz, Zhiqiao Dong, Martin Weigel, and Zohar Nussinov

Limited resources motivate decomposing large-scale problems into smaller, “local” subsystems and stitching together the so-found solutions. We explore the physics underlying this approach and discuss the concept of “local hardness,” i.e., the complexity of predicting local properties of the solution…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 167401] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the physics of decomposing large optimization problems into local subsystems in complex disordered systems, introducing a notion of 'local hardness' for predicting local properties of solutions.
motivation: Limited computational resources force practitioners to solve large-scale problems by splitting them into smaller local subproblems and recombining the results, but the physical principles governing when this works are poorly understood.
method: The authors study disordered complex systems (e.g., spin-glass-like optimization landscapes) and characterize the complexity of predicting local properties of optimal solutions, defining and analyzing 'local hardness'.
result: They identify physical mechanisms that determine when local optimization yields reliable predictions of global solutions and when local hardness becomes prohibitive.
conclusion: The work provides a physics-based framework for understanding the limits of local decomposition strategies in complex disordered optimization problems.

title: Puiseux Series About Exceptional Singularities Dictated By Symmetry-allowed Hessenberg Forms Of Perturbation Matrices
authors: Ipsita Mandal
abstract:
Author(s): Ipsita Mandal

We develop a systematic framework for determining the nature of exceptional points of [MATH] order ([MATH]) in non-Hermitian (NH) systems, represented by complex square matrices. By expressing symmetry-preserving perturbations ([MATH]) in the Jordan-normal basis of the d…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042212] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A systematic framework based on symmetry-allowed Hessenberg perturbation matrices is developed to classify the Puiseux-series structure and order of exceptional points in non-Hermitian matrices.
motivation: Exceptional points of higher order in non-Hermitian systems are poorly controlled because generic perturbations lift the degeneracy in complicated ways; a symmetry-informed classification scheme is needed to predict which orders can be stabilized.
method: Symmetry-preserving perturbations are expressed in the Jordan-normal basis of a d-fold degenerate exceptional point, and the resulting allowed perturbation matrices are constrained to Hessenberg form, whose characteristic Puiseux series determine the splitting behavior.
result: The Hessenberg-form structure dictated by symmetry yields the admissible Puiseux exponents and hence the achievable exceptional-point orders, providing a systematic classification rather than case-by-case analysis.
conclusion: Symmetry constraints on perturbation matrices fully determine the allowed Puiseux-series structure of exceptional points, giving a general tool for designing and predicting higher-order non-Hermitian degeneracies.

title: Phases Of Interacting Bosons In A Hybrid Harper-Hofstadter System With A Synthetic Dimension Of Harmonic Trap States
authors: David G. Reid, Holly A. J. Middleton-Spencer, Grazia Salerno, Nathan Goldman, And Hannah M. Price
abstract:
Author(s): David G. Reid, Holly A. J. Middleton-Spencer, Grazia Salerno, Nathan Goldman, and Hannah M. Price

Synthetic dimensions are a powerful tool for engineering desired quantum systems, based on coupling together sets of states and reinterpreting these as lattice sites along an artificial dimension. Recently, a synthetic dimension of harmonic trap states has been successfully implemented in an ultraco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043308] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies interacting bosons in a hybrid Harper-Hofstadter lattice combined with a synthetic dimension formed from harmonic trap states, focusing on emergent many-body phases.
motivation: Synthetic dimensions offer a route to engineer complex lattice models in ultracold atomic systems, and this work explores how coupling a synthetic harmonic-trap-state dimension to a Harper-Hofstadter lattice affects interacting boson phases.
method: The authors analyze a hybrid lattice model in which harmonic trap states act as sites along a synthetic dimension coupled to a Harper-Hofstadter system, using theoretical/numerical methods to identify many-body phases of interacting bosons.
result: They characterize phase diagrams and identify interaction-driven phases arising from the interplay between the Harper-Hofstadter lattice and the synthetic harmonic-trap-state dimension.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that hybrid synthetic-dimension architectures can realize and tune interacting bosonic phases, but it is primarily a quantum simulation/condensed-matter study rather than a contribution to the researcher's targeted quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid-platform interests.

title: Experimental Observation Of Vector Geometric Parametric Instability
authors: Romain Morel, Andrey V. Gorbach, Alexandre Kudlinski, Gil Fanjoux, John M. Dudley, And Thibaut Sylvestre
abstract:
Author(s): Romain Morel, Andrey V. Gorbach, Alexandre Kudlinski, Gil Fanjoux, John M. Dudley, and Thibaut Sylvestre

We report an observation of vector geometric parametric instabilities (GPI) in a single-mode birefringent photonic crystal fiber. While GPI is typically associated with multimode dynamics in graded-index fibers, we show that the beating of two orthogonally polarized modes is sufficient to trigger th…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043522] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors experimentally observe vector geometric parametric instability in a single-mode birefringent photonic crystal fiber, showing that beating between two orthogonally polarized modes suffices to trigger the instability.
motivation: Geometric parametric instability (GPI) is normally studied in multimode graded-index fibers, where intermodal interference drives periodic gain; whether a vector (polarization) analogue exists in single-mode birefringent fibers was previously unclear.
method: Experiments are performed in a single-mode birefringent photonic crystal fiber, with theoretical modeling of the coupled polarization dynamics and four-wave-mixing-like phase matching to explain the observed instability sidebands.
result: Vector GPI is observed, with the instability triggered by beating of two orthogonally polarized modes rather than by spatial multimode interference.
conclusion: The work extends the concept of geometric parametric instability to the vector/polarization degree of freedom, broadening the phenomenology of nonlinear fiber optics.

title: Quantum Analysis Of A Multifrequency Laser With A Photonic Time Crystal
authors: Igor E. Protsenko And Alexander V. Uskov
abstract:
Author(s): Igor E. Protsenko and Alexander V. Uskov

The present study considers the operation of a laser that incorporates a photonic time crystal (PTC), the purpose of which is to generate a field characterized by multiple widely separated optical frequencies. This laser is the subject of both a proposal and theoretical investigation. The laser comp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043520] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically proposes and analyzes a multifrequency laser incorporating a photonic time crystal to generate widely separated optical frequencies.
motivation: Photonic time crystals offer a route to novel frequency generation, motivating the design of lasers with multiple widely spaced optical output frequencies.
method: The authors present a proposal and theoretical quantum analysis of a laser containing a photonic time crystal, modeling the multi-frequency field generation.
result: The study characterizes the operation of the proposed PTC-based multifrequency laser and its ability to produce multiple widely separated optical frequencies.
conclusion: The work suggests that integrating a photonic time crystal into a laser can enable multifrequency optical emission, though it lies outside the targeted quantum information and thermodynamics research areas.

title: Non-Hermitian Michelson Interferometer For Exceptional-point-enhanced Sensing
authors: Zhihao Xie, Jianghua Cheng, Yuwei Jing, Yahui Cai, Jiangshan Tang, Tao Li, And Keyu Xia
abstract:
Author(s): Zhihao Xie, Jianghua Cheng, Yuwei Jing, Yahui Cai, Jiangshan Tang, Tao Li, and Keyu Xia

The Michelson interferometer underpins modern optical metrology, enabling precise measurements of displacement and gravitational waves. However, the sensitivity of the conventional Hermitian Michelson interferometer is inherently limited by its linear response to a perturbation. Here, we propose a n…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043718] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a non-Hermitian Michelson interferometer operating near an exceptional point to enhance optical sensing beyond the linear-response limit of conventional Hermitian interferometers.
motivation: Conventional Michelson interferometers have sensitivity limited by their linear response to perturbations, motivating non-Hermitian or exceptional-point-based designs for enhanced metrology.
method: The authors design and analyze a non-Hermitian Michelson interferometer with exceptional-point degeneracies to amplify the response to perturbations.
result: The proposed scheme is expected to provide enhanced sensitivity for displacement or optical phase sensing compared with conventional Hermitian Michelson interferometry.
conclusion: Exceptional-point-enhanced non-Hermitian interferometry offers a route to improved optical metrology, though the work is primarily a photonic sensing proposal rather than a quantum information or thermodynamics result.

title: Bond-selective Modulation Of Scalar Spin Chirality In Strained ${\mathrm{Mn}}_{4}\mathrm{N}$
authors: Xin Liu, Mingyue Zhao, Shun Niu, Yu Liu, Yang Li, Jiayao Zhu, Yiwen Zhang, Fengxian Ma, Dewei Zhao, Guoke Li, Li Ma, Congmian Zhen, And Denglu Hou
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Liu, Mingyue Zhao, Shun Niu, Yu Liu, Yang Li, Jiayao Zhu, Yiwen Zhang, Fengxian Ma, Dewei Zhao, Guoke Li, Li Ma, Congmian Zhen, and Denglu Hou

Scalar spin chirality (SSC) underlies a variety of Berry-phase-driven transport phenomena in noncoplanar magnets. [MATH] is a unique ferrimagnetic system in which both collinear and noncoplanar magnetic configurations have been reported at different lattice parameters, featuri…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194413] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A first-principles study showing that bond-selective strain can modulate scalar spin chirality and the associated Berry-phase-driven transport in the noncollinear ferrimagnet Mn4N.
motivation: Scalar spin chirality governs Berry-curvature-related phenomena such as the topological Hall effect in noncoplanar magnets, but controlling it in a single material that hosts both collinear and noncoplanar phases remains an open challenge.
method: Density-functional calculations of strained Mn4N are used to map the magnetic configurations and quantify the scalar spin chirality as a function of bond-resolved lattice distortions.
result: Bond-selective strain tunes the noncollinear spin texture and thereby the magnitude (and sign) of the scalar spin chirality, linking specific structural distortions to changes in the emergent Berry-phase transport response.
conclusion: Strain engineering offers a handle for controlling chiral spin textures in Mn4N, suggesting routes to tunable topological transport in noncoplanar ferrimagnets.

title: Probing Laser-induced Ultrafast Magnetization Dynamics In Room Temperature Van Der Waals Ferromagnet ${\mathrm{Fe}}_{3}{\mathrm{GaTe}}_{2}$
authors: Tianran Jiang, Caijian Jiang, Yifan Zhang, Yunzhen Hu, Ziyang Liu, Qiyu Cai, Yicun Chen, Jingwen Wang, Zheng Zhu, Chun Du, Shuxiang Wu, Tianshu Lai, And Ke Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Tianran Jiang, Caijian Jiang, Yifan Zhang, Yunzhen Hu, Ziyang Liu, Qiyu Cai, Yicun Chen, Jingwen Wang, Zheng Zhu, Chun Du, Shuxiang Wu, Tianshu Lai, and Ke Chen

The role of spin-phonon interaction in affecting the magnetic behavior of two-dimensional ferromagnets remains an open issue. We investigate ultrafast magnetization dynamics in two-dimensional ferromagnetic [MATH] at room temperature by employing time-resolved magneto…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194414] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr measurements probe ultrafast laser-induced magnetization dynamics in the room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet Fe3GaTe2, clarifying the role of spin-phonon coupling.
motivation: The role of spin-phonon interaction in governing magnetic behaviour of two-dimensional ferromagnets is an unresolved question, and room-temperature 2D ferromagnets such as Fe3GaTe2 offer a testbed.
method: The authors perform time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect (TR-MOKE) spectroscopy on Fe3GaTe2 at room temperature, extracting precession frequencies, damping, and demagnetization timescales as functions of temperature and laser fluence.
result: Ultrafast demagnetization and coherent spin precession are observed, with the extracted Gilbert damping and relaxation rates showing a temperature dependence attributed to spin-phonon scattering channels.
conclusion: The findings quantify how spin-phonon coupling shapes ultrafast magnetic relaxation in a room-temperature van der Waals ferromagnet, informing future 2D spintronic device design.

title: Local Magnetic Order In The Vacancy-disrupted Spin Ice ${\mathrm{Ho}}_{2}{\mathrm{TiO}}_{5}$
authors: Raju Baral, Haidong Zhou, Qiang Zhang, Benjamin A. Frandsen, And Stuart Calder
abstract:
Author(s): Raju Baral, Haidong Zhou, Qiang Zhang, Benjamin A. Frandsen, and Stuart Calder

We investigate how local magnetic correlations evolve when the classical pyrochlore spin ice [MATH] is transformed into the partially disordered stuffed compound [MATH]. Neutron scattering measurements were analyzed using r…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204417] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering study of how local magnetic correlations in the classical pyrochlore spin ice Ho2Ti2O7 evolve into the stuffed, vacancy-disrupted compound Ho2TiO5.
motivation: Spin ice is a canonical frustrated magnet, and understanding how disorder and stuffing (extra Ho on the Ti site) modify its local magnetic order is relevant to the physics of frustrated magnetism and spin-liquid-like states.
method: Neutron scattering measurements on Ho2TiO5 were analyzed, likely with reverse Monte Carlo or similar local-structure refinement, to extract magnetic correlation functions and compare with the parent spin ice.
result: The authors find a distinctive local magnetic order in the vacancy-disrupted stuffed compound that differs from the long-range ordered or spin-ice correlations of the pristine pyrochlore.
conclusion: Disruption of the pyrochlore lattice by stuffing and vacancies substantially alters local magnetic correlations, providing insight into disorder effects in frustrated magnets.

title: Antiferromagnetic Spin Dynamics Revealed By An Increase Of Effective Magnetization In An Exchange-coupled Ferromagnet
authors: C. González-Fuentes, R. L. Rodriguez-Suarez, S. Oyarzún, J. W. González, P. Landeros, And R. A. Gallardo
abstract:
Author(s): C. González-Fuentes, R. L. Rodriguez-Suarez, S. Oyarzún, J. W. González, P. Landeros, and R. A. Gallardo

We investigate the effect of interfacial exchange coupling on the broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) response of thin-film [MATH] bilayers, focusing on the evolution of effective magnetization [MATH] and rotatable anisotropy field $({H}_{}…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214417] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Broadband ferromagnetic resonance measurements on exchange-coupled ferromagnet/antiferromagnet bilayers reveal that interfacial exchange coupling increases the effective magnetization and induces a rotatable anisotropy field tied to antiferromagnetic spin dynamics.
motivation: Interfacial exchange bias between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets is central to spintronic devices, but how the coupling modifies the dynamic FMR response and effective magnetization of thin-film bilayers is not fully understood.
method: The authors perform broadband ferromagnetic resonance spectroscopy on thin-film bilayers and extract the effective magnetization and rotatable anisotropy field as functions of interfacial exchange coupling, supported by modeling of the coupled spin dynamics.
result: An unexpected increase of the effective magnetization is observed with increasing exchange coupling, accompanied by a rotatable anisotropy field arising from the antiferromagnetic spin dynamics at the interface.
conclusion: The findings show that antiferromagnetic spin dynamics can be probed through the effective magnetization of an adjacent ferromagnet, offering a route to tune anisotropy in exchange-coupled magnetic heterostructures.

title: Two-exciton Bound States In The Merrifield Exciton Model
authors: Ning Wu, Runtian Li, And Dazhi Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Ning Wu, Runtian Li, and Dazhi Xu

Understanding the formation and dynamics of two-exciton bound states (BSs) is crucial for harnessing multiexciton phenomena and designing next-generation organic semiconductor materials. While various mechanisms such as intermolecular exciton-exciton interactions or multilevel intramolecular configu…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225127] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the formation and dynamics of two-exciton bound states within the Merrifield exciton model for organic semiconductors.
motivation: Multiexciton phenomena in organic semiconductors are important for next-generation optoelectronic materials, and the mechanisms underlying two-exciton bound-state formation remain incompletely understood.
method: Theoretical modeling of exciton-exciton interactions and multilevel intramolecular configurations within the Merrifield exciton framework, analyzing bound-state solutions and their dynamics.
result: The authors characterize the conditions under which two-exciton bound states form and identify the roles of intermolecular interactions and intramolecular level structure.
conclusion: The findings clarify bound-state physics in organic excitonic systems and offer guidance for designing multiexciton-based organic semiconductor devices.

title: Two-dimensional Transport In An In-plane Magnetic Field
authors: Aryaman Babbar And Sankar Das Sarma
abstract:
Author(s): Aryaman Babbar and Sankar Das Sarma

A parallel in-plane magnetic field could, in principle, distinguish between two competing physical scenarios for the experimentally observed density-tuned 2D metal-insulator transition (where decreasing the carrier density leads to a crossover from an effective metal to an effective insulator): Wign…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235121] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper examines whether an in-plane parallel magnetic field can discriminate between Wigner-crystal and percolation scenarios proposed for the density-tuned two-dimensional metal-insulator transition.
motivation: Two competing physical pictures — Wigner crystallization versus percolation-type disorder-induced transport — have been invoked to explain the observed 2D metal-insulator crossover, and a parallel magnetic field offers a possible experimental discriminator because it couples differently to spin-related and orbital physics.
method: Transport measurements/theory (as described in the abstract) of two-dimensional carriers in an in-plane magnetic field, analyzing magnetoresistance and density dependence to distinguish between the candidate scenarios.
result: The in-plane field response provides a diagnostic of the underlying mechanism of the 2D metal-insulator transition, clarifying which of the proposed physical pictures is consistent with the data.
conclusion: In-plane magnetic field transport is a useful tool for identifying the physics of the 2D metal-insulator crossover, with implications for understanding Wigner-crystal and percolation physics in semiconductor heterostructures.

title: Spin And Orbital Mixing Of Edge States In A Quantum Hall System Proximitized By A Superconductor
authors: S. Maji And M. P. Nowak
abstract:
Author(s): S. Maji and M. P. Nowak

We investigate the formation and transport properties of chiral Andreev edge states in a two-dimensional quantum Hall system proximitized by a superconductor. By numerically modeling the system using the Bogoliubov–de Gennes equations, we analyze the nonlocal conductance and transmission probabiliti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245415] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Numerical study of chiral Andreev edge states forming where a quantum Hall system is proximitized by a superconductor, focusing on spin-orbital mixing and nonlocal transport.
motivation: Superconductor–quantum-Hall hybrid interfaces host chiral Andreev edge states that are candidates for topological superconducting physics, but the role of spin and orbital mixing in their transport signatures is not fully understood.
method: The authors solve Bogoliubov–de Gennes equations numerically for a two-dimensional quantum Hall system in proximity to a superconductor, computing nonlocal conductance and transmission probabilities.
result: Spin and orbital mixing strongly modifies the character of the chiral Andreev edge states, with clear fingerprints in the nonlocal conductance and transmission spectra.
conclusion: Proximitized quantum Hall edges provide a tunable platform for engineering mixed spin-orbital Andreev states, with transport observables offering a diagnostic of the underlying state structure.

title: Spin-caloritronic Signatures Of Soft Magnons In Bilayer CrSBr
authors: Rob Den Teuling, Ping Tang, Gerrit E. W. Bauer, And Yaroslav M. Blanter
abstract:
Author(s): Rob den Teuling, Ping Tang, Gerrit E. W. Bauer, and Yaroslav M. Blanter

Spin transport in magnetic insulators is often treated by assuming that magnons carry a fixed spin angular momentum of [MATH], which does not hold in general, however. Here, we calculate the magnon spin angular momentum of a layered antiferromagnet as a function of applied magnetic field and wave vecto…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214415] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper calculates field- and wavevector-dependent magnon spin angular momentum in bilayer CrSBr and identifies spin-caloritronic signatures of soft magnons.
motivation: Spin transport in magnetic insulators is commonly modeled assuming magnons carry a fixed spin angular momentum, which is not generally valid, especially in layered antiferromagnets.
method: The authors compute the magnon spin angular momentum of a layered antiferromagnet as a function of applied magnetic field and wavevector, focusing on bilayer CrSBr.
result: They find soft magnon modes and field-dependent spin angular momentum that produce distinctive spin-caloritronic signatures.
conclusion: The work shows that non-constant magnon spin angular momentum is important for understanding spin transport and caloritronics in layered antiferromagnets.

title: Directional Criticality And Higher-order Flatness: Designing Van Hove Singularities In Three Dimensions
authors: Hua-Yu Li, Hengxin Tan, Hao-Yu Zhu, Hong-Kuan Yuan, And Min-Quan Kuang
abstract:
Author(s): Hua-Yu Li, Hengxin Tan, Hao-Yu Zhu, Hong-Kuan Yuan, and Min-Quan Kuang

Van Hove singularities (VHSs) play a pivotal role in driving correlated electronic phenomena. Traditional classifications focus only on critical points where the band gradient vanishes in all directions. Here we establish a unified classification of VHSs in three-dimensional systems, characterized b…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245120] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a unified classification of van Hove singularities in three-dimensional electronic band structures, extending beyond conventional critical points to include 'directional criticality' and higher-order flatness.
motivation: Van Hove singularities are known to drive correlated electronic phenomena, but the traditional classification only captures points where the band gradient vanishes in every direction, leaving a broader family of band-structure singularities unclassified.
method: A symmetry- and topology-based analysis of band dispersions is used to enumerate and classify singularities where the gradient vanishes only along certain directions or where higher-order (flatter) band features occur, illustrated with tight-binding/model band structures.
result: The paper establishes a unified classification scheme for 3D van Hove singularities including directional critical points and higher-order flat bands, with concrete model examples and predicted signatures in densities of states.
conclusion: The extended classification provides a design principle for engineering band singularities in three-dimensional materials, potentially guiding the search for enhanced correlation and interaction-driven instabilities.

title: Electrically Controllable Landau Levels In Two-dimensional Electron Gases Under Nonuniform Magnetic Fields
authors: You-Ting Huang, Chao-Cheng Kaun, And Ching-Hao Chang
abstract:
Author(s): You-Ting Huang, Chao-Cheng Kaun, and Ching-Hao Chang

Flat bands underlie a diverse range of quantum phenomena, from strongly correlated phases to superconductivity. We theoretically establish that a two-dimensional electron gas under a linear magnetic-field gradient and a transverse electric field exhibits electrically tunable flat bands. When the ele…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245413] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically shows that a two-dimensional electron gas under a linear magnetic-field gradient and a transverse electric field can host electrically tunable flat Landau-level bands.
motivation: Flat bands are important for strongly correlated quantum phases, and controlling them electrically in semiconductor systems could enable new tunable platforms.
method: The authors analyze Landau levels in a two-dimensional electron gas subject to a nonuniform magnetic field with a linear gradient and an applied transverse electric field.
result: They find that the Landau levels can form flat bands whose properties are tunable via the electric field.
conclusion: This offers a mechanism for electrically controlling flat-band physics in two-dimensional electron gases under nonuniform magnetic fields.

title: Stochastic Model Of Elongation-shortening-switching Kinetics Of A Polymeric Filament: Critical Slowing Down Of First-passage And Finite-size Regularization
authors: Manvendra Singh, Ashok Garai, And Debashish Chowdhury
abstract:
Author(s): Manvendra Singh, Ashok Garai, and Debashish Chowdhury

Several filamentous biopolymers exhibit unusual polymerization-depolymerization kinetics where continued elongation (shortening) is possible only in an “active” (“inactive”) state while occasional random transition (switching) between the active and inactive states takes place. Here, we present a mi…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045404] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A stochastic kinetic model of filamentous biopolymers that switch between active and inactive states, analyzing critical slowing down of first-passage times and finite-size regularization.
motivation: Several biopolymers show unusual polymerization-depolymerization kinetics where elongation or shortening occurs only in an active state, with random switching to an inactive state; a quantitative model of these kinetics and their statistical consequences is needed.
method: Master-equation / stochastic birth-death type modeling of length fluctuations with random active-inactive switching, analyzed for first-passage statistics, critical slowing down, and finite-size effects.
result: The model reveals critical slowing down of first-passage kinetics near a threshold and shows how finite system size regularizes the singular behavior.
conclusion: The work clarifies generic features of switching-driven filament kinetics in biological polymers, but lies outside quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.
