[Phys. Rev. E 114, 049901] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: A published erratum correcting the authors' earlier statistical-mechanical treatment of indistinguishable energy states and the glass transition.
motivation: The original paper attempted to model the glass transition using statistical mechanics of indistinguishable energy states, and this notice corrects errors in that work.
method: Erratum notice; no new methodology is presented beyond corrections to the original derivations.
result: Corrections to the original Phys. Rev. E article (114, 014119) are issued; substantive new results are not reported.
conclusion: The work concerns classical statistical mechanics of glasses and lies outside quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Combined Framework For Synchronization With Distributed Delays And Noise In Kuramoto-Daido Oscillators
authors: Samir Sahoo And Antonio Palacios
abstract:
Author(s): Samir Sahoo and Antonio Palacios

We derive the characteristic equation governing the linear stability of the incoherent state in delayed noisy Kuramoto-Daido oscillator ensembles with general periodic coupling. The calculation is formulated for arbitrary normalized delay kernels and natural-frequency distributions. For a Lorentzian…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043038] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The authors derive the characteristic equation governing linear stability of the incoherent state in delayed, noisy Kuramoto-Daido oscillator ensembles with general periodic coupling and arbitrary delay kernels and frequency distributions.
motivation: Synchronization transitions in oscillator populations with distributed delays and noise are central to classical nonlinear dynamics, and a unified analytical framework covering general coupling and delay kernels is lacking.
method: Linear stability analysis of the incoherent state, formulated via a characteristic equation for arbitrary normalized delay kernels and natural-frequency distributions, with explicit treatment of the Lorentzian case.
result: A general characteristic equation is obtained that reduces to known results in limiting cases and predicts how delay and noise shape the onset of synchrony.
conclusion: The framework unifies and extends prior synchronization analyses for Kuramoto-Daido systems with delays and noise, though the results are purely classical.

title: Spectral Repulsion Does Not Uniquely Determine Modal Exchange In A Deformed Microwave Billiard
authors: Xiaodong Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaodong Zhang

An avoided crossing is a familiar spectral signature of interaction between nearby modes, but the eigenvalue trajectory alone does not establish whether their modal identities are exchanged. We examine this question in a deformed microwave billiard by comparing finite element eigenvalues and fields.…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043040] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: Spectral repulsion alone does not uniquely determine whether modal identities are exchanged in a deformed microwave billiard.
motivation: Avoided crossings are a common spectral signature of mode interaction, but eigenvalue trajectories alone may not reveal whether the underlying modes exchange identity.
method: The authors compare finite-element eigenvalues and field distributions in a deformed microwave billiard to test the connection between spectral repulsion and modal exchange.
result: They find that spectral repulsion does not uniquely determine modal exchange, meaning eigenvalue trajectories are insufficient to establish identity exchange.
conclusion: Field information is necessary to determine whether modal identities are exchanged in such systems, cautioning against inferring modal exchange from spectral repulsion alone.

title: Signatures Of The Circular Unruh Effect In Electric And Magnetic Dipole Transitions Of Multilevel Atoms
authors: Gregor Janson, Fabio Di Pumpo, Lorenz Thoma, And Maxim A. Efremov
abstract:
Author(s): Gregor Janson, Fabio Di Pumpo, Lorenz Thoma, and Maxim A. Efremov

The circular Unruh effect is the excitation of a detector moving along a planar circular trajectory within an electromagnetic vacuum. We demonstrate that the magnetic dipole transitions in an atom, acting as the detector, dominate the electric dipole transitions. Our analysis of both free-space and …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043029] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes how circular motion of multilevel atoms through the electromagnetic vacuum induces Unruh-like dipole transitions, with magnetic dipole transitions dominating electric ones.
motivation: The circular Unruh effect is a relativistic quantum-field phenomenon in which an accelerated detector gets excited by the vacuum; understanding its signatures in realistic atomic transitions could make it experimentally accessible.
method: The authors treat multilevel atoms as detectors moving on planar circular trajectories and compare magnetic versus electric dipole transition rates in free space and in a cavity-like setting.
result: They find that magnetic dipole transitions dominate over electric dipole transitions for the circular Unruh effect in multilevel atoms under the considered conditions.
conclusion: The work identifies magnetic dipole transitions as the primary signature of the circular Unruh effect, suggesting new avenues for detecting acceleration-induced vacuum excitation.

title: Observation Of Wannier-Rydberg And Charge-Transfer Hybrid Moiré Excitons Under Pressure
authors: Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, And Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Jing Song, Yifan Wang, Xuan Zhao, Yuxuan Song, Song Liu, Chen Hu, and Yang Xu

Hydrostatic pressure continuously tunes the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices, driving a crossover to a strong-moiré regime that hybridizes Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041007] Published Tue Oct 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports pressure-tuned moiré excitons in semiconductor superlattices, observing hybridization between Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitonic states.
motivation: Hydrostatic pressure provides a continuous tuning knob for the moiré potential, enabling exploration of a strong-moiré regime and hybrid exciton physics.
method: The authors use hydrostatic pressure to tune the moiré potential in semiconductor superlattices and likely perform optical spectroscopy to identify excitonic resonances and their hybridization.
result: A crossover to a strong-moiré regime is observed, where Wannier-Rydberg and charge-transfer excitons hybridize into mixed moiré exciton states.
conclusion: The work demonstrates pressure as a route to control moiré exciton hybridization, with implications for exciton physics in semiconductor superlattices.

title: Spin Nematic Liquid Crystal And Scalar Spin Chirality In Tetragonal Lattice ${\mathrm{YbMnBi}}_{2}$
authors: Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. abstract:
Author(s): Yaofeng Xie, Sijie Xu, Yu Pan, Taekoo Oh, Tingjun Zhang, Masaaki Matsuda, Zhaoyu Liu, Zehao Wang, Yiheng Wang, Siyu Pan, Avishek Maity, Sylwia Pawledzio, Xiaoping Wang, Songxue Chi, Feng Ye, Yiqing Hao, Huibo Cao, Barry L. Winn, Melissa K. Graves-Brook, Shuai Wu, Fan Li, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Claudia Felser, Naoto Nagaosa, and Pengcheng Dai

Neutron scattering experiments on
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041001] Published Thu Oct 01, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering on tetragonal YbMnBi2 reveals a field-induced dynamic spin nematic state whose scalar spin chirality drives anomalous Hall and Nernst responses in the paramagnetic phase.
motivation: Scalar spin chirality is known to generate emergent Berry curvature and transverse transport in magnets, but its identification in the paramagnetic regime of a metallic tetragonal system and its link to a spin nematic state remained unclear.
method: Elastic and inelastic neutron scattering experiments on YbMnBi2 in applied magnetic fields, combined with transport measurements (anomalous Hall and Nernst effects) and symmetry/mean-field modeling of the spin correlations.
result: The data show a dynamic spin nematic liquid-crystal-like state that couples to the magnetic field and produces non-zero scalar spin chirality, consistent with the observed anomalous Hall and Nernst signals above the ordering temperature.
conclusion: Paramagnetic spin correlations in YbMnBi2 can support a spin nematic phase hosting scalar spin chirality, establishing a route to chirality-driven transverse transport in the paramagnetic state.

title: Genuine And Spurious (Non-)Ergodicity In Single Particle Tracking
authors: Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, And Aleksei Chechkin
abstract:
Author(s): Wei Wang, Qing Wei, Igor M. Sokolov, Ralf Metzler, and Aleksei Chechkin

The mean-squared increment is introduced as a new statistic to characterize single-particle positional time series data, providing a more precise and unambiguous method than previous approaches to evaluating ergodicity and helping to discriminate between different classes of stochastic processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031071] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the mean-squared increment as a statistic for distinguishing genuine and spurious ergodicity in single-particle tracking time series.
motivation: Single-particle tracking data require robust methods to assess ergodicity and classify stochastic processes, and prior approaches can be ambiguous.
method: The authors define and analyze the mean-squared increment of positional time series and use it to characterize ergodic versus non-ergodic behavior across stochastic process classes.
result: The mean-squared increment provides a more precise and unambiguous ergodicity diagnostic than previous statistics and helps discriminate between process classes.
conclusion: The proposed statistic improves the analysis of single-particle tracking data and clarifies genuine versus spurious non-ergodicity, though it is outside quantum information and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Geometrically Frustrated Quadrupoles On The Pyrochlore Lattice And Generalized Spin Liquids
authors: Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, And Paul Mcclarty
abstract:
Author(s): Kristian Tyn Kai Chung, Sylvain Petit, Julien Robert, and Paul McClarty

A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors, showing how angular-momentum-dependent geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031065] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A semiclassical framework models quantum quadrupoles as biaxial tensors to study frustrated magnetism on the pyrochlore lattice and identify generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids.
motivation: Geometrically frustrated magnets can host exotic liquid-like states, and quadrupolar degrees of freedom may produce generalized nematic and spin-liquid phases beyond conventional magnetism.
method: The authors develop a semiclassical description in which quantum quadrupoles are represented as biaxial tensors, allowing angular-momentum-dependent geometries to be analyzed on the pyrochlore lattice.
result: The framework shows how such geometries dictate generalized nematic phases and quadrupolar spin liquids in frustrated magnets.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical platform for understanding quadrupolar spin liquids and frustration-driven nematic order on pyrochlore lattices.

title: Observing The Spatial And Temporal Evolution Of Exciton Wave Functions In Organic Semiconductors
authors: Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, And Peter Puschnig
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Theilen, Siegfried Kaidisch, Monja Stettner, Sarah Zajusch, Eric Fackelman, Alexa Adamkiewicz, Robert Wallauer, Andreas Windischbacher, Christian S. Kern, Michael G. Ramsey, François C. Bocquet, Serguei Soubatch, F. Stefan Tautz, Ulrich Höfer, and Peter Puschnig

Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography tracks photoelectron profiles to reconstruct the real-space distribution and internal quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031054] Published Fri Aug 28, 2026.
tldr: Femtosecond time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography is used to reconstruct the real-space distribution and quantum phase of excitons in an organic semiconductor.
motivation: Understanding how exciton wave functions evolve in space and time is central to organic optoelectronics, but direct experimental access to the real-space shape and internal phase of excitons has been lacking.
method: The authors combine femtosecond time-resolved photoemission with orbital tomography, tracking photoelectron momentum maps as a function of delay to reconstruct the real-space exciton distribution and its internal quantum phase.
result: The measurement yields spatially and temporally resolved images of the exciton wave function in an organic semiconductor film, revealing its real-space structure and phase evolution.
conclusion: Time-resolved photoemission orbital tomography provides a route to directly visualize exciton quantum wave functions in molecular materials, with implications for understanding energy transport in organic electronics.

title: Particle View Of Many-Body Electronic Structure With Neural Network Wave Function
authors: Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, And Ji Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Wang, Weizhong Fu, Zhe Li, Weiluo Ren, and Ji Chen

A combination of theoretical approaches bridges the gap between complex quantum wave functions and the classical picture of electron positions for molecules and solids.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031048] Published Mon Aug 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper combines neural-network quantum wave functions with particle-resolved classical-like descriptions to interpret many-body electronic structure in molecules and solids.
motivation: Complex many-body wave functions are hard to connect to intuitive classical pictures of electron positions, limiting physical insight from highly expressive variational ansätze.
method: Neural-network wave function ansätze (e.g., FermiNet/Psiformer-style) are trained for molecular and solid-state electronic structure, and analysis tools are developed to extract particle-level/correlation information from the learned wave functions.
result: The approach yields accurate ground-state energies while providing an interpretable particle view that bridges quantum wave functions and classical electron-position intuition.
conclusion: Neural-network wave functions can serve both as high-accuracy solvers and as a route to physical interpretation of electronic correlations in molecules and solids.

title: Erratum: Faster Quantum Chemistry Simulations On A Quantum Computer With Improved Tensor Factorization And Active Volume Compilation [prx Quantum 6, 030337 (2025)]
authors: Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, And Christofer S. Tautermann
abstract:
Author(s): Athena Caesura, Cristian L. Cortes, William Pol, Sukin Sim, Mark Steudtner, Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, Michael Streif, and Christofer S. Tautermann
[PRX Quantum 7, 049901] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the authors' earlier PRX Quantum paper on faster quantum chemistry simulations using improved tensor factorization and active volume compilation.
motivation: The original work aimed to reduce the quantum resources required for molecular energy estimation on fault-tolerant quantum computers by improving tensor factorization and circuit compilation.
method: No new method is presented; the erratum records corrections to the published results of the original quantum-chemistry simulation study.
result: The erratum supplies corrected statements/details for the original article rather than new technical findings.
conclusion: The item is administrative in nature and offers no contribution to quantum information theory, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Orbitally Tuned Composite-Fermion Pairing Transitions In Bilayer Graphene
authors: Ravi Kumar, Tomer Firon, André Haug, Misha Yutushui, Alon Ner Gaon, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, David F. Mross, And Yuval Ronen
abstract:
Author(s): Ravi Kumar, Tomer Firon, André Haug, Misha Yutushui, Alon Ner Gaon, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, David F. Mross, and Yuval Ronen

The effective interaction between composite fermions, set entirely by the Coulomb potential and the underlying electronic Landau level orbitals, can stabilize exotic fractional quantum Hall states. In particular, half-filled Landau levels with different orbital character can host either metallic or …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166602] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies how orbital character of half-filled Landau levels in bilayer graphene tunes transitions between metallic and paired composite-fermion fractional quantum Hall states.
motivation: The effective interaction between composite fermions in the fractional quantum Hall regime can stabilize exotic paired states, and bilayer graphene offers orbital degrees of freedom that may control which state appears.
method: The authors use transport measurements in bilayer graphene devices to probe half-filled Landau levels with different orbital character, tuning the composite-fermion pairing transition via experimental parameters.
result: Different orbital characters of the underlying electronic Landau levels are found to stabilize either metallic or paired composite-fermion states, demonstrating orbital tuning of the pairing transition.
conclusion: The work shows that Landau-level orbital character is a key control parameter for composite-fermion pairing in bilayer graphene, enabling access to distinct fractional quantum Hall phases.

title: Raman Scattering Spectroscopic Observation Of A Ferroelastic Crossover In Bond-frustrated ${\mathrm{PrCd}}_{3}{\mathrm{P}}_{3}$
authors: Jackson Davis, Jesse Liebman, Dibyata Rout, S. J. Gomez Alvarado, Stephen D. Wilson, And Natalia Drichko
abstract:
Author(s): Jackson Davis, Jesse Liebman, Dibyata Rout, S. J. Gomez Alvarado, Stephen D. Wilson, and Natalia Drichko

Two-dimensional magnetism in triangular lattices has already shown a potential for hosting exotic magnetic states. Control of these magnetic states, both in terms of magnetic properties and in terms of charge doping would be the next step. This makes materials which combine triangular lattice magnet…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204308] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Raman scattering spectroscopy is used to observe a ferroelastic structural crossover in the bond-frustrated triangular-lattice material PrCd3P3.
motivation: Triangular-lattice magnets host exotic magnetic states, and controlling them via structural or charge degrees of freedom requires understanding the lattice response of candidate materials.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman scattering spectroscopy as a function of temperature, interpreted alongside the material's structural and magnetic characterization.
result: A ferroelastic crossover is identified spectroscopically, revealing how lattice degrees of freedom couple to the frustrated magnetism in PrCd3P3.
conclusion: The work establishes the structural behavior of a triangular-lattice magnet, providing a materials basis for future control of frustrated magnetic states.

title: Strain Engineering Of Transient Exciton Diffusion In ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Monolayers At Cryogenic Temperatures
authors: Roberto Rosati, Mohammed Adel Aly, Robert Schmidt, Rudolf Bratschitsch, And Ermin Malic
abstract:
Author(s): Roberto Rosati, Mohammed Adel Aly, Robert Schmidt, Rudolf Bratschitsch, and Ermin Malic

Here, the authors show how strain allows control of the spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in WSe
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245414] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how strain controls transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures through phonon-mediated scattering effects.
motivation: Understanding and controlling exciton transport in two-dimensional semiconductors is important for optoelectronic and valleytronic applications.
method: The authors analyze spatiotemporal exciton dynamics in strained WSe2 monolayers, attributing changes in diffusion to hot-exciton excess energy and phonon-mediated bright-to-dark exciton scattering.
result: Tensile strain accelerates transient exciton diffusion by increasing hot-exciton excess energy and suppressing phonon-mediated bright-to-dark scattering, while compressive strain is predicted to produce periodic modulation via phonon emission.
conclusion: Strain engineering provides a route to manipulate exciton diffusion dynamics in monolayer semiconductors at cryogenic temperatures.

title: Pumping Of Spin Supercurrent And Quasiparticle Spin Current In Unitary Triplet Superconductors
authors: Ping Li And Tao Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Ping Li and Tao Yu

One efficient mechanism for generating a charge supercurrent is Andreev reflection, in which the electric current injected from a normal metal into a conventional superconductor (SC) is converted into a supercurrent, thereby preserving charge conservation. Here, we propose a general principle for ge…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194412] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a mechanism for generating spin supercurrent and quasiparticle spin current in unitary triplet superconductors, analogous to Andreev reflection for charge supercurrents.
motivation: Charge supercurrents can be generated efficiently via Andreev reflection, but an analogous general principle for spin supercurrents in triplet superconductors is less established.
method: The authors develop a theoretical principle for converting injected currents into spin supercurrents and quasiparticle spin currents in unitary triplet superconducting systems.
result: The proposal identifies conditions under which spin supercurrent and quasiparticle spin current can be pumped in unitary triplet superconductors.
conclusion: This work provides a general mechanism for spin-current generation in triplet superconductors, with potential relevance to superconducting spintronics.

title: Noise-induced Bistability Of Information-driven Active Agents In Turbulence
authors: Chenfeng Ma And Yan Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Chenfeng Ma and Yan Cui

Information-driven active matter relies on continuous feedback loops subject to intrinsic processing latency. We investigate how this temporal nonlocality interacts with the spatial fluctuations of homogeneous isotropic turbulence for agents operating in the dilute, noncommunicating limit. This inte…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045403] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies noise-induced bistability in information-driven active agents with feedback latency moving through homogeneous isotropic turbulence.
motivation: Information-driven active matter involves delayed feedback, and the authors ask how this temporal nonlocality interacts with turbulent spatial fluctuations in the dilute noncommunicating limit.
method: The analysis considers active agents in homogeneous isotropic turbulence and examines the interplay between intrinsic processing latency and turbulent fluctuations, likely through stochastic modeling or numerical simulation.
result: The work reports noise-induced bistability arising from the coupling of feedback latency and turbulent fluctuations.
conclusion: The findings show that delayed information-driven dynamics in turbulence can produce bistable behavior, but the paper is in classical active matter and does not connect to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Time-domain Transient Growth In non-Hermitian Cascaded $lc$ Circuits
authors: Liangliang Ye, Mingyong Ye, Xiang Chen, Gongwei Lin, And Xiumin Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Liangliang Ye, Mingyong Ye, Xiang Chen, Gongwei Lin, and Xiumin Lin

Transient growth is a counterintuitive dynamical process in which a system state or observable undergoes pronounced temporary amplification during its evolution, even in the presence of substantial dissipation. Here, we demonstrate time-domain transient growth in non-Hermitian cascaded LC circuits w…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044210] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors demonstrate and analyze time-domain transient growth—temporary state amplification despite dissipation—in cascaded non-Hermitian LC circuits.
motivation: Transient growth is a counterintuitive non-normal dynamical effect known from fluid mechanics and photonics; the paper asks whether it can be realized and controlled in a simple classical electrical circuit platform.
method: Cascaded LC circuit networks with non-Hermitian (gain/loss) couplings are modeled, and their time-domain response is computed and (likely) experimentally or numerically characterized to identify regimes of large transient amplification and non-normality-driven dynamics.
result: Pronounced temporary amplification of the circuit state is observed even with substantial dissipation, with the growth characteristics tied to the non-Hermitian structure and cascading of the circuit stages.
conclusion: Cascaded LC circuits provide a tunable classical testbed for non-Hermitian transient-growth physics, potentially useful for sensing or signal amplification schemes.

title: Geometric And Dynamical Signatures Of Chaos In An Effective beyond-Newtonian Circular Restricted Three-body Problem With Rotating Compact Primaries
authors: Yeasin Ali, Suparna Roychowdhury, Betti Hartmann, And Roopkatha Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Yeasin Ali, Suparna Roychowdhury, Betti Hartmann, and Roopkatha Banerjee

We study the transition from order to chaos in an effective Hamiltonian three-body system governed by a static, position-dependent effective beyond-Newtonian potential for rotating compact primaries derived from the Fodor–Hoenselaers–Perjés formalism. The model constitutes a perturbed extension of t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044207] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper maps the order-to-chaos transition in a classical effective Hamiltonian three-body problem built from a beyond-Newtonian Fodor–Hoenselaers–Perjés potential with rotating compact primaries.
motivation: Beyond-Newtonian corrections to the circular restricted three-body problem are relevant for describing dynamics around compact objects, but the chaotic behaviour of such effective potentials is not yet well characterized.
method: The authors construct the effective Hamiltonian from the Fodor–Hoenselaers–Perjés formalism and diagnose chaos geometrically and dynamically, presumably via Poincaré sections, Lyapunov exponents, and basin/fractal or curvature-based indicators.
result: The system exhibits a transition from regular to chaotic motion as parameters (e.g., rotation and beyond-Newtonian correction strength) are varied, with geometric indicators of chaos correlating with dynamical instability measures.
conclusion: Beyond-Newtonian corrections qualitatively reshape the phase-space structure and chaos onset of the restricted three-body problem, with implications for the stability of orbits around rotating compact binaries.

title: Efficient Simulation Of Bose-Einstein Condensates In Nontrivial Topologies
authors: A. Beregi, J.-B. Gerent, And N. Lundblad
abstract:
Author(s): A. Beregi, J.-B. Gerent, and N. Lundblad

Bubble-shaped Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) constitute a unique class of quantum fluids with a hollow, thin-shell geometry that supports a wide variety of phenomena distinct from those of compact condensates. Numerical simulation of such systems is particularly challenging due to their inherently…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043051] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents efficient numerical methods for simulating bubble-shaped Bose-Einstein condensates in nontrivial topologies.
motivation: Bubble-shaped BECs have hollow thin-shell geometry that enables phenomena distinct from compact condensates, but their numerical simulation is challenging.
method: The authors develop efficient simulation techniques tailored to the nontrivial topology and thin-shell geometry of bubble BECs.
result: The work enables practical numerical study of bubble-shaped BEC systems that were previously difficult to simulate.
conclusion: The methods provide a computational tool for exploring quantum fluid phenomena in hollow, shell-like condensates.

title: Population Pumping Of Vibrational And Rotational Quantum States In The Triatomic Hydrogen Ion Observed By Electron-beam-assisted High-resolution Spectroscopy
authors: Marleen Maxton, Lukas Berger, Jonas Bechtel, Lucia Enzmann, Manfred Grieser, Florian Grussie, Jannis Himmelsbach, Leonard W. Isberner, Viviane C. Schmidt, Deepak Sharma, Andreas Wolf, Aigars Znotins, Xavier Urbain, Oldřich Novotný, And Holger Kreckel
abstract:
Author(s): Marleen Maxton, Lukas Berger, Jonas Bechtel, Lucia Enzmann, Manfred Grieser, Florian Grussie, Jannis Himmelsbach, Leonard W. Isberner, Viviane C. Schmidt, Deepak Sharma, Andreas Wolf, Aigars Znotins, Xavier Urbain, Oldřich Novotný, and Holger Kreckel

We present a technique to observe the optical manipulation of individual quantum states of [MATH] ions stored inside a heavy-ion storage ring, where the excitation is detected by electron-beam-assisted action spectroscopy. The transitions addressed here are chosen to enable multicolo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043045] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates optical pumping and high-resolution action spectroscopy of vibrational and rotational states of triatomic hydrogen ions stored in a heavy-ion storage ring.
motivation: The work aims to enable precise optical manipulation and detection of individual rovibrational quantum states of molecular ions in a storage-ring environment.
method: Stored triatomic hydrogen ions are optically excited, and the resulting state changes are detected via electron-beam-assisted action spectroscopy in a heavy-ion storage ring.
result: The authors observe population pumping of selected vibrational and rotational states and resolve transitions chosen for multicolor spectroscopic schemes.
conclusion: The technique provides a route to high-resolution state-selective spectroscopy and optical control of molecular ion quantum states in storage rings.

title: Pressure-induced Unconventional Charge-density-wave States In Kagome Metal ${\mathrm{AV}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$ ($\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{K}$, Rb, Cs)
authors: Zhimian Wu, Linpeng Nie, Ye Yang, Kuanglv Sun, Huachen Rao, Dan Zhao, Zhongjun Li, Tao Wu, And Xianhui Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Zhimian Wu, Linpeng Nie, Ye Yang, Kuanglv Sun, Huachen Rao, Dan Zhao, Zhongjun Li, Tao Wu, and Xianhui Chen

Since the discovery of charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity, kagome metal [MATH] ([MATH], Rb, Cs) provides a new platform for exploring novel many-body quantum phenomena. In [MATH], a stripelike CDW with commens…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043050] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally investigates pressure-induced unconventional charge-density-wave states in kagome metals AV3Sb5 (A = K, Rb, Cs).
motivation: Kagome metals AV3Sb5 host charge density waves and superconductivity, providing a platform for exploring correlated many-body quantum phenomena.
method: The study uses pressure as a tuning parameter to probe changes in the charge-density-wave states of AV3Sb5 compounds, likely through high-pressure experimental measurements.
result: Pressure is reported to induce unconventional charge-density-wave states in the kagome metal family AV3Sb5.
conclusion: The work clarifies the pressure-dependent behavior of charge order in kagome metals and its relationship to other correlated phases such as superconductivity.

title: Two-dimensional Spectroscopy Of Bosonic Collective Excitations In Disordered Many-body Systems
authors: Alex Gómez-Salvador, Ivan Morera, Marios H. Michael, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Danica Pavicevic, Albert Liu, Andrea Cavalleri, And Eugene Demler
abstract:
Author(s): Alex Gómez-Salvador, Ivan Morera, Marios H. Michael, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Danica Pavicevic, Albert Liu, Andrea Cavalleri, and Eugene Demler

We present a theoretical approach for computing and analyzing two-dimensional spectroscopy of bosonic collective excitations in disordered many-body systems. Specifically, we employ the Keldysh formalism to derive, within a nonperturbative treatment of disorder effects, the third-order nonlinear res…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043031] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a Keldysh-formalism theory for computing and interpreting two-dimensional spectroscopy of bosonic collective excitations in disordered many-body systems.
motivation: Two-dimensional spectroscopy is a powerful probe of collective dynamics, but its theoretical description in disordered bosonic many-body systems requires a nonperturbative treatment of disorder and nonlinear response.
method: The authors use the Keldysh formalism to derive the third-order nonlinear response for bosonic collective excitations while treating disorder effects nonperturbatively.
result: The approach provides a theoretical framework for calculating and analyzing 2D spectroscopic signals of disordered bosonic collective modes.
conclusion: This work offers a tool for interpreting multidimensional spectroscopy in complex many-body systems, though it does not directly address quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum-system platforms.

title: Effective Ionic Valence And Local Magnetic Moment In Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, And Wei Ku
abstract:
Author(s): Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, and Wei Ku

Revealing concealed ionic local moments in kagome superconductors reflects strong local correlations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031064] Published Thu Sep 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the effective ionic valence and hidden local magnetic moments in kagome superconductors, arguing that concealed local moments indicate strong local electronic correlations.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between superconductivity and magnetism in kagome metals requires clarifying the charge state and magnetic character of the constituent ions, which is obscured in bulk measurements.
method: The authors combine spectroscopic, thermodynamic, and local-probe techniques (including muon spin relaxation) with theoretical modeling to extract effective ionic valences and local moments in kagome superconductor compounds.
result: They find evidence for concealed ionic local moments that deviate from naive formal valence expectations, pointing to strong local correlations in these materials.
conclusion: The work emphasizes that local moments and correlation effects must be accounted for in models of kagome superconductivity.

title: Precision Hypernuclear Structure From Interaction Cross Sections
authors: Carlos A. Bertulani
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos A. Bertulani

We establish interaction cross sections as a quantitative structural observable for hypernuclei. Using the hypertriton, [MATH], as the most stringent benchmark, microscopic three-body wave functions are combined with a finite-range coupled-channel Glauber calculation and Bayes…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 162502] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes nuclear interaction cross sections as a quantitative structural observable for hypernuclei, using hypertriton as a benchmark.
motivation: Hypernuclear structure is difficult to probe directly, so the authors aim to validate interaction cross sections as a practical observable for extracting structural information about hypernuclei.
method: Microscopic three-body wave functions are combined with a finite-range coupled-channel Glauber calculation and a Bayesian analysis to compute and fit interaction cross sections.
result: The approach reproduces the hypertriton benchmark and yields quantitative structural constraints, demonstrating that cross-section measurements can serve as a precision structural probe.
conclusion: Interaction cross sections are shown to be a viable quantitative observable for hypernuclear structure, with implications for future precision measurements.

title: Hidden Simplicity In AdS Spinning Mellin Amplitudes Via Scaffolding
authors: Song He (何颂), Xiang Li (李想), Yuyu Mo (莫裕宇), And Dongyu Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Song He (何颂), Xiang Li (李想), Yuyu Mo (莫裕宇), and Dongyu Yang (杨东昱)

We uncover surprising hidden simplicity in Mellin amplitudes for tree-level anti–de Sitter (AdS) holographic correlators for AdS “gluon” (spin-1) operators. We define Mellin amplitudes with [MATH] spinning operators via the so-called scaffolding of [MATH]-scalar ones with specific projection operators fo…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 161602] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper uncovers hidden simplicity in tree-level AdS Mellin amplitudes for holographic correlators of spin-1 'gluon' operators by constructing spinning Mellin amplitudes through scaffolding of scalar ones with projection operators.
motivation: Mellin amplitudes provide a natural language for AdS/CFT holographic correlators, but treating spinning operators has been technically cumbersome; the authors aim to simplify the computation and reveal structure for spin-1 operators.
method: They define Mellin amplitudes for spinning operators via a scaffolding procedure that builds them from scalar Mellin amplitudes dressed with specific projection operators, then analyze the resulting tree-level correlators.
result: The construction reveals unexpected compactness and hidden simplicity in the spinning Mellin amplitudes, indicating that the scaffolding approach efficiently captures the tensor structure of holographic correlators.
conclusion: Scaffolding offers a practical and structurally revealing route to spinning Mellin amplitudes, potentially extendable to higher spins and loop-level holographic correlators.

title: Geometry Of In-In Correlators
authors: Ross Glew
abstract:
Author(s): Ross Glew

We introduce a family of polytopes—in-in zonotopes—whose boundary structure organizes the contributions to scalar equal-time correlators in flat space computed via the in-in formalism. We provide explicit Minkowski sum and facet descriptions of these polytopes, and show that their boundaries factori…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 161603] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces 'in-in zonotopes', a family of polytopes whose boundary structure organizes contributions to equal-time scalar correlators in flat space computed via the in-in formalism.
motivation: Equal-time correlators in the in-in (Schwinger-Keldysh) formalism involve complicated sums over diagrams and time orderings; a geometric organizing principle could systematize these contributions.
method: Constructs a family of polytopes via explicit Minkowski sum and facet descriptions, and shows that their boundaries factorize in a way that mirrors the structure of the correlator contributions.
result: Explicit Minkowski-sum and facet characterizations of in-in zonotopes are given, with the boundary factorization shown to encode the organization of scalar equal-time correlator terms.
conclusion: Polytope geometry provides a compact combinatorial framework for in-in cosmological/field-theoretic correlators, but the work lies outside quantum information science.

title: Particle Correlations In Jets
authors: Wenbin Zhao, Volker Koch, And Feng Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Wenbin Zhao, Volker Koch, and Feng Yuan

We study particle correlations in high energy jets by comparing the measured energy-energy correlator with that constructed from two individual energy flows with respect to the jet axis. This comparison demonstrates that the genuine correlations are stronger at moderate or large angles across all je…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 162301] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares measured energy-energy correlators in high-energy jets with correlators built from two independent energy flows, showing that genuine particle correlations dominate at moderate to large angles across jet energies.
motivation: Energy-energy correlators are a powerful probe of jet substructure, but it is unclear how much of the observed correlation reflects genuine many-particle dynamics versus trivial kinematic or single-particle effects.
method: Using jet data, the authors construct a baseline correlator from two separate energy flows measured relative to the jet axis and compare it to the full energy-energy correlator, isolating the genuine correlation component as a function of angle and jet energy.
result: Genuine correlations are found to be stronger at moderate and large angles for all jet energies considered, while the baseline construction captures the small-angle behavior.
conclusion: The two-flow baseline provides a useful reference for interpreting energy-energy correlators, and the residual correlation quantifies non-trivial jet dynamics at wider angles.

title: Minimum Energy And Photon Content In $PT$-Symmetric Metamaterials
authors: J. B. Pendry And S. A. R. Horsley
abstract:
Author(s): J. B. Pendry and S. A. R. Horsley

In the context of waves in space-time modulated materials, we ask two questions: (1) how much energy does it cost to break time reversal symmetry ([MATH]-symmetry) and transition to a [MATH]-symmetric state? and (2) can a [MATH]-symmetric system have a “ground state” in the sense that no photons are presen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 163604] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the minimum energy required to break time-reversal symmetry and the possible existence of a zero-photon ground state in PT-symmetric metamaterials.
motivation: PT-symmetric and space-time-modulated materials raise fundamental questions about symmetry breaking, energy cost, and photon occupation in classical wave systems.
method: The authors theoretically study electromagnetic waves in space-time modulated PT-symmetric metamaterials, quantifying the energy needed to transition from a time-reversal-symmetric state to a PT-symmetric state and examining whether a no-photon ground state can exist.
result: The paper derives conditions and energy bounds for PT-symmetry breaking and clarifies the photon content of the resulting PT-symmetric states.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the energetics and ground-state properties of PT-symmetric photonic metamaterials, but they are not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Hybrid Ab Initio And Empirical Machine Learning Models For The Potential Energy Surface
authors: Pablo Peña-Cano And Pablo M. Piaggi
abstract:
Author(s): Pablo Peña-Cano and Pablo M. Piaggi

We propose a methodology to generate hybrid machine learning models for the potential energy surface trained simultaneously on data from ab initio electronic structure calculations and on thermodynamic and/or structural observables from experiment. The approach is based on the use of a loss function…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166102] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes hybrid machine-learning models for potential energy surfaces trained jointly on ab initio data and experimental thermodynamic or structural observables.
motivation: Machine-learned potential energy surfaces often rely solely on ab initio data and may not reproduce experimental thermodynamic or structural properties accurately.
method: A loss function is designed to train hybrid models simultaneously on ab initio electronic-structure data and experimental thermodynamic and/or structural observables.
result: The hybrid training methodology yields models that incorporate both quantum-chemical and experimental information for improved potential energy surface construction.
conclusion: Combining ab initio and empirical data in machine-learning potentials can improve their physical fidelity, but the work is outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Orbitronics: Orbit-Spin Interconversions For Long-Range Orbital Propagation Enabled By Spin Current
authors: Melissa Yactayo, A. Pezo, J. L. Ampuero, M. Tian, L. Badie, J. Quispe-Marcatoma, C. V. Landauro, Y. Xu, Sébastien Petit-Watelot, Michel Hehn, A. Fert, And J.-C. Rojas-Sánchez
abstract:
Author(s): Melissa Yactayo, A. Pezo, J. L. Ampuero, M. Tian, L. Badie, J. Quispe-Marcatoma, C. V. Landauro, Y. Xu, Sébastien Petit-Watelot, Michel Hehn, A. Fert, and J.-C. Rojas-Sánchez

Long distance orbital effects in light elements like titanium are not due to long orbital diffusion lengths, but rather by a multistep mechanism in which orbital accumulation is locally converted into spin current that mediates long-range transport and is reconverted at a distant interface.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166701] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Long-range orbital accumulation in light elements such as titanium arises not from long orbital diffusion lengths but from a multistep mechanism in which orbital accumulation is locally converted into spin current, transported, and reconverted at a distant interface.
motivation: Orbital transport phenomena in light metals are poorly understood, and naive interpretations based on long orbital diffusion lengths are questionable; the authors aim to identify the actual mechanism enabling long-distance orbital effects.
method: Spin/charge transport and interface-conversion experiments on Ti-based heterostructures, analyzing orbital-to-spin and spin-to-orbital interconversion as a function of distance and geometry.
result: The observed long-range orbital signals are explained by local orbital-to-spin conversion followed by spin-current-mediated transport and reconversion to orbital accumulation at a remote interface.
conclusion: Orbitronics functionalities in light elements rely on spin-current mediation rather than long orbital diffusion, which reframes design rules for orbital-based spintronic devices.

title: Spin-orbit-resolved Resonant Auger Spectrum Of A Dissociating HCl Molecule
authors: M. Žitnik, J. Turnšek, K. Bučar, And A. Mihelič
abstract:
Author(s): M. Žitnik, J. Turnšek, K. Bučar, and A. Mihelič

The photodissociation of HCl via the antibonding [MATH] resonance occurs on the same 10-fs timescale as the Auger decay of the [MATH] vacancy. This means that the [MATH], and [MATH] valence molecular orbitals involved in the electronic transition can signif…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043111] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A time-resolved spectroscopic study of how the spin-orbit-resolved resonant Auger spectrum of HCl is modified by photodissociation occurring on the same 10-fs timescale as the core-hole decay.
motivation: The antibonding resonance in HCl dissociates on a timescale comparable to Auger decay of the core vacancy, so the valence molecular orbitals involved in the electronic transition change appreciably during the decay, requiring a treatment that goes beyond the frozen-nuclei picture.
method: High-resolution resonant Auger electron spectroscopy of HCl combined with modeling of the competing electronic decay and nuclear dissociation dynamics, resolving the spin-orbit components of the final states.
result: The measured spectrum shows spin-orbit-resolved features whose intensities and positions deviate from the static-molecule prediction, reflecting the influence of the ~10-fs dissociation on the Auger transition matrix elements.
conclusion: Coupling between ultrafast nuclear motion and core-hole decay must be included to interpret resonant Auger spectra of small molecules, providing a benchmark for femtosecond molecular dynamics models.

title: Modeling Angularly Resolved Resonant Phase Jumps In Fine-structure-split Regions Of Heavy Atoms
authors: Elisei Mankov, Soumyajit Saha, Anton Ljungdahl, Johanna Sörngård, Jimmy Vinbladh, Eva Lindroth, And C. Leon M. Petersson
abstract:

In the current communication, we use the random phase approximation with exchange method to investigate the fine-structure split energy region between the first and second ionization thresholds of xenon and radon. Such regions can be found in all noble gases, save for helium, and contain a series of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043112] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper models angularly resolved resonant phase jumps in fine-structure-split ionization regions of Xe and Rn using the random phase approximation with exchange.
motivation: Fine-structure-split regions between ionization thresholds in heavy noble gases host complex resonant photoionization dynamics that require accurate theoretical treatment.
method: The authors apply the random phase approximation with exchange to compute photoionization amplitudes and angularly resolved phase behavior in xenon and radon.
result: The calculations characterize resonant phase jumps across the fine-structure-split energy region and identify corresponding resonance structures.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical description of angularly resolved resonant phase behavior in heavy noble-gas photoionization, relevant to atomic and molecular physics rather than quantum information.

title: Geometro-optical Depolarization Manifold As An Organizing Principle For Plasmonic Transitions
authors: Isuf Tredhaku, Ana Sánchez-Iglesias, Ivan Petranović, Marek Grzelczak, Jordi Sancho-Parramon, And Stefano A. Mezzasalma
abstract:
Author(s): Isuf Tredhaku, Ana Sánchez-Iglesias, Ivan Petranović, Marek Grzelczak, Jordi Sancho-Parramon, and Stefano A. Mezzasalma

Using differential calculus, we derive an exact dipolar condition for the extinction peak position of a nanocrystal, reducing the problem of locating the extinction maximum to a differentiable state equation. This leads to a characteristic polynomial for the plasmon frequency whose coefficients are …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043521] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors derive an exact differential-calculus condition for the dipolar extinction peak of a nanocrystal, recasting plasmon-peak location as a differentiable state equation and a characteristic polynomial in the plasmon frequency.
motivation: Locating the extinction maximum of plasmonic nanocrystals is typically handled numerically or through approximations; a closed, differentiable condition would give a cleaner organizing principle for plasmonic transitions and depolarization behavior.
method: Differential calculus is applied to the dipolar polarizability/extinction cross-section, yielding a characteristic polynomial whose coefficients encode the plasmon frequency and depolarization factors of the nanocrystal geometry.
result: An exact dipolar condition for the extinction peak position is obtained, reducing peak-finding to solving a characteristic polynomial, with the geometry entering through depolarization parameters.
conclusion: The depolarization manifold provides a compact organizing framework for plasmon resonances in nanocrystals, potentially useful for interpreting and designing plasmonic extinction spectra.

title: Vortex Photoelectron Holography In Strong-field Tunneling Ionization
authors: Yongkun Chen, Oleg I. Tolstikhin, Toru Morishita, Yueming Zhou, And Peixiang Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Yongkun Chen, Oleg I. Tolstikhin, Toru Morishita, Yueming Zhou, and Peixiang Lu

The authors theoretically demonstrate vortex photoelectron holography in strong-field tunneling ionization, in which the vortex photoelectron is generated via tunneling ionization of an atom in a state with a nonzero magnetic quantum number. They show that the phase of the elastic scattering amplitude for the vortex electron–atom interaction can be extracted from the hologram.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, L041101] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors theoretically demonstrate vortex photoelectron holography arising in strong-field tunneling ionization of atoms prepared in a state with nonzero magnetic quantum number, and show that the phase of the elastic electron–atom scattering amplitude can be extracted from the resulting hologram.
motivation: Strong-field tunneling ionization produces holographic interference structures that encode the electron's rescattering dynamics; extending this to vortex (angular-momentum-carrying) photoelectrons offers a new probe of scattering phases.
method: Theoretical treatment of tunneling ionization from an atomic state with nonzero magnetic quantum number, computing the vortex photoelectron wavefunction and its interference hologram, then inverting the hologram to recover the elastic scattering amplitude phase.
result: Vortex photoelectron holograms are predicted, and the phase of the elastic scattering amplitude for the vortex electron–atom interaction is shown to be retrievable from the holographic pattern.
conclusion: Vortex photoelectron holography provides a viable route to characterizing electron–atom scattering phases in strong-field ionization, though it lies outside quantum information science.

title: Suppression Of Electron-phonon Coupling And Emergence Of Spin-phonon Coupling In Orthorhombic ${\mathrm{CsCr}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$
authors: Bingru Lu, Yi Liu, Keyi Li, Jing Kang, Hao Li, Xiang Li, Wenbo Sang, Anmin Zhang, Jianting Ji, Guanghan Cao, Feng Jin, And Qingming Zhang

In the correlated kagome metal [MATH], the interplay among lattice, charge, and spin degrees of freedom governs its rich quantum phases, yet remains poorly understood. Here, we present a comprehensive investigation of these couplings through temperature- and magnetic-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204106] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies electron-phonon and spin-phonon coupling in the correlated kagome metal CsCr3Sb5 using temperature- and magnetic-field-dependent measurements.
motivation: The interplay among lattice, charge, and spin degrees of freedom in correlated kagome metals is poorly understood, motivating a detailed investigation of coupling mechanisms in CsCr3Sb5.
method: The authors perform a comprehensive experimental investigation using temperature- and magnetic-field-dependent techniques to probe phonon and spin dynamics in orthorhombic CsCr3Sb5.
result: They report suppression of electron-phonon coupling and the emergence of spin-phonon coupling in this material.
conclusion: The work clarifies how lattice, charge, and spin degrees of freedom interact in CsCr3Sb5, but it is a condensed-matter study without direct relevance to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Lattice Instability In The Charge Density Wave System $R{\mathrm{Pt}}_{2}{\mathrm{Si}}_{2}$ $(R=\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}\mathrm{Pr}, \mathrm{Nd})$
authors: V. Petkov, A. Zafar, M. Jakhar, L. Gallington, P. Kenesei, And S. D. Shastri
abstract:
Author(s): V. Petkov, A. Zafar, M. Jakhar, L. Gallington, P. Kenesei, and S. D. Shastri

Charge-density-wave (CDW) order in [MATH] [MATH] develops through a complex sequence of structural and electronic transitions. Using atomic pair distribution function analysis and large-scale structural modeling, we show that b…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214105] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Atomic pair distribution function analysis and large-scale structural modeling reveal a lattice instability underlying the charge-density-wave transitions in PrPt2Si2 and NdPt2Si2.
motivation: CDW order in intermetallic R Pt2 Si2 compounds develops through a complex sequence of structural and electronic transitions whose microscopic origin, particularly the role of lattice degrees of freedom, remains unclear.
method: The authors use synchrotron-based atomic pair distribution function (PDF) analysis combined with large-scale structural modeling to probe local lattice distortions across the CDW transitions.
result: The study identifies a local lattice instability that precedes and accompanies the CDW ordering, showing that structural disorder and local distortions are essential ingredients of the transition sequence.
conclusion: The findings establish lattice instability as a key driver of CDW formation in these systems, emphasizing the need for local-structure probes beyond average crystallographic descriptions.

title: Spin-locked Helical Currents And Charge-neutral Spin-channel Pumping In Altermagnetic Nanotubes
authors: Xin Chen, Zhen Han, Linyang Li, And Mingwen Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Xin Chen, Zhen Han, Linyang Li, and Mingwen Zhao

Altermagnetism has been widely explored in three- and two-dimensional crystals, but its one-dimensional realization remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose an altermagnetic nanotube formed by rolling a two-dimensional altermagnet, which converts symmetry-enforced directional spin anisotropy in …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235410] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes one-dimensional altermagnetic nanotubes and studies spin-locked helical currents and charge-neutral spin-channel pumping.
motivation: Altermagnetism has been explored mainly in two- and three-dimensional crystals, while its one-dimensional realization and transport consequences remain largely unexplored.
method: The authors roll a two-dimensional altermagnet into a nanotube and analyze symmetry-enforced spin anisotropy and current/pumping properties theoretically.
result: The nanotube geometry supports spin-locked helical currents and enables charge-neutral spin-channel pumping.
conclusion: Altermagnetic nanotubes provide a platform for one-dimensional altermagnetism and spin-based transport phenomena.

title: Concomitant Manipulation Of Effective Demagnetization Field And Magnetic Damping In ${\mathrm{Mn}}_{2}\mathrm{Au}/\mathrm{CoFeB}$ Heterostructures By Ultrafast Laser Excitation
authors: Donghang Xie, Shuai Zhang, Haozhe Wang, Zhuoyi Li, Jiarui Chen, Jiahua Lu, Bo Liu, Jun Du, Jing Wu, Ronghua Liu, Rong Zhang, Yongbing Xu, And Xuezhong Ruan
abstract:
Author(s): Donghang Xie, Shuai Zhang, Haozhe Wang, Zhuoyi Li, Jiarui Chen, Jiahua Lu, Bo Liu, Jun Du, Jing Wu, Ronghua Liu, Rong Zhang, Yongbing Xu, and Xuezhong Ruan

We report the magnetic dynamics of as-deposited [MATH] heterostructures via time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect spectroscopy. Increasing the pump fluence from 5 to [MATH] results in …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204414] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect measurements show that ultrafast laser excitation in Mn2Au/CoFeB heterostructures simultaneously tunes the effective demagnetization field and magnetic damping.
motivation: Antiferromagnet/ferromagnet heterostructures such as Mn2Au/CoFeB are promising for ultrafast spintronic devices, but how optical excitation controls the interfacial magnetic anisotropy and damping is not well understood.
method: As-deposited Mn2Au/CoFeB heterostructures were studied by time-resolved magneto-optical Kerr effect spectroscopy while varying the pump fluence from 5 to higher values, extracting precessional dynamics to obtain effective demagnetization fields and Gilbert damping.
result: Increasing pump fluence produces concomitant changes in the effective demagnetization field and the magnetic damping of the heterostructure, revealing fluence-dependent control of both anisotropy and relaxation.
conclusion: Ultrafast laser excitation provides a route to simultaneously manipulate magnetic anisotropy and damping in Mn2Au/CoFeB, relevant for optically driven spintronic applications.

title: Density Waves In Low-pressure Bilayer Nickelates
authors: Lauro B. Braz, Steffen Bötzel, Frank Lechermann, Igor Plokhikh, Rustem Khasanov, Luis G. G. V. Dias Da Silva, And Ilya M. Eremin

The low-pressure phase diagram of [MATH] provides an important reference for understanding its pressure-induced high-temperature superconductivity. While the spin-density-wave transition at [MATH] is …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 225124] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the low-pressure phase diagram and density-wave instabilities of bilayer nickelates as a reference for understanding their pressure-induced high-temperature superconductivity.
motivation: The low-pressure phase of bilayer nickelates is important for contextualizing the emergence of high-temperature superconductivity under pressure, but its density-wave ordering and transitions are not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze the low-pressure bilayer nickelate system theoretically and/or experimentally, focusing on spin-density-wave and related density-wave transitions in the phase diagram.
result: The paper characterizes density-wave behavior in the low-pressure bilayer nickelate phase diagram and discusses its relation to the pressure-induced superconducting state.
conclusion: These findings provide a baseline for understanding how density-wave order evolves with pressure and how it may compete or coexist with superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.

title: Theory Of A Strange Metal In A Quantum Superconductor To Metal Transition
authors: Jaewon Kim, Erez Berg, And Ehud Altman
abstract:
Author(s): Jaewon Kim, Erez Berg, and Ehud Altman

Recent experiments with nanopatterned thin films revealed an unusual quantum superconductor to metal phase transition (QSMT) with a linear-in-temperature resistivity. In contrast, most known examples of such transitions and standard theoretical considerations predict a temperature-independent sheet …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235119] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a theory for a strange-metal regime arising at a quantum superconductor-to-metal transition with linear-in-temperature resistivity.
motivation: Recent experiments on nanopatterned thin films observed an unusual quantum superconductor-to-metal transition with linear-in-T resistivity, contradicting standard expectations of temperature-independent sheet resistance.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for the quantum superconductor-to-metal transition and analyze the resulting metallic transport properties, focusing on the origin of strange-metal behavior.
result: The theory accounts for the observed linear-in-temperature resistivity and identifies a plausible mechanism for the strange-metal phase near the transition.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for understanding anomalous metallic transport in quantum superconductor-to-metal transitions, but it lies outside the specified quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems interests.

title: Imaging Van Hove Singularity Heterogeneity In Overdoped Graphene
authors: Raymond Blackwell, Zengyi Du, Takuya Okugawa, Asish K. Kundu, Zebin Wu, Ilya Drozdov, Kazuhiro Fujita, Angel Rubio, Dante M. Kennes, And Abhay N. Pasupathy
abstract:
Author(s): Raymond Blackwell, Zengyi Du, Takuya Okugawa, Asish K. Kundu, Zebin Wu, Ilya Drozdov, Kazuhiro Fujita, Angel Rubio, Dante M. Kennes, and Abhay N. Pasupathy

Tuning the chemical potential of a solid to the vicinity of a Van Hove singularity (VHS) is a well-established route to discovering emergent quantum phases. In monolayer graphene, the use of electron-donating metal layers has recently emerged as a method to dope the chemical potential to the nearest…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 245119] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy is used to image spatial heterogeneity of the Van Hove singularity in alkali-metal-doped overdoped monolayer graphene.
motivation: Tuning the chemical potential near a Van Hove singularity is a known route to emergent quantum phases, but the spatial uniformity of the VHS in electron-doped graphene had not been characterized at the nanoscale.
method: The authors use low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy to map the local density of states of overdoped graphene on a substrate, extracting the local VHS position and comparing with theory (including ab initio and lattice-model calculations).
result: They observe significant nanoscale heterogeneity in the VHS energy across the sample, correlated with structural/electronic disorder, indicating that the doping is not spatially uniform.
conclusion: The heterogeneity of the VHS must be accounted for when interpreting correlated or symmetry-broken phases induced by VHS tuning in doped graphene.

title: Mott Insulating Interface In Cuprate-based $p\text{−}n$ Bilayers
authors: Maxime Dion, Guo-Zhen Zhu, Guillaume Hardy, Gianluigi A. Botton, And Patrick Fournier

tldr: The authors fabricate and characterize all-cuprate p-n bilayers of PCCO and LSCO, showing that charge transfer at the atomically sharp interface produces a Mott insulating layer.
motivation: The p-n junction underpins modern electronics, and realizing one entirely from correlated cuprate superconductors could expose strong-correlation physics at interfaces, but the nature of such interfaces is poorly understood.
method: Epitaxial cuprate thin-film bilayers were grown and structurally assessed with x-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy, then probed electrically with a series of transport experiments.
result: A charge transfer between Pr2-xCexCuO4 and La2-xSrxCuO4 is observed, from which a Mott insulating layer emerges at the atomically sharp interface.
conclusion: Cuprate-based p-n junctions host correlation-driven interfacial insulating behavior, offering a materials platform for studying electronic reconstruction in strongly correlated oxides.

The effect can be understood as a consequence of the supercurrent-induced spin polarization, owing to the interplay between sp…

tldr: The paper predicts a supercurrent-driven Néel spin-orbit torque in superconductor/altermagnet heterostructures arising from spin-triplet correlations and supercurrent-induced spin polarization.
motivation: The work aims to understand how supercurrents can exert torques on altermagnetic order and how spin-triplet correlations mediate superconducting-spintronic effects in hybrid materials.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a superconductor/altermagnet heterostructure, focusing on the interplay between supercurrent-induced spin polarization and altermagnetic order.
result: They predict a Néel torque driven by the supercurrent, associated with the emergence of spin-triplet correlations in the hybrid system.
conclusion: The effect suggests a route for controlling altermagnetic order via superconducting currents, but it is primarily a condensed-matter/spintronics result rather than a quantum-information or information-thermodynamics contribution.

title: Pressure-induced Structural Modifications And Suppression Of Antiferromagnetism In The Van Der Waals Material CrSBr
authors: D. P. Kozlenko, O. N. Lis, S. E. Kichanov, E. V. Lukin, I. Yu. Zel, And B. N. Savenko

The crystal structure, vibrational spectra, and magnetic structure of the quasi-two-dimensional layered van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr were studied by means of x-ray diffraction (XRD) and Raman spectroscopy at high pressures up to 33 GPa and ambient temperature and neutron diffraction (ND) up t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194107] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure XRD, Raman and neutron diffraction reveal structural modifications and suppression of antiferromagnetic order in the layered van der Waals magnet CrSBr up to 33 GPa.
motivation: CrSBr is a quasi-two-dimensional van der Waals antiferromagnet of interest for layered magnetism, and its behavior under pressure probes the coupling between structure and magnetic order.
method: X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy at pressures up to 33 GPa at ambient temperature, combined with neutron diffraction under pressure to track the magnetic structure.
result: Pressure drives structural modifications of the layered lattice and progressively suppresses the antiferromagnetic ordering of CrSBr.
conclusion: The results map the pressure–structure–magnetism phase behavior of CrSBr, clarifying how lattice compression destabilizes its antiferromagnetic ground state.

The discovery of infinite-layer nickelate superconductors has generated great enthusiasm for exploring new nickelate superconductors with higher [MATH] and further elucidating their superconducting mechanism. In this work, we systematically investigate the pressure effect on both the nor…

tldr: This paper studies how positive pressure affects the superconducting transition in infinite-layer La0.8Sr0.2NiO2 thin films.
motivation: Infinite-layer nickelates have attracted interest as possible analogues of cuprate superconductors, and understanding pressure effects may help clarify their superconducting mechanism and guide the search for higher transition temperatures.
method: The authors systematically measure the pressure dependence of normal and superconducting states in La0.8Sr0.2NiO2 thin films under applied pressure.
result: The study reports the effect of positive pressure on the superconducting transition temperature and related transport properties of the nickelate thin film.
conclusion: The findings contribute to understanding superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates, but the work is a condensed-matter materials study rather than a quantum-information or quantum-thermodynamics paper.

title: Electron Transport In Disordered Borophene Nanoribbons With Hexagonal Vacancies
authors: Pei-Jia Hu, Jia-Le Yu, Irfan Hussain Bhat, Tie-Feng Fang, Ai-Min Guo, And Qing-Feng Sun

Borophene, an outstanding platform to elucidate the structure-property relationship, possesses diverse concentration and spatial arrangement of hexagonal vacancies (HVs) owing to its structural polymorphism. Here, we study electron transport in disordered borophene nanoribbons (BNRs) with two types …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204201] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies electron transport in disordered borophene nanoribbons containing hexagonal vacancies using theoretical transport calculations.
motivation: Borophene's structural polymorphism allows diverse arrangements of hexagonal vacancies, motivating a structure-property study of how disorder and vacancy configuration affect electronic transport.
method: The authors theoretically model disordered borophene nanoribbons with two types of hexagonal vacancy arrangements and compute electron transport properties, likely using tight-binding or related quantum transport methods.
result: The paper characterizes how hexagonal vacancies and disorder modify conductance and transport in borophene nanoribbons, revealing structure-dependent electron transport behavior.
conclusion: The findings clarify the relationship between vacancy disorder and transport in borophene nanoribbons, but the work is a condensed-matter transport study with no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ferroelectric-controllable Spin-orbit Torque In Two-dimensional Multiferroic Heterostructure
authors: Weiyi Pan, Gusthavo M. S. Brizolla, And Jaroslav Fabian
abstract:

Spin-orbit torque (SOT), which enables electrical control of magnetization, plays a crucial role in the development of next-generation spintronic devices. Realizing SOT in two-dimensional van der Waals systems, together with achieving efficient nonvolatile manipulation via ferroelectricity, would be…

tldr: The paper proposes ferroelectric control of spin-orbit torque in a two-dimensional van der Waals multiferroic heterostructure for nonvolatile spintronic device applications.
motivation: Spin-orbit torque enables electrical control of magnetization for next-generation spintronic memory and logic, but achieving efficient nonvolatile tunability in two-dimensional van der Waals systems remains challenging.
method: First-principles/electronic-structure modeling of a 2D multiferroic heterostructure is used to quantify spin-orbit torque and its response to ferroelectric polarization switching.
result: The ferroelectric polarization is shown to controllably modulate the magnitude and sign of the spin-orbit torque in the 2D heterostructure, enabling nonvolatile switching of the torque.
conclusion: Ferroelectric-multiferroic 2D heterostructures offer a viable route toward electrically reconfigurable, nonvolatile spintronic devices based on spin-orbit torque.

title: Optimal Skyrmion Stability In Antisymmetric Ultrathin Ferromagnetic Bilayers
authors: Anne Bernand-Mantel, Valeriy V. Slastikov, And Cyrill B. Muratov
abstract:

We demonstrate the stray-field-mediated skyrmion stabilizing capabilities of ultrathin exchange-decoupled antisymmetric ferromagnetic bilayers based on conventional transition metal materials. Using an asymptotically exact micromagnetic model valid in the ultrathin film limit, we show that the antis…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204412] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: An asymptotically exact micromagnetic analysis shows that exchange-decoupled antisymmetric ultrathin ferromagnetic bilayers made from conventional transition metals can stabilize skyrmions via stray-field effects.
motivation: Skyrmions are promising nanoscale magnetic textures for spintronic devices, but stabilizing them in ultrathin films of conventional transition metals without bulk Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction or chiral multilayer engineering remains difficult.
method: The authors derive and solve an asymptotically exact micromagnetic model in the ultrathin-film limit for an antisymmetric bilayer, treating the stray field (magnetostatic) coupling between the two exchange-decoupled layers.
result: The antisymmetric bilayer geometry yields a stray-field-mediated stabilization of skyrmions whose stability range is shown to be optimal with respect to layer thickness and material parameters.
conclusion: Antisymmetric ferromagnetic bilayers of conventional transition metals provide a practical route to robust skyrmion stabilization, with quantitative design rules from the asymptotic model.

title: Two-dimensional Anomalous Diffusion Of Coupled Active-passive Particles In Viscoelastic Media
authors: Pankaj Jangid And Srabanti Chaudhury
abstract:
Author(s): Pankaj Jangid and Srabanti Chaudhury

Anomalous diffusion is well studied in complex environments where viscoelasticity, crowding, and nonequilibrium activity strongly influence particle motion. Several biological systems are not independent; rather, they are coupled to another system, which shows distinct viscoelastic responses and het…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044126] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anomalous diffusion of coupled active-passive particles in viscoelastic media using a classical stochastic/biophysical modeling framework.
motivation: Many biological and complex-fluid systems involve coupled particles whose motion is affected by viscoelasticity, crowding, and nonequilibrium activity, motivating a better characterization of anomalous transport in such environments.
method: The authors likely model two coupled particles—one active and one passive—in a viscoelastic medium and analyze their two-dimensional diffusive behavior, possibly through stochastic equations or simulation.
result: The paper reports anomalous diffusion behavior arising from the coupling and viscoelastic response, showing distinct transport regimes compared with uncoupled or homogeneous cases.
conclusion: The findings clarify how active-passive coupling and viscoelasticity shape anomalous diffusion in complex media, with relevance to biological and soft-matter transport.

title: Critical Temperature Of The One-dimensional Ising Model With Inverse-square Interactions
authors: Owen Tower, Abdulai Gassama, Jonah Eick, Han Zhang, Lijie Ding, Jan Tobochnik, Robert A. Pelcovits, J. Michael Kosterlitz, And Xinsheng Sean Ling
abstract:
Author(s): Owen Tower, Abdulai Gassama, Jonah Eick, Han Zhang, Lijie Ding, Jan Tobochnik, Robert A. Pelcovits, J. Michael Kosterlitz, and Xinsheng Sean Ling

We analyze the critical temperature of the one-dimensional Ising model with inverse-square interactions. In the Anderson-Yuval-Kosterlitz (AYK) renormalization-group framework the transition temperature depends sensitively on the bare domain-wall fugacity, which is controlled by the domain-wall core…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044128] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes the critical temperature of the one-dimensional Ising model with inverse-square interactions using the Anderson-Yuval-Kosterlitz renormalization-group framework.
motivation: The transition temperature in this model is known to depend sensitively on the bare domain-wall fugacity, which is controlled by domain-wall core energy, motivating a detailed analysis of the critical temperature.
method: The authors use the Anderson-Yuval-Kosterlitz renormalization-group framework to study the domain-wall fugacity and determine the critical temperature.
result: The analysis shows that the critical temperature depends sensitively on the bare domain-wall fugacity and hence on the domain-wall core energy.
conclusion: The work clarifies the critical behavior of the one-dimensional inverse-square Ising model within the AYK renormalization-group picture.

title: Percolation In The Three-dimensional Ising Model
authors: Jinhong Zhu, Tao Chen, Zhiyi Li, Sheng Fang, And Youjin Deng
abstract:

tldr: The paper studies percolation transitions of geometric spin clusters in the three-dimensional Ising model, extending prior two-dimensional results.
motivation: Geometric representations offer insight into critical phenomena in the Ising model, and prior work found consecutive percolation transitions in the two-dimensional critical Ising model.
method: It analyzes geometric spin clusters in the three-dimensional Ising model, likely using numerical or cluster-based methods to identify percolation behavior as bond occupation varies.
result: The study characterizes percolation transition behavior for geometric clusters in the 3D Ising model, extending the 2D finding of multiple percolation transitions.
conclusion: The work provides a geometric percolation perspective on 3D Ising criticality but is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Gate Control Improves Routing Efficiency For Periodic Traffic
authors: Hyunwook Song, Hoyun Choi, And B. Kahng
abstract:
