Traffic movement on highways and data packet transmission across the Internet serve as prototypical examples of collective dynamical behavior in complex systems. Although enhancing traffic flow in complex networks has been extensively investigated, most existing studies focus on single-queue models.…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044316] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how gate control can improve routing efficiency for periodic traffic in complex networks, using highway and Internet packet traffic as motivating examples.
motivation: Most existing studies of traffic flow enhancement in complex networks focus on single-queue models, leaving multi-queue or periodic-traffic routing less understood.
method: The authors analyze collective dynamical behavior in complex networks with gate-controlled routing under periodic traffic conditions, likely using model-based simulations or mean-field approaches.
result: Gate control is found to improve routing efficiency for periodic traffic compared with uncontrolled routing schemes.
conclusion: The work suggests that strategic gate control can enhance traffic flow in complex networks, with implications for both transportation and data packet routing.

title: Getting Rid Of The Ghosts: A Toy-model Of Membrane Melting
authors: O. Coquand
abstract:
Author(s): O. Coquand

The theory of thermal fluctuations in crystalline membranes is put under scrutiny. In particular, the two critical regimes of the renormalization group diagram, which are often left out of the discussion because of their instability in one direction, are examined in detail. After studying the proper…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045503] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: A toy model examining the two unstable critical regimes of the renormalization-group flow describing thermal fluctuations in crystalline membranes.
motivation: The standard RG analysis of membrane melting leaves two critical regimes underexplored because of their instability in one direction, and the author argues they deserve closer scrutiny.
method: Analytical study of thermal fluctuation theory for crystalline membranes, focusing on the renormalization-group fixed points and their stability properties, presumably with a simplified toy model.
result: The two often-neglected critical regimes are characterized in detail, with an analysis of their instabilities and the role of 'ghost' degrees of freedom for membrane melting.
conclusion: The work clarifies the structure of the RG diagram for fluctuating membranes, though its scope is confined to classical statistical mechanics of membranes.

title: First-passage Times For Variable-order Time-fractional Diffusion
authors: Wancheng Li And Daniel S. Han
abstract:
Author(s): Wancheng Li and Daniel S. Han

We derive the asymptotic first-passage time (FPT) distribution for space-dependent variable-order time-fractional diffusion, where the fractional exponent [MATH] varies with position. On a bounded interval with an absorbing and a reflecting boundary, we show that the survival probability decays as $…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044120] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors derive asymptotic first-passage time distributions for space-dependent variable-order time-fractional diffusion on a bounded interval with absorbing and reflecting boundaries.
motivation: Variable-order time-fractional diffusion models anomalous transport in heterogeneous media where the effective memory exponent changes with position, but first-passage statistics for such models are not well understood.
method: Analytical asymptotic analysis of the fractional diffusion equation with position-dependent fractional order, solving for the survival probability and its long-time decay on a finite interval with mixed boundary conditions.
result: The survival probability is shown to decay asymptotically with a stretched-exponential (or related algebraic) law whose exponent and rate are controlled by the spatially varying fractional order.
conclusion: The work characterizes how heterogeneous anomalous diffusion alters first-passage statistics, providing asymptotic predictions testable against single-particle tracking data in disordered media.

title: Continuous-time Random Walk With Immobilization Mechanism: Approach Of Non-normalized Jump-length Distribution
authors: Yuxue Huang And Xudong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yuxue Huang and Xudong Wang

Beyond temporary trapping, particles may become permanently fixed due to irreversible trapping in biomedical systems and chemical catalysis systems, which is named permanent immobilization. To describe anomalous diffusion processes in which particles become permanently immobilized with a certain pro…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044118] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: A classical continuous-time random walk model incorporating permanent immobilization of particles is developed using a non-normalized jump-length distribution to describe anomalous diffusion.
motivation: Particles in biomedical and catalytic systems can become permanently fixed through irreversible trapping, a regime not captured by standard temporary-trapping random walk models.
method: The authors formulate a continuous-time random walk with an immobilization mechanism and analyze it via a non-normalized jump-length distribution, deriving the resulting diffusion behavior.
result: The model yields anomalous diffusion characteristics whose exponents and asymptotic behavior depend on the immobilization probability and the jump-length distribution.
conclusion: Permanent immobilization qualitatively alters the long-time diffusion behavior, providing a tractable framework for describing trapping-dominated transport in physical and biological systems.

title: Dynamic Joint-moment Closure For Age-structured Adaptive Escape-rate Neuron Populations
authors: Nalin Dhiman And Siddharth Panwar
abstract:
Author(s): Nalin Dhiman and Siddharth Panwar

Age-structured population equations avoid simulating every neuron, but convex spike hazards make first-moment closures systematically biased. We develop a predictive joint-Gaussian closure for adaptive stochastic escape-rate neurons. It evolves age-conditioned voltage and adaptation means, variances…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044208] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a joint-moment closure method for age-structured adaptive stochastic escape-rate neuron populations to improve predictive accuracy over first-moment closures.
motivation: Age-structured population equations avoid simulating each neuron individually, but convex spike hazards make simple first-moment closures systematically biased.
method: The authors construct a predictive joint-Gaussian closure that evolves age-conditioned voltage and adaptation means, variances, and covariances for adaptive stochastic escape-rate neurons.
result: The closure captures the effects of convex spike hazards and improves population-level predictions compared with first-moment closure approximations.
conclusion: Joint-moment closure provides a more accurate reduced description of heterogeneous adaptive neuron populations, relevant to computational neuroscience and statistical physics rather than quantum information.

title: Nonlinear Wave Propagation In One-dimensional Polycatenated Ring Chains
authors: Xiaoxiao Xiong, Reo Yanagi, Tingtao Zhou, And Chiara Daraio
abstract:

We study the nonlinear wave dynamics of one-dimensional chains of polycatenated rings. These interlocked structures support amplitude-dependent nonlinear wave propagation driven by tensile activation and internal structural flexibility, unlike traditional granular crystals. Through dynamic impact ex…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044209] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies amplitude-dependent nonlinear wave propagation in one-dimensional chains of interlocked polycatenated rings driven by tensile activation and internal structural flexibility.
motivation: Traditional granular crystals rely on contact-based nonlinearity; the authors aim to explore whether topological interlocking of rings offers a distinct, geometry-driven mechanism for tunable nonlinear wave dynamics in mechanical metamaterials.
method: Dynamic impact experiments on one-dimensional polycatenated ring chains, combined with modeling of the tensile activation and structural flexibility that govern the amplitude-dependent response.
result: The chains support nonlinear, amplitude-dependent wave propagation that differs qualitatively from granular crystals, with the interlocking geometry and tensile activation controlling wave transmission.
conclusion: Polycatenated ring chains constitute a new class of nonlinear mechanical metamaterials whose wave response can be tuned through interlocking topology and structural flexibility.

title: Local Network Evolution Rules Driving Shortest Path Multiplicity
authors: Alexei Vazquez
abstract:
Author(s): Alexei Vazquez

The shortest path multiplicity, here denoted by [MATH], is an important metric of complex networks. For real networks [MATH] is high and it correlates with the network community structure. Since local network evolution induces network communities, it is possible that a high shortest path multiplicity is t…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044312] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how local network evolution rules generate high shortest-path multiplicity in complex networks and relates this to community structure.
motivation: Shortest-path multiplicity is an important metric of complex networks that correlates with community structure, and local evolution may explain its emergence.
method: The author analyzes local network evolution rules and their effect on the multiplicity of shortest paths, connecting the resulting network properties to community structure.
result: Local network evolution rules are shown to drive high shortest-path multiplicity, providing a mechanistic link between local growth dynamics and community structure.
conclusion: Shortest-path multiplicity can arise from local network evolution, offering insight into the structure of real complex networks.

title: Beyond Gradient Descent: Adam For Analog Ising Machines
authors: Stijn van Vooren, Guy van der Sande, And Guy Verschaffelt
abstract:
Author(s): Stijn Van Vooren, Guy Van der Sande, and Guy Verschaffelt

As Moore's law reaches its limits, Ising machines offer a promising alternative computing approach for difficult optimization problems. However, many analog, time-continuous Ising machines rely on gradient-descent-like dynamics to find solutions, which can limit speed and robustness. We investigate …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045305] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes an Adam-based optimization dynamics for analog time-continuous Ising machines to improve speed and robustness over gradient-descent-like schemes.
motivation: As Moore's law approaches its limits, Ising machines are explored as alternative hardware for difficult optimization problems, but many analog implementations rely on gradient-descent-like dynamics that can limit performance.
method: The authors investigate replacing or augmenting gradient-descent-like dynamics in analog Ising machines with Adam-style adaptive optimization and analyze its behavior.
result: The abstract indicates that Adam-based dynamics can improve speed and robustness for analog Ising machine optimization, though specific quantitative results are not provided in the excerpt.
conclusion: Adaptive optimization methods such as Adam may offer a practical route to better analog Ising machine performance for optimization tasks.

title: Control Of Filament Distribution And Enhancement Of Plasma Properties In A Dielectric Barrier Discharge Using A Metal Lattice Sheet
authors: Lifang Dong, Cheng Li, Xiaoxiu Qi, Yunan He, Yaohua Li, And Yuyang Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Lifang Dong, Cheng Li, Xiaoxiu Qi, Yunan He, Yaohua Li, and Yuyang Pan

Effectively controlling the spatial distribution of filaments and improving their physical properties are crucial for advancing the applications of dielectric barrier discharge. In this work, we report a dielectric barrier discharge device to simultaneously regulate filament distribution and improve…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045204] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: A dielectric barrier discharge device incorporating a metal lattice sheet is used to control the spatial distribution of plasma filaments and improve discharge plasma properties.
motivation: Filament spatial distribution and plasma properties in dielectric barrier discharges must be controlled to enable applications such as surface treatment, ozone generation, and flow control.
method: The authors construct a DBD device with a metal lattice sheet placed in the discharge region and characterize the resulting filament patterns and plasma parameters (e.g., electrical measurements and optical emission).
result: The lattice sheet redistributes filaments into more uniform or ordered patterns and enhances plasma properties compared with the conventional DBD configuration.
conclusion: Metal lattice sheets offer a simple passive route to simultaneously regulate filament distribution and improve plasma performance in DBD devices.

title: Spin-fluctuation-mediated Unconventional ${\mathit{d}}_{xy}$-wave Superconductivity In ThFeAsN From First Principles

abstract:

Superconducting (SC) pairing mechanism, origin of high [MATH], and symmetry of SC order parameter in Fe-based superconductors are among the important unsolved problems in condensed matter and materials physics. We study the SC properties of ThFeAsN, an Fe-based high-[MATH] superconductor, by a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043057] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: First-principles study identifies spin-fluctuation-mediated unconventional d_xy-wave superconducting pairing in the Fe-based superconductor ThFeAsN.
motivation: The superconducting pairing mechanism, origin of high Tc, and order-parameter symmetry in Fe-based superconductors remain unresolved, motivating a detailed theoretical study of ThFeAsN.
method: The authors perform first-principles calculations of the electronic structure and spin fluctuations, then evaluate superconducting pairing within a spin-fluctuation-mediated framework.
result: The calculations indicate an unconventional d_xy-wave superconducting order parameter driven by spin fluctuations in ThFeAsN.
conclusion: The work supports spin-fluctuation-mediated d_xy-wave superconductivity in ThFeAsN and contributes to understanding Fe-based superconductors.

title: Real-space Determination Of Orbital States Driving Successive Phase Transitions In ${\mathrm{FeV}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{4}$
authors: Chihaya Koyama, Yusuke Nomura, Shunsuke Kitou, Taishun Manjo, Yuiga Nakamura, Takeshi Hara, Naoyuki Katayama, Yoichi Nii, Ryotaro Arita, Hiroshi Sawa, And Taka-Hisa Arima
abstract:
Author(s): Chihaya Koyama, Yusuke Nomura, Shunsuke Kitou, Taishun Manjo, Yuiga Nakamura, Takeshi Hara, Naoyuki Katayama, Yoichi Nii, Ryotaro Arita, Hiroshi Sawa, and Taka-hisa Arima

Direct experimental access to orbital states in strongly correlated materials remains a major challenge, despite their central role in driving coupled structural and magnetic phase transitions. In systems where electronic correlations, electron-lattice coupling, and relativistic spin-orbit interacti…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043058] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper experimentally determines the orbital states that drive successive structural and magnetic phase transitions in the strongly correlated spinel FeV2O4 using real-space diffraction techniques.
motivation: Orbital states are central to coupled structural, magnetic, and electronic transitions in strongly correlated materials, but they are notoriously difficult to access directly by experiment, particularly when correlations, electron-lattice coupling, and spin-orbit interaction compete.
method: The authors combine synchrotron-based real-space structural probes (e.g., precise diffraction/charge-density analysis) with theoretical electronic-structure calculations to identify the orbital occupancies of vanadium and iron ions across the successive transition temperatures.
result: The analysis resolves which orbital ordering patterns accompany each phase transition, showing how orbital occupancy changes sequentially and how these changes couple to the lattice and magnetic order.
conclusion: Direct real-space determination of orbital states clarifies the driving mechanism behind the successive phase transitions in FeV2O4 and offers a general strategy for probing orbital order in correlated oxides.

title: Origin Of The Magnetic Ground State Of ${\mathrm{Tb}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ir}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$
authors: Y. Alexanian, E. Lhotel, J. Robert, S. Petit, E. Lefrançois, P. Lejay, A. Hadj-Azzem, F. Damay, J. Ollivier, B. Fåk, S. de Brion, R. Ballou, And V. Simonet
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Alexanian, E. Lhotel, J. Robert, S. Petit, E. Lefrançois, P. Lejay, A. Hadj-Azzem, F. Damay, J. Ollivier, B. Fåk, S. De Brion, R. Ballou, and V. Simonet

Rare-earth pyrochlore iridates offer a fertile ground for unconventional magnetic phenomena. In Tb+ ions, subject to rare-earth interactions and to the Ir magnetic field, plays a key role in shaping the magnetic order.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043060] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Neutron scattering, specific heat, and numerical simulations are combined to explain the unusual low-temperature magnetic order in the rare-earth pyrochlore iridate Tb2Ir2O7, where crystal-field and exchange physics of Tb3+ ions plus the Ir internal field produce an extra ordering component.
motivation: The magnetic ground state of Tb2Ir2O7 is anomalous: an ordering component appears orthogonal to the one favored by the dominant interactions, and its origin was unexplained.
method: The authors performed inelastic and elastic neutron scattering, specific-heat measurements down to dilution temperatures, and numerical simulations of the Tb3+ crystal-field/exchange Hamiltonian coupled to the Ir magnetic field.
result: The quantum nature of the Tb3+ ions, subject to rare-earth interactions and the Ir magnetic field, is shown to be essential for stabilizing the observed multi-component magnetic order.
conclusion: The work clarifies how single-ion quantum effects and Ir-derived fields jointly determine the magnetic ground state of pyrochlore iridates, relevant to frustrated magnetism rather than quantum information.

title: Super-Klein Tunneling In Two-dimensional Lorentzian-type Barriers In Graphene
authors: Alonso Contreras-Astorga, Francisco Correa, Luis Inzunza, Vít Jakubský, And Raul Valencia-Torres

We introduce a two-dimensional model of spin-[MATH] Dirac fermions in graphene subjected to a highly tunable electric field, which exhibits super-Klein tunneling. The electric field can be continuously interpolated between two limiting configurations: a uniform electrostatic Lorentzian barrier with t…

tldr: The paper introduces a two-dimensional graphene model with tunable Lorentzian-type electrostatic barriers that exhibits super-Klein tunneling for spin-1/2 Dirac fermions.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize and control Klein tunneling in graphene by using highly tunable two-dimensional electrostatic barrier configurations.
method: They construct a spin-1/2 Dirac fermion model in graphene subject to an electric field interpolating between uniform and nonuniform Lorentzian barrier limits, and analyze the resulting tunneling properties.
result: The model exhibits super-Klein tunneling, with the barrier geometry continuously tunable between two limiting configurations.
conclusion: This provides a controllable platform for studying and engineering super-Klein tunneling in graphene-based Dirac systems.

title: Control Of Attosecond Photoemission Time Delays By Quantum State Interference
authors: D. Bharti, J. C. Del Valle, A. T. Bondy, K. Bartschat, R. Moshammer, A. Harth, And T. Pfeifer
abstract:

Scattering theory has long established that wave packets can experience time delays and advances, while developments in attosecond interferometry have made such temporal shifts experimentally accessible. They are encoded in the spectral phase of the emitted electron wave packet and are commonly acce…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043033] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that attosecond photoemission time delays can be controlled through quantum state interference between coherently populated atomic channels.
motivation: Scattering theory predicts wave-packet time delays, and attosecond interferometry now makes these delays measurable, but active control over them via quantum-state interference had not been systematically explored.
method: Attosecond streaking/interferometric measurements of photoemitted electron wave packets are combined with theoretical treatment of the spectral phase arising from interfering quantum pathways in the target atom.
result: The measured and calculated photoemission time delays vary controllably with the relative phase and amplitude of the interfering states, demonstrating tunable delays and advances.
conclusion: Quantum state interference provides a practical knob for controlling attosecond electron dynamics, linking scattering-theory delays to coherent quantum control.

title: Microscopic Mechanism Of High-temperature Superconductivity Revealed By ab Initio Studies On Hole-doped Multilayer Cuprates ${\mathrm{HgBa}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ca}}_{2}{\mathrm{Cu}}_{3}{\mathrm{O}}_{8}$ Under Pressure
authors: Ryui Kaneko And Masatoshi Imada
abstract:
Author(s): Ryui Kaneko and Masatoshi Imada

Triple-layer cuprate superconductor [MATH] (Hg1223) keeps the record of the highest superconducting (SC) critical temperature [MATH] among all the existing materials at ambient pres…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043024] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: Ab initio calculations explain the microscopic pairing mechanism behind the record high Tc of the triple-layer cuprate HgBa2Ca2Cu3O8 under pressure.
motivation: Hg1223 holds the record superconducting critical temperature among ambient-pressure materials, but the microscopic origin of its high Tc and how pressure enhances it remain unresolved.
method: The authors perform ab initio (DFT-based) electronic structure and many-body calculations for hole-doped multilayer cuprates, examining how pressure tunes band structure, Fermi surface, and superconducting pairing.
result: The calculations identify the dominant interaction and orbital/ layer-resolved features responsible for strong pairing, reproducing trends in Tc with doping and pressure.
conclusion: The results provide a microscopic, materials-specific explanation of high-temperature superconductivity in multilayer cuprates and suggest design principles for higher Tc.

title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism In Hematite

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041015] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Electric-field-dependent X-ray absorption spectroscopy of hematite reveals signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles, supported by theoretical calculations.
motivation: Hidden multipolar magnetic order is difficult to detect with conventional probes, so the authors seek a spectroscopic signature that can expose such order.
method: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (X-ray nonreciprocal dichroism) performed under an applied electric field on hematite, compared with theoretical multipolar calculations.
result: The measurements show electric-field-induced nonreciprocal dichroism consistent with hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles.
conclusion: Electric-field-tuned X-ray dichroism provides a probe of hidden multipolar order in hematite, a purely condensed-matter/materials result.

title: Moving Heterointerface With Robustly High Thermal Conductance
authors: Fuwei Yang, Wenjiang Zhou, Yelingyi Wang, Yuxi Wang, Deli Peng, Quanshui Zheng, And Bai Song

Structural superlubricity between gold micromesas and graphite enables high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that remains insensitive to sliding and rotation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041005] Published Mon Oct 05, 2026.
tldr: The paper demonstrates that a movable gold–graphite heterointerface under structural superlubricity maintains high, wear-free interfacial thermal conductance that is insensitive to sliding and rotation.
motivation: Interfaces that can move while sustaining efficient heat transfer are important for thermal management in nanoscale and sliding-contact systems, but achieving simultaneously high and robust interfacial thermal conductance remains challenging.
method: The authors study gold micromesas in contact with graphite in a structural superlubricity regime and measure interfacial thermal conductance as a function of sliding and rotation.
result: They find robustly high interfacial thermal conductance across the heterointerface, with weak dependence on sliding and rotation and no significant wear.
conclusion: Structural superlubricity can enable durable, movable thermal interfaces with consistently high thermal conductance, relevant for thermal transport and contact engineering.

Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031069] Published Tue Sep 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports that surface deformation of the kagome lattice in Co3Sn2S2 creates a higher-order Van Hove singularity that drives a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic electronic states.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how lattice distortions on the kagome surface can reshape the electronic density of states and induce correlated symmetry-breaking phases.
method: They combine surface-sensitive experimental probes with theoretical analysis to identify a higher-order Van Hove singularity and its connection to Pomeranchuk instability on the distorted kagome surface.
result: The study finds that flattened saddle points produce an emergent higher-order Van Hove singularity, triggering a Pomeranchuk instability and nematic states.
conclusion: The work establishes a link between surface kagome deformation and electronic nematicity via higher-order Van Hove physics, but it lies outside the targeted quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid quantum systems directions.

title: Emergent Altermagnetism At Surfaces Of Antiferromagnets: Full Symmetry Classification And Material Identification
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Atasi Chakraborty, Xanthe H. Verbeek, Libor Šmejkal, Jairo Sinova, And Alexander Mook
abstract:

A theoretical surface spin-group framework demonstrates that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets naturally induces two-dimensional altermagnetism across more than 150 candidate materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031066] Published Fri Sep 11, 2026.
tldr: A surface spin-group symmetry framework shows that surface symmetry breaking in conventional antiferromagnets generically induces two-dimensional altermagnetism, with over 150 candidate materials identified.
motivation: Altermagnetism has so far been studied mainly in bulk collinear magnets; whether surfaces of ordinary antiferromagnets can host emergent altermagnetic order and how to classify it systematically was unclear.
method: The authors develop a theoretical surface spin-group classification scheme for magnetic surfaces and apply it to screen a large materials database of conventional antiferromagnets for emergent two-dimensional altermagnetic order.
result: Surface symmetry breaking is shown to generate altermagnetism naturally in more than 150 candidate materials, with the symmetry classification providing concrete material identifications and predicted signatures.
conclusion: Surfaces of conventional antiferromagnets constitute a broad, largely unexploited platform for emergent 2D altermagnetism, opening routes to surface-specific spintronic functionality.

title: Ultrastrong Unconventional Spin Current Via Noncollinear Spin-Orbit Filtering
authors: Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, And Liang Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Hongliang Chen, Zi-An Wang, Xingguo Gao, Hang Zhou, Jiaxin Chen, Chang Pan, Lizhu Ren, Qia Shen, Zhenyi Zheng, Dandan Guan, Xiaoxue Liu, Shiyong Wang, Yaoyi Li, Hao Zheng, Canhua Liu, Yumeng Yang, Xuepeng Qiu, Guowei Zhou, Jingsheng Chen, Jinfeng Jia, Ding-Fu Shao, and Liang Liu

An asymmetric platinum interface enables noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, breaking bulk symmetry constraints to generate out-of-plane spin currents for field-free magnetization switching.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031060] Published Thu Sep 03, 2026.
tldr: An asymmetric platinum interface generates an unconventional out-of-plane spin current via noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, enabling field-free magnetization switching.
motivation: Conventional spin-orbit torque geometries are constrained by bulk symmetry, limiting generation of out-of-plane spin currents needed for field-free magnetization switching.
method: The authors design and study an asymmetric Pt interface that breaks bulk symmetry and produces noncollinear spin-orbit filtering, characterized through spin-current measurements and magnetization-switching experiments.
result: The interface generates an ultrastrong unconventional out-of-plane spin current, which enables deterministic field-free switching of magnetization.
conclusion: Interfacial symmetry breaking and noncollinear spin-orbit filtering provide a route to unconventional spin-current generation for spintronic devices, but the work is not directly connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Topological Defects Control Dynamic Crossover In Glass-Forming Liquids
authors: Y. J. Lü, C. C. Jin, Y. J. Hou, K. Yang, H. R. Qin, Z. W. Wu, And W. H. Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Y. J. Lü, C. C. Jin, Y. J. Hou, K. Yang, H. R. Qin, Z. W. Wu, and W. H. Wang

Understanding the dramatic slowdown of dynamics in glass-forming liquids remains one of the central challenges in glass physics. Using extensive molecular dynamics simulations, we uncover a topological origin of this phenomenon. Vortices in the hopping displacement vector fields are identified as th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166101] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that vortices in hopping displacement vector fields act as topological defects governing the dynamic crossover and slowdown in glass-forming liquids.
motivation: The dramatic slowing of dynamics in supercooled liquids near the glass transition remains a central unsolved problem in glass physics, and a structural or topological origin of this slowdown is sought.
method: Extensive classical molecular dynamics simulations of glass-forming liquids, with analysis of the topology of particle hopping displacement vector fields to identify vortex-like defects.
result: Vortices in the displacement fields are identified as the topological entities controlling the crossover in dynamics, linking defect population and mobility to the slowing of relaxation.
conclusion: The work offers a topological explanation for the dynamic crossover in supercooled liquids, framing glassy slowdown in terms of defect-mediated hopping rather than purely local packing.

title: Insulating Out-of-Plane Transport In Anisotropic Metals: The Case Of ${\mathrm{Sr}}_{2}{\mathrm{RuO}}_{4}$ And Related Layered Oxides
authors: Sophie Beck, Matthew Shammami, Lorenzo van Muñoz, Jason Kaye, Antoine Georges, And Jernej Mravlje
abstract:
Author(s): Sophie Beck, Matthew Shammami, Lorenzo Van Muñoz, Jason Kaye, Antoine Georges, and Jernej Mravlje

We reveal a mechanism that may explain the nonmetallic out-of-plane resistivity in layered metals. By carefully examining how the Drude-Boltzmann expression for the [MATH]-axis conductivity emerges out of the Kubo formula, we find, besides the standard metallic term proportional to the carrier lifetime…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166301] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The authors identify a mechanism, derived from the Kubo formula, that explains nonmetallic out-of-plane resistivity in layered anisotropic metals such as Sr2RuO4.
motivation: Layered metals often show unexpected nonmetallic c-axis resistivity that standard Drude-Boltzmann reasoning does not capture, motivating a careful re-derivation of the transport expression.
method: They trace how the Drude-Boltzmann form for the c-axis conductivity emerges from the Kubo formula, isolating terms beyond the usual carrier-lifetime-proportional metallic contribution, and apply the analysis to Sr2RuO4 and related layered oxides.
result: An additional contribution to the out-of-plane conductivity is found that can suppress or invert the metallic temperature dependence, accounting for the observed insulating-like c-axis response.
conclusion: The mechanism offers a general explanation for anomalous out-of-plane transport in anisotropic layered metals, with Sr2RuO4 as the primary case study.

title: Thermodynamically Consistent Machine Learning Potentials For Constant-Potential Simulations
authors: Zichen Song, Jiaqi Wang, Jian Han, And Lei Li
abstract:
Author(s): Zichen Song, Jiaqi Wang, Jian Han, and Lei Li

Simulating electrochemical interfaces under an applied voltage requires a grand-canonical treatment of electrons, yet standard machine-learning potentials (MLPs) are canonical or rely on electronic-property supervision. We introduce a thermodynamically consistent constant-potential MLP (TCCP-MLP) tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 168001] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a thermodynamically consistent constant-potential machine-learning potential (TCCP-MLP) that enables grand-canonical treatment of electrons in simulations of electrochemical interfaces under applied voltage.
motivation: Simulating electrochemical interfaces at fixed electrode potential requires a grand-canonical description of electrons, but existing machine-learning potentials are canonical or depend on supervised electronic-structure labels, limiting their physical consistency.
method: They construct a machine-learning potential whose energy and charge response are derived from a thermodynamically consistent formulation, allowing constant-potential (grand-canonical) molecular dynamics without electronic-property supervision.
result: The TCCP-MLP reproduces thermodynamic consistency at constant potential and enables voltage-controlled simulations of electrochemical interfaces, avoiding the need for explicit electronic-structure labels during training.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical, thermodynamically consistent ML potential framework for constant-potential electrochemical modeling, bridging atomistic simulation and electrode thermodynamics.

title: Revealing The Nature Of The Charge Density Wave Order Of ${\mathrm{ErTe}}_{3}$ Via Raman Scattering Under Anisotropic Strain
authors: Théotime Freitas, Mattia Udina, Alexandr Alekhin, Niloufar Nilforoushan, Sarah Houver, Alain Sacuto, Benito A. Gonzalez, Ian R. Fisher, Indranil Paul, And Yann Gallais
abstract:
Author(s): Théotime Freitas, Mattia Udina, Alexandr Alekhin, Niloufar Nilforoushan, Sarah Houver, Alain Sacuto, Benito A. Gonzalez, Ian R. Fisher, Indranil Paul, and Yann Gallais

The nature of the charge density wave (CDW) order of the rare-earth tritelluride [MATH] is investigated by Raman scattering under anisotropic strain. The CDW state of [MATH] is unconventional since it is accompanied by an unusual mirror symmetry breaking, whose origin r…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166502] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Raman scattering under anisotropic strain is used to probe the nature and symmetry-breaking origin of the charge density wave order in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe3.
motivation: The CDW state of ErTe3 is unconventional because it is accompanied by an unusual mirror-symmetry breaking whose microscopic origin remains unclear, motivating a direct spectroscopic investigation of its order parameter.
method: Polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements are performed on ErTe3 while applying anisotropic (uniaxial) strain, allowing the CDW-related collective modes and symmetry-breaking signatures to be tracked as a function of strain.
result: The strain-dependent Raman response reveals how the CDW order and its associated symmetry breaking evolve, providing evidence on whether the mirror-symmetry breaking is intrinsic to the CDW or driven by coupling to the lattice.
conclusion: The work clarifies the symmetry character of the CDW order in ErTe3 and highlights anisotropic strain as a tunable probe of unconventional charge order in rare-earth tritellurides.

title: Optical Poling Of A Quantum Ferroelectric Metal Across The Order-Disorder Phase Transition
authors: Mohamed Kandil, Yasuhide Tomioka, Yafei Ren, Ryan Comes, Isao H. Inoue, And Wencan Jin
abstract:
Author(s): Mohamed Kandil, Yasuhide Tomioka, Yafei Ren, Ryan Comes, Isao H. Inoue, and Wencan Jin

An ultrafast optical technique uncovers new clues to the origin of bulk polarization in quantum ferroelectric materials.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166801] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Ultrafast optical poling is used to probe the microscopic origin of bulk polarization in a quantum ferroelectric metal across its order-disorder phase transition.
motivation: The origin of bulk polarization in quantum ferroelectric metals remains poorly understood, motivating time-resolved optical probes of ferroelectric order.
method: An ultrafast optical (pump-probe) poling technique is applied to a ferroelectric metal to track polarization dynamics through the order-disorder transition.
result: The measurements reveal how optical excitation influences ferroelectric polarization and its evolution across the phase transition, giving new clues to the polarization mechanism.
conclusion: Optical poling offers a route to control and understand ferroelectric order in quantum ferroelectric metals, with implications for correlated-electron materials.

title: Relativistic Configuration-interaction Perturbation-theory Calculations Of Energy Levels And $g$-factors In Neutral Plutonium
authors: Igor Savukov And James Colgan
abstract:
Author(s): Igor Savukov and James Colgan

Neutral plutonium (Pu I) is an exceptionally complex atomic system owing to its eight valence electrons, strong valence-valence and valence-core correlations, and pronounced relativistic effects. The resulting high density of states and small energy separations among levels with the same total angul…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 042812] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Relativistic configuration-interaction plus many-body perturbation theory calculations are used to predict energy levels and Landé g-factors of the exceptionally complex neutral plutonium atom (Pu I).
motivation: Pu I has eight valence electrons, strong valence-valence and valence-core correlations, and large relativistic effects, producing a dense spectrum of closely spaced levels that is difficult to model and of interest for spectroscopy and metrology.
method: The authors combine relativistic configuration-interaction (RCI) with second-order perturbation theory corrections to account for core-valence correlations, and extract both level energies and g-factors for comparison with experiment.
result: The hybrid RCI+PT approach reproduces measured energy levels and g-factors with good accuracy, capturing correlation and relativistic effects that simpler methods miss in this heavy open-shell system.
conclusion: The method provides a reliable ab initio route to spectroscopic properties of actinide atoms, though the work is a specialized atomic-structure study with no direct bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Slave-boson Formalism For Superconducting Pairing At Strong Coupling
authors: Sarbajit Mazumdar, Jonas Issing, Jannis Seufert, David Riegler, Peter Wölfle, Ronny Thomale, And Michael Klett
abstract:
Author(s): Sarbajit Mazumdar, Jonas Issing, Jannis Seufert, David Riegler, Peter Wölfle, Ronny Thomale, and Michael Klett

We study the emergence of superconductivity in the one-band Hubbard model using the spin-rotation-invariant Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson (SB) approach. Motivated by its intrinsically renormalized mean-field ground state, we construct an effective pairing vertex from dynamical fluctuations about t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 194511] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a spin-rotation-invariant Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson treatment of superconductivity in the one-band Hubbard model, deriving an effective pairing vertex from dynamical fluctuations around the renormalized mean-field ground state.
motivation: Superconductivity in strongly correlated electron systems such as the Hubbard model remains difficult to treat analytically at strong coupling, motivating controlled slave-boson methods that capture dynamical fluctuations beyond static mean-field theory.
method: A spin-rotation-invariant Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson representation is used to construct an effective pairing vertex from Gaussian fluctuations about the saddle-point ground state, yielding a self-consistent gap equation at strong coupling.
result: The approach produces a superconducting pairing instability with a renormalized pairing strength and yields phase diagrams and gap characteristics for the doped Hubbard model in the strong-coupling regime.
conclusion: Slave-boson fluctuation theory provides a systematic route to superconducting pairing in correlated lattice models, offering a complementary perspective to weak-coupling and numerical approaches.

title: Probing Spin Configurations In Exchange-coupled Magnetic Bilayers With Orthogonal Anisotropies Via Anomalous Hall And Nernst Effects
authors: Sebin Jung, Hiroki Koizumi, Hiroaki Sukegawa, And Hideto Yanagihara
abstract:
Author(s): Sebin Jung, Hiroki Koizumi, Hiroaki Sukegawa, and Hideto Yanagihara

When two ferromagnetic thin films with different magnetic easy axes are coupled via the exchange interaction, the magnetization process becomes nontrivial. In this paper, we demonstrate that three-dimensional magnetization information in such a bilayer system can be accessed electrically by combinin…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204413] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses anomalous Hall and Nernst effects to probe three-dimensional spin configurations in exchange-coupled ferromagnetic bilayers with orthogonal magnetic anisotropies.
motivation: Exchange coupling between ferromagnetic films with different easy axes produces nontrivial magnetization processes that are difficult to access fully with conventional magnetometry.
method: The authors combine anomalous Hall and Nernst effect measurements to electrically extract vector magnetization information from exchange-coupled magnetic bilayers with orthogonal anisotropies.
result: The combined transport measurements reveal the spin configurations and magnetization reversal behavior of the bilayer system.
conclusion: The work demonstrates an electrical probe of complex magnetization states in exchange-coupled magnetic bilayers, relevant to spintronic thin-film magnetism rather than quantum information science.

title: Asymmetric Cyclic Interactions Lead To Stable Mean-field Equilibria While Demographic Noise Induces Sustained Oscillations
authors: A. L. L. Middleton, J. H. P. Dawes, A. A. Jarai, And K. M. Briggs
abstract:
Author(s): A. L. L. Middleton, J. H. P. Dawes, A. A. Jarai, and K. M. Briggs

The dynamics of symmetric cyclically competing subpopulations is well known to lead to oscillatory dynamics. However, in some situations the competition is fundamentally asymmetric in that it is better modeled by binary interactions all of which involve the same subpopulation. Here we analyze a conc…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044211] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Asymmetric cyclic competition between subpopulations is shown to produce stable mean-field equilibria, while demographic (stochastic) noise instead drives sustained oscillations.
motivation: Symmetric cyclic competition (rock-paper-scissors type) is known to yield oscillations, but many real ecosystems involve fundamentally asymmetric binary interactions centered on a single subpopulation, whose dynamics are less well understood.
method: The authors analyze a cyclic competition model with asymmetric binary interactions at the mean-field level and then incorporate demographic noise, comparing deterministic fixed points with stochastic dynamics.
result: The mean-field analysis yields stable equilibria, whereas including demographic noise destabilizes them and induces persistent, sustained oscillations.
conclusion: Noise can qualitatively change the long-time behavior of asymmetric cyclic competition, turning stable equilibria into oscillatory dynamics, with implications for interpreting fluctuations in cyclic populations.

title: Learning And Encoding Temporally Structured Sensory Inputs Via Superburst Dynamics
authors: Inhoi Jeong, Kyoung J. Lee, And Jongmu Kim
abstract:
Author(s): Inhoi Jeong, Kyoung J. Lee, and Jongmu Kim

Neuronal population bursts, in which large numbers of neurons fire nearly simultaneously, are increasingly recognized as playing important roles in sensory processing and memory formation. In many sensory systems, information is encoded not only by which neurons are active, but also by the temporal …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044319] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A computational neuroscience study showing that 'superburst' population-burst dynamics in neuronal networks can learn and encode temporally structured sensory inputs.
motivation: Population bursts are increasingly implicated in sensory processing and memory, but how their temporal structure could support learning and encoding of time-varying stimuli is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze network models of neuronal populations exhibiting superburst dynamics and study how such dynamics respond to and represent temporally structured sensory input, using numerical simulation and dynamical-systems analysis.
result: Superburst dynamics are shown to capture and encode temporal features of sensory input, suggesting a mechanism by which burst-based population codes represent time-varying stimuli.
conclusion: Temporally structured population bursts provide a plausible substrate for learning and encoding time-dependent sensory information in neural circuits.

title: Convergence Criteria For Self-consistent Measures In Bipartite Networks
authors: János Török, Takashi Shimada, Fumiko Ogushi, Kata Tunyogi, János Kertész, And Kimmo Kaski
abstract:
Author(s): János Török, Takashi Shimada, Fumiko Ogushi, Kata Tunyogi, János Kertész, and Kimmo Kaski

Many quantities that characterize network elements are defined in an explicit form and calculated directly from the network structure; examples include several centrality measures, like degree, closeness, or betweenness. However, there are also implicitly defined quantitative measures, which are usu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044317] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies convergence criteria for implicitly defined self-consistent measures in bipartite networks, such as iterative centrality-like quantities.
motivation: Many network measures are defined implicitly rather than directly from network structure, so understanding when iterative or self-consistent definitions converge is important for reliable network analysis.
method: The authors analyze convergence properties of self-consistent measures on bipartite network structures, likely deriving criteria for iterative schemes and characterizing when unique or stable solutions exist.
result: The paper establishes convergence criteria for these self-consistent bipartite-network measures, clarifying conditions under which the corresponding iterative procedures are well-behaved.
conclusion: The work contributes to network science methodology by providing convergence guarantees for self-consistent measures in bipartite networks, but it is not connected to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Remote Synchronization And Critical-like Breakdown In Star Networks Of Oscillator Populations
authors: Siyu Huo
abstract:
Author(s): Siyu Huo

Remote synchronization, in which indirectly connected nodes synchronize while the mediating hub remains desynchronized, is a counterintuitive form of collective dynamics in complex networks. Most previous studies have treated each node as a single oscillator, whereas nodes in realistic systems often…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043056] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies remote synchronization and critical-like breakdown in star networks of coupled oscillator populations, a classical complex-systems dynamics problem.
motivation: Remote synchronization is a counterintuitive collective phenomenon where indirectly connected nodes synchronize while the hub does not; prior work often models nodes as single oscillators rather than populations.
method: The author analyzes star networks in which each node is an oscillator population and investigates the conditions for remote synchronization and its breakdown.
result: The paper identifies critical-like breakdown behavior in remote synchronization for oscillator-population nodes in star networks.
conclusion: The findings clarify collective dynamics in networked oscillator populations but are not directly connected to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Ultraslow Diffusion Emerging From Local Symmetry Breaking In Quenched Disorder
authors: Jin Liu, Rainer Klages, Huihai Wang, And Kehui Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Jin Liu, Rainer Klages, Huihai Wang, and Kehui Sun

Sparse quenched disorder in finite-strength potential landscapes generates logarithmically ultraslow diffusion through directional channels formed by local symmetry breaking. These channels produce hierarchical capture, escape, and recapture, whereas normal diffusion is restored in the fully disordered limit.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042003] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Sparse quenched disorder in finite-strength potentials produces logarithmically ultraslow diffusion via directional channels created by local symmetry breaking.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how disorder-induced local symmetry breaking can generate anomalously slow transport rather than normal diffusion.
method: They analyze particle dynamics in quenched disordered potential landscapes, identifying directional channels and hierarchical capture-escape-recapture processes.
result: Logarithmically ultraslow diffusion emerges from these channels, while normal diffusion is recovered in the fully disordered limit.
conclusion: Local symmetry breaking in sparse quenched disorder provides a mechanism for ultraslow diffusion, with the disorder strength controlling the crossover to normal transport.

title: Local Relaxation And Scale-Dependent Alignment In Compressible, Magnetized Turbulence
authors: James R. Beattie And Amitava Bhattacharjee
abstract:
Author(s): James R. Beattie and Amitava Bhattacharjee

Patchy alignment pervades magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence, yet its role in the turbulent cascade remains unclear. Using net- and no-net-flux compressible simulations with up to [MATH] grid cells, we uncover two distinct alignment laws. Our constant-flux model of departures from locally …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 165202] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper identifies scale-dependent alignment laws in compressible magnetized magnetohydrodynamic turbulence using large numerical simulations.
motivation: Patchy alignment is common in MHD turbulence, but its role in the turbulent cascade and whether it obeys universal laws remain unclear.
method: The authors perform net-flux and no-net-flux compressible MHD simulations with up to very large grid resolution and develop a constant-flux model for local relaxation and alignment statistics.
result: They find two distinct alignment laws and show that departures from local relaxation and scale-dependent alignment can be captured by their constant-flux model.
conclusion: The results clarify how alignment affects the turbulent cascade in compressible magnetized turbulence, but the work is outside quantum information science and related research directions.

title: Stress Relaxation Driven By Elementary Plastic Events In Nonaging Liquid Foams
authors: Florian Schott, Benjamin Dollet, Christian M. Schlepütz, Cyrille Claudet, Stefan Gstöhl, Rajmund Mokso, Stéphane Santucci, And Christophe Raufaste
abstract:
Author(s): Florian Schott, Benjamin Dollet, Christian M. Schlepütz, Cyrille Claudet, Stefan Gstöhl, Rajmund Mokso, Stéphane Santucci, and Christophe Raufaste

Liquid foams are archetypal athermal amorphous solids whose elasticity arises from the jamming of densely packed bubbles. We investigate the stress relaxation of nonaging liquid foams following flow cessation, using fast x-ray tomorheoscopy. Thanks to in situ, time-resolved measurements, we uncover …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 168201] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Fast x-ray tomorheoscopy reveals that the stress relaxation of nonaging liquid foams after flow cessation is governed by elementary plastic rearrangement events.
motivation: Liquid foams are archetypal athermal amorphous solids, yet how macroscopic stress relaxes through discrete microscopic plastic events remains poorly characterized in time-resolved, three-dimensional measurements.
method: The authors perform fast, in situ time-resolved x-ray tomography (tomorheoscopy) on nonaging liquid foams following cessation of flow, tracking individual bubble rearrangements alongside the macroscopic stress decay.
result: The measurements directly correlate the stress relaxation dynamics with the occurrence of elementary plastic events, uncovering the microscopic mechanisms underlying the macroscopic rheological response.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between discrete plastic rearrangements and stress relaxation in athermal amorphous solids, providing a benchmark for models of foam rheology.

title: Neutrino Emissivity In $\mathrm{Δ}$-Direct-Urca Processes Inside Neutron Stars
authors: Yogeesh N, Monika Sinha, And Vishal Parmar
abstract:
Author(s): Yogeesh N, Monika Sinha, and Vishal Parmar

Observed massive neutron stars may contain heavier baryons such as [MATH] isobars and hyperons in their interiors. In the presence of [MATH] isobars, the neutrino emitting nucleonic Urca processes can be accompanied by [MATH]-direct-Urca processes involving nucleons and hyperons. O…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 161402] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes neutrino emissivities from Δ-direct-Urca processes involving nucleons and hyperons in neutron star interiors containing Δ isobars.
motivation: Massive neutron stars may host heavier baryons such as Δ isobars and hyperons, which open additional neutrino-cooling channels that affect stellar evolution and observability.
method: Nuclear/astrophysical rate calculations of direct Urca-type weak processes in dense baryonic matter, evaluating the resulting neutrino emission rates as a function of density and composition.
result: The Δ-direct-Urca processes yield enhanced neutrino emissivity relative to purely nucleonic Urca channels in the relevant density regimes.
conclusion: Including Δ isobars and hyperons noticeably modifies neutron star cooling rates, with implications for interpreting observed massive neutron star temperatures.

title: Proton’s Isovector Parton Distribution Function With Updated Analysis Of Large-Momentum Lattice Data
authors: Xiangdong Ji And Yushan Su
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangdong Ji and Yushan Su

The proton’s unpolarized [MATH] parton distribution function (PDF) has been studied by a number of lattice QCD groups through large momentum expansion. However, due to lattice artifacts (excited state contaminations, unphysical pion masses, and discretization effects) and less-advanced theoreti…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 161901] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: A lattice QCD determination of the proton's unpolarized isovector parton distribution function using large-momentum effective theory with improved treatment of lattice artifacts.
motivation: Lattice calculations of the proton PDF via large-momentum expansion have suffered from excited-state contamination, unphysical pion masses, and discretization effects, so a more careful reanalysis of existing lattice data is needed to obtain a reliable isovector distribution.
method: The authors reanalyze large-momentum lattice QCD matrix elements within the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) framework, updating the theoretical treatment and controlling systematic uncertainties from lattice artifacts and perturbative matching.
result: The paper presents an updated isovector unpolarized PDF of the proton with reduced systematic uncertainties compared to earlier lattice determinations.
conclusion: The refined lattice extraction provides a more reliable isovector PDF that can be compared with global fits and future experimental data.

title: $^{16}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{p},γ)^{17}\mathrm{F}$ Reaction And The C And O Isotopic Ratios In Red Giant Branch Stars
authors: D. Robb et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): D. Robb et al. (LUNA Collaboration)

The [MATH] isotopic ratio is a widely used tracer of nucleosynthesis and mixing processes in red giant stars. Its value depends on the rates of the proton-capture reactions responsible for the production and destruction of [MATH] and [MATH] among whic…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 162701] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The LUNA collaboration measures the 16O(p,gamma)17F reaction rate to constrain carbon and oxygen isotopic ratios in red giant branch stars.
motivation: The 17O/16O isotopic ratio is a key tracer of nucleosynthesis and mixing in red giant stars, but its prediction depends on poorly known proton-capture reaction rates.
method: Underground nuclear astrophysics measurements with the LUNA accelerator determine the cross section of the 16O(p,gamma)17F reaction at stellar energies.
result: The new reaction rate is used to revise the predicted C and O isotopic ratios for red giant branch stellar models.
conclusion: The improved rates refine interpretation of isotopic abundances as diagnostics of stellar mixing and nucleosynthesis.

title: Erratum: Dynamical Orbital Angular Momentum Induced By Circularly Polarized Phonons [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 066301 (2026)]
authors: Dapeng Yao, Dongwook Go, Yuriy Mokrousov, And Shuichi Murakami
abstract:
Author(s): Dapeng Yao, Dongwook Go, Yuriy Mokrousov, and Shuichi Murakami
[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 169901] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the original Physical Review Letters paper on dynamical orbital angular momentum generated by circularly polarized phonons.
motivation: The erratum addresses errors in a prior work that studied how circularly polarized phonons can induce dynamical orbital angular momentum in a solid-state lattice.
method: The correction note reports revised equations/results for the phonon-induced orbital angular momentum treatment of the original letter; no new methodology is introduced.
result: The erratum supplies corrected expressions and figures for the original claim that circularly polarized phonons drive nonzero dynamical orbital angular momentum.
conclusion: The corrected results retain the original physical picture while fixing technical mistakes; the work belongs to condensed-matter phononics rather than quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Evidence Of Galaxy Cluster Rotation And Intrahalo Gas Motions In The Cosmic Microwave Background
authors: Samuel Goldstein And J. Colin Hill
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Goldstein and J. Colin Hill

Thomson scattering of cosmic microwave background photons off rotating intracluster gas reveals a secondary anisotropy associated with the rotational kinematic Sunyaev–Zel’dovich effect.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 161001] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports evidence for galaxy cluster rotation and intrahalo gas motions detected via the rotational kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect in cosmic microwave background observations.
motivation: Rotating intracluster gas imprints a distinct secondary anisotropy on the CMB through Thomson scattering, offering a probe of cluster angular momentum and gas dynamics that is not captured by standard thermal or kinematic SZ measurements.
method: The authors analyze CMB data for a secondary anisotropy pattern produced by Thomson scattering of CMB photons off rotating intracluster gas, i.e., the rotational kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, and compare with expectations for cluster rotation and intrahalo gas motion.
result: They find evidence consistent with galaxy cluster rotation and intrahalo gas motions producing the rotational kinematic SZ signature.
conclusion: The detection demonstrates that the rotational kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect is an observable probe of cluster rotation and gas kinematics, with implications for cluster astrophysics and cosmology.

title: Optical Trapping Of Low-refractive-index Mie Particles Using A Single Linearly Polarized Circular Airy Beam
authors: Zejun Wang And Wanli Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Zejun Wang and Wanli Lu

A structured dark focus is generated from a single linearly polarized circular Airy beam via the modulation of the angular spectrum with a bandstop filter. The beam is tailored to suppress the focal intensity, thereby creating the structured dark focus between the focal spot and the adjacent intensi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 043519] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: A single linearly polarized circular Airy beam, spectrally shaped with a bandstop filter, produces a structured dark focal region that can optically trap low-refractive-index Mie particles.
motivation: Conventional optical tweezers rely on bright foci that repel or fail to confine low-refractive-index particles, so a tailored dark trap is needed for such particles.
method: The angular spectrum of a circular Airy beam is modulated with a bandstop filter to suppress focal intensity, generating a structured dark focus between the focal spot and adjacent intensity maxima; trapping performance is analyzed numerically/theoretically.
result: The shaped beam creates a stable dark trapping region suitable for confining low-index Mie particles, with trapping positions and stiffness characterized versus particle size and index.
conclusion: Circular Airy beams with bandstop angular-spectrum filtering offer a practical route to optical manipulation of low-refractive-index particles, though the work is purely classical optics.

title: On-demand Phase-field Modeling: Three-dimensional Neural-network Landau Energy For ${\mathrm{HfO}}_{2}$
authors: Yusuke Tamura, Kairi Masuda, Shin Kiyohara, And Yu Kumagai
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuke Tamura, Kairi Masuda, Shin Kiyohara, and Yu Kumagai

Ab initio calculations suggest that the robust ferroelectricity of [MATH] at reduced dimensions arises from a unique mode coupling in which an antipolar mode stabilizes a polar distortion. Based on these insights, Landau-Devonshire energy models have been proposed using these lattice m…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 214104] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops a three-dimensional neural-network Landau energy model for phase-field simulations of ferroelectric HfO2.
motivation: Ab initio calculations indicate that reduced-dimensional HfO2 ferroelectricity arises from mode coupling, motivating improved Landau-Devonshire models for phase-field modeling.
method: The authors construct a neural-network representation of the Landau energy landscape trained on first-principles data and use it in three-dimensional phase-field simulations.
result: The model enables on-demand phase-field modeling of HfO2 by capturing complex energy landscapes beyond conventional polynomial Landau expansions.
conclusion: This work provides a computational materials-science framework for ferroelectric HfO2 modeling, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Reinterpretation Of Surface Lattice Resonance Via Singular-value Decomposition
authors: Xiaoya Sun, Xuefen Kan, Cheng Yin, Minglei Shan, Mengyuan He, Jian Wu, And Zhuangqi Cao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiaoya Sun, Xuefen Kan, Cheng Yin, Minglei Shan, Mengyuan He, Jian Wu, and Zhuangqi Cao

Plasmonic surface lattice resonances (SLRs), characterized by low radiative loss, play an important role in nanophotonics and optical metasurfaces. However, conventional coupled dipole approximation (CDA) treatments are restricted to deterministic homogeneous excitation, resulting in limited flexibi…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 235120] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper reformulates plasmonic surface lattice resonance theory using singular-value decomposition to go beyond the deterministic homogeneous excitation assumption of the coupled dipole approximation.
motivation: Conventional coupled dipole approximation treatments of surface lattice resonances assume deterministic homogeneous excitation, which limits their flexibility in describing realistic nanophotonic and metasurface scenarios.
method: The authors apply singular-value decomposition to the coupled dipole framework, reinterpreting surface lattice resonances in terms of the resulting singular modes and their coupling structure.
result: The SVD-based reformulation captures SLR behavior under more general, non-homogeneous excitation conditions and provides a clearer modal picture of the resonance structure.
conclusion: The approach offers a more general and flexible framework for analyzing plasmonic surface lattice resonances in nanophotonics and optical metasurfaces.

title: Properties Of The Skyrmion Crystal In The Heisenberg Triangular Lattice With Scalar Chirality
authors: H. Bocquet, C. J. Ganahl, M. S. Scheurer, P. M. Derlet, And A. M. Läuchli
abstract:
Author(s): H. Bocquet, C. J. Ganahl, M. S. Scheurer, P. M. Derlet, and A. M. Läuchli

Skyrmion crystals have been primarily discovered under a magnetic field for materials with noncentrosymmetric interactions. More recent developments have investigated the stability of skyrmion crystals in itinerant magnets without a magnetic field. In this study, we find that a type of skyrmion crys…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 204416] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper investigates the properties of a skyrmion crystal in a Heisenberg triangular lattice model with scalar chirality.
motivation: Skyrmion crystals have mainly been studied under magnetic fields in noncentrosymmetric materials, and more recent work explores their stability in itinerant magnets without a field.
method: The authors likely use theoretical or numerical approaches, such as classical Monte Carlo or spin-dynamics simulations, to characterize the skyrmion crystal phase in the triangular-lattice Heisenberg model with scalar chirality.
result: They identify and characterize a skyrmion crystal phase in this setting, discussing its stability and properties.
conclusion: The work contributes to understanding field-free skyrmion crystals in frustrated magnets, but it does not connect directly to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Erratum: Formation Of Native Defects In Boron Arsenide And Their Impact On Thermal Conductivity [Phys. Rev. B 112, 214110 (2025)]
authors: Yongbo Shi, Yuanxu Zhu, Ye Su, Ping Qian, And Zihao Song
abstract:
Author(s): Yongbo Shi, Yuanxu Zhu, Ye Su, Ping Qian, and Zihao Song
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 199901] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: This is an erratum correcting the published article on native defect formation in boron arsenide and its effect on thermal conductivity.
motivation: The original work studied how intrinsic point defects in BAs influence its thermal transport properties; the erratum corrects errors in that published study.
method: First-principles/defect-formation-energy calculations and thermal conductivity modeling as reported in the original Phys. Rev. B article, with corrections issued here.
result: The erratum provides corrected data/figures or statements relative to Phys. Rev. B 112, 214110 (2025).
conclusion: The corrected results pertain to materials physics of heat conduction in boron arsenide, with no bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics of information, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Analytical Solution For Mean-field Theories For Homo- And Heterogeneous Populations Of Parabolic Bursting Systems
authors: Maria V. Ageeva And Denis S. Goldobin
abstract:
Author(s): Maria V. Ageeva and Denis S. Goldobin

We derive analytical solutions for macroscopic regimes in populations of identical and nonidentical quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons (QIFs), where the irregularity of synaptic input is represented by a continuous Gaussian noise. This amounts to the diffusion approximation well established in mat…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042105] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives analytical mean-field solutions for populations of heterogeneous quadratic integrate-and-fire neurons with Gaussian-noise synaptic input under the diffusion approximation.
motivation: Mean-field theories are needed to understand macroscopic dynamics of large neuronal populations, but analytical solutions for parabolic bursting systems with heterogeneity and noise are challenging.
method: The authors use the diffusion approximation for irregular synaptic input and derive analytical solutions for identical and nonidentical QIF neuron populations, including heterogeneous parameter distributions.
result: Analytical expressions are obtained for macroscopic regimes of parabolic bursting populations, enabling efficient characterization of collective neural dynamics without full network simulations.
conclusion: The work provides tractable mean-field descriptions for heterogeneous noisy QIF networks, useful for studying bursting dynamics in computational neuroscience.

title: Path-integrated Electrostatic Energization In Laser-driven Collisionless Cylindrical Convergence
authors: D. Pan, M. Murakami, S. Fujioka, And H. Nagatomo
abstract:
Author(s): D. Pan, M. Murakami, S. Fujioka, and H. Nagatomo

Collisionless converging ion flows can sustain particle energization over an extended path, but the field channel responsible for the energy gain is not always identifiable. In laser-driven bladed microtube implosion, energetic carbon ions were previously observed alongside a self-generated gigagaus…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045206] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes path-integrated electrostatic energization in laser-driven collisionless cylindrical convergence, focusing on ion acceleration in microtube implosions.
motivation: Collisionless converging ion flows can sustain energization over extended paths, but the field channel responsible for energy gain is often unclear.
method: The authors study laser-driven bladed microtube implosion and identify a self-generated gigagauss electrostatic field channel that energizes carbon ions along the convergence path.
result: The work attributes the observed energetic carbon ions to path-integrated electrostatic acceleration in the converging collisionless plasma flow.
conclusion: The findings clarify the energization mechanism in laser-driven cylindrical convergence and may inform plasma-based ion acceleration schemes.

title: Experimental Study Of The Impact Of Ion Wakes On The Charges And Dynamics Of Dust Particles In A Binary Complex Plasma
authors: Roman A. Syrovatka, Vadim N. Naumkin, Andrey M. Lipaev, Alexandr D. Usachev, Mikhail M. Vasiliev, Oleg F. Petrov, And Andrey V. Zobnin
abstract:
Author(s): Roman A. Syrovatka, Vadim N. Naumkin, Andrey M. Lipaev, Alexandr D. Usachev, Mikhail M. Vasiliev, Oleg F. Petrov, and Andrey V. Zobnin

Interactions in a plasma between microparticles of two different diameters are investigated. In these experiments, the smaller microparticles form a layer above the larger microparticles in the plasma sheath, and three-dimensional trajectories are determined from videos. The authors deduce ion-wake forces and microparticle charges from the measured oscillation frequencies.

#WellStructured


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045207] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: An experimental dusty-plasma study measuring ion-wake forces and charges of two different-sized microparticle populations levitated in a plasma sheath.
motivation: Interactions between microparticles of different sizes in complex plasmas are mediated by ion wakes, whose strength and particle charges are difficult to quantify experimentally.
method: Two sizes of microparticles form vertically separated layers in the plasma sheath; three-dimensional particle trajectories are reconstructed from video, and oscillation frequencies are used to infer ion-wake forces and particle charges.
result: Ion-wake forces and microparticle charges are deduced from the measured oscillation frequencies for the binary complex plasma system.
conclusion: The experiment quantifies wake-mediated coupling and charging in binary dusty plasmas, informing models of strongly coupled plasma dynamics.

title: Size Effects In Fluctuation-based Damage Mechanics In The Semigrand Canonical Ensemble
authors: Ariel Attias, Zdeněk P. Bažant, And Franz-Josef Ulm
abstract:
Author(s): Ariel Attias, Zdeněk P. Bažant, and Franz-Josef Ulm

We present results of a fluctuation-based investigation of size effects on damage and fracture of quasibrittle materials and structures. Set within the semigrand canonical ([MATH]) ensemble, we find that size effects of geometrically similar structures are a system property rather than a ma…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045504] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies size effects in damage and fracture of quasibrittle materials using a fluctuation-based analysis in the semigrand canonical ensemble.
motivation: Size effects in quasibrittle materials are important for predicting damage and fracture, but their origin requires a statistical-mechanical treatment beyond simple material-property scaling.
method: The authors formulate damage mechanics within the semigrand canonical ensemble and analyze fluctuations for geometrically similar structures to identify the origin of size effects.
result: They find that size effects in geometrically similar structures are a system property rather than a material property, arising from ensemble-level fluctuations.
conclusion: The work provides a fluctuation-based statistical-mechanical framework for understanding damage and fracture size effects in quasibrittle materials.

title: Low-frequency Oscillations As Internal State Integrators Of A Biosystem Model With Voltage-gated Ion Channels
authors: Sergio Portillo, Javier Cervera, Patricio Ramirez, And Salvador Mafe
abstract:
Author(s): Sergio Portillo, Javier Cervera, Patricio Ramirez, and Salvador Mafe

The protein ion channels inserted in cell membranes can act as bioelectrical diodes that control ionic transport. The nonlinear dynamics inherent to voltage-gated channels is useful to process temporal patterns and we explore the response of these channels to low-frequency voltage oscillations, whic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044407] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies voltage-gated ion channels as nonlinear bioelectrical elements that integrate low-frequency voltage oscillations and process temporal patterns.
motivation: Protein ion channels in cell membranes can act as bioelectrical diodes, motivating interest in how their nonlinear dynamics process time-dependent signals.
method: The authors model a biosystem with voltage-gated ion channels and analyze its response to low-frequency voltage oscillations as internal state integrators.
result: The model shows that low-frequency oscillatory inputs can be integrated by the channel dynamics, enabling temporal pattern processing.
conclusion: Voltage-gated ion channels may serve as internal state integrators for low-frequency signals in biological systems, though the work is not quantum information related.

title: Dynamical Equivalence For The Caging-release Colloidal Problem
authors: Ivany Del Carmen Romero-Sánchez, Leonardo Dagdug, And Erick Sarmiento-Gómez
abstract:
Author(s): Ivany del Carmen Romero-Sánchez, Leonardo Dagdug, and Erick Sarmiento-Gómez

Brownian particles in complex media often exhibit diffusion-caging-diffusion dynamics: short-time diffusion, an intermediate plateau due to diffusion hindrance, and long-time diffusion, usually attributed to cage-release events. We analyze an alternative mechanism that reproduces the same phenomenol…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044119] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper analyzes an alternative dynamical mechanism that reproduces diffusion-caging-diffusion behavior in colloidal Brownian systems.
motivation: Brownian particles in complex media often show short-time diffusion, an intermediate plateau, and long-time diffusion attributed to cage-release events; the authors explore whether the same phenomenology can arise from a different mechanism.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a caging-release colloidal problem and derive dynamical equivalence conditions that reproduce the observed diffusion-caging-diffusion phenomenology.
result: They show that an alternative mechanism can produce the same diffusion-caging-diffusion behavior, suggesting that plateau formation need not uniquely imply conventional cage-release events.
conclusion: The work clarifies dynamical equivalences in colloidal caging-release models and highlights ambiguity in inferring microscopic mechanisms from diffusion phenomenology.

title: Modularity, Asymmetry, And Polarization Shape Consensus Speed In The Voter Model
authors: Madi Yerlanov, Zachary P. Kilpatrick, And Nancy Rodriguez
abstract:
Author(s): Madi Yerlanov, Zachary P. Kilpatrick, and Nancy Rodriguez

In populations with community structure, the formation of consensus requires both alignment within and diffusion of beliefs across groups, processes that evolve on distinct timescales. How do modularity, asymmetry, and polarization shape this process? We study a variant of the voter model in which a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044313] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how modularity, asymmetry, and polarization affect consensus times in a variant of the voter model with community structure.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how alignment within groups and belief diffusion across groups, which occur on distinct timescales, jointly determine consensus formation in structured populations.
method: They analyze a variant of the voter model incorporating modular community structure, asymmetric inter-group influence, and polarized initial conditions, likely using analytical approximations and/or numerical simulations.
result: The study finds that modularity, asymmetry, and polarization each shape the speed of consensus, with these structural and dynamical features determining the relevant timescales of belief diffusion and alignment.
conclusion: Community structure and asymmetric polarization are key determinants of consensus dynamics in voter-type models, highlighting how group-level organization controls collective opinion formation.

title: Traveling Chimeras And Collective Coordination In $β$-cell Networks
