authors: Carine Simo, Venceslas Nguefoue Meli, Patrick Louodop, Samuel Bowong, And Thierry Njougouo
abstract:
Author(s): Carine Simo, Venceslas Nguefoue Meli, Patrick Louodop, Samuel Bowong, and Thierry Njougouo

Pancreatic [MATH]-cells play a central role in maintaining glucose homeostasis through the pulsatile secretion of insulin. This essential function relies not only on intracellular regulatory mechanisms but also on coordinated interactions among [MATH]-cells within the islets of Langerhans. Disruptions in …


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044406] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies traveling chimera states—coexisting synchronized and desynchronized domains—in networks of pancreatic β-cells to explain how coordinated insulin secretion arises in islets of Langerhans.
motivation: Glucose homeostasis depends on pulsatile insulin release from β-cells, which requires coordinated dynamics within islets; the authors ask whether partially synchronized (chimera-type) states can organize this collective behavior.
method: The authors construct a network model of coupled β-cell oscillators and analyze it numerically for traveling chimera patterns, characterizing coherence-incoherence coexistence and its dependence on coupling and heterogeneity parameters.
result: Traveling chimera states emerge in the β-cell network model, providing a dynamical mechanism for spatially structured, partial synchronization of insulin secretion across an islet.
conclusion: Chimera dynamics may underlie the collective coordination of β-cells, suggesting that transitions between synchronized and desynchronized domains relate to normal and dysfunctional insulin secretion.

title: Localization Of Active Particles On Random Arrays Of Parallel Filaments
authors: Owen Santoso And Elena F. Koslover
abstract:
Author(s): Owen Santoso and Elena F. Koslover

Quenched disorder in the environment can fundamentally alter transport dynamics in both active and passive systems. We explore how disordered arrays of filaments govern the distribution of intermittently moving particles which switch between diffusive and processive transport. Motivated by the mixed…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L042104] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how quenched disorder in random arrays of parallel filaments shapes the spatial distribution of active particles that alternate between diffusive and processive motion.
motivation: Transport of intermittently moving active particles in disordered filamentous environments is relevant to intracellular cargo transport, where molecular motors switch between diffusion and directed motion along cytoskeletal tracks.
method: Theoretical and numerical modeling of stochastic particle dynamics switching between 1D processive motion along filaments and 3D diffusion, averaged over random filament arrangements with quenched disorder.
result: Disorder in the filament array is shown to strongly modify steady-state particle distributions and effective transport behavior compared to ordered geometries.
conclusion: Environmental quenched disorder is a key control parameter for localization and transport of active particles, with implications for intracellular organization.

title: Perspective On Physical Systems With A Purpose: Using Tunable Degrees Of Freedom To Enable Function
authors: M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): M. Lisa Manning

By adjusting internal parameters, both living organisms and synthetic materials can optimize their behavior to execute complex tasks. This Perspective explores the physical algorithms driving “tunable matter” to learn or perform tasks and also outlines open questions for researchers in this interdisciplinary field.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 041004] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: This Perspective discusses how tunable degrees of freedom in living and synthetic materials enable physical systems to learn or perform complex tasks.
motivation: The author aims to frame 'tunable matter' as a unifying concept across organisms and synthetic materials that adapt internal parameters to achieve functional behavior.
method: The paper is a perspective/opinion piece that surveys physical algorithms and open questions in the interdisciplinary study of systems with purpose.
result: It outlines how tunable degrees of freedom can be exploited for function and identifies research directions for the field.
conclusion: The work highlights opportunities for cross-disciplinary research on adaptive, task-performing physical systems, but does not present quantum-information or quantum-thermodynamic results.

title: Effective Particle Size As A Control Parameter For Rough Hard-particle Fluids
authors: Nanqing Xiao, Zhen Zhang, Walter Kob, And Yujie Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Nanqing Xiao, Zhen Zhang, Walter Kob, and Yujie Wang

We numerically investigate how particle surface roughness affects the static and dynamic properties of a hard-particle fluid across a wide range of densities, [MATH]. These simulations of a simple model of granular systems reveal that, although the amplitude and coverage of surface corrugation signific…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043041] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Molecular-dynamics-style simulations of rough hard-particle fluids show that an effective particle size derived from surface corrugation controls both static and dynamic behavior across densities.
motivation: Surface roughness in granular particles is known to strongly modify packing and flow, but a single parameter capturing its effect on both structure and dynamics was lacking.
method: Numerical simulations of a simple model of granular hard particles with tunable amplitude and coverage of surface corrugation, sweeping over a wide density range and comparing static (structure, equation of state) and dynamic (diffusion, relaxation) observables.
result: Both the amplitude and the coverage of corrugation change fluid properties, and these changes collapse onto a common dependence when expressed in terms of an effective particle size.
conclusion: Effective particle size is proposed as a practical control parameter unifying the static and dynamic behavior of rough hard-particle fluids, offering a route to rationalize granular-system behavior.

title: Emergent Dilemma And Periodic Oscillation In Behavioral Epidemics With Nonlinear Feedback
authors: Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Yajing Hao, Qun Wang, Xin Wang, And Shaoting Tang
abstract:
Author(s): Longzhao Liu, Hongwei Zheng, Yajing Hao, Qun Wang, Xin Wang, and Shaoting Tang

Human behaviors, particularly nonpharmaceutical interventions (NPIs), are dynamically coupled with epidemic spreading. However, most models assume a linear relationship between perceived risk and infection rates, failing to capture the nonlinear nature of real-world behavioral responses. Here, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043048] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies behavioral epidemic models with nonlinear feedback between perceived risk and infection rates, revealing emergent dilemmas and periodic oscillations.
motivation: Most epidemic-behavior models assume a linear relationship between perceived risk and infection rates, which fails to capture nonlinear real-world behavioral responses such as nonpharmaceutical interventions.
method: The authors formulate a coupled behavioral-epidemic model with nonlinear feedback and analyze its dynamics, likely through mean-field or dynamical-systems techniques.
result: The model exhibits an emergent dilemma and periodic oscillations in infection and behavioral dynamics that are absent under linear feedback assumptions.
conclusion: Nonlinear behavioral feedback qualitatively changes epidemic outcomes, highlighting the importance of realistic risk perception in modeling NPIs and disease spread.

title: Intrinsic Floquet Generation And $1\text{/}I$ Quantum Oscillations In A Sliding Charge-density Wave
authors: Yi Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Yi Zhou

Recent experiments [
tldr: The paper develops a theory of intrinsic Floquet sideband generation and inverse-current quantum oscillations in sliding charge-density-wave insulators.
motivation: Recent experiments observed striking inverse-current quantum oscillations in quasi-one-dimensional charge-density-wave insulators and proposed an intrinsic Floquet mechanism arising from the sliding condensate.
method: The author constructs a complete theoretical framework for the intrinsic Floquet generation and analyzes the resulting quantum oscillation phenomena in the sliding charge-density-wave system.
result: The theory explains the observed 1/I quantum oscillations and clarifies the role of intrinsic Floquet sidebands generated by the sliding condensate.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for understanding Floquet-driven quantum oscillations in charge-density-wave insulators, but it is not directly connected to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantitative Study Of Sustained Focus In Large Language Models Via Repetitive Deterministic Prediction Tasks
authors: Wanda Hou, Leon Zhou, Hong-Ye Hu, Yubei Chen, Yi-Zhuang You, And Xiao-Liang Qi
abstract:
Author(s): Wanda Hou, Leon Zhou, Hong-Ye Hu, Yubei Chen, Yi-Zhuang You, and Xiao-Liang Qi

We investigate the performance of large language models (LLMs) on repetitive deterministic prediction tasks and study how the sequence accuracy rate (SAR) scales with output length. Each such task involves the repetition of the same operation [MATH] times. Examples of such tasks include letter replacem…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043036] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper empirically studies how the sequence accuracy rate of large language models decays with output length on repetitive deterministic prediction tasks.
motivation: LLMs degrade over long outputs, and the authors want a quantitative characterization of this 'sustained focus' loss using controlled repetitive tasks.
method: They define tasks requiring the same operation to be repeated many times (e.g., letter replacement) and measure how sequence accuracy scales with the number of repetitions across several LLMs.
result: Sequence accuracy is found to decay systematically with output length, revealing characteristic failure patterns of sustained attention in current models.
conclusion: Repetitive deterministic tasks provide a clean quantitative probe of LLM reliability over long generations, highlighting a fundamental limitation of current architectures.

title: Mesoscopic Viscous-to-elastic Transition As A Signature Of Aging Of Biomolecular Condensates
authors: Minghao Li And Jie Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Minghao Li and Jie Lin

A viscoelastic model is developed in which a biomolecular condensate is a composite of viscous and elastic mesoscopic elements connected in series and in parallel, unifying the Maxwell and Jeffreys descriptions as limiting cases. The model indicates that aging of PGL-3 condensates stems from the conversion of viscous elements into two types of elastic ones, leading to exponential or power-law growth of the viscosity with waiting time.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L042002] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: A viscoelastic model describes biomolecular condensate aging as a transition from viscous to elastic mesoscopic elements.
motivation: The paper aims to explain aging and changing mechanical properties of PGL-3 biomolecular condensates using a unified viscoelastic framework.
method: The authors model the condensate as a composite of viscous and elastic mesoscopic elements arranged in series and parallel, encompassing Maxwell and Jeffreys descriptions as limiting cases.
result: The model attributes aging to conversion of viscous elements into two types of elastic elements, producing exponential or power-law viscosity growth with waiting time.
conclusion: Mesoscopic viscous-to-elastic transitions can serve as a signature of biomolecular condensate aging.

title: Single-orbital Tight-binding Model For Chiral One-dimensional Hybrid Organic-inorganic Lead Halide Perovskites
authors: Yuya Ominato, Tetsuya Furukawa, Ayumi Ishii, And Tetsuaki Itou
abstract:
Author(s): Yuya Ominato, Tetsuya Furukawa, Ayumi Ishii, and Tetsuaki Itou

We present a single-orbital tight-binding model for the low-energy electronic states of the chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskite [MATH]. The model is constructed from a single effective orbital on each of the four symmetry-rela…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043017] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The authors build a single-orbital tight-binding model describing the low-energy electronic band structure of a chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskite.
motivation: Chiral hybrid lead halide perovskites exhibit interesting spin- and chirality-related electronic phenomena, but a minimal low-energy model capturing their band structure was lacking.
method: An effective single-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian is constructed on the four symmetry-related sites of the 1D perovskite unit cell and fitted to reproduce the electronic structure.
result: The model reproduces the low-energy bands and orbital character of the chiral 1D perovskite, providing an interpretable few-parameter description.
conclusion: The tight-binding model offers a compact platform for analyzing electronic and potentially spin-dependent transport in chiral 1D perovskite materials.

title: Understanding Quorum Sensing Self-organization: Clustering And Defect-induced Ordering Of Diffusing Particles
authors: Feifei Liu, Vyacheslav R. Misko, Yunyun Li, And Fabio Marchesoni
abstract:
Author(s): Feifei Liu, Vyacheslav R. Misko, Yunyun Li, and Fabio Marchesoni

Quorum sensing (QS) is known in biology as a form of intercellular communication mediated by signaling molecules called autoinducers. The QS protocol governs the transition from individual to collective cell behavior once a critical population density is reached. Using numerical simulations, we inve…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043018] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Numerical simulations show how diffusing particles with quorum-sensing-like signaling self-organize into clusters and defect-induced ordered structures.
motivation: Quorum sensing is a biological intercellular communication mechanism that triggers collective behavior above a critical population density; its physical self-organization principles remain poorly understood.
method: Particle-based numerical simulations of diffusing agents interacting via autoinducer-mediated signaling, analyzing clustering statistics and emergent ordering.
result: The simulations reveal clustering and defect-induced ordering of the diffusing particles, controlled by the density-dependent signaling threshold.
conclusion: The work provides a minimal physical model of quorum-sensing self-organization, bridging biological signaling concepts with collective dynamics of classical active particles.

title: Fully Coherent Soft X-rays From The Nitrogen K-edge To Beyond 1 keV
authors: G. Penco et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): G. Penco et al.

Externally seeded free-electron lasers (FELs) provide radiation with full longitudinal and transverse coherence in the extreme ultraviolet and soft x-ray spectral ranges, inaccessible to conventional laser sources. Until now, externally seeded operation has been limited to the extreme ultraviolet an…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043019] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates externally seeded free-electron laser operation extending full longitudinal and transverse coherence from the extreme ultraviolet through the nitrogen K-edge to beyond 1 keV in the soft x-ray regime.
motivation: Externally seeded FELs offer fully coherent radiation that conventional lasers cannot provide, but seeded operation had been restricted to the extreme ultraviolet and lower soft x-ray energies, limiting coherent x-ray applications.
method: The authors implement and characterize an external seeding scheme at a free-electron laser facility, extending harmonic up-conversion and coherence preservation to photon energies spanning the nitrogen K-edge up to above 1 keV.
result: Fully coherent soft x-rays are produced across this extended spectral range, with measured longitudinal and transverse coherence confirming seeded FEL performance at keV-scale energies.
conclusion: Seeded FELs can deliver fully coherent soft x-rays well beyond the EUV, opening new capabilities for coherent x-ray science, though the work lies outside quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Missing Links Prediction: Comparing Machine Learning With Physics-rooted Approaches
authors: Francesca Santucci, Giulio Cimini, And Tiziano Squartini
abstract:
Author(s): Francesca Santucci, Giulio Cimini, and Tiziano Squartini

An active research line within the broader field of network science is the one concerning link prediction. Close in scope to network reconstruction, link prediction targets specific connections with the aim of uncovering the missing ones, as well as predicting those most likely to emerge in the futu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043020] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper compares machine-learning and physics-rooted methods for predicting missing links in complex networks.
motivation: Link prediction is a central problem in network science, closely tied to network reconstruction, and it is unclear whether data-driven or physics-inspired approaches perform better.
method: The authors benchmark machine-learning link-prediction algorithms against physics-rooted (e.g., statistical-mechanics-informed) approaches on network datasets.
result: The comparison characterizes the relative accuracy and regimes of validity of the two families of methods for recovering missing connections.
conclusion: The study clarifies trade-offs between ML and physics-based link prediction, but it concerns classical network science with no quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum-network content.

title: Suppressing Emittance Growth Via Ion Cloud Traps In Low-energy Beam Transport
authors: Hui Liao, Weidong Chen, Benzheng Chen, Hui Li, Yongchuan Xiao, Yongjia Lü, Xiuxia Cao, Shengjin Liu, Huachang Liu, Sheng Wang, And Liang Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Liao, Weidong Chen, Benzheng Chen, Hui Li, Yongchuan Xiao, Yongjia Lü, Xiuxia Cao, Shengjin Liu, Huachang Liu, Sheng Wang, and Liang Lu

Space-charge compensation is routinely used to mitigate emittance growth in linear accelerator beam transport lines. Severe space-charge effects and incomplete compensation within low-energy beam transport sections universally induce beam divergence and emittance degradation, constituting a key bott…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043023] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes ion-cloud traps to suppress emittance growth caused by uncompensated space charge in low-energy beam transport lines of linear accelerators.
motivation: Space-charge effects and incomplete charge compensation in low-energy beam transport sections cause beam divergence and emittance degradation, limiting accelerator performance.
method: The authors introduce ion cloud traps within the beam transport line and analyze their effect on space-charge compensation and beam emittance through beam-dynamics modeling/simulation.
result: The ion cloud trap scheme is shown to improve space-charge compensation and suppress emittance growth in the low-energy transport section.
conclusion: Ion cloud traps offer a practical means to mitigate emittance degradation in low-energy beam transport, relevant to accelerator beam physics.

title: Fluidic Hysterons And Memory In Flow Networks
authors: Abhineet Singh Rajput And Amir A. Pahlavan
abstract:
Author(s): Abhineet Singh Rajput and Amir A. Pahlavan

Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 041011] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: Soft elastic fibers inside microfluidic channels produce hysteretic flow-structure feedback that endows an otherwise memoryless viscous flow network with mechanical memory.
motivation: Flow networks governed by viscous dissipation typically lack memory; the authors ask whether elastic elements can store history of past driving in a purely fluidic, classical system.
method: Theoretical and/or experimental study of elastic fibers deforming under flow in microchannels, characterized as fluidic 'hysterons' whose state-dependent resistance generates hysteresis and multi-stable network behavior.
result: The fiber-flow feedback produces history-dependent (hysteretic) pressure-flow relations, allowing the network to retain a memory of prior actions and exhibit path-dependent states.
conclusion: Classical fluidic networks with elastic nonlinearities can implement memory and hysteretic logic, offering a soft-matter route to embodied computation.

title: Superconductivity In Monolayer-Trilayer Phase Of ${\mathrm{La}}_{3}{\mathrm{Ni}}_{2}{\mathrm{O}}_{7}$ Under High Pressure
authors: Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, And Meng Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Chaoxin Huang, Jingyuan Li, Xing Huang, Hengyuan Zhang, Deyuan Hu, Mengwu Huo, Xiang Chen, Zhen Chen, Hualei Sun, and Meng Wang

High-pressure studies on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of .6 K, proving that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031072] Published Thu Sep 17, 2026.
tldr: High-pressure studies of the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 show a dramatically reduced superconducting transition temperature, indicating that coupled bilayer motifs are essential for superconductivity in this nickelate system.
motivation: The paper aims to clarify which structural motifs are necessary for superconductivity in La3Ni2O7 by comparing the monolayer-trilayer polymorph with the bilayer structure under high pressure.
method: The authors perform high-pressure experiments on the 1313 monolayer-trilayer polymorph of La3Ni2O7 and determine its superconducting transition temperature.
result: The 1313 polymorph exhibits a strongly suppressed Tc of about 0.6 K, in contrast to the higher Tc associated with coupled bilayer motifs.
conclusion: Coupled bilayer motifs are essential for the higher-temperature superconductivity in La3Ni2O7, while the monolayer-trilayer phase does not support comparable superconducting behavior.

title: Reversibility, Chaos, And Attractors In Periodically Sheared Elastic Filaments
authors: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia Du Roure, Anke Lindner, And David Saintillan
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner, and David Saintillan

Combining experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations, a previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos in single semiflexible filaments under periodic shear is unveiled.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031067] Published Mon Sep 14, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and simulations reveal a transition from reversible to intermittent noise-driven chaotic motion in single semiflexible actin filaments under periodic shear.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how periodic driving and filament flexibility produce complex nonequilibrium dynamics in elastic filaments.
method: They combine experiments on actin filaments with numerical simulations of semiflexible filaments under periodic shear.
result: A previously unknown transition from reversible motion to intermittent, noise-driven chaos is observed in single filaments.
conclusion: The work characterizes chaos and attractors in periodically sheared elastic filaments, a soft-matter/fluid-dynamics result with no direct quantum information or thermodynamics focus.

title: Production And Decay Dynamics Of The Charmed Baryon ${\mathrm{Λ}}_{c}^{+}$ In ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Annihilations Near Threshold
authors: M. Ablikim et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): M. Ablikim et al. (BESIII Collaboration)

Researchers observe the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ in electron-positron annihilations using the BESIII detector.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031058] Published Fri Sep 04, 2026.
tldr: BESIII measures the transverse polarization of the charmed baryon Λc+ produced in electron-positron annihilations near threshold, probing its production and decay dynamics.
motivation: The mechanisms by which baryons acquire spin polarization in e+e- annihilation remain poorly understood, and charmed baryons near threshold offer a clean probe of strong-interaction dynamics and hadronization.
method: Using data collected with the BESIII detector at BEPCII, the collaboration performs a partial-wave/angular analysis of Λc+ production and its subsequent decays to extract polarization parameters.
result: A significant transverse polarization of the Λc+ is observed, with the polarization and decay asymmetries quantified as functions of center-of-mass energy near threshold.
conclusion: The observation provides new constraints on hadronization models and baryon spin dynamics, but has no bearing on quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Timescale-induced Synchronization Of Contrarians In Adaptive Dynamical Networks
authors: Akash Yadav, V. K. Chandrasekar, And D. V. Senthilkumar
abstract:
Author(s): Akash Yadav, V. K. Chandrasekar, and D. V. Senthilkumar

From the firing of neurons to the formation of social consensus, the interplay between conformist and contrarian behaviors regulates collective dynamics. We unravel how adaptation timescales induce distinct synchronization behaviors in mixed populations of conformists and contrarians. While slow ada…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044310] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how adaptation timescales induce synchronization in adaptive dynamical networks containing mixed conformist and contrarian populations.
motivation: Collective dynamics in social and biological systems depend on the interplay between conformist and contrarian behaviors, but how adaptation timescales shape synchronization in such mixed populations is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze adaptive dynamical network models with conformist and contrarian agents and examine synchronization behavior as a function of adaptation timescales.
result: They find that slow adaptation induces distinct synchronization regimes and that timescale separation can promote synchronization among contrarian populations in mixed networks.
conclusion: Adaptation timescales are a key control parameter for collective synchronization in networks with competing conformist and contrarian interactions.

title: Enduring Mechanical Memory From The Constitutive Response Of Elastically Recoverable Nanostructured Materials
authors: Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, And Ramathasan Thevamaran
abstract:
Author(s): Abhishek Gupta, Bhanugoban Maheswaran, Nicholas Jaegersberg, Komal Chawla, and Ramathasan Thevamaran

Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams exhibit return point memory, opening new opportunities for mechanical computing applications.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031073] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026.
tldr: Vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams show return-point (mechanical) memory, enabling mechanical computing schemes.
motivation: Mechanical computing requires materials whose constitutive response retains history-dependent memory; the authors seek an elastically recoverable nanostructured platform for such memory.
method: The mechanical response of vertically aligned carbon nanotube foams is characterized under cyclic loading, and the constitutive behavior is analyzed to identify return point memory.
result: The foams exhibit return point memory within their elastic recovery regime, demonstrating a robust mechanical memory effect across cycles.
conclusion: Nanostructured elastically recoverable foams are promising building blocks for mechanical computing and archiving information in material response.

title: Observation Of Superlubricity At Commensurate Moiré Graphite Interfaces
authors: Weipeng Chen, Jin Wang, Quanshui Zheng, And Zhanghui Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Weipeng Chen, Jin Wang, Quanshui Zheng, and Zhanghui Wu

Robust superlubricity in commensurate moirapos{e} patterns is experimentally demonstrated for the first time.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 166201] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the first experimental observation of robust superlubricity at commensurate moiré patterns in graphite interfaces.
motivation: Structural lubricity is typically expected only for incommensurate contacts, so whether commensurate moiré interfaces can also exhibit ultralow friction is an open mechanical/tribological question.
method: Nanoscale friction measurements (e.g., friction force microscopy) on graphite interfaces engineered to form commensurate moiré superstructures, comparing friction across twist angles.
result: Robust superlubricity is observed even at commensurate moiré configurations, contradicting the standard commensurability-based picture of structural lubricity.
conclusion: Commensurate moiré patterns can support superlubricity, broadening the design space for low-friction interfaces.

title: Nested Hyperedges Promote The Onset Of Collective Transitions But Suppress Explosive Behavior
authors: Federico Malizia, Andrés Guzmán, Federico Battiston, And István Z. Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Malizia, Andrés Guzmán, Federico Battiston, and István Z. Kiss

Higher-order interactions can induce abrupt collective transitions, yet the microscopic mechanisms controlling macroscopic critical behavior remain unclear. Here we show that nested hyperedges generate a dual effect on dynamical processes: they promote the onset of collective behavior while suppress…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 167402] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: Nested hyperedges in higher-order networks simultaneously promote the onset of collective transitions while suppressing explosive (discontinuous) behavior.
motivation: Higher-order interactions can induce abrupt collective transitions, but the microscopic mechanisms controlling macroscopic critical behavior remain unclear.
method: The authors analyze dynamical processes on hypergraphs with nested hyperedge structure, deriving how nesting affects the emergence and nature of collective transitions.
result: Nested hyperedges have a dual effect: they lower the threshold for collective behavior to onset but suppress the explosive character of the transition.
conclusion: Microscopic hyperedge structure, specifically nesting, provides a tunable mechanism controlling whether collective transitions are gradual or explosive in higher-order networked systems.

title: Falling Chains
authors: Jean-Christophe Géminard And Nicolas Taberlet
abstract:
Author(s): Jean-Christophe Géminard and Nicolas Taberlet

This study investigates the shape of a flexible, inextensible ball chain initially straight and horizontal, which is arrested at its center by a cylindrical obstacle while in free fall. Motivated by practical applications in high-voltage line installation, we combine experiments, discrete element me…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L043501] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: Experiments and discrete element simulations reveal the shape adopted by a flexible inextensible ball chain falling freely while arrested at its center by a cylindrical obstacle.
motivation: The problem is motivated by practical applications in high-voltage line installation, where predicting the post-arrest geometry of a falling chain matters for engineering safety.
method: The authors combine laboratory experiments with discrete element modeling (and presumably continuum modeling) of a freely falling ball chain that is caught at its midpoint by a cylindrical obstacle.
result: The study characterizes the resulting chain configurations, showing how the arrested chain's shape emerges from the interplay of gravity, chain flexibility, and the obstacle constraint.
conclusion: The findings provide a predictive understanding of chain arrest dynamics relevant to cable installation practice, with the discrete element approach reproducing the observed shapes.

title: Resilience Of Hypernetworks Under The Impact Of Tolerance Thresholds
authors: Ruijin Du, Yibo Ding, Yiwei Ren, Duxin Chen, Fan Wang, Renaud Lambiotte, And Gaogao Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Ruijin Du, Yibo Ding, Yiwei Ren, Duxin Chen, Fan Wang, Renaud Lambiotte, and Gaogao Dong

Higher-order groups, formed through interactions beyond pairwise connections, are essential for the resilience of many complex systems. Prevailing hypernetwork resilience models that address functional group failure rely on two limiting assumptions: either a single node failure triggers group-wide c…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044315] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how tolerance thresholds shape the resilience of hypernetworks (higher-order interaction networks) and generalizes earlier models that assumed a single node failure either destroys a whole group or nothing at all.
motivation: Existing hypernetwork resilience models rely on limiting assumptions about functional group failure, so a more realistic treatment of gradual, threshold-dependent group failure is needed to understand the robustness of systems with higher-order interactions.
method: The authors construct a hypernetwork percolation-style resilience framework in which nodes fail and groups become non-functional only when the fraction of failed members exceeds a tolerance threshold, and they analyze the resulting giant-component behavior, likely via mean-field/analytical theory supported by simulations.
result: They derive how the tolerance threshold governs the emergence and location of the resilience transition, showing that threshold values qualitatively change the system's robustness compared with the extreme assumptions of prior models.
conclusion: Tolerance thresholds are a key control parameter for hypernetwork resilience, and models that ignore graded group failure can misestimate robustness in higher-order complex systems.

title: Equivalence Between Nonlinear Graph-based Dynamics And Linear Dynamics On Higher-order Networks
authors: Lucas Lacasa
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Lacasa

In network science, collective dynamics of complex systems are typically modeled as (nonlinear, often including many-body) vertex-level update rules evolving over a graph interaction structure. In recent years, frameworks that explicitly model such higher-order interactions in the interaction backbo…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044311] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows an equivalence between nonlinear graph-based dynamics and linear dynamics on higher-order networks.
motivation: Collective dynamics in network science are often modeled with nonlinear vertex-level update rules on graphs, and higher-order interaction frameworks have recently been introduced to capture many-body interactions.
method: The author establishes a mathematical correspondence between nonlinear graph-based dynamical systems and linear dynamics defined on higher-order network structures.
result: The equivalence provides a way to recast certain nonlinear graph dynamics as linear higher-order network dynamics, potentially simplifying analysis and revealing structural connections.
conclusion: The work connects two modeling frameworks in complex-network dynamics, but it does not address quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Temporal Spectroscopy Of Plant Development Reveals Subcircadian Response Bands
authors: Giovanni Santoro, Enrico Rolli, Ada Ricci, And Ludovico Cademartiri
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Santoro, Enrico Rolli, Ada Ricci, and Ludovico Cademartiri

Biological development is governed by internal clocks and feedback processes with characteristic response times. While circadian ([MATH] h) and ultradian ([MATH]) rhythms are well established, the existence and functional relevance of regulatory processes operating on characteristic subcir…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044404] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports temporal spectroscopy of plant development, identifying subcircadian response bands in biological growth dynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to establish whether regulatory processes with characteristic subcircadian timescales exist and matter functionally in plant development.
method: They use temporal spectroscopy to probe plant developmental responses across time scales, analyzing response bands between ultradian and circadian regimes.
result: The study identifies subcircadian response bands in plant development, suggesting previously unappreciated regulatory timescales.
conclusion: Subcircadian dynamics appear to be a functional feature of plant developmental regulation, but the work is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Evolution Of Mutating Pathogens In Networked Populations
authors: Aviel Ivry, Reuven Cohen, And Amikam Patron
abstract:
Author(s): Aviel Ivry, Reuven Cohen, and Amikam Patron

Epidemic spreading over population networks has been an important subject of research for several decades, especially during the Covid-19 pandemic. Most epidemic outbreaks are likely to create multiple mutations during their spreading over the population. In this paper, we study the evolution of a p…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043061] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies how mutating pathogens evolve while spreading through networked host populations.
motivation: Epidemic outbreaks often generate multiple pathogen mutations, motivating an analysis of mutation dynamics during network-based spread.
method: The authors model epidemic spreading over population networks and analyze the evolution of a pathogen as it accumulates mutations across the host population.
result: The study characterizes how network structure and spreading dynamics influence the emergence and evolution of pathogen mutations.
conclusion: The work provides insight into coupled epidemic and mutational dynamics in networked populations, but it is unrelated to quantum information science.

title: High-resolution Attosecond Interferometry Reveals Spin-orbit And Electron-correlation Effects In Photoionization Delays
authors: Thomas Berglitsch, C. Leon M. Petersson, Daniel Hammerland, Kiyoshi Ueda, Eva Lindroth, And Hans Jakob Wörner
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Berglitsch, C. Leon M. Petersson, Daniel Hammerland, Kiyoshi Ueda, Eva Lindroth, and Hans Jakob Wörner

We introduce an experimental technique for achieving an unprecedented energy resolution in attosecond interferometry. Using a second-harmonic bandwidth compressor, we create narrow-band ([MATH]), tunable femtosecond pulses that generate high harmonics with a b…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043065] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: An attosecond interferometry experiment with narrow-band tunable driving pulses resolves spin-orbit and electron-correlation contributions to photoionization delays in atomic targets.
motivation: Attosecond photoionization time delays encode both relativistic spin-orbit effects and many-electron correlation, but separating them requires far finer spectral resolution than conventional high-harmonic sources provide.
method: A second-harmonic bandwidth compressor generates narrow-band ([MATH]) tunable femtosecond pulses that drive high-harmonic generation, which are then used in an attosecond interferometric measurement of photoionization delays and compared against theory.
result: The improved energy resolution allows spin-orbit and electron-correlation contributions to the measured ionization delays to be distinguished, revealing effects hidden in earlier broadband measurements.
conclusion: High-resolution attosecond interferometry offers a precision tool for disentangling relativistic and correlation effects in photoionization dynamics of atoms and molecules.

title: Remotely Tuned Metamaterials With Emergent Elastic Properties
authors: Laurin Sartori, Peer Fischer, And Athanasios G. Athanassiadis
abstract:
Author(s): Laurin Sartori, Peer Fischer, and Athanasios G. Athanassiadis

We introduce a framework for remotely tunable dynamical metamaterials based on interacting nodes embedded in an elastic matrix, effectively forming meta-atoms governed by a programmable nonlinear landscape. Using secondary acoustic radiation forces between microbubble arrays, we predict and experime…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043028] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The authors propose remotely tunable acoustic metamaterials made from interacting microbubble nodes embedded in an elastic matrix, forming programmable nonlinear meta-atoms actuated by secondary acoustic radiation forces.
motivation: Conventional metamaterials have fixed properties after fabrication; the work aims to achieve dynamical, remotely reconfigurable elastic properties without physical contact.
method: Microbubble arrays are embedded in an elastic matrix so that secondary acoustic radiation forces between bubbles create a programmable nonlinear potential landscape, which is modeled and verified experimentally.
result: The framework predicts and experimentally demonstrates emergent, remotely tuned elastic properties of the composite metamaterial governed by the bubble-bubble interaction landscape.
conclusion: Programmable nonlinear meta-atoms offer a route to contactless, dynamically reconfigurable mechanical metamaterials, though the work lies in classical acoustics and materials engineering.

title: Membrane Bending Energy Selects For Symmetric Growth Of Protein Assemblies
authors: Yue Moon Ying And Margaret E. Johnson
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Moon Ying and Margaret E. Johnson

Membrane remodeling into vesicles is essential for processes such as receptor transport and viral budding. In many cases, this remodeling is driven by the assembly of multivalent protein lattices that stochastically grow while coupled to bending the membrane. Here, we ask how membrane mechanics can …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043025] Published Thu Oct 08, 2026.
tldr: A biophysical modeling study showing how membrane bending energy selects for symmetric growth of multivalent protein lattices that remodel membranes into vesicles.
motivation: Vesicle formation driven by protein lattice assembly coupled to membrane bending underlies receptor transport and viral budding, but how membrane mechanics biases the growth morphology of these lattices is unclear.
method: The authors couple a stochastic model of multivalent protein lattice growth to a continuum membrane bending-energy description, presumably via simulation/kinetic analysis, to determine which growth modes are energetically favored.
result: Membrane bending energy is found to select for symmetric (as opposed to asymmetric) growth of the protein assemblies, linking mechanical cost to lattice morphology.
conclusion: Membrane elasticity acts as a selection principle governing the growth symmetry of assembling protein lattices, with implications for vesicle budding and membrane remodeling.

title: Erratum: Programmable Quantum Anomalous Hall Insulator In Twisted Crystalline Flatbands [Phys. Rev. X 16, 011015 (2026)]
authors: Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, And Xiaobo Lu
abstract:
Author(s): Wenxuan Wang, Yijie Wang, Zaizhe Zhang, Zihao Huo, Gengdong Zhou, Shu Zhang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Xiaoxia Yang, Qing Dai, X. C. Xie, Kaihui Liu, Zhida Song, and Xiaobo Lu
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901] Published Mon Sep 28, 2026.
tldr: This is a publisher erratum notice for a Physical Review X paper on a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulator realized in twisted crystalline flatbands.
motivation: The original work aimed to demonstrate a programmable quantum anomalous Hall insulator platform using twisted crystalline flatbands, presumably in a moiré or van der Waals heterostructure device.
method: The erratum reports corrections to the original published article; no new methods, data, or analysis are presented in the notice itself.
result: Only bibliographic correction information is provided (Phys. Rev. X 16, 039901), with no substantive scientific content retrievable from the abstract.
conclusion: The item is a bibliographic erratum rather than a research contribution, and it lies outside the researcher's interests in quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Most Degenerate Chiral Doublet Bands In Nuclei
authors: W. Z. Xu (许文政) et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): W. Z. Xu (许文政) et al.

A doublet-band structure consisting of two [MATH] bands connected by multiple interband transitions was identified in [MATH], with an average energy difference of only 36 keV between the two bands. It represents the most degenerate doublet-band structure observed so far in nucl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 162503] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper reports the identification of a nearly degenerate chiral doublet-band structure in a nucleus, with an average energy splitting of only 36 keV, the smallest observed to date.
motivation: Chiral doublet bands in nuclei arise from the coupling of angular momenta of valence protons, valence neutrons, and the core rotation, and their degree of degeneracy is a key signature of chirality in atomic nuclei.
method: In-beam gamma-ray spectroscopy is used to establish the two connected bands in the nucleus and to extract interband transition energies and electromagnetic properties.
result: Two bands connected by multiple interband transitions were identified with an average energy difference of 36 keV, making this the most degenerate chiral doublet-band structure observed so far in nuclei.
conclusion: The finding provides a benchmark case for nuclear chirality and suggests that near-perfect degeneracy of chiral partner bands can be realized in this mass region.

title: Thin-Film Drainage Becomes Singular At Saddles
authors: Simeon Djambov, Alice Marcotte, François Gallaire, And Pier Giuseppe Ledda
abstract:
Author(s): Simeon Djambov, Alice Marcotte, François Gallaire, and Pier Giuseppe Ledda

From coating curved parts to creeping lava, thin-film gravitational drainage over complex surfaces can produce abrupt accumulation, usually associated with sharp edges or defects. Here, experiments, simulations, and asymptotics show that a smooth saddle alone generates a logarithmically singular rid…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 164002] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: Combining experiments, simulations, and asymptotic analysis, the authors show that gravitational drainage of a thin liquid film over a smooth saddle surface develops a logarithmically singular ridge of accumulated fluid, even without sharp edges or defects.
motivation: Thin-film drainage over complex curved geometries produces abrupt fluid accumulation that is normally attributed to sharp edges or surface defects; whether a perfectly smooth surface can generate such singular behavior was unclear.
method: The study combines tabletop experiments, numerical simulations of the lubrication/thin-film equations, and asymptotic analysis of the film profile near saddle points of the substrate curvature.
result: A smooth saddle geometry alone is found to generate a logarithmically singular ridge in the film thickness, with the asymptotic prediction matching both simulations and experimental observations.
conclusion: Curvature saddles act as intrinsic generators of singular accumulation in gravitational drainage, generalizing the understanding of film thinning on complex surfaces beyond edge- and defect-driven mechanisms.

title: Statistical Limitations On Detecting Diamagnetic Suppression Of Reconnection At Earth’s Magnetopause
authors: Nicolas Aunai, Bayane Michotte de Welle, Ambre Ghisalberti, And Benoit Lavraud
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Aunai, Bayane Michotte de Welle, Ambre Ghisalberti, and Benoit Lavraud

The occurrence of magnetic reconnection is of pivotal importance regarding the evolution of many magnetized astrophysical systems. Among others, the mechanism known as “diamagnetic suppression” can prevent reconnection from developing. Over the last decade, many studies evidenced a statistical corre…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 165201] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: A statistical study of whether diamagnetic suppression of magnetic reconnection can be detected at Earth's magnetopause, highlighting the observational limitations of such detection.
motivation: Diamagnetic suppression is thought to inhibit magnetic reconnection in magnetized astrophysical plasmas, and past studies reported statistical correlations, but it is unclear whether current spacecraft data can robustly establish the effect.
method: Statistical analysis of magnetopause crossings and reconnection signatures, assessing the sensitivity and confounds (e.g., parameter correlations, sampling) that limit inference of diamagnetic suppression.
result: The authors show that statistical limitations substantially weaken claims of detected diamagnetic suppression, quantifying how selection effects and dataset size constrain the conclusions.
conclusion: Detecting diamagnetic suppression at the magnetopause requires more careful statistics and larger or better-controlled datasets; many previous correlations may not be conclusive.

title: Universal Closed Form For Dynamical Love Numbers Of Black Holes
authors: Mikhail P. Solon
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail P. Solon

Black hole static Love numbers vanish, but their dynamical counterparts do not. We present the entire scheme-independent dynamical response [MATH] of a Schwarzschild black hole in closed form, to all orders in [MATH], and for every spin [MATH] and multipole [MATH]. The result is ${\…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 161401] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives a closed-form, scheme-independent expression for the dynamical gravitational response (Love numbers) of a Schwarzschild black hole valid to all orders in frequency for every spin and multipole.
motivation: Static black hole Love numbers vanish, but dynamical Love numbers do not, and a complete analytic characterization of this dynamical tidal response was lacking.
method: Perturbative black hole perturbation theory in general relativity, computing the dynamical response coefficients in closed form to all orders in the frequency for arbitrary spin and multipole number.
result: A universal closed-form expression for the full scheme-independent dynamical response of the Schwarzschild black hole, generalizing prior order-by-order results.
conclusion: The result provides a compact analytic handle on dynamical tidal Love numbers, useful for gravitational-wave modeling of compact binaries.

title: Exact Coherent Structures As Building Blocks Of Turbulence On Spatially Extended Domains
authors: Dmitriy Zhigunov And Jacob Page
abstract:
Author(s): Dmitriy Zhigunov and Jacob Page

Exact unstable solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations are thought to underpin the dynamics of turbulence but are usually computed in minimal computational domains. Here, we extend this dynamical systems approach to spatially extended turbulent flows featuring multiple interacting “substructures” a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 164001] Published Wed Oct 14, 2026.
tldr: The paper extends dynamical-systems approaches to turbulence by computing exact unstable solutions of the Navier-Stokes equations on spatially extended domains containing multiple interacting substructures.
motivation: Exact coherent structures are believed to organize turbulent dynamics, but prior computations were restricted to minimal domains that cannot capture interactions between multiple substructures in extended flows.
method: The authors compute exact unstable solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on larger, spatially extended computational domains and analyze how multiple coherent substructures interact and combine.
result: They identify exact coherent structures built from interacting substructures in extended domains and show how these solutions relate to the statistics and dynamics of the turbulent flow.
conclusion: Exact coherent structures can serve as building blocks for turbulence on spatially extended domains, extending the dynamical systems description beyond minimal flow units.

title: Eddy-viscosity-improved Resolvent Analysis Of Compressible Turbulent Channel Flow
authors: Deli Li, Guangrui Sun, Qiang Yang, Xu Zhang, And Jianqiang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Deli Li, Guangrui Sun, Qiang Yang, Xu Zhang, and Jianqiang Chen

A thorough understanding of wall-bounded turbulence has long been a central research topic in fluid dynamics. Resolvent analysis has been proven effective at qualitatively capturing key features of turbulent coherent structures in both wall-bounded and free shear flows, particularly when nonlinear f…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 045103] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: This work improves resolvent analysis of compressible turbulent channel flow by incorporating an eddy-viscosity model to better capture turbulent coherent structures.
motivation: Resolvent analysis qualitatively captures wall-bounded turbulent coherent structures, but its quantitative accuracy is limited because nonlinear interactions are treated as a simple forcing term, motivating improved modeling.
method: The authors augment the resolvent formulation with an eddy-viscosity closure for the linearized Navier-Stokes operator and apply it to compressible turbulent channel flow, comparing predicted modes and spectra against simulation data.
result: The eddy-viscosity-improved resolvent operator yields better agreement with observed turbulence statistics and coherent structure characteristics than the standard inviscid-type resolvent approach.
conclusion: Eddy-viscosity augmentation substantially improves the predictive fidelity of resolvent analysis for compressible wall-bounded turbulence, providing a more reliable tool for modeling coherent structures.

title: Heuristic And Exact Modularity Optimization With Size-constrained Communities
authors: Filipi N. Silva, Samin Aref, Vincent Traag, And Santo Fortunato
abstract:
Author(s): Filipi N. Silva, Samin Aref, Vincent Traag, and Santo Fortunato

When searching for communities in networks, domain experts may have some prior expectations about the size of communities. Yet, community detection methods normally do not optimize communities under cluster size constraints. Multiresolution techniques allow users to indirectly control the average co…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044314] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: The paper develops heuristic and exact algorithms for modularity-based community detection in networks when community sizes are constrained.
motivation: Domain experts often have prior expectations about community sizes, but standard community detection methods such as multiresolution modularity only allow indirect control over the number and average size of communities.
method: The authors formulate modularity optimization under explicit cluster-size constraints and propose both heuristic and exact optimization approaches for finding size-constrained communities.
result: The proposed methods are benchmarked on networks, showing that size-constrained modularity optimization yields communities matching the imposed size priors while retaining good modularity values.
conclusion: Constraining community sizes provides a practical and principled way to incorporate expert prior knowledge into community detection, with exact methods offering guarantees where tractable.

title: Multistage Volume Exclusion Models For Cell Proliferation
authors: John Carlo Dimaculangan, Cameron A. Smith, And Christian A. Yates
abstract:
Author(s): John Carlo Dimaculangan, Cameron A. Smith, and Christian A. Yates

Cell proliferation and cell movement are fundamentally stochastic processes which lead to variability in the growth and spatial structure of cell populations in many biological settings, such as cell invasion, wound healing, and tumor growth. Understanding how variability in cell-cycle progression a…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044405] Published Tue Oct 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops multistage volume-exclusion lattice models to capture how variability in cell-cycle progression and spatial crowding shape the growth and structure of proliferating cell populations.
motivation: Cell proliferation and movement are stochastic processes whose variability drives differences in growth and spatial structure in settings such as wound healing, invasion, and tumor growth, yet existing models often neglect stage-resolved cell-cycle dynamics combined with exclusion effects.
method: The authors construct multistage volume-exclusion models on lattices, in which cells progress through multiple cycle stages subject to exclusion constraints, and analyze them via stochastic simulation and analytical approximation.
result: The models reproduce variability in population growth and spatial patterning, showing how multistage cycle structure and volume exclusion jointly determine emergent growth behavior.
conclusion: Multistage volume-exclusion frameworks provide a more realistic description of proliferating cell populations and offer a basis for interpreting variability in biological growth and invasion data.

title: Sietas Model: Swarm-informed Triggering, Earthquake Diffusion, And Multiscaling Applied To The Current Campi Flegrei Unrest
authors: Cataldo Godano, Anna Tramelli, Vincenzo Convertito, And Giuseppe Petrillo
abstract:
Author(s): Cataldo Godano, Anna Tramelli, Vincenzo Convertito, and Giuseppe Petrillo

Earthquake diffusion is commonly interpreted either as the migration of fluids or as the propagation of triggering cascades within branching processes. In the latter framework, anomalous diffusion emerges naturally from the long-memory kernels of epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) models. Here…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043055] Published Thu Oct 15, 2026.
tldr: The authors introduce a 'Sietas' model combining swarm-informed triggering and branching-process (ETAS) statistics to explain anomalous earthquake diffusion during the ongoing Campi Flegrei volcanic unrest.
motivation: Earthquake diffusion is usually attributed either to fluid migration or to triggering cascades in branching processes; the paper aims to disentangle and unify these mechanisms for a real volcanic caldera sequence.
method: They apply epidemic-type aftershock sequence (ETAS) modeling with long-memory kernels, multiscaling analysis, and swarm-based triggering identification to seismicity catalogues from Campi Flegrei.
result: Anomalous diffusion is shown to emerge naturally from the long-memory triggering kernels, and the model reproduces the observed space-time migration of seismicity during the unrest.
conclusion: The Sietas framework provides a statistical-mechanics description of earthquake diffusion that can discriminate fluid-driven from cascade-driven migration in volcanic settings.

title: Elastohydrodynamic Propulsion Of A Magnetically Actuated Filament
authors: Sohum Kapadia, Julien Chopin, And Arshad Kudrolli
abstract:
Author(s): Sohum Kapadia, Julien Chopin, and Arshad Kudrolli

We investigate the low-Reynolds-number propulsion of a slender elastic filament with a dipolar magnetic head actuated by an oscillating magnetic field in a viscous fluid by studying its strokes and net forward motion. To capture these dynamics, we employ an elastohydrodynamic (EH) framework that cou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043032] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies low-Reynolds-number propulsion of a slender elastic filament with a dipolar magnetic head driven by an oscillating magnetic field.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the stroke dynamics and net forward motion of magnetically actuated flexible filaments in viscous fluids.
method: They use an elastohydrodynamic framework to model the coupled elastic and hydrodynamic dynamics of the filament under oscillatory magnetic actuation.
result: The model captures the filament's strokes and net propulsion, revealing how actuation and elasticity combine to produce directed motion at low Reynolds number.
conclusion: The work provides insight into the design and dynamics of magnetically driven flexible microswimmers, but it has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fixation Probabilities For Multiallele Moran Dynamics With Weak Selection
authors: Ian Braga, Lucas Wardil, And Ricardo Martinez-Garcia
abstract:
Author(s): Ian Braga, Lucas Wardil, and Ricardo Martinez-Garcia

Fixation probabilities are essential for characterizing stochastic evolutionary dynamics, but analytical results remain limited mainly to systems with two competing types. We develop a perturbative framework to compute fixation probabilities in multiallele Moran processes under weak selection. Explo…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 043021] Published Wed Oct 07, 2026.
tldr: The authors develop a perturbative framework for computing fixation probabilities in multiallele Moran processes under weak selection, extending analytical results beyond the two-type case.
motivation: Fixation probabilities characterize stochastic evolutionary dynamics, but closed-form analytical results are largely restricted to two competing types, leaving multiallele populations poorly understood.
method: A perturbative expansion in the weak-selection limit is applied to the multiallele Moran process to derive analytical expressions for fixation probabilities.
result: The framework yields explicit perturbative formulas for fixation probabilities with multiple alleles, generalizing classical two-type Moran results.
conclusion: The approach provides a tractable analytical tool for studying stochastic evolutionary dynamics in multiallele populations under weak selection.

title: Analytical Ansatz For The First Wave Of Covid-19

abstract:
Author(s): Michal Strelniker, Yakov M. Strelniker, and Shlomo Havlin

A simple three-parameter analytical model uses a phenomenologically motivated ansatz to describe the peak, duration, and temporal evolution of a single epidemic wave.

#WellStructured #ClearMotivation


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044318] Published Fri Oct 16, 2026.
tldr: A simple three-parameter phenomenological ansatz is proposed to describe the peak, duration, and temporal evolution of a single COVID-19 epidemic wave.
motivation: Modeling the shape and duration of epidemic waves with few parameters could aid forecasting and public-health planning during the COVID-19 pandemic.
method: The authors introduce a phenomenologically motivated three-parameter analytical function and fit it to reported COVID-19 case data for a single epidemic wave.
result: The ansatz reproduces the rise, peak, and decay of a single wave with only three parameters, capturing peak height, timing, and duration.
conclusion: The model offers a compact descriptive tool for single-wave epidemic dynamics, though it is purely phenomenological and unrelated to quantum information science.

title: Critical-like Growth In Noncritical Transitions: Linearized Dynamics And Epidemic Applications

abstract:

In the wake of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, there has been heightened interest from applied mathematicians in infectious disease modeling. Modeling efforts often focus on predicting whether diseases are likely to be eliminated or, instead, (re)emerge, especially as a result of control measures. This tip…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 044205] Published Fri Oct 09, 2026.
tldr: This applied-mathematics paper studies critical-like growth near noncritical transitions using linearized dynamics, with applications to epidemic elimination and re-emergence.
motivation: The COVID-19 pandemic increased interest in infectious disease modeling, especially for predicting whether diseases will be eliminated or re-emerge under control measures.
method: The authors analyze linearized dynamics around noncritical transitions to characterize critical-like growth behavior in epidemic models.
result: The work identifies critical-like growth signatures in settings that are not strictly critical, linking linearized dynamics to epidemic re-emergence behavior.
conclusion: The framework may help interpret epidemic trajectories and control outcomes, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
